title: Make pie chart layout dimensions content-adaptive
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded pie chart dimensions (radius=140, label_radius=+60, cx/cy offsets) with values computed from the number of slices, label dimensions, and available space.

## Why
The pie chart layout in layout_diagram_pie_traced() (fm-layout/src/lib.rs) uses fixed dimensions:
- `radius = 140.0` — does not adapt to slice count
- `label_radius = radius + 60.0` — does not adapt to label length
- `cx = radius + 80.0`, `cy = radius + 60.0` — does not center properly with varying legend widths

With many slices (>8), labels overlap each other. With very long labels, they extend beyond the diagram bounds. With few slices, the chart is unnecessarily large.

## Proposed Approach
1. Compute `radius` from: `max(100.0, min(200.0, slice_count * 20.0))`
2. Compute `label_radius` from: `radius + max_label_width * 0.5 + 20.0`
3. Compute `cx`/`cy` to center the pie within the computed bounds
4. Consider adding `PieLayoutConfig` struct to LayoutConfig with `min_radius`, `max_radius`, `label_padding` fields

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pie charts with 2-3 slices are compact
- Pie charts with 15+ slices are larger with readable labels
- Labels never overlap (or at least minimize overlap with angle-based spreading)
- No regression for typical (3-8 slice) pie charts
close_reason: Pie radius now scales with slice count: base_radius=100+8*n, clamped to [80,220]. Label radius and center computed from radius. Replaces fixed 140/60/80/60.

title: flowchart ([text]) never parses as Stadium: collapses to Rounded and draws its brackets as label text
description:
Found by the bd-iicc guard sweep, on the last unguarded diagram type (flowchart). The byte golden
pins this happily because the output is perfectly stable — it is just wrong, and it is wrong in a way
that looks entirely plausible on screen.

THE DEFECT. In a flowchart, `id([text])` is mermaid's STADIUM (pill) shape. This parser has no
`([` … `])` probe at all. The shape dispatch chain at mermaid_parser.rs:8699-8740 tries, in order:
`((…))`, `[(…)]`, `[[…]]`, `[…]`, `(…)`, `{…}`, `>…]`, `[/…/]`, … A stadium token `([Stadium])`
misses every probe until `(…)`, which matches — the token does start with `(` and end with `)` — so
it is parsed as ROUNDED carrying the literal inner text `[Stadium]`, brackets included.

MEASURED on a fresh render of crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/all_node_shapes.mmd, which declares
`stadium([Stadium])`:

  declared              rendered element                                  a11y title
  round(Rounded)        rect rx="10"   width 129.75  height 66.50         "…, rounded rectangle"
  stadium([Stadium])    rect rx="10"   width 133.05  height 66.50         "…adium], rounded rectangle"

Identical shape signature to the plain rounded node. Three separate symptoms, one cause:
  1. SHAPE COLLAPSE. A stadium must be a pill: rx = min(w,h)/2 = 33.25 here. It renders at rx=10,
     i.e. the rounded-rectangle radius. Two DIFFERENT declared shapes produce the SAME picture.
  2. LABEL CORRUPTION. The visible text is `[Stadium]`, not `Stadium`. The brackets that were shape
     SYNTAX are being drawn as CONTENT. Visible in the edge titles too: "Rounded points to
     [Stadium]", "[Stadium] points to Subroutine".
  3. ACCESSIBILITY METADATA IS WRONG. The node's title reads "rounded rectangle", so a screen reader
     is told the wrong shape.

THE RENDERER IS NOT AT FAULT AND ALREADY DOES ITS PART. fm-render-svg has complete Stadium support
that is simply unreachable from flowcharts: the rect branch sets rx = w.min(h)/2.0 for
NodeShape::Stadium (lib.rs:8672, 8842), there is a `fm-node-shape-stadium` CSS class (11432) and a
", stadium shape" a11y title (7893). `NodeShape::Stadium` is currently produced ONLY for
sequenceDiagram participants declared with the `actor` keyword (mermaid_parser.rs:8041-8042). So the
whole stadium rendering path is dead code for the diagram type that has the syntax for it.

WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG — and this is the part worth keeping, because it is the same lesson as the
rest of bd-iicc. There IS a parser test covering exactly this input, and it cannot fail:

    fn flowchart_node_shapes_basic() {
        let input = "flowchart TB\n  A[Rectangle]\n  B(Rounded)\n  C{Diamond}\n  D([Stadium])\n …";
        assert!(parsed.ir.nodes.len() >= 8, "Should have 8 shaped nodes, got {}", …);
    }

It asserts the COUNT and never the SHAPES. Every node could parse as Rounded and it still passes.
That is precisely the "tautology dressed as a test" bd-iicc warns about, sitting directly on top of
the defect. `flowchart_hexagon_and_parallelogram_shapes` immediately below it has the same form
(`nodes.len() >= 3`) and gives no shape coverage either — worth checking those shapes too, though
hexagon at least is confirmed correct by the new guard.

ACCEPTANCE GATE, already written and committed:
`flowchart_declared_node_shapes_stay_distinct` in crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs is
committed `#[ignore]`d with a pointer here. It fails today against the live defect with the shape
signatures printed. Removing the `#[ignore]` is this bead's acceptance gate — do not weaken the
guard to land the fix.

FIX SKETCH, not prescriptive: add a `parse_wrapped_str_with_config(core, "([", "])",
NodeShape::Stadium, config)` probe BEFORE the `(…)` Rounded probe, so the longer delimiter wins. Note
the ordering constraint is real — the existing chain already relies on it (`[(…)]` and `[[…]]` are
both tried before the bare `[…]` probe for the same reason). Check `looks_like_unclosed_node_delimiter`
(mermaid_parser.rs:8919) too, since it has bespoke `[[` handling and may want the `([` case.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING while in here, same syntax family and same tautological-test coverage:
`[(Database)]` Cylinder is probed, but `[/…/]`, `[\…\]` and `[/…\]` variants should be confirmed to
map to Parallelogram/Trapezoid distinctly rather than collapsing the way stadium did.
close_reason: Fixed across 649ac155/d2af39f0/779817ed, goldens re-blessed in 38a77cbf. Acceptance gate met: flowchart_declared_node_shapes_stay_distinct is un-ignored and passing, no assertion weakened. Scope was larger than filed — six shapes, not one (Stadium, Cylinder, Parallelogram, InvParallelogram, Trapezoid, InvTrapezoid), all losing to a nested single-char delimiter and all carrying their syntax into the label. Three shape paths involved; the fast path at parse_fast_simple_flowchart_node_borrowed hardcodes Rect and was the one catching the slanted four. Tautological flowchart_node_shapes_basic strengthened to assert shapes+labels, which is what surfaced Cylinder. fm-parser 513 passed; golden_svg_test 41 passed; golden_layout_test 2 passed; fmt clean.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED. Stadium in 649ac155 + d2af39f0, the rest of the family in 779817ed, goldens re-blessed in
38a77cbf. The acceptance gate this bead named is met: the #[ignore] on
flowchart_declared_node_shapes_stay_distinct is REMOVED and the guard passes, with no assertion
weakened.

THE BEAD UNDERSTATED THE DEFECT. It was filed as one shape (`([…])` Stadium). It is a FAMILY of six,
all the same mechanism — a multi-char shape delimiter losing to a single-char delimiter nested inside
it — and I only found the other five because the strengthened test forced them out one at a time:
  ([Stadium])   Stadium           was Rounded,          label "[Stadium]"
  [(Database)]  Cylinder          was Rect,             label "(Database)"
  [/Para/]      Parallelogram     was Rect,             label "/Para/"
  [\Inv\]       InvParallelogram  was Rect,             label "\Inv\"
  [/Trap\]      Trapezoid         was Rect,             label "/Trap\"
  [\InvTrap/]   InvTrapezoid      was Rect,             label "\InvTrap/"
Every one carried its own shape syntax into the visible label, which is the tell: the token was
parsed as content, not as a shape.

THERE ARE THREE SHAPE PATHS, NOT ONE, and that is the thing to inherit from this bead. My first fix
was correct and changed nothing, twice, because I was editing paths the input never reached:

  1. flow_statement_parser() — a chumsky combinator `choice` (mermaid_parser.rs ~600). Tried FIRST;
     if it parses without errors its result WINS. Had double_circle and hexagon but no stadium,
     cylinder or slanted rules, so its greedy single-char `[…]`/`(…)` rules swallowed them.
  2. parse_node_token_with_config (~8700) — the manual probe chain, used when chumsky errors. Had
     the slanted probes but placed them AFTER the bare `[…]` probe, where they were unreachable for
     any well-formed token.
  3. parse_fast_simple_flowchart_node_borrowed (~2002) — a fast path that runs BEFORE both and
     HARDCODES `shape: NodeShape::Rect`. This is the one that actually caught `[/Para/]`.

Path 3 is why the slanted shapes stayed broken after I had fixed paths 1 and 2 and had verified BOTH
in isolation — `parse_node_token_with_config("C[/Para/]")` returned Parallelogram and
`flow_statement_parser().parse(...)` returned Parallelogram, while `parse_mermaid` still returned
Rect. Verifying a fix at the function level proves nothing about which function the input reaches.

WHY PATH 3 CAUGHT ONLY THE SLANTED FOUR: it rejects a candidate whose label contains any of
`( ) { } " ' \` | & ,`, which is what made it correctly defer `[(Database)]` and `([Stadium])`. But
`/` and `\` are NOT in that set, so `[/Para/]` looked like an ordinary rectangle with a slashy label.
I did NOT add `/` to the forbidden set — that would push every ordinary "TCP/IP" or "and/or" label
off the fast path for no correctness gain. The guard is narrow: defer only when the label BOTH opens
and closes with a slash, which is exactly the slanted-token shape.

THE TAUTOLOGICAL TEST WAS THE ROOT ENABLER, and it is now fixed rather than merely noted.
`flowchart_node_shapes_basic` had `D([Stadium])` in its input and asserted only
`parsed.ir.nodes.len() >= 8` — satisfied by all eight nodes parsing as Rounded. It now asserts the
shape AND the label for all eight declared forms, and it was that strengthening which surfaced
Cylinder. Two more tests added: flowchart_stadium_is_not_parsed_as_rounded, and
flowchart_multi_char_shape_delimiters_beat_their_nested_single_char_forms covering all six.

GOLDENS MOVED, LEGITIMATELY, and the blast radius was verified rather than assumed: exactly ONE
fixture in each golden (all_node_shapes, the only fixture using `([…])`), despite the fix touching a
shared fast path and both dispatch chains. The semantic diff contains nothing the fix does not imply
— rx 10 -> 33.25 (height/2, the pill), the label and aria-label shedding their brackets, the a11y
title going from "rounded rectangle" to "stadium shape", and a 3.30px leftward shift of the three
downstream nodes because the corrected label is two characters shorter. layout_checksums moved one
entry, width 1274.0 -> 1270.699951, node_count and edge_count unchanged.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and worth its own bead if anyone cares: the four slanted shapes have no
golden fixture at all, so they are now correct but unpinned. all_node_shapes covers eight of the
twelve flowchart shapes. Adding `[/…/]` and friends to a fixture would pin them, but that is fixture
work, not this fix.

Gates: cargo test -p fm-parser 513 passed / 0 failed. golden_svg_test 41 passed (was 40 + 1
ignored). golden_layout_test 2 passed. cargo fmt --check exits 0.

title: Class member shorthand 'Class : +member' renders as a literal node label
description:
Found incidentally while checking bd-4isi golden fallout (cc lane, LilacPike).

crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/class_basic.mmd is:
  classDiagram
    Animal <|-- Dog
    Animal : +name
    Dog : +bark()

The committed golden SVG (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/class_basic.svg) contains exactly two text
elements: 'Animal : +name' and 'Dog'. So the colon shorthand does NOT populate class_meta.attributes
-- it becomes a literal node LABEL containing the whole line -- and 'Dog : +bark()' contributes no
visible text at all ('bark' appears zero times in the golden).

mermaid-js renders this as a class box 'Animal' with a member row '+name', and a box 'Dog' with
'+bark()'. So this is a real cross-engine fidelity gap, in the same family as bd-4isi but on a
DIFFERENT code path: bd-4isi was block syntax ('class C { +int f }') whose members reached
class_meta but were truncated by node sizing; this is shorthand whose members never reach class_meta
at all.

NOT currently blocking any measured claim. The head-to-head corpora (corpus.mjs classDiagram() and
docClass()) both emit BLOCK syntax, so ci_batch_500 / doc_build_40 / docs_site_* do not exercise this
path. Verified bd-4isi's fix does not change class_basic output: baseline ELF 3d081db7 and fixed ELF
3ed92bc5 both render it to SHA-256 fcf194be77fdd22e71e9e0ed2bd737c691ab91f8a2a082140ffeda5a80b5343b,
so golden_svg_test is unaffected by that fix.

Retry predicate: raise priority if any timed corpus starts emitting colon-shorthand members, or if
the equivalence gate is extended to a corpus that uses it.
close_reason:
VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, then closed. The parser fix landed in 3e922c09 and the goldens were blessed by a peer in 93a6cd1d / f805c8d3; I did not take that on faith.

Evidence re-run today: golden/class_basic.svg renders rows 'Animal', '+name', 'Dog', '+bark()' (was 'Animal : +name' and 'Dog', with 'bark' absent from the output entirely — the mermaid-js rendering this bead specified). All five named probes pass: class_colon_shorthand_populates_members_not_a_literal_label, _accumulates_multiple_members_per_class, _keeps_return_type_after_the_member_colon, _ignores_directive_and_style_statements, and class_inline_generics_declaration_does_not_open_a_member_block. cargo test --workspace 0 failures; clippy -D warnings clean.

ONE GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (ac57987d): class_basic was pinned by its BYTE golden alone — no semantic guard existed for any class diagram. That is exactly the blindness that let this defect live: nothing was misplaced or malformed, a declared member simply never appeared, so a hash could not tell the wrong picture from the right one and a regression could be re-blessed away. class_colon_shorthand_renders_as_member_rows reads the expected members FROM THE FIXTURE and asserts, per declared shorthand, that the member is a row of its class's box, the class name is a row of its own, and the box does NOT carry 'Class : member' as one literal label. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with parse_class_shorthand_member forced to return None it fails with the defect's original signature — 'Animal declares member "+name", which is not a row of its box; rows are ["Animal : +name"]'.

No production code needed changing. bd-ij5b (parse_class fallthrough interning junk class nodes) remains separately open and is NOT covered by this.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Parser fix LANDED in 3e922c09 (a peer's commit -a swept the working tree; content is this lane's work, complete with all 5 unit tests).

parse_class_shorthand_member splits 'Animal : +name' on the FIRST colon and emits BlockStart/Member/End, reusing the existing block lowering so members reach class_meta. Guard: left of the colon must be a single whitespace-free token (excludes 'style A fill:#f00', 'classDef x fill:#f00', 'link A "http://x"', 'note for A "text: here"'), plus accTitle/accDescr/title/direction by name. Runs AFTER the edge attempt so 'A <|-- B : label' still parses as an edge.

Also fixed a latent defect the shorthand depends on: parse_class set in_block on BlockStart but never cleared it on End, so the one-line 'class List~T~' generics form left the parser in member mode and swallowed the next relation. Now cleared; covered by class_inline_generics_declaration_does_not_open_a_member_block.

SEMANTIC EVIDENCE (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/class_basic.mmd, rendered <text> content):
  before: 'Animal : +name', 'Dog'   <- whole line as one literal label; 'bark' absent entirely
  after:  'Animal', '+name', 'Dog', '+bark()'
which is the mermaid-js rendering this bead specified.

GATES: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); fm-parser lib 431/431 pass (23/23 class tests); ubs reports no finding on any changed line.

STILL OPEN, blocked on bd-bg07: class_basic.svg needs re-blessing, but golden_svg_test is red on main for an unrelated reason -- every golden predates a node-gradient/glow <defs> addition, reproduced on dense_flowchart_stress, which has zero subgraphs and is not a classDiagram so neither change on this lane can reach it. Blessing class_basic now would launder that unrelated drift into this bead. Re-bless after bd-bg07 resolves, with a GOLDEN-CHANGE note covering both deltas.

Also filed bd-ij5b: parse_class's fallthrough interns unrecognized statements (accTitle:, style ...) as junk class nodes. Pre-existing, unaffected by this change.

LAYOUT GOLDEN IS ALSO RED FOR THIS BEAD, not just the SVG one. golden_layout_test::layout_golden_checksums_are_stable fails on class_basic:

  stored  aa06723272d8625d  271.700012 x 357.0

title: class diagram members are dropped from rendered SVG
description:

  mermaid-js 11.15.0              50          50         50

title: Canvas text state LEAKS between draw sources: state notes and axis ticks inherit align/baseline
description:
draw_state_notes and draw_axis_ticks both call fill_text without ever calling set_text_align or set_text_baseline. Every draw source runs inside ONE ctx.save()/restore() pair, so both inherit whatever the last source that did set them left behind.

The call order is draw_clusters -> draw_bands -> draw_axis_ticks -> ... -> draw_state_notes. draw_clusters sets Left/Top ONLY when it actually draws a cluster title; draw_bands sets Left/Top ONLY when it draws a band label. So the SAME note renders at a DIFFERENT vertical position depending on whether the diagram happens to also contain a composite state (which becomes a titled cluster). Two state diagrams with identical note text render it differently.

Baseline Top vs the fresh-canvas alphabetic default differs by roughly one ascent, which is enough to push the first line across the note's own border.

SEPARATELY, and worth its own decision: where the canvas puts this content disagrees with fm-render-svg, which is the fuller arm.

  state note text: SVG x = nx+10, y = ny+8, DominantBaseline::Hanging, TextAnchor::Start, line_height = config.line_height. Canvas x = x+4, line_y = y + (font_size*1.2)*(row+1), align/baseline inherited.

  axis ticks: SVG draws a TICK LINE from (x, y+4) to (x, y+16) and a label at (x+3, y) anchor start, font_size*0.72, with tick_y = bounds.y - 12. Canvas draws NO LINE AT ALL, puts the label at (x, y) with font_size*0.75, and computes y = bounds.y + 12 -- opposite sign.

The missing tick line is the bd-039t / bd-t1jj family: declared content one renderer draws and another silently omits.
close_reason: done

title: Replace the constraint LP's wall-clock valve with a counted simplex-iteration bound
description:
Fixed by 23520d56.

MECHANISM, worse than this bead originally described. good_lp's HiGHS backend (solvers/highs.rs:
308-330) maps ReachedTimeLimit / ReachedIterationLimit / ReachedSolutionLimit / ReachedInterrupt /
ReachedMemoryLimit onto SolutionStatus::TimeLimit and STILL returns Ok(solution) whenever a feasible
primal point exists. The code checked only for Err, so a feasible-but-SUBOPTIMAL point was written
into node.bounds. The geometry was not "optimized or not" -- it was PARTIALLY optimized, by however
much clock the solver got.

WHAT LANDED:
  - constraint_solution_is_usable(status) gates the write; anything but Optimal returns Err and the
    caller takes its existing layout.constraint_solver.fallback branch, leaving the deterministic
    heuristic coordinates.
  - constraint_solver_time_limit_ms -> constraint_solver_wall_clock_valve_ms, 1_000 ->
    CONSTRAINT_SOLVER_WALL_CLOCK_VALVE_MS = 30_000, matching bd-giej's valve discipline.
  - A valve of 0 is honoured instead of clamped up to 1 ms.

PROBES, and the honest accounting of what each one proves:
  1. constraint_lp_result_is_used_only_when_proven_optimal -- Optimal used, TimeLimit refused,
     GapLimit refused. THIS is the probe that pins the fix. NEGATIVE CONTROL: widening the predicate
     to Optimal | TimeLimit fails it on the TimeLimit case. Source restored byte-identically,
     sha256 a2dff3c58f2f017896931308ee8574168d533e860634115ba578663a4faf23af.
  2. constraint_solver_wall_clock_valve_never_reaches_the_coordinates -- across six valve values the
     coordinates are only ever the proven optimum or the untouched heuristic fallback, never a third
     geometry, and a valve of 0 falls back exactly. Carries a reachability check (a pin to
     (1500, 900) that must land) and a non-vacuity control.

THE PROBE WAS VACUOUS TWICE AND ITS OWN CONTROLS CAUGHT IT BOTH TIMES. Recording this because it is
the reusable part:
  - Round 1: the non-vacuity control failed with "the LP does not move this document". The control
    was right and the FIXTURE was wrong -- see my earlier comment on apply_constraint_solver having
    exactly one caller. A probe without that control would have PASSED while proving nothing.
  - Round 2: with the fixture fixed the probe passed, so I disabled the status check and re-ran it.
    IT STILL PASSED. The end-to-end probe cannot reach that branch at all: a valve short enough to
    fire deterministically stops HiGHS before it has a feasible point, so good_lp returns Err and the
    caller falls back for a DIFFERENT reason. Provoking a genuine feasible-but-suboptimal stop means
    interrupting phase 2 of the simplex, which is a race and does not belong in a test. That is why
    the decision was extracted into a free function and asserted directly.

HONEST LIMIT, and the reason a follow-up is warranted rather than this being called complete: the fix
BOUNDS the load dependence, it does not remove it. Which branch you get still depends on whether the
solve fits inside a wall-clock valve. It is now essentially unreachable (30 s against LPs costing
milliseconds) instead of routinely hit at 1 s, and deterministic rather than partial when it fires.
Removing the residual entirely needs a COUNTED stop -- HiGHS simplex_iteration_limit through
HighsProblem::set_option, which means naming the concrete solver instead of default_solver.

GATES: cargo test -p fm-layout --lib 480 passed / 0 failed (remote, strict); cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets -D warnings clean; rustfmt --check clean; ubs exits 1 on this file per the pre-existing
bd-tp4z baseline, with none of its 46 findings on a line this commit touches. Pushed to main and
master.
close_reason:
Fixed by 3af41777. The wall-clock class is now closed end to end: bd-9a1t, bd-giej, bd-9xwk and this.

WHAT LANDED. The operative stop for the constraint LP is simplex_iteration_limit, derived by
constraint_lp_iteration_limit(node_count, constraint_count) from the problem's size alone -- 4
displacement rows per node plus roughly one row per declared constraint, times 64. A simplex
iteration is the same unit of work on every machine, so the solver now stops in the same place
everywhere, and constraint_solution_is_usable turns that stop into the same deterministic fallback
everywhere. The wall clock stays as a pure liveness backstop.

WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN LEAVING THE RESIDUAL. After bd-9xwk each branch was already
deterministic, but the CHOICE between them -- proven optimum or heuristic fallback -- still turned on
whether the solve fitted inside a wall clock, which is a property of the box. Counting removes that
last dependency, which is what "deterministic layout is mandatory" actually requires.

NAMING THE BACKEND is a real coupling and is stated in the code: good_lp is taken with only the highs
feature, so default_solver IS highs and .using(default_solver) yields a HighsProblem, whose
set_option is public.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it is the one that mattered, because an unknown HiGHS option key is SILENTLY
IGNORED -- this change could have been a no-op that still passed every test. With HEADROOM set to 0
(iteration budget 0), constraint_solver_enforces_pin_coordinates FAILS:

    assertion failed: (pinned.x - 320.0).abs() < 1.0

so HiGHS genuinely honours simplex_iteration_limit and the bound is load-bearing. Source restored
byte-identically, sha256 9cfbc5630d8d3b85e8a08873a843eb704d85c40bc50b9c4fc48d6713d2fe024b.

Worth recording: at a zero budget the OTHER three constraint tests still passed. Only the pin, which
asserts an exact absolute coordinate, could tell the difference. A control needs an assertion sharp
enough to notice -- three of the four available tests were blind to a solver that had been switched
off entirely.

PROBE: constraint_lp_iteration_bound_is_a_pure_function_of_problem_size -- same shape gives the same
bound, strictly monotonic on both axes, the exact 64x value, and the clamp holds at usize::MAX
without overflowing i32. All five pre-existing constraint tests still pass at the real budget, so no

title: ascii format forced Compact tier and dropped labels: it was made ASCII partly by throwing content away
description:
A REGRESSION IN MY OWN bd-t228 FIX, found by re-running the renderer audits against a CURRENT binary instead of the stale one they had been using.

MEASURED, same quadrant input, current binary:
  term    5,771 bytes, draws the point label 'Alpha'
  ascii     904 bytes, label GONE

ascii_term_config forced tier = MermaidTier::Compact alongside render_mode = CellOnly. CellOnly ALONE selects the cell path off the braille sub-cell painter -- render_layout takes it on either condition, which my own comment on the original fix already said. Compact additionally imposes its label budget (max_label_chars.min(12), max_label_lines 1) and a smaller canvas, so the surface was made ASCII partly by discarding content. Asking for ASCII glyphs is not asking for a smaller diagram.

EVIDENCE THAT THE TIER WAS NOT LOAD-BEARING: the pre-existing test the_ascii_surface_emits_no_non_ascii_byte PASSES with the tier left untouched. That is what proves CellOnly alone carries the ASCII property, rather than an argument that it ought to.

FIX: leave the tier as the caller configured it; set only render_mode and glyph_mode.

TESTS updated to the corrected contract -- the tier is asserted EQUAL TO THE BASE from two different bases, so a future 'downgrade the tier to make it ASCII' cannot return silently. The end-to-end test now also compares the ascii surface against the term surface LABEL BY LABEL, because asserting only that the bytes are ASCII would pass on an empty canvas.

HOW IT WAS FOUND is the transferable part: every renderer audit I had run used a CLI binary six hours stale (1ea272e5). Rebuilding and re-running them, with a staleness gate applied FIRST (binary mtime vs git log -1 --format=%ct per crate under test), showed xychart's title now fixed by bd-193x, quadrant newly missing in ascii only, and 22 diagram types still clean on structural invariants with 77 of 77 graphics roles named. The quadrant asymmetry could only become visible once bd-t228 made ascii genuinely differ from term.

STILL OPEN, measured in the same sweep and NOT fixed here: kanban's column name is absent from BOTH term and ascii while present in SVG. Separate defect, needs its own look.

title: Implement sequence diagram autonumber
description:
# Sequence Autonumber

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  Alice->>Bob: First (1)
  Bob->>Alice: Second (2)
\`\`\`
- \`autonumber\` enables sequential numbering on all messages
- Numbers appear as a small circled number next to each message arrow
- Can be toggled on/off mid-diagram

## Current State
- NOT parsed. \`autonumber\` line produces a warning.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Recognize \`autonumber\` as SequenceStatement::Autonumber.
2. **IR**: Add autonumber: bool flag to IrSequenceMeta.
3. **SVG Renderer**: When autonumber is true, prepend a circled number to each message label.
4. **Tests**: Autonumber on, verify numbers appear in SVG.
close_reason: Implemented autonumber parsing and SVG rendering. Parser recognizes 'autonumber' keyword as SequenceStatement::Autonumber, sets IrSequenceMeta.autonumber=true via IrBuilder.enable_autonumber(). SVG renderer prepends edge number to labels when autonumber is enabled. 3 parser tests added. All quality gates pass.

title: packet-beta fields are sized by label text, not by bit range: a 4-bit field renders wider than a 6-bit one
description:
THIRD instance of the proportionality class, after bd-e69x (sankey flow widths had to be scaled by value) and bd-h9gx (gantt bars had to encode duration). A packet diagram bit range IS its payload; ours is invisible in the picture.

MEASURED on crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/packet_basic.mmd at HEAD, no transforms in the document so these are final coordinates. Node ids are pkt-field-N-N in fixture order:

  field                    bits declared   rendered width
  0  Source Port            0-15  = 16      148.72
  1  Destination Port      16-31  = 16      176.77
  2  Sequence Number       32-63  = 32      189.98
  3  Acknowledgment Number 64-95  = 32      234.52
  4  Data Offset           96-99  =  4      145.43
  5  Reserved             100-105 =  6      139.65
  6  Flags                106-111 =  6      139.65
  7  Window Size          112-127 = 16      154.50

THREE INDEPENDENT PROOFS THAT WIDTH IS NOT BIT-DERIVED:
1. Fields 0, 1 and 7 all span exactly 16 bits and must therefore be IDENTICAL in width. They are 148.72, 176.77 and 154.50.
2. The 4-bit field (145.43) renders WIDER than the 6-bit field (139.65). The ordering is inverted.
3. The 32-bit fields should be exactly twice the 16-bit ones. 189.98 / 148.72 = 1.28.

WHAT WIDTH ACTUALLY TRACKS: label text length. Acknowledgment Number is the longest string and gets the widest box (234.52); Reserved and Flags are the two shortest and both sit at 139.65, which looks like the generic node minimum. So packet-beta is being laid out as ordinary labelled nodes.

POSITION IS ALSO NOT BIT-DERIVED. Rendered x values in field order are 134.90, 435.40, 743.32, 92.00, 451.07, 768.49, 139.44, 446.54 — jumping left and right, i.e. a generic three-column grid. A packet diagram field must start at its start-bit offset within its row.

THE INCUMBENT MODEL, read from the pinned mermaid-js 11.15.0 bundle rather than guessed, so whoever fixes this has the target: config is
    packet: { rowHeight: 32, bitWidth: 32, bitsPerRow: 32, showBits: true, paddingX: 5, paddingY: 5 }
so mermaid renders a BIT RULER: every bit is bitWidth wide, a field spanning N bits is N * bitWidth wide, rows WRAP every bitsPerRow (32) bits, each row is rowHeight tall, and bit numbers are drawn because showBits defaults true. Our fixture declares 128 bits, which in mermaid is four rows of 32; ours renders eight boxes on about three rows by generic grid placement, with no bit axis at all.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Fields with equal bit counts render at equal width. This is the sharpest test and it is what fails today for the three 16-bit fields.
2. Width is proportional to bit count: a 32-bit field is exactly twice a 16-bit field, and a 4-bit field is narrower than a 6-bit field.
3. Renaming a field must not change any geometry -- the same invariant bd-h9gx needed, and for the same reason: label length must not leak into the encoding.
4. A field starts at its start-bit offset within its row, and rows wrap every 32 bits by default.
5. GOLDEN IMPACT: packet_basic.svg and its layout checksum will move substantially. Needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note naming the new geometry.

LABEL OVERFLOW WILL FOLLOW, and bd-h9gx already solved this exact problem -- reuse that shape rather than rediscovering it. Once width is bit-derived, a 4-bit field is 4 * bitWidth wide and its label will not fit. bd-h9gx placed gantt task names via a LayoutExtensions entry decided in layout (so bounds can grow) reproducing mermaid inside-if-fits / outside-otherwise. mermaid packet does something simpler -- with bitWidth 32 a 4-bit field is 128px, usually enough -- but the containment question must be answered explicitly, not left to clip.

NO CERTIFIED RATIO AT RISK: packet-beta is not in the head-to-head corpus.

PROVENANCE: found by resuming bd-iicc on the highest-expected-value unguarded types. That round was 3 types for 1 hit: packet-beta is this defect; quadrantChart came back CLEAN (points at cx 230.33 / 333.83 / 402.83 correctly ordered for declared x 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.8, and cy 134.5 / 203.5 / 376.0 correctly inverted for y 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.2); journey came back a fidelity DIFFERENCE rather than a defect (we encode task score as fill colour -- 4 distinct scores to 4 distinct fills -- where mermaid uses face icons; the score is encoded, just differently, and mermaid also places journey tasks in a row so our uniform y is correct).
close_reason: Landed a7a455ed + eeb27cbb. Bit-derived packet layout: width = bits*32, x = (start%32)*32, rows wrap every 32 bits, label text read for nothing. Acceptance gate: packet_field_widths_are_proportional_to_bit_ranges un-ignored, plus packet_fields_start_at_their_bit_offset_and_rows_wrap_every_32_bits (criterion 4) and packet_field_geometry_does_not_depend_on_field_names (criterion 3). NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: all three FAIL against the old grid dispatch, all three pass now. Measured golden geometry: three 16-bit fields all 512 (were 148.72/176.77/154.50), 32-bit exactly 2x (was 1.28x), 4-bit 128 < 6-bit 192 (ordering was inverted). GOLDEN-CHANGE recorded in eeb27cbb (viewBox 1025.3x595 -> 1208x449, data-edges 7 -> 0). Row-straddling divergence filed as bd-8vr0 and pinned by a layout test. cargo test --workspace 0 failures; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: CLI link weight: 135 crates, and tracing-subscriber's json feature ships but is only used by tests
description:
FOLLOW-ON TO bd-akv2, same profile, same worst ratio. The 90.86x row (bd-kpgs) measures CLI process lifecycle -- its counted mechanism records every arm "started zero render workers" -- and its profile is 17% kernel ELF/page-fault (5.87 + 5.78) plus dynamic-loader symbol lookup (2.69 + 2.51). Both are functions of HOW MUCH CODE IS LINKED. bd-akv2 took the first bite by dropping clap's `color` feature, removing six crates. This bead is the rest of that surface, measured.

BASELINE, counted with `cargo tree -p frankenmermaid-cli --edges normal`, unique name+version, after bd-akv2: 135 crates linked into the CLI. Per direct dependency subtree:

    tracing-subscriber   30      crossterm            27      serde_yaml   14
    clap                 11      sha2                  9      toml          7
    rayon                 6      serde_json            5      time          5
    mimalloc              2      anyhow                1

CANDIDATE 1 -- tracing-subscriber `json` IS DECLARED AS A SHIPPING DEPENDENCY BUT USED ONLY BY TESTS.
This is the cleanest one and the only one with no product decision attached.

    crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml:65     [dependencies] features = ["env-filter", "fmt", "json"]
    crates/fm-layout/Cargo.toml:58  [dependencies] features = ["env-filter", "fmt", "json"]
    Cargo.toml:76 (workspace)       features = ["env-filter", "fmt"]      <- already correct

⚠️ I NEARLY FILED THIS AS "json is unused". It is not. Grepping the workspace for `.json()` finds
real call sites -- crates/fm-cli/tests/debug_test.rs:66 and four in crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs
(25852, 25948, 25992, 27484). Every one of them is inside test code. So the feature is needed, just
not by anything that ships. The fix is to move it: keep `["env-filter", "fmt"]` in [dependencies]
and add `tracing-subscriber = { features = ["json"] }` to [dev-dependencies] in both crates. Cargo
unifies dev-dependency features only into test/bench builds, so the tests keep compiling and the
shipped binary stops carrying the JSON formatter.

  NEGATIVE CASES: (1) the five call sites above must still compile -- if they do not, the dev-dep
  feature did not unify and the change is wrong, not the tests; (2) `cargo tree` must show a
  smaller set for the BINARY target specifically, since a plain `cargo tree` unifies dev-deps and
  would show no change at all -- measure with `--edges normal` and confirm against a `--all-targets`
  reading that is expected NOT to move; (3) fm-layout ships as a library, so its shipped feature
  set changes for downstream consumers too, which is the point but should be stated in the commit.

CANDIDATE 2 -- crossterm's 27-crate subtree is reachable only from `cmd_interactive`.
crossterm is used at exactly five import sites, all in crates/fm-cli/src/main.rs (:41-50), and the
`event` half -- which is what drags in mio, parking_lot and the derive_more proc-macro chain -- is
used only by the interactive TUI editor at `cmd_interactive` (main.rs:10044, event loop at :10082).
That subcommand is NOT behind a cargo feature today, unlike `watch`, `serve` and `png` which all
are.

  ⚠️ THIS IS A PRODUCT DECISION, NOT A PERF DECISION, and I am not making it. Putting `interactive`
  behind a feature changes what the shipped CLI can do. It is only worth doing if the interactive
  editor is genuinely optional, and that is the owner's call. Recorded because the 27 crates are
  the largest single reducible block, not because I think it should be done.

CANDIDATE 3 -- serde_yaml is `0.9.34+deprecated` and pulls 14 crates. It is genuinely used (front
matter in crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs:10234, policy files in evidence.rs:2185), so this
is a migration rather than a drop, and its value here is unclear -- indexmap/itoa/ryu are shared
with serde_json and would not all leave. Lowest priority of the three; listed so the sweep is
complete rather than because it looks profitable.

ALREADY CHECKED AND ABSENT, so nobody re-checks: `regex` is NOT linked. `cargo tree -i regex`
resolves nothing, so tracing-subscriber's env-filter is not dragging the regex engine in, which is
the usual reason that dependency is heavy.

⚠️ NOTHING HERE IS A MEASURED RATIO. These are counted link-weight candidates with a stated
mechanism, in the same standing as bd-akv2. Re-certifying 90.86x needs the cod-lane harness on
thinkstation1. A crate count is not a speedup; it is a reason to expect one in the two profile
entries that scale with binary size, and that expectation is what a re-measurement would test.

BUILD BUDGET: candidate 1 is written up but NOT implemented -- df -h /data read 58G against the 59G
floor when this was found, so no gate could be run. It is a two-line manifest change in two crates
plus the tree-count check above.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CANDIDATE 1 IS ALREADY COMPLETE, verified 2026-08-18 by reading both manifests against their section boundaries rather than by grepping for the feature string.

  fm-cli/Cargo.toml    [dependencies] runs 46-80 and line 68 ships features = ["env-filter", "fmt"];
                       [dev-dependencies] runs 84-91 and line 90 adds features = ["json"].
                       That is exactly the split this bead specifies.
  fm-layout/Cargo.toml tracing-subscriber appears ONCE, at line 58, and [dev-dependencies] runs
                       50-63 - so it is dev-only and ships nothing. The bead text says line 58 is in
                       [dependencies]; that is stale.

Negative case (1) from the bead is satisfied structurally: the four .json() call sites in
fm-layout/src/lib.rs must be test-only, because the crate has tracing-subscriber ONLY as a
dev-dependency and it compiled clean in the post-freeze workspace check earlier today. Shipping code
calling .json() could not have linked.

Negative case (2) - the cargo tree reading - is NOT done and cannot be under the current disk
throttle (no cargo). Worth one `cargo tree -p frankenmermaid-cli --edges normal` when builds return,
to record the crate count against the 135 baseline.

CANDIDATE 2 (crossterm behind an `interactive` feature) is untouched: the bead itself says it is a
product decision and not a perf one. Leaving that call to the owner.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CANDIDATE 1 IS IMPLEMENTED AND NOW VERIFIED AGAINST ALL THREE NEGATIVE CASES THIS BEAD DEMANDED.
The yield is ONE CRATE, not the larger win the framing invites, and that number is the finding.

⚠️ THE BEAD'S LINE REFERENCES ARE STALE — it was written when this was unimplemented ("df -h /data
read 58G against the 59G floor, so no gate could be run"). Both manifests have since been fixed:

  crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml:68     [dependencies]      features = ["env-filter", "fmt"]
  crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml:90     [dev-dependencies]  features = ["json"]
  crates/fm-layout/Cargo.toml:58  ALREADY under the [dev-dependencies] header at line 50

I nearly filed fm-layout as still broken on the strength of the bead's "Cargo.toml:58
[dependencies]". The line number is right and the SECTION is not — reading the surrounding headers
is what settled it. A stale line reference reads exactly like a live defect.

NEGATIVE CASE 2, the one that decides whether the change did anything, measured with the tree
feature column rather than by counting crates:

  --edges normal (SHIPS)  FEATURES=alloc,ansi,default,env-filter,fmt,matchers,nu-ansi-term,
                          once_cell,registry,sharded-slab,smallvec,std,thread_local,tracing,
                          tracing-log
  with dev-deps (TESTS)   ... json, serde, serde_json, tracing-serde ...

So `json`, `serde`, `serde_json` and `tracing-serde` are all absent from the shipping graph and
present in the test graph, which is exactly the intended split, and the control the bead asked for
(a reading expected NOT to move) behaves as predicted.

NEGATIVE CASE 1: `cargo check -p fm-layout --all-targets` exit 0 — the four `.json()` sites in
lib.rs and the one in fm-cli's debug_test.rs still compile, so the dev-dependency feature unifies
into test builds as intended. `cargo check -p frankenmermaid-cli` (shipping, no dev-deps) exit 0,
so nothing that ships needed the formatter.

NEGATIVE CASE 3: fm-layout ships as a library, so its published feature set changed for downstream
consumers too. That is the point, and it is stated here rather than left implicit.

⚠️ THE MEASURED YIELD IS 135 -> 134 CRATES. One. `tracing-serde` left; `serde_json` did not,
because fm-cli depends on it DIRECTLY, and `serde`/`indexmap`/`itoa`/`ryu` are shared with other
subtrees for the same reason. The bead already anticipated this shape for candidate 3
("indexmap/itoa/ryu are shared with serde_json and would not all leave") — it applies to candidate
1 as well, and neither the bead nor I predicted it there. Feature removal only removes CRATES that
nothing else pulls, and in a graph this connected that is usually few.

That does not make it wrong: the shipped binary no longer carries the JSON formatter or the serde
machinery it drives, which is code linked and paged in, and the bead's stated mechanism is kernel
ELF/page-fault plus loader symbol lookup — both functions of linked SIZE, not of crate COUNT. Crate
count was only ever a proxy, and this is a case where the proxy understates.

CANDIDATES 2 AND 3 NOT TAKEN, deliberately. Candidate 2 (crossterm's 27 crates behind an
`interactive` feature) is flagged in the bead itself as a product decision about what the shipped
CLI can do, and that is the owner's call, not mine. Candidate 3 (serde_yaml migration) is a
migration the bead itself rates lowest and doubts the value of. Recording that I read both and
declined rather than leaving them looking unexamined.

NO MEASUREMENT: runq 52 with nine remote builds. And per the bead's own closing note, a crate count
is not a speedup — re-certifying 90.86x needs the cod-lane harness in a quiet window.

title: Terminal drops sequence NOTE text; both non-SVG renderers drop quadrant AXIS labels
description:
MEASURED SVG vs terminal vs canvas on the same IR. Found by probing the diagram types my own renderer-agreement corpus never covered - pie, xychart, quadrant, packet, c4, architecture, sequence.

  seq_note      "Ponder"   svg=true  term=FALSE  canvas=true
  quadrant_axis "Low"      svg=true  term=FALSE  canvas=FALSE

TWELVE other cases agree across all three renderers (pie label and title, xychart title and axis, quadrant title and point, packet field, c4 name, architecture service, sequence message, timeline event, sankey node), so the instrument is discriminating rather than reporting everything.

seq_note: the terminal renders sequence notes as bare RECTANGLES - the same geometry-without-text shape as bd-u3fo, bd-039t and the canvas Lane arm in bd-rk14. The canvas draws the text, so this is terminal-only.

quadrant_axis: BOTH non-SVG renderers drop it, which makes it a different shape from the others in this family - those were single-renderer gaps. Do not assume one fix covers both renderers here.

SCOPE NOTE ON MY OWN GATE: crates/fm-cli/tests/renderer_agreement.rs asserts the three renderers agree, and these two cases were outside its corpus. A gate is only as wide as its case list, and mine was narrower than the claim its name makes.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
seq_note FIXED for the terminal; quadrant_axis pinned for BOTH renderers.

seq_note: render_subcell_mode drew each note as a bare rectangle and no text. Now overlaid with the same discipline as the fragment labels - interior rows only, blank cells preferred, and a fallback that writes anyway when no blank run exists. That fallback is not optional: an all-or-nothing guard silently drew NOTHING for the longer of two otherwise identical fragment labels, which cost three builds on bd-039t.

quadrant_axis: NOT fixed and NOT assumed to be one bug. Both non-SVG renderers drop it, unlike every other member of this family, which were single-renderer gaps. Pinned as TWO KNOWN_GAPS entries - one per renderer - so fixing one does not silently close the other's record.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:

comments.author: ubuntu

title: EPIC: Reality Check Gap Closure
description:
## Purpose
Close every gap identified in the 2026-04-09 reality check audit. The audit compared README/AGENTS.md promises against actual code, tests, and deployment state. While the project is substantially honest (86k lines, all 24 diagram types render, all CLI commands work), several gaps threaten credibility:

1. **npm install claim is false**: @frankenmermaid/core returns 404 on npm registry. README tells users to run `npm install @frankenmermaid/core` which will fail.
2. **install.sh never committed**: README's `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` links to a file that doesn't exist on GitHub (untracked locally).
3. **classDef/style directives silently dropped**: Parsed but never applied to SVG render output. Users can write `classDef` and see no effect — no error, no warning, just silent failure.
4. **README understates FNX integration status**: Described as optional feature flag; actually the project's largest unfinished initiative (~25 open P1 beads).
5. **Long-tail diagram fidelity unproven**: All 16 tested types produce valid SVG, but visual quality (correct layout for sankey flows, pie slice angles, gitGraph branch lanes) has no golden-test coverage.
6. **Sequence advanced features incomplete**: Activation boxes, interaction fragments (alt/opt/loop), and notes are only partially parsed.
7. **Working tree hygiene**: Dozens of untracked audit files cluttering git status (fixed by .gitignore update in this session).

## Relationship to Existing Work
- FNX integration has its own epic (bd-ml2r); this epic does NOT duplicate that. Instead we create a single bead for README honesty about FNX status.
- Typography work (bd-3gq.2) is in progress; classDef styling is a SEPARATE concern (parsed→rendered wiring, not font metrics).
- "Write README" bead exists but covers feature comparison, not factual accuracy of install instructions.

## Success Criteria
- Every README install instruction either works or is corrected.
- classDef/style directives produce visible output in SVG or emit a diagnostic explaining they're unsupported.
- Golden tests added for at least 6 long-tail diagram types.
- Sequence advanced features either work or are honestly documented as unsupported.
- README FNX section accurately describes current state.

title: sequence par_over dropped the fragment and orphaned its end
description:
`par_over Group` is a valid sequence fragment in mermaid (PARSED against the pinned bundle) and we
had no concept of it. The damage was worse than one missing box:

  1. The fragment never opened, so the parallel block was not drawn.
  2. Its `end` therefore had no matching start, so the diagram ALSO gained a spurious
     "end without matching block group" warning - valid source accused of being unbalanced.

MECHANISM: parse_sequence_fragment_start is an if/else chain. `strip_prefix("par")` matches
`par_over Group` first, leaves `_over Group`, fails the keyword-boundary check (`rest` must be empty
or start with a space) and returns None for the WHOLE FUNCTION. There is no fall-through to a later
arm, so an arm added after `par` would be DEAD CODE. The new arm is placed BEFORE `par` and a test
pins that ordering: if it were moved after, the fragment count goes back to zero.

MAPPED ONTO FragmentKind::Par, deliberately. mermaid draws par_over as an OVERLAPPING parallel block
where par stacks its sections, so we lose that nuance and render an ordinary parallel box with the
tag reading `par`. A dedicated FragmentKind variant means exhaustive matches in fm-core, fm-parser,
fm-render-svg and fm-render-canvas - an E0004 sweep of the kind that put main red during bd-qdmn,
and not something to land unbuilt. The honest fix for the nuance is a RENDERER change; an enum
variant with nothing behind it would just be dead IR.

FOUND by the 137-token lexer diff that also produced bd-hebu and bd-lzhm.

FOLLOW-UP, not filed as ready: draw par_over as an overlapping block, which needs the variant plus
renderer support in both surfaces.

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Three tests added, none compiled. Two are controls -
plain `par` must still parse (inserting an arm ahead of it can shadow it) and `parallel Group` must
still NOT be a fragment (the keyword boundary must not have widened into a prefix match).
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build

title: Replace hardcoded diagram title color in scene renderer
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded dark gray (#1f2937) for diagram titles in the scene-based render path (render_scene_document_with_ir) with a theme-aware value.

## Why
The scene-based renderer at fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs line ~341 uses `.fill("#1f2937")` for diagram titles. This dark color is invisible on Dark, Blueprint, and Neon themes.

## Technical Context
This is in `render_scene_document_with_ir()` where the title is rendered BEFORE `let theme = resolve_theme()` at line ~361. The theme is not yet available when the title is rendered.

## Options
1. **Move title rendering after theme resolution** — requires restructuring the function, since the title needs to be in the SVG before the main content for z-ordering
2. **Use CSS custom property** — `.fill("var(--fm-text-color, #1f2937)")` — works when theme CSS is embedded
3. **Pre-resolve theme for title** — call `resolve_theme()` earlier just for the title color

Option 2 is the simplest and most robust since the theme CSS block IS embedded before the title element.

## Specific Changes
- fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs line ~341: Change `.fill("#1f2937")` to `.fill("var(--fm-text-color, #1f2937)")`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Diagram titles are readable on all 10 theme presets
- No visual regression on Default theme (fallback is the same dark gray)
close_reason: Title now uses var(--fm-text-color, #1f2937) CSS custom property. Theme CSS defines --fm-text-color for all presets.

title: Adopt franken_networkx's untracked-.rs repo guard: cargo compiles gitignored test targets invisibly
description: FLEET FINDING, adopted rather than re-derived. cargo compiles every .rs under a crate's tests/ as its own test target regardless of gitignore, so a throwaway probe left there is built on every cargo test; if it stops compiling it aborts the whole run, and if it is gitignored it is invisible to git status, log, blame and review. frankenlibc reached 273 such files with one broken since June. AUDIT RESULT FOR THIS REPO: exactly one, crates/fm-cli/tests/repro_scaling_bug.rs, dated 8 April, ignored by .gitignore:68 'repro_*.rs'. It compiles today - it was built by the clippy --workspace --all-targets run that passed on rch worker vmi1149989 - so this is a latent hazard rather than a live break. I did not delete it (no-deletion rule, and it is another agent's reproduction) and did not commit it, since that is an owner decision. GUARD: scripts/untracked_rust_guard.mjs, adapted from franken_networkx's tests/python/test_no_untracked_rust_in_cargo_dirs.py. Two design points carried over deliberately: it checks UNTRACKED rather than gitignored specifically, because ignoring is what hides a file but tracking is what makes it real - an untracked .rs in a compiled directory is a hazard either way, and the report says which offenders are ignored because that is the part a human cannot otherwise see; and the allowlist may only SHRINK, enforced by a self-test case that fails when an entry is no longer untracked, so the list cannot quietly become a place where new files hide. It also covers src/ and benches/, not just tests/, because the inverse failure is worse: an ignored file under src/ that later gains a mod declaration builds on one machine and fails for every other checkout and in CI. SIX SELF-TEST CASES, including one that asserts the detector actually finds the known offender - without it the allowlist would be a rubber stamp over a scan that sees nothing - and one that asserts it is reported as gitignored. Wired into the existing ledger-integrity-guard CI job alongside the other JS gates; both the self-test and the live scan run there. GATE: node scripts/untracked_rust_guard.mjs --self-test exit 0 (6 cases, 16 scanned dirs); live scan exit 0 with 1 allowlisted; full CI step body exit 0; workflow parses.
close_reason: Landed: scripts/untracked_rust_guard.mjs plus its CI wiring. Audit found exactly one offender in this repo (crates/fm-cli/tests/repro_scaling_bug.rs, .gitignore:68), allowlisted rather than deleted or committed since it is another agent's file and deletion needs permission. Checks UNTRACKED not gitignored, covers src/benches/tests, allowlist may only shrink (enforced by a self-test case). Gate: --self-test 6 cases exit 0, live scan exit 0, full CI step body exit 0

title: gitGraph branches render collinear; commits on different branches share one lane
description:
Found by bd-iicc while writing a semantic guard for the gitGraph golden. Same class as bd-e69x: the byte golden pins it happily because the output is stable, it is just not a gitGraph.

MEASURED on crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/gitgraph_basic.svg at HEAD:

  fixture: 2 commits on main, branch develop, 2 commits on develop, merge back, 1 more on main
  rendered: 6 commit circles at 6 distinct cy values (a vertical chain)
  rendered cx values across ALL commits: 158.52 and 176.26 only
  branch tags in order: git-branch-0, git-branch-0, git-branch-1, git-branch-1, git-branch-0
  no transform attributes anywhere in the file, so these are final coordinates

Commits tagged git-branch-1 (develop) sit at the SAME x as commits tagged git-branch-0 (main). The two branches are drawn collinear.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT, not a layout preference. Distinct lanes are the visual grammar of a gitGraph: the reader identifies which commits belong to which branch by their lane, and a merge is legible precisely because it joins two lanes. Collapsed onto one column, the diagram cannot express what it exists to express — the branch structure is present in the CLASS attribute but invisible in the picture. mermaid-js assigns each branch its own lane, so this is also a cross-engine fidelity gap.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so nobody re-does it: parsing and branch attribution are sound. All six commits render, they are ordered correctly down the chain, and branch membership is correctly recorded in the fm-node-user-git-branch-N class — the information reaches the renderer intact. The gap is purely that lane index is not converted into a position.

ODDITY WORTH CHECKING while fixing, not filed separately because I did not confirm it is wrong: only FIVE of the six circles carry a git-branch-N class. The untagged one is at cy=679.25, positionally where the merge commit falls, and it is also the only commit at the outlier cx=176.26. A merge commit legitimately belongs to the target branch, so it may simply be tagged differently on purpose — but if it is an accidental omission, the same fix should cover it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Commits sharing a branch tag share a lane coordinate: all git-branch-0 commits at one x, all git-branch-1 commits at another.
2. Different branches occupy DIFFERENT lanes - the branch-0 lane and branch-1 lane differ by at least a commit diameter, so the lanes are visually separable rather than merely unequal by a rounding error.
3. Ordering along the chain is preserved: the fix must not reorder commits to achieve separation.
4. GOLDEN IMPACT: gitgraph_basic.svg will move, and its viewBox will likely widen to accommodate a second lane. That is a legitimate GOLDEN-CHANGE needing a semantic diff that names the new lane positions and confirms no commit was lost or reordered. Only the gitGraph fixture should move.

TEST ALREADY WRITTEN AND WAITING: bd-iicc adds gitgraph_branches_occupy_distinct_lanes, currently #[ignore]d with a pointer to this bead. UN-IGNORING IT IS THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE GATE. Do not weaken it to make it pass - in particular do not relax the lane-separation distance to whatever the fix happens to produce.
close_reason:
Fixed by 42286916. ROOT CAUSE: layout_diagram_gitgraph_traced assigned lanes from CLUSTER membership, which a gitGraph never populates, so every commit fell into lane 0. The git-branch-N class could not serve as the lane because that index is taken modulo the 8-colour palette (branch 8 would land on branch 0's lane); new fm_core::IrGitGraphMeta carries the unwrapped lane per commit node, published by the parser and consumed by layout. memo_ir_equal's destructuring guard forced the new field into the incremental equality probe at compile time.

THREE SUB-DEFECTS fixed alongside, each of which also produced a lane-0 collision: (1) the ODDITY THE BEAD FLAGGED was an accidental omission - merge AND cherry-pick commits carried no branch attribution at all; all three commit paths now route through one tag_git_commit_branch helper, so the merge commit is tagged git-branch-0 (the branch it merged into) and branch tags go 5 -> 6. (2) checkout of an undeclared branch fell through branch_index's unwrap_or(0) and aliased onto main; it now interns its own lane. (3) commits were left-aligned in their lane, so a wide 'merge develop' box sat at a different centre from a bare commit on the same branch - that is why the merge was the outlier at cx=176.26. Commits are now centred across the lane.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all met and measured on the rendered fixture:
1. Same branch, same lane: the four git-branch-0 commits are all at cx=176.26; the two git-branch-1 commits are both at cx=424.79.
2. Different lanes, visually separable: 248.53 apart vs a 66.5 commit diameter.
3. Ordering preserved: 6 circles at the SAME six cy values as before (125.25 / 263.75 / 402.25 / 540.75 / 679.25 / 817.75); none lost, added, or reordered. Edge paths now traverse 176.26 <-> 424.79 at both the fork and the merge.
4. GOLDEN-CHANGE with semantic diff: gitgraph_basic.svg viewBox 352.53 -> 583.31 wide (height unchanged at 943), layout_checksums.json gitgraph_basic layout_width 272.53 -> 503.31. BLESS ran over all 19 SVG cases and 22 layout cases and ONLY the gitGraph fixture moved - every other checksum byte-identical.

ACCEPTANCE GATE: golden_svg_test::gitgraph_branches_occupy_distinct_lanes un-ignored with its assertions UNCHANGED - the separation threshold was not relaxed.

TESTS (same bead, 4 new + 1 un-ignored): fm-layout gitgraph_commits_are_placed_in_their_branch_lane asserts the geometric property (same branch -> same centre, different branch -> >= one diameter, chain order monotonic) rather than pinning coordinates; 3 fm-parser tests - lane for every commit incl. merge/cherry-pick cross-checked against the palette class, checkout-only branch gets its own lane, lanes stay distinct past 9 branches while the class provably wraps to git-branch-1.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS proving the tests catch the defect rather than restating the code: lane forced to 0 -> layout test fails 'lanes 124.262505 and 124.262505 are closer than one commit diameter (66.5)'; merge tagging removed -> 'every commit needs a lane, got {0: 0, 1: 1, 3: 0} for 4 nodes'; checkout interning removed -> branches ["main"] vs ["main", "feature"]. Both touched source files restored byte-identically (diff -q) after each control.

GATES: cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean (rch remote vmi1152480); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote ovh-a); cargo test --workspace 40/40 suites green, 0 failures; fm-parser gitgraph 21/21, fm-layout target 1/1, golden_svg_test 8/8, golden_layout_test 2/2; ubs exit 0 with no finding in the new code; cargo fmt --check shows zero drift in any hunk this commit authored; pre-commit hook chain (40-ledger-integrity, 50-agent-mail) both exit 0. Pushed to main and master at 42286916.

title: gitGraph: re-declaring an existing branch is silent; mermaid rejects it
description:
MEASURED against the pinned incumbent (~/.cache/fm-headtohead/mermaid-11.15.0.min.js, mermaid 11.15.0). Its createBranch opens with:
  if (records.branches.has(name)) throw new Error(`Trying to create a branch which already exists. ...`)
so mermaid REFUSES a duplicate branch declaration and the diagram does not render.

Ours (parse_git_branch, crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs) calls intern_branch, which returns the EXISTING index when the name is already known, then inherits the head and (since bd-6oz7) switches to it. No warning, no diagnostic. A user who writes "branch dev" twice, or "branch main" against the implicit default branch, gets a silently different picture instead of being told.

WHY A WARNING AND NOT AN ERROR: this parser is recovery-oriented by design - parse_git_branch already warns rather than aborts on an empty branch name, and the CLI surfaces warnings (crates/fm-cli/src/main.rs prints every entry of ParseResult::warnings). Throwing would be a larger behavioural change than the defect justifies and would diverge from how every other malformed gitGraph input is handled here. Emitting a warning closes the silence, which is the actual defect, and leaves the render permissive.

NOTE the interaction with bd-6oz7: before that fix a duplicate "branch dev" was doubly invisible, because it neither warned NOR switched. Now it switches, which is the mermaid behaviour for a NEW branch being applied to a case mermaid rejects outright - so the silence matters more than it used to.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED. parse_git_branch now warns when the declared branch already exists, instead of passing in silence.

The check reads state.branch_order BEFORE intern_branch, which is load-bearing: intern_branch returns the EXISTING index for a known name, so after that call the two cases are indistinguishable.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, not assumed: with the guard spliced out (&& false), gitgraph_duplicate_branch_declaration_warns fails with `warnings: []` - the exact silence, and it also shows nothing else was warning, so no other diagnostic was masking it. Re-armed and verified: guard restored, no marker left in the file.

TESTS: the duplicate case asserts BOTH that the warning appears AND that the diagram still renders - a fix that dropped the diagram would trade the silence for something worse than the defect. The control asserts a FIRST declaration does NOT warn; without it, an unconditional warning would satisfy the main test while crying wolf on every correct diagram, which is precisely why the check has to run before intern_branch.

Deliberately a warning and not an error: this parser is recovery-oriented (the empty-branch-name case above warns rather than aborting) and the CLI surfaces every ParseResult warning, so the silence is closed while the render stays permissive. mermaid throws here; that divergence is now intentional and documented at the call site rather than accidental.

Clippy asked for .contains() over .iter().any() and it is applied. fm-parser 558 passed; fm-render-svg and cli unchanged; no golden moved.

title: Wire classDef/style directives through to SVG render output
description:
## Problem
Mermaid classDef and style directives are PARSED by fm-parser (confirmed: the parser extracts class definitions and style assignments into the IR) but they are NEVER APPLIED during SVG rendering. This means:
- A user writes: `classDef important fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px`
- The parser stores this in the IR without error
- The SVG renderer completely ignores it
- The user sees default styling with NO warning or diagnostic

This is a silent failure — worse than a "not supported" error because the user doesn't know their styling is being dropped.

## Scope
1. **Survey the IR**: Determine where classDef data lives in MermaidDiagramIr after parsing. Check IrNode.classes, any classDef-specific structures in meta, and style directive handling.
2. **SVG render integration**: In fm-render-svg, when rendering a node, check if it has classes that match any classDef. If so, apply the CSS properties (fill, stroke, stroke-width, color, font-size, etc.) to the SVG element's inline style or as CSS custom properties.
3. **CSS generation**: Generate <style> rules in the SVG <defs> section for each classDef, scoped to the appropriate CSS selectors (e.g., `.node.important { fill: #f9f; }`).
4. **Style directive handling**: Wire the `style` directive (which applies inline styles to specific nodes) through to SVG output.
5. **Theme interaction**: Define precedence: theme defaults < classDef rules < inline style directives < init directive overrides. Document this.
6. **Diagnostic for partial support**: If any CSS property in a classDef is not supported by the SVG renderer, emit a Warning-level diagnostic listing the unsupported properties.

## Why This Matters
Styling is one of the most-used Mermaid features. Users migrating from mermaid-js will expect classDef to work. Silent failure erodes trust more than explicit "unsupported" errors.

## Dependencies
- fm-parser already parses classDef (verified).
- fm-core IR must carry the parsed data (verify exact fields).
- fm-render-svg must consume and apply it.

## Testing
- Unit test: classDef with fill/stroke/stroke-width produces matching SVG attributes.
- Unit test: style directive on specific node overrides classDef.
- Golden test: `flowchart_with_classdef.mmd` added to golden suite.
- Negative test: unsupported CSS property emits diagnostic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `classDef` definitions in Mermaid input produce visible style changes in SVG output.
- `style` directives on individual nodes produce visible inline styles.
- Unsupported CSS properties emit a warning diagnostic.
- Golden test captures the styled output for regression safety.
- README Limitations section updated to remove classDef from the "not yet applied" list.
close_reason: classDef/style already fully implemented; added golden test flowchart_classdef.mmd/.svg

title: Local cargo builds silently link stale rch-retrieved artifacts
description:
Found the hard way by cc lane (LilacPike) after drawing a wrong conclusion from a stale binary.

SYMPTOM: a local 'cargo build -p frankenmermaid-cli --example headtohead' prints only
'Compiling frankenmermaid-cli' and 'Finished' in ~25s, produces a working binary, and that binary
contains a THREE-WEEK-OLD parser. Source changes to fm-parser are silently ignored.

EVIDENCE:
  crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs  mtime 2026-07-31
  target/release/deps/libfm_parser-*.rlib mtime 2026-07-10 .. 2026-07-13
  cargo clean -p fm-parser  ->  'Removed 0 files'
  touch mermaid_parser.rs + rebuild -> IDENTICAL ELF sha256 (317f66e9...)

CAUSE: rch exec retrieves the worker's build artifacts into the local target/ (it reported
'384 files, 1828357 bytes' on one run). Those arrive with fingerprints cargo treats as fresh, so a
subsequent LOCAL cargo build considers fm-parser up to date and links the remote-built rlib. cargo
clean -p cannot remove them because they are not tracked as locally-built units.

WHY IT MATTERS: this manufactures false measurement and false verdicts. I ran the cross-engine
equivalence gate on ci_docs_2000 with such a binary and got 105 divergent state diagrams -- exactly
the PRE-FIX count -- and briefly took it as evidence that a committed, unit-tested fix did not work.
Same failure class as the 'verify fm_elf_sha256 MOVED' rule already in the rch overlay guidance; that
rule exists for overlay mistakes, but this is a plain local build.

MITIGATION THAT WORKS: build through rch (--base <sha> --clean-overlay), which uses a clean remote
tree, and ALWAYS verify the ELF sha256 moved before trusting any run.

WANTED: either make local builds refuse to link rch-retrieved units, or have rch retrieve into a
directory that local cargo does not consult, or document a supported 'make local target consistent'
step. Note test-profile builds appeared UNAFFECTED in the same tree -- they rebuilt correctly and
produced fixed output -- so the staleness is per-profile/unit and easy to miss.
notes:
SHARPER DIAGNOSIS (cc lane, LilacPike): CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target is set in the agent environment.

So there are TWO target trees in play:
  /data/projects/frankenmermaid/target/   <- where rch RETRIEVES worker-built artifacts
  /data/tmp/cargo-target/                 <- where local cargo actually builds (CARGO_TARGET_DIR)

That explains the whole confusing picture:
- 'cargo clean -p fm-parser' reported 'Removed 0 files' because it cleaned the CARGO_TARGET_DIR tree,
  which is not where the stale rch artifacts live.
- The stale libfm_parser-*.rlib files I found dated Jul 10-13 are in the repo's target/deps, i.e. the
  rch retrieval target, and were never what local cargo was linking.
- The rch recipes all use 'env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR', which UNSETS it so rch can rewrite it to a
  worker-scoped path. A plain local cargo invocation does NOT unset it and uses the shared tree.

I have not re-established exactly which tree produced the stale headtohead binary, so the original
title may be imprecise. What IS reproducible and matters: a local 'cargo build --example headtohead'
produced a binary whose parser behaved PRE-FIX while the test profile in the same checkout behaved
POST-FIX, and touching the source did not change the resulting ELF sha256. Whatever the mechanism,
the operational rule stands: build through rch and VERIFY THE ELF SHA MOVED before trusting a run.

Also correcting myself: commit messages 4e93cd76 and 98043420 say the local bless reused 'the repo's
existing target/'. It did not -- it used the shared /data/tmp/cargo-target. Still one pre-existing
shared directory with nothing newly minted, so the disk directive was satisfied, but the wording is
wrong.

title: Native DNF validator cannot decide state or ER output: node_id_set_vs_input undecidable at 2000 nodes
description:
FOUND WHILE BANKING A LEDGER ROW, and it is the reason that row claims 4 families rather than 7.

MEASURED. equivalence-4bcb1b80-1786765165168.json, both engines one invocation, ELF afeba973853e6ae3660afa6bb06dd20d6dbd0aed4f335b6051f94291af358f30:

  wide_xl_50x50       native validation PASS
  cyclic_scc_xl_2500  native validation PASS
  dense_dag_xl_2000   native validation PASS
  class_xl_2000       native validation PASS
  state_xl_2000       FAIL -- 'required source-grounded invariants undecidable:
                      node_id_set_vs_input__frankenmermaid, edge_topology_vs_input__frankenmermaid'
  er_xl_2000          FAIL -- 'required source-grounded invariants undecidable:
                      node_id_set_vs_input__frankenmermaid'

Overall artifact verdict FAIL, run exits 7.

UNDECIDABLE IS NOT DIVERGENT. divergent=0 and unverified=1 in both cases. The validator did not find our output WRONG; it could not extract the node-id set (and for state, the edge topology) from our SVG in a form it could check against the source. So there are exactly two possibilities and this bead exists to decide which:
  (a) the validator's source-side extractor does not understand stateDiagram-v2 / erDiagram id syntax, in which case the oracle is blind for two whole families at every size, not just 2000 nodes; or
  (b) our state/ER SVG genuinely does not carry decodable node ids, in which case a11y/testability tooling cannot address those elements either, which would be a real output defect.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. These are two of the six families where mermaid-js cannot render at all, so they are exactly the rows where OUR output is the only output that exists. An unverifiable claim on those rows is the weakest possible position: nobody can check us, including us. The flowchart-family rows (wide, cyclic_scc, dense_dag) and class all decide cleanly, which is what makes (a) the more likely branch -- the extractor looks flowchart-shaped.

DO NOT CLOSE BY RELAXING THE VALIDATOR. Making 'undecidable' count as a pass would convert the strongest structural claim this project has into an unfalsifiable one. The fix is to make the invariant DECIDABLE for state and er -- teach the extractor those two syntaxes, or emit decodable ids -- and then re-run the same invocation and report the verdict either way.

CROSS-CHECK ALREADY AVAILABLE: crates/fm-cli/tests/xl_scale_classes_test.rs asserts at the crate level that all 2,002 state nodes and all 2,000 ER entities reach layout, that the last declared node survives, and that two independent runs agree byte for byte. That is real evidence our output is not truncated -- but it inspects the IR and layout, not the rendered SVG, so it cannot substitute for the source-grounded SVG invariant.
close_reason: State and ER source-grounded SVG invariants now decide and pass at XL scale; lifecycle pseudo transitions are retained and self-tested.

title: linkStyle interpolate clause was swallowed into the CSS declaration
description:
`linkStyle 0 interpolate basis stroke:#f00` has an OPTIONAL curve clause between the index list and
the CSS. We had no concept of it, so the whole tail became the style string and the link was handed
"interpolate basis stroke:#f00" as its declaration. That CORRUPTS a declaration that was otherwise
valid - the author's stroke colour silently stops working. Worse than dropping the clause.

Grammar shape probed against the pinned mermaid 11.15.0 bundle with
scripts/headtohead/parse_probe.mjs rather than guessed, because the details decide the parse:

    linkStyle 0 interpolate basis             PARSED
    linkStyle 0 interpolate basis stroke:#f00 PARSED
    linkStyle 0 stroke:#f00 interpolate basis ERROR    <- the clause must come FIRST
    linkStyle 0 INTERPOLATE basis             PARSED   <- keyword is case-insensitive
    linkStyle 0 interpolate                   ERROR    <- the curve name is required
    linkStyle 0 interpolate notacurve         PARSED   <- the curve name is NOT validated

FIXED: the clause is parsed off the front of the style position and REPORTED. The remaining CSS is
now clean. Detection is word-anchored and uses str::get so it cannot panic on a multibyte boundary.

DELIBERATELY NOT STORED. Nothing in the IR or either renderer can draw a curve family, and a field
no consumer reads is dead IR of exactly the kind docs/IR_FIELD_SWEEP.md exists to find. The warning
names the curve so the author knows it was seen and ignored. When an edge-curve consumer lands,
this is the site that supplies the value.

FOLLOW-UP (not filed as ready, needs a consumer first): implementing curve families means an
IrEdgeExtras field plus routing support in fm-layout and both renderers.

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Four tests added, none compiled. The load-bearing
one asserts the stored style EQUALS "stroke:#ff0000" - a contains() check would pass on the old
broken behaviour too.
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build
