title: DOT: node fillcolor/color and edge color become style refs, with graphviz's style=filled rule
description:
The next increment bd-9yjo named as "a small local change rather than new machinery", and it was: the
defaults machinery landed there took the colors without restructuring.

WHAT WAS MISSING. DOT color attributes were parsed by nobody. `a [fillcolor=red]`, `a [color=blue]`
and `a -> b [color=red]` all rendered in default theme colors, so any .dot file that colors its graph
— a large share of real ones — lost that entirely. Now mapped onto IrStyleRef, the same structure
Mermaid's `style A fill:#f9f` produces, so the renderer needs no DOT-specific path:

  node fillcolor=X               -> fill:X          (IrStyleTarget::Node)
  node color=X                   -> stroke:X
  node style=filled, color=X     -> fill:X          <-- graphviz's rule, see below
  node style=filled + both       -> fill:<fillcolor>,stroke:<color>
  edge color=X                   -> stroke:X        (IrStyleTarget::Link(index))

THE NON-OBVIOUS RULE, which is why the three node attributes resolve together rather than
independently: in graphviz `color` is the BORDER and `fillcolor` the interior, but with `style=filled`
and NO `fillcolor`, the `color` value FILLS the shape instead of outlining it. `style=filled,
color=lightgrey` is one of the most common lines in real DOT, so reading it as a stroke would paint
borders where users expect fills across a large share of input. There is a test for both halves.

Defaults participate, and merge ATTRIBUTE BY ATTRIBUTE rather than all-or-nothing: with
`node [color=blue]` in force, a node naming only `fillcolor=red` gets `fill:red,stroke:blue`, not just
the fill. Scoping is inherited from bd-9yjo — a color default reverts at the closing brace of the
subgraph that declared it, with a test.

TWO TESTS EXIST ONLY TO STOP FALSE PASSES:
  - a plain node must produce NO style entry at all. An unconditional entry would make every
    assertion above vacuous and would emit dead CSS for every uncoloured node.
  - the end-to-end test asserts on the RENDERED SVG, because style refs are only worth emitting if
    the renderer honors them — otherwise the parser is producing work nothing consumes.

A NEEDLE MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING, caught by my own control. The end-to-end test first searched the
SVG for the bare colour names "red" and "blue". Both appear in the stylesheet unconditionally: "red"
inside `prefers-reduced-motion` and "blue" inside the `blueprint` theme name. The control (an
uncoloured graph must contain neither) failed and exposed that the positive assertions were equally
worthless. Needles are now the property:value pairs `fill:red` / `stroke:blue`. This is the second
time this session a bare-substring needle in an SVG proved meaningless — the first was
`stroke-dasharray`, which the theme CSS also mentions unconditionally.

TESTS: 7 new parser unit tests (fillcolor/color mapping, the style=filled rule both ways, no-style
control, attribute-by-attribute default merge, scope revert, edge colour on the right index by
index, edge default with per-edge override) plus 1 end-to-end SVG test with its control.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p fm-parser --lib -> 0 (480 passed); cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli -> 0;
cargo test -p fm-wasm -> 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -> 0. No golden
moved — that corpus is Mermaid, not DOT.

STILL NOT SUPPORTED: penwidth, fontname, fontsize, fontcolor, bgcolor, and cluster-level colors. Each
is now the same shape of small change as this one.
close_reason: Landed; unsupported attributes listed in the bead rather than implied

title: bd-2gr9: evidenced Swiss-Tables target = LayoutDependencyGraph BTreeMap probes (1.91% incremental), gated on an iteration-order audit
description:
bd-2gr9 asks for Swiss/Fx hash maps in the graph IR but names no measured target. This one is measured.

EVIDENCE (deterministic callgrind, single_node_label_edit/incremental/1000, ELF 6cd47a15a0cb01f7bdb422e91792f292fa838b7b1b4746035d8da6a9d1b663b7):
  LayoutDependencyGraph::from_ir  1.91% self, attributed to
  library/alloc/src/collections/btree/search.rs
i.e. the cost is B-tree DESCENTS, not the work from_ir does. Also visible in the same profile:
  BTreeMap<SubgraphRegionId,_>::IntoIter::dying_next  0.77%

SURFACE (crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs:222):
  regions: BTreeMap<SubgraphRegionId, SubgraphRegion>
  index:   BTreeMap<RegionInput, BTreeSet<SubgraphRegionId>>
plus BTreeMap/BTreeSet locals inside from_ir (explicit_region_ids, covered_nodes).

⚠️ HARD PRECONDITION — DO NOT SKIP. This repo mandates deterministic layout, and BTreeMap iterates in key order while FxHashMap does not. The one landed precedent (72ffc1f, node_size_cache BTreeMap -> FxHashMap) was safe for a specific stated reason: that map is lookup-only and carries an in-code comment saying so ('never iterated for output', lib.rs ~1086). These maps are NOT obviously in that class — dirty-region propagation reads them, and if region iteration order reaches node ordering or edge routing, a hash map silently makes layout nondeterministic. That is a correctness regression that goldens may not even catch reliably, since a hash map can happen to iterate stably within one run.

REQUIRED ORDER OF WORK:
1. AUDIT every read of regions/index and prove whether iteration order can reach output. Write the answer down. If any path can, either keep the BTreeMap or sort at the boundary and re-measure with the sort included (a sort may eat the entire 1.91%).
2. Only then swap, and only the maps the audit cleared.
3. Determinism probe as a NEGATIVE CONTROL: layout the same input N times in one process and assert byte-identical output. Run it against the PRE-change binary too — if it passes there and after, it proves nothing unless it can fail; construct it so a deliberately nondeterministic iteration order makes it red.
4. Instruction-gate the result. The substrate is in place: callgrind (perf is dead here, perf_event_paranoid=4), A/A null came out EXACTLY 1.000000 on this bench, and incremental_layout now self-reports its ELF as of 5b0ff735 so a KEEP row is finally writable.

CEILING: 1.91% + 0.77%. Do not expect more, and do not widen the swap beyond what the audit clears to chase a bigger number. Related: [[project_layout_stable_priorities_hoist_and_mimalloc_profile]] PROBE TAXONOMY — the cheapest outcome is often DELETING a probe rather than making it faster, so check first whether these lookups are needed at all.
close_reason:
AUDIT DONE (step 1 of this bead's required order) — and it REFUTES the swap. No code changed; the deliverable is the finding.

VERDICT PER MAP:

1. LayoutDependencyGraph.regions (BTreeMap<SubgraphRegionId, SubgraphRegion>) — ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING. NOT swappable.
   Of all .regions() callers, only two ITERATE (lib.rs:3368 and :3484) and both are order-INSENSITIVE — they insert into a BTreeSet and sum a count, so the result is identical under any order. That part looked safe. The blocker is elsewhere: the test at lib.rs:15716, layout_dependency_graph_prefers_explicit_subgraphs_then_connectivity_fragments, iterates .regions().values() and asserts an EXACT ORDERED sequence. Its name states that the order IS the property. SubgraphRegionId is assigned in construction order (explicit subgraphs first, then connectivity fragments), so the BTreeMap's key ordering is the mechanism that encodes it. FxHashMap would destroy it, and rewriting that assertion to accept the new order would be gate self-weakening on a named behavioural property. Nearby lib.rs:15755 layout_dependency_graph_build_is_deterministic_for_identical_ir guards the same area.
   A hash map here would require a parallel Vec<SubgraphRegionId> to carry enumeration order — real complexity for the ceiling below.

2. LayoutDependencyGraph.index (BTreeMap<RegionInput, BTreeSet<SubgraphRegionId>>) — SWAPPABLE. Sole use is .get(&edit.input()).cloned() at lib.rs:409; its BTreeSet value is extended into a DirtySet, which is order-insensitive. Never iterated.

3. explicit_region_ids (local in from_ir) — SWAPPABLE. Only .insert() and .get(&parent.0).copied(). Never iterated. Same class as the 72ffc1f node_size_cache precedent.

4. covered_nodes / recursive_members / node_indexes (BTreeSets) — NOT swappable. node_indexes is iterated into ordered Vecs that feed layout_bounds_for_members and thus geometry.

5. DirtySet.regions is a BTreeSet and MUST stay one: it is iterated at lib.rs:415, 1540, 3388, 3506 and 3624, and those iterations reach node geometry and the reported dirty-region rectangles. It was never the target but is easy to hit by accident while editing this area.

CEILING AFTER THE AUDIT: the swappable set is items 2 and 3 only. The measured 1.91% is LayoutDependencyGraph::from_ir self time attributed to btree/search.rs, and the bulk of that is the BTreeSet work in items 4 plus the regions map in item 1 — none of which may move. Items 2 and 3 are a handful of probes per subgraph. Expected well under 1%, i.e. a predicted wash, which is why no swap was implemented rather than implementing one and measuring a wash.

Both key types already derive Hash, so the mechanical blocker is absent — the blocker is semantic.

RETRY PREDICATE: implement items 2 and 3 only if a profile attributes >=1% specifically to those two probe sites (not to from_ir as a whole), and gate it on instructions with the callgrind substrate (A/A null was EXACTLY 1.000000 on this bench; incremental_layout self-reports its ELF as of 5b0ff735, so a KEEP row is now writable). Do NOT touch item 1 without first replacing the ordering contract with an explicit ordered structure AND keeping the lib.rs:15716 assertion exactly as written.

title: LEVER (surface): spatial index for edge-routing obstacles — O(E*V) -> O(E*k), ~60% of large-flowchart layout
description: Profiled large-flowchart layout (frankenmermaid-cc): large_500 uses Tree algo (guardrail fallback). TREE_TIMING breakdown (us): sizes=107, tree_struct=79, spans+centers=28, boxes=91, EDGE_PATHS=476 (~60%), post=19. Edge routing dominates. Root cause: route_edge_points_with_obstacles (lib.rs:11208) calls cga_routing::find_horizontal/vertical_segment_nudge (cga_routing.rs:155/90) ~1-2x per edge, each scanning ALL ~V node-obstacles (my AABB prefilter rejects cheaply but still VISITS all V). So O(E*V) ~ 375k visits for 500 edges. LEVER: spatial index (grid / Y-band bucket) so each segment queries only nearby obstacles -> O(E*k). CONSTRAINTS for output-identity: (1) find_*_segment_nudge returns the FIRST intersecting obstacle in slice order (cga_routing.rs:205) -> the index must return candidates and pick MIN original index; (2) build_edge_paths_with_orientation parks source/target via FAR_AWAY sentinel per edge (obstacle_bounds mutated) -> the index stores indices and the nudge must read current (parked) obstacle_bounds[i], so parked endpoints AABB-reject correctly. Conservative-superset query = output-identical (verify 426 fm-layout tests + snapshots). REJECTED this turn: per-edge bbox pre-filter (nudge called only ~1-2x/edge, so filtering O(V) once doesn't beat 1-2 scans); singleton-rank skip (~0, wrong path). compute_node_sizes Cow (avoid 500 label clones) is micro (~3% of tree). title: gitGraph: branch X does not switch to X, so later commits land in the wrong lane
description:
MEASURED against the pinned incumbent bundle (~/.cache/fm-headtohead/mermaid-11.15.0.min.js), the same one the head-to-head harness uses.

mermaid's createBranch (the function labelled "branch") ends with:
  records.branches.set(name, head?.id ?? null)
  records.branchConfig.set(name, {name, order})
  qEe(name)
and qEe is mermaid's checkout: it begins by sanitizing the name and then does records.currBranch = e. So in mermaid, "branch dev" CREATES AND SWITCHES TO dev.

Our parse_git_branch (crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs:8418) interns the branch and inherits the head, but never assigns state.current_branch. Only parse_git_checkout does that. So after a bare "branch dev", every following commit is still recorded on main.

OBSERVED: parsing
  gitGraph / commit id: "Alpha" / branch dev / commit id: "Beta" tag: "v1"
yields IrGitGraphMeta { branches: ["main", "dev"], commit_lanes: {0: 0, 1: 0} } - BOTH commits on lane 0. mermaid would put Beta on dev. The commit is drawn in the wrong branch column, which is the one thing a gitGraph exists to communicate.

comments.text:
FIXED. parse_git_branch now sets state.current_branch, matching mermaid's create-and-checkout.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, not assumed: with the one-line fix spliced out, gitgraph_branch_switches_to_the_new_branch_without_an_explicit_checkout fails with lanes {0: 0, 1: 0} - both commits on lane 0, the exact defect. Re-armed and verified afterwards: the assignment is back, no control marker survived, and the file has exactly 2 occurrences of it (branch + checkout).

The anchor for that splice mattered. The bare line `state.current_branch = normalized;` appears TWICE in the file - once in parse_git_branch and once in parse_git_checkout - so an unanchored replace would have silently disarmed CHECKOUT instead and produced a green run that proved nothing. I anchored on the unique trailing comment and asserted count == 1 before splicing.

TESTS: the defect case writes NO checkout line, which is the whole point - the pre-existing lane test writes an explicit `checkout dev`, and that is precisely what masked this for so long. Two controls: `checkout main` after a bare `branch dev` must still pull commits back (the fix mutates the state checkout owns, so making it stick would trade this defect for its mirror image), and the new branch must still inherit the current head as its parent (the fix appends to a function whose set_head inheritance must survive, or a branch's first commit would silently disconnect the graph).

NO GOLDEN MOVED, as predicted - gitgraph_basic.mmd writes the explicit checkout, so its output is unchanged. fm-parser 556 passed, and fm-render-svg / fm-layout / cli / fm-render-term all unchanged.

The SVG text-parity gate's gitgraph case now drops its explicit `checkout dev`, so it covers both this and bd-jgco at once: `dev` appears only if the branch got a lane band AND the commit after the bare branch landed on that lane.

NOT ADDRESSED, out of scope: mermaid THROWS on `branch X` when X already exists ("Trying to create a branch which already exists"). We silently re-intern and switch. That is a divergence, but a permissive one, and worth its own bead rather than a silent behaviour change here.

# XyChart Full Implementation

\`\`\`
xychart-beta
  title "Sales Revenue"

  y-axis "Revenue (in $)" 4000 --> 11000

- Multiple series types: bar, line (on same chart)
- Chart title
- Auto-scaling to data range
- Grid lines

3. **Parser**: Ensure y-axis range parsing works (min --> max syntax). Parse title.
4. **Tests**: Bar chart, line chart, mixed bar+line, custom y-axis range, multiple x-axis labels.

## This moves XyChart from UNSUPPORTED to IMPLEMENTED.

title: Tighten layout_svg_capacity_hint (over-reserves 1.33-2.08x); the large-diagram 'double-copy' is only ~3.4% of render
description:
PARKED, ANALYSIS-ONLY. Full write-up: tests/artifacts/perf/PARKED_large_render_capacity_and_double_copy.md

FINDING (corrects the 2026-07-04 DIG frontier map). No pinned corpus item reaches the large slow path: the streaming gate is 'edges < 4096 && nodes < 2048' (lib.rs:2892) and the corpus tops out at 512 nodes. Generated wide_40x80 (3200 nodes / 6201 edges / 3,475,207 B output) and profiled it.

memmove+memcpy is 2.54% of the whole pipeline (<=11.7% of render, consistent with cod_fm's 14.82% on the render-only bench). But the folded call-chains show it is NOT mostly the double copy:
  0.72%  unresolved kernel chain -- page-fault/zeroing of the multi-MB output buffer
  0.72%  __memcpy_avx (inlined, unattributed)
  0.37%  write_common_node_fragment_into::<true> -> String::write_fmt   (streaming buffer GROWTH, not a copy)
  0.37%  alloc::str::join_generic_copy                                   (copy 1: chunks -> node_svg/edge_svg)
  0.36%  Element::write_to_string -> push_str                            (copy 2: raw_svg_parts -> final String)

=> the identifiable double-copy is ~0.73% of pipeline ~= 3.4% of render.

NO-SHIP the rope/arena output contract (the escape hatch named in render_large_raw_part_body_fusion_NEGATIVE.md). It is a PUBLIC API change to render_svg_with_layout's return type and buys at most ~3.4% of render. This also explains all three prior rejections at once (large to_string_with_body 2026-07-05; raw-part body fusion +22.65% regression; empty between-child guards flat) -- each attacked a ~0.4% frame.

WHAT THE PROFILE DOES SUPPORT: finish_layout_svg_document presizes via layout_svg_capacity_hint = 16 KiB + 768*nodes + 384*edges + 512*clusters + 192*aux (lib.rs:3187/3202). It never under-reserves; it OVER-reserves 1.33-2.08x on every measured item:
  small_10 2.08x | medium_100 1.81x | large_500 1.72x | wide_8x16 1.49x | wide_16x32 1.46x | dense_dag_200 1.33x | wide_40x80 1.40x (4,855,168 B hint vs 3,475,207 B actual = 1.38 MB of surplus pages the kernel maps+zeroes -- exactly the 0.72% kernel chain).

LEVER: tighten NODE_BYTES(768)/EDGE_BYTES(384). Byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION (only affects String::with_capacity). DO NOT move the constants on this table alone: a hint that is too SMALL costs a realloc + full-buffer memmove, strictly worse than over-reserving, and the corpus generators emit short labels. Measure against a label-heavy corpus first. Also unknown: whether mimalloc actually faults in the surplus.

BLOCKER (why parked): no valid A/B substrate today.
 * local cargo bench prohibited (disk at 96%);
 * rch exec CANNOT carry a split A/B -- it exposes no worker-pinning flag and picks workers non-deterministically (confirmed: RCH_WORKER=hz1 was silently ignored, both arms ran on hz2). See the CORRECTION entry in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.
 * the prescribed one-binary/one-invocation alternating criterion substrate is not expressible: layout_svg_capacity_hint is private and capacity is not a parameter of any public entry point.

UNPARK BY: (1) thread the hint through a bench-only parameter on render_svg_with_layout and register hint_current vs hint_tight as two arms of ONE criterion group in crates/fm-cli/benches/pipeline_bench.rs, run in a single rch exec invocation; or (2) wait for the disk constraint to lift and use the machine-local 'perf stat -e instructions:u' two-point A/B with a code-layout control (the substrate that carried bd-w5sn; it resolved a 0.03% effect and is immune to both the worker-selection problem and the +/-5% code-layout roulette). Option 2 preferred.

FILE-OWNERSHIP: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs (capacity hint region ~3187-3230).
close_reason:
REJECTED on measurement (cc_fm, 2026-07-10). The premise was wrong and it was MY premise: I claimed the 1.38 MB of over-reserved capacity was 'surplus pages the kernel maps and zeroes -- precisely the 0.72% kernel chain'. That was inference, never measured.

MEASURED (wide_40x80, 3200 nodes / 6201 edges / 3,475,207 B output, perf stat two-point delta reps 36-6, 60 renders per delta, FM_H2H_FORCE_PROFILE=default):
  page-faults  delta 886  -> 14.8 per render
  minor-faults delta 917  -> 15.3 per render
Against: bytes written 3,475,207 = 848 pages; hint reservation 4,855,168 = 1,185 pages; surplus = 336 pages.
14.8 faults/render -- NOT 848, NOT 1,185.

MECHANISM: String::with_capacity(n) calls malloc(n) and does NOT touch the memory; pages fault lazily on first WRITE, so the 336-page surplus is never touched. And mimalloc RECYCLES the 3.47 MB buffer between renders rather than munmap/refault, so even the written pages fault once and the two-point delta cancels them. The over-reservation is FREE.

Tightening NODE_BYTES/EDGE_BYTES therefore saves nothing on the upside and risks a realloc + whole-buffer memmove on the downside. An under-reserving hint is strictly worse than an over-reserving one. DO NOT RETRY unless a profile shows non-zero per-render fault cost attributable to the output buffer.

SELF-TIME RECORDED. memmove+memcpy = 2.54% of sampled pipeline, dominant chain String::write_fmt / push_str -> copy_nonoverlapping = BUFFER APPEND (the unavoidable act of writing bytes), not a redundant copy. The identifiable double copy is join_generic_copy 0.37% + Element::write_to_string 0.36% = 0.73% of pipeline ~= 3.4% of render. Kernel frames total 18.27% and are NOT output-buffer faults; dwarf call-graph sampling overhead is the plausible bulk.

ALSO SETTLED: the three double-copy rejections PASS the ledger-integrity rule (unlike the 4/4 crossing-min failures). large_wide_stages/render/40x80 builds gen_wide(40,80) = 3200 nodes, and the streaming gate is nodes < 2048, so the large slow path DOES execute. The rejections are evidence about live code and they hold.

AND: the double-copy frame provably did not move. wide_40x80 default-profile pipeline instructions: 830d672 1.0000x -> bc56f72 0.9984x -> 0f9efd4 0.9984x. Both landings are structural no-ops on the large path. Lean profile: 0.7274x (-27.3%), the biggest measured effect of the edge-fragment lever anywhere.

Evidence: .benchmarks/render_capacity_preshaping_NEGATIVE.md

title: flowchart arrow LENGTH is unhandled: A ---> B parses as --- plus a mangled target
description:
FLOWCHART ARROW LENGTH IS UNHANDLED. `A ---> B` is valid mermaid (extra dashes are a rank-distance
hint, drawn as an ordinary arrow) and PARSES in the pinned bundle. We have no `--->` entry, no
length normalisation anywhere, and no test - greps for `--->` in the parser and in every test file
return nothing.

MECHANISM, read out of find_operator_core and FLOW_OPERATORS:

  find_operator returns the FIRST TABLE MATCH at each position - the table's own doc says "operator
  tables must put a token before every shorter prefix of that token, so the first match is also the
  longest match". For `A ---> B` at the first `-`: `-.->` no, `<-.->` no, `-.-` no, `==>` no,
  `<==>` no, `-->` NO (its third byte is `>`, the input's is `-`), `<-->` no, then `---` MATCHES.

  So the operator is `---` (Line), the left endpoint is `A`, and the right endpoint is the token
  `> B`. The arrow is drawn as a plain line and the target endpoint is parsed from text beginning
  with a shape delimiter.

SAME SHAPE FOR THE THICK LINE: `===` is absent too, so `A === B` matches `==` and leaves `= B`.

NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY, and this is the whole reason it is a bead rather than a commit.
FLOW_OPERATORS is the hottest operator scan in the parser and this repo has landed MEASURED levers
on exactly that scan (the first-byte gate exists because re-deriving it per line was the dominant
cost). Both candidate fixes have a cost that must be measured, and the disk throttle forbids builds:

  A. EXTEND THE TABLE with the longer runs (`--->`, `---->`, `===`, `====`, `-..->`, ...), sorted
     longest-first so the existing first-match-is-longest-match property still holds. Correct and
     mechanical - a generated table, no typo risk - but it grows a per-line scan from 14 entries to
     ~30-55, and the run lengths are unbounded in the grammar so any table is a bound.

  B. EXTEND THE MATCH instead of the table: after find_operator returns, walk the dash/equals/dot
     run at that index and re-classify from the terminator (`>`/`o`/`x`/none). O(1) per matched
     edge, no table growth, unbounded - but it is a rewrite of the matcher's contract for one
     diagram type, and writing that blind is how the last batch of unbuilt work produced inert code.

RECOMMEND B, measured, with an A/A null on the parse benchmark. Sorting the table longest-first is
worth doing in either case: it is behaviour-preserving (equal-length operators cannot both match a

comments.text:
GRAMMAR EVIDENCE, and it RULES OUT option A. mermaid 11.15.0 lexes a flowchart link as:

    /^(?:\s*[xo<]?--+[-xo>]\s*)/

`--+` is TWO OR MORE dashes, so arrow length is UNBOUNDED in the grammar - optional leading x/o/< head, a run of 2+ dashes, then one terminator from [-xo>]. The same file also carries a quadrant variant, / *--+> */i.

That kills the table-extension option outright, not just on cost. I had been weighing adding ---> / ----> / ===> and so on, bounded at four or five characters, and treating the per-line scan cost as the only objection. It is not the main one: ANY fixed table is a bound the grammar does not have, so a diagram with six dashes would still mangle its target while looking like a supported case. Knowingly-partial correctness is worse here than the current honest breakage, because the failure is silent either way.

So option B is the only correct fix: match the RUN, not a literal. Given the regex above the shape is now precise - at a candidate position, take the optional [xo<] head, count the dash run (>= 2), then classify from the single terminator char in [-xo>]. That is O(1) per matched edge and needs no table growth.

⚠️ IT STILL NEEDS A BUILD, for a reason beyond benchmarking: parse_edge_statement_asts is SHARED - flowchart and state pass FLOW_OPERATORS, class passes CLASS_OPERATORS - so a run-aware matcher must be gated to the flow table or it will change class parsing, where `..` and `--` mean different things. Getting that gate wrong is exactly the kind of silent cross-diagram breakage that only a test run catches.

Filed evidence only; no code, because a fixed-length table would be a knowingly wrong answer and the correct one cannot be verified under the current throttle.

title: Quotient Filters for Fast Duplicate Edge Detection
description:
## Quotient Filters for Fast Duplicate Edge Detection

Use quotient filters (a cache-friendly alternative to Bloom filters) to detect duplicate edges during graph construction, enabling O(1) amortized duplicate detection with minimal memory overhead.

## Mathematical Foundation
A quotient filter stores a set of fingerprints compactly using quotienting: for hash h(x), split into quotient q and remainder r where h(x) = q * 2^r_bits + r. Store remainder r in slot q of a compact array, using linear probing for collisions. Properties:
- Space: ~10-25% less than Bloom filters at the same false positive rate
- Cache behavior: elements stored in contiguous sorted runs → excellent locality
- False positive rate: 2^{-r_bits} (configurable via remainder size)
- No false negatives: if element was inserted, it will be found

**For duplicate edge detection:**
When parsing a Mermaid diagram, each edge (u, v) must be checked for duplicates. For n edges:
- Naive HashSet: O(n) space, O(1) per lookup, but HashSet overhead per entry
- Quotient filter: O(n * r_bits / 8) bytes, O(1) per lookup, much lower constant factor
- For r_bits = 16: false positive rate = 1/65536, space = 2 bytes per edge
- For 10000 edges: quotient filter = ~20KB vs HashSet = ~400KB (20x savings)

**Practical consideration:** The space savings are significant for WASM target where memory is constrained. For native target, the HashSet overhead is negligible. This is primarily a WASM optimization.

## Key Papers
- Bender et al., "Don't Thrash: How to Cache Your Hash on Flash" (VLDB 2012) — quotient filter
- Pandey et al., "A General-Purpose Counting Filter" (SIGMOD 2017) — counting quotient filter
- Fan et al., "Cuckoo Filter: Practically Better Than Bloom" (CoNEXT 2014) — alternative approach

## Implementation in FrankenMermaid
1. Implement `QuotientFilter<H>` generic over hash function.
2. Use FxHash for fingerprint computation (fast, non-cryptographic).
3. Implement `insert(edge_hash)` and `may_contain(edge_hash)` operations.
4. On `may_contain() == true`: verify with exact edge comparison (handle false positives).
5. Replace `HashSet<(NodeId, NodeId)>` in parser with `QuotientFilter` for WASM target.
6. Keep `HashSet` for native target (simpler, negligible space overhead).
7. Benchmark: memory usage and parse time for 1000, 10000, 100000 edge graphs on WASM.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] QuotientFilter implementation with configurable false positive rate
- [ ] Duplicate edge detection correct (no false negatives, false positives handled)
- [ ] Memory reduction >= 10x vs HashSet for 10000-edge graphs
- [ ] Parse time comparable to HashSet (within 10%)
- [ ] WASM-specific optimization (cfg-gated)
- [ ] Property test: no false negatives over 100000 random edge sets
- [ ] Decision contract: adopt for WASM if memory reduction > 5x
close_reason: Implemented QuotientFilter in fm-core/src/quotient_filter.rs with: configurable q/r bit widths, FxHash-based fingerprinting, linear probing with sorted runs, insert/may_contain O(1) amortized operations, with_capacity auto-sizing (75% load target), memory/FP rate introspection. 14 unit tests all passing: basic operations, duplicates, edge tuples, stress testing (1000 elements, zero false negatives), empirical FP rate verification, memory comparison vs HashSet. All quality gates pass (check, clippy, fmt).

title: Implement class relationship cardinality and namespace grouping
description:
# Class Cardinality and Namespace Grouping

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
classDiagram
  namespace Animals {
    class Dog
    class Cat
  }
  Dog "1" --> "*" Cat : chases
  Vehicle "1" *-- "0..*" Wheel
\`\`\`
- Cardinality labels: "1", "*", "0..1", "1..*", "0..*" on relationship ends
- Namespace blocks group classes visually (like packages in UML)
- Relationship types: inheritance (<|--), composition (*--), aggregation (o--), association (-->), dependency (..>), realization (..|>)

## Current State
- Cardinality labels on relationships: NOT parsed
- Namespace blocks: NOT parsed
- All relationship arrow types ARE parsed

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Parse quoted cardinality labels before/after relationship arrows. Parse \`namespace Name { ... }\` blocks as clusters.
2. **IR**: Add source_cardinality/target_cardinality: Option<String> to IrEdge. Namespaces map to IrCluster.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Render cardinality labels near edge endpoints. Render namespaces as labeled boundary boxes.
4. **Tests**: Various cardinality labels, namespace grouping, nested namespaces.

title: Sugiyama edge anchors use box side midpoints, which fall outside triangle/trapezoid/parallelogram outlines
description:
Same defect CLASS as bd-kaxw (closed, fixed) but on the MAIN Sugiyama path, so the blast radius and the golden cost are much larger. Filed with evidence rather than fixed, because the fix moves emitted geometry for every diagram using these shapes and that is a GOLDEN-CHANGE decision, not a drive-by.

MECHANISM. edge_anchors (crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs:13896) attaches every edge at a BOX SIDE MIDPOINT: for horizontal ranks, (bounds.x + width, centre.y) on the source and (bounds.x, centre.y) on the target; vertical ranks use the top/bottom midpoints. That is exactly right for shapes inscribed touching their box at side midpoints — Rect, Rounded, Circle, Diamond — which is why this went unnoticed and why the Sugiyama path was correctly ruled OUT of bd-kaxw.

It is wrong for shapes that do not. VERIFIED against the renderer's own path, crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:9008: a Triangle is drawn apex-top at (cx, y) with base corners (x, y+h) and (x+w, y+h). At the vertical midpoint y + h/2 the triangle spans only x + w/4 .. x + 3w/4, so the left and right side midpoints that edge_anchors uses sit w/4 — a full 25% of the node width — OUTSIDE the drawn shape. In an LR or RL flowchart the arrowhead floats in empty space beside the triangle.

DIRECTION-DEPENDENT, which is worth knowing before anyone 'fixes' it globally: for a Triangle, TD/BT is already CORRECT because the apex is at top-centre and the base is flat, so the top and bottom midpoints do lie on the outline. Only the horizontal anchors are wrong. A shape-aware anchor must therefore be computed per side, not per shape.

LIKELY ALSO AFFECTED, not individually verified — check each against its renderer path before acting: Trapezoid, InvTrapezoid, Parallelogram, InvParallelogram, Pentagon, Star, Cloud, Tag, Hexagon. Hexagon and Stadium may be fine or nearly so depending on how far their outline is inset at the midpoint; do not assume.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST COSMETIC: cross-engine output equivalence is part of the ratio in this repo, and mermaid-js terminates edges on the drawn outline. An edge that visibly misses its node is a fidelity loss, and per AGENTS.md a renderer that mislays an edge is not faster, it is wrong.

REQUIRED APPROACH:
1. Decide the contract first: does an anchor sit on the OUTLINE, or on the box with the renderer responsible for hiding the gap? bd-kaxw chose the outline for the force path; the two paths should agree.
2. Per-side, per-shape anchor geometry — not a single 'shape radius'. Reuse the approach from clip_to_shape_border (lib.rs, added in cf2dd848): exact analytic outlines for shapes where the box is clearly wrong, box fallback otherwise, so shapes nobody has reported wrong do not move.
3. Expect goldens to move. Every changed golden needs a semantic diff explaining which edge endpoint moved, by how much, and why the new position is the more correct one — never a bulk refresh.
4. Test the HELPER with a guaranteed diagonal/side-on approach, not an end-to-end layout. bd-kaxw's first test passed while exercising nothing because two force nodes settle axis-aligned; a layout-level test of a geometry bug can silently avoid the geometry.
5. Negative controls: Rect must still anchor at the box, and Circle/Diamond must be UNCHANGED by this work, since they are already correct — that is what proves the change is targeted rather than a global shift.
close_reason:
Fixed in c84da534.

DEFECT: edge_anchors attached every edge at a bounding-box side midpoint. Correct for Rect/Rounded/Circle/Diamond/Hexagon/Stadium, which touch their box there — that is why the Sugiyama path was correctly ruled OUT of bd-kaxw — but wrong for shapes whose sides slant away from the box between the horizontal edges.

VERIFIED against the renderers' own paths rather than assumed:
  Triangle (fm-render-svg lib.rs:9008): apex (cx, y) over a full-width base, so at mid-height it spans only x+w/4..x+3w/4. The side anchor floated a QUARTER of the node width outside the drawn shape in LR/RL.
  Trapezoid / InvTrapezoid / Parallelogram / InvParallelogram: slant by SLANTED_SHAPE_INSET_RATIO (0.15w) across full height, so half is gone by mid-height => 7.5% of width.

PER-DIRECTION, as the bead required: vertical anchors are untouched and were already correct (a triangle's apex is at top-centre, its base spans the full width). The inset is reported for the horizontal direction only.

CONTRACT (bead step 1): anchors sit on the OUTLINE, matching the choice bd-kaxw made for the force path. The two paths now agree.

PLACEMENT: the ratio is a method on NodeShape in fm-core, beside the shape it describes and beside the slant constant, so layout agrees with what is drawn. NOTE FOR FOLLOW-UP: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs still hardcodes 0.15 at BOTH of its draw sites (~7559 and ~8960); they should adopt fm_core::SLANTED_SHAPE_INSET_RATIO so the constant cannot drift between drawing and anchoring. Not done here to keep this change to one concern.

SHAPES DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE: Hexagon, Stadium, Asymmetric, Pentagon, Star, Cloud, Tag. They are either correct or unverified, and Hexagon/Stadium/Asymmetric are the ones the golden corpus actually exercises. Guessing at them would move goldens to fix shapes nobody has reported wrong. The bead's 'likely also affected' list is therefore only partly consumed — Pentagon/Star/Cloud/Tag remain unverified and unfixed.

NO GOLDEN MOVES: no golden uses any shape in the table (all_node_shapes.mmd covers rect/round/stadium/subroutine/diamond/hexagon/circle/asymmetric), and every shape outside it gets ratio 0.0, where x + w - 0.0 and x + 0.0 are exact float identities.

title: Class stereotype written inside the braces is interned as a member named <<interface>> and never sets IrClassNodeMeta.stereotype
description:
MEASURED at the IR level. fm-core has ClassStereotype (Interface/Abstract/Enum/Service/Custom) and IrClassNodeMeta.stereotype; the parser never populated it for the spelling mermaid's own documentation uses.

  class Shape {
      <<interface>>
      +area() float
  }

  BEFORE  stereotype=None  attributes=["<<interface>>"]  methods=["area()"]
  AFTER   stereotype=Some(Interface)  attributes=[]  methods=["area()"]

So the class box grew a MEMBER ROW reading the raw annotation, where mermaid renders the stereotype centred under the class name. Same for <<abstract>>, <<enumeration>> and any custom word.

MECHANISM: the statement-level branch handles '<<interface>> ClassName' and requires a non-empty name AFTER the closing angles. A bare annotation line has nothing after it, so class_name is empty, the branch falls through, and the line reaches parse_class_member, which happily makes an attribute out of it.

FIX: recognise an annotation-only line while a class block is open and resolve it through the same current_class_node_id the members already use, rather than re-looking-up a name that was never written. The annotation word mapping is now SHARED with the named form so the two spellings cannot drift apart on which words they recognise.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the interception disabled the test fails with 'the annotation did not reach the stereotype'.
CONTROLS THAT MUST NOT FIRE: a class with no annotation gains none; the real member survives (a guard that ate the whole line would pass the absence assertion alone); the named form is unchanged.

⚠️ MY FIRST CONTROL FOR THE NAMED FORM WAS WRONG AND FAILED. I wrote '<<interface>> Shape' BEFORE 'class Shape'. In that order the class node does not exist yet, set_class_stereotype cannot resolve the name and returns silently. mermaid's documented order declares the class first. The control now uses that order. Worth knowing: an annotation naming a class that has not been declared yet is silently discarded.

title: Implement markdown labels in node text (backtick syntax)
description:
# Markdown Labels in Nodes

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
flowchart LR
  A["\`**Bold** and *italic* text\`"]
  B["\`Multi
  line text\`"]
\`\`\`
Backtick-quoted labels support basic markdown: bold, italic, strikethrough, code, and line breaks.

## Current State
- Parser handles quoted labels (single/double quotes)
- Backtick markdown syntax is NOT parsed — backticks are treated as part of the label text
- SVG renderer does not render any markdown formatting in labels

1. **Parser**: Detect backtick-enclosed labels. Strip backticks and parse inline markdown to a simple AST (bold, italic, code spans, line breaks).

3. **SVG Renderer**: Render segments as <tspan> elements with appropriate font-weight/font-style attributes. Line breaks become separate <text> or <tspan dy=...> elements.
4. **Tests**: Bold, italic, code, mixed, multi-line.

title: CI quality gates cannot run: 17 sites use 'cargo -p fm-cli', which is a BINARY name, not the package
description:
FALSE-GREEN GATE FAMILY, and it disables five gates that are all switched ON.

MEASURED. The package in crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml is named frankenmermaid-cli. 'fm-cli' is one of its three BINARY targets, not a package. So every CI invocation spelled 'cargo ... -p fm-cli' fails before it does any work:

  $ cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_svg_test --no-run
  error: package ID specification `fm-cli` did not match any packages

There are 17 such sites in .github/workflows/ci.yml, plus the same mistake inside .ci/quality-gates.toml which supplies commands to the workflow:

  ci.yml:234  cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_svg_test              (golden-checksum-guard)
  ci.yml:237  cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_layout_test           (golden-checksum-guard)
  ci.yml:307  cargo test -p fm-cli --test integration_test e2e_pipeline_determinism_all_types
  ci.yml:333  cargo run  -p fm-cli -- determinism-manifest
  ci.yml:362  cargo build -p fm-cli --target wasm32-wasip1
  ci.yml:183/186  cargo check/test -p fm-cli --features png            (png-smoke)
  ci.yml:491,569,575,587,600,607,609,633,658,717  evidence-ledger-guard and friends
  quality-gates.toml:33  cargo test -p fm-cli --test invariant_proof_harness   (invariant_proof.command)
  quality-gates.toml:47  cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_layout_test layout_golden_cases_are_deterministic_across_runs  (determinism.command)
  quality-gates.toml:57  cargo test -p fm-cli --test invariant_proof_harness deg_   (degradation.command)

EVERY GATE IS ENABLED, so this is not dormant configuration. .ci/quality-gates.toml has enabled = true for golden_checksum, performance_regression, property_test, invariant_proof, evidence_ledger, determinism, decision_contract, degradation, release_gate_overrides, release_signoff, demo_evidence. The jobs exist with real bodies and real steps. They simply cannot execute the check they are named for.

THE TARGETS ALL EXIST AND ALL PASS, which is what makes this purely a spelling defect rather than missing work. With the package spelled correctly:
  cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test invariant_proof_harness --no-run   -> builds
  cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test integration_test e2e_pipeline_determinism_all_types -> 1 passed
crates/fm-cli/tests/ contains golden_svg_test.rs, golden_layout_test.rs, integration_test.rs and invariant_proof_harness.rs. Nothing is missing; the gates were pointing at a name that does not resolve.

SECOND, COUPLED DEFECT — correcting the package name alone is NOT sufficient. The package declares three binaries (frankenmermaid, fm-cli, evidence) and has NO default-run key, so the sites of the form 'cargo run -p <pkg> -- determinism-manifest' become ambiguous the moment the package resolves:

  $ cargo run -p frankenmermaid-cli -- --help
  error: `cargo run` could not determine which binary to run. Use the `--bin` option to specify a binary, or the `default-run` manifest key.
  available binaries: evidence, fm-cli, frankenmermaid

So the fix is two-part: correct the package spec everywhere, AND make the bare 'cargo run' sites unambiguous (add default-run = "fm-cli" to crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml, which is the mechanism cargo's own error recommends, or pass --bin explicitly at each site). Landing only the first half converts a resolve failure into an ambiguity failure.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR bd-17e4.5, which is what led me here: that bead asks for six CI gates and every one of them ALREADY EXISTS as a named job — golden-checksum-guard, performance-regression-guard, property-test-guard, evidence-ledger-guard, determinism-guard, decision-contract-guard, plus extras (invariant-proof-guard, degradation-guard, cross-platform-determinism-native/wasm/compare, release-gate-override-guard, demo-evidence-guard, quality-summary, ledger-integrity-guard). The bead is not unimplemented; its deliverable is implemented and BROKEN. It should be re-scoped to this defect rather than re-implemented.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Every 'cargo ... -p <spec>' in .github/workflows/ci.yml and .ci/quality-gates.toml names a package that 'cargo metadata' actually lists. Worth asserting mechanically, since this is the second time a gate has been trusted without being run (see the false-green note below).
2. Each corrected command RUNS — verified by executing it locally, not by reading it.
3. No 'cargo run -p ...' without an unambiguous binary.
4. The correction does not silently change which tests run: the referenced test names must match existing targets.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, for the record: a job that fails at 'package ID specification did not match any packages' fails fast and identically regardless of the code under test, so it produces the same red on every commit and stops carrying information. This is the same family as the documented `cargo check --all-targets` without --workspace incident, where main sat red for six hours under green claims. A gate that cannot fail differently is not a gate.

NOT INVESTIGATED, deliberately: whether CI has actually been red on these jobs, or whether something upstream marks them non-blocking. I have no CI run history here, only the workflow definition. Either answer makes the fix necessary; the difference only changes how long it has been broken.

ALSO NOTICED, not filed: crates/fm-cli declares two binaries (frankenmermaid, fm-cli) from the SAME src/main.rs, which cargo warns about on every single build ('file ... found to be present in multiple build targets'). Cosmetic, unrelated to this defect, and I have not established which of the two is intended to be canonical.
close_reason:
Fixed by b363bdba, all three parts together.

1. Package spec corrected at all 21 sites (17 in ci.yml, 4 in .ci/quality-gates.toml): -p fm-cli -> -p frankenmermaid-cli.
2. default-run = "frankenmermaid" added to crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml, because correcting the package alone converts the resolve failure into an AMBIGUITY failure at the bare 'cargo run -p ... -- determinism-manifest' sites (three binaries, no default). Points at the canonical binary, not the transitional fm-cli alias.
3. 'set -euo pipefail' added to the five gate steps that pipe into tee. This is the part that makes 1 and 2 into a gate rather than a decoration.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, which was acceptance criterion 2 — every command from the config run for real, exit codes captured with no pipe in the way:
  EXIT=0  invariant_proof.command                 12 passed
  EXIT=0  determinism.command                      1 passed
  EXIT=0  degradation.command                      3 passed
  EXIT=0  performance_regression cmd[0] fm-layout 11 passed
  EXIT=0  performance_regression cmd[1] perf_slo_  6 passed
  EXIT=0  ci.yml golden_svg_test                   8 passed
  EXIT=0  ci.yml golden_layout_test                2 passed
Every one previously exited non-zero on the package spec.

CONTROL for the pipefail half, measured not reasoned:
  bash -e            -c 'false | tee /dev/null'  -> EXIT=0  (masked)
  bash -e + pipefail -c 'false | tee /dev/null'  -> EXIT=1  (surfaced)
GitHub Actions' default shell is 'bash -e {0}', so -e alone could not have saved these steps.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1, the mechanical check, done and worth keeping: every 'cargo ... -p <spec>' in both files is cross-checked against cargo metadata's package names -> NONE unresolved. The probe asserts it found >= 5 packages BEFORE judging, because my first version silently received an empty package list and reported every spec as broken. A check that can degrade into a meaningless verdict is the same bug class as the one this bead fixes; I did not want to ship that shape while fixing this shape.

CRITERION 3: no 'cargo run -p ...' without an unambiguous binary — satisfied via default-run; 'cargo run -p frankenmermaid-cli -- determinism-manifest' now emits its JSON manifest instead of erroring.
CRITERION 4: the referenced test targets all exist (golden_svg_test.rs, golden_layout_test.rs, integration_test.rs, invariant_proof_harness.rs) and the corrected commands select real tests, as the pass counts above show. Nothing silently changed which tests run.

ONE PIPE DELIBERATELY LEFT: ci.yml:795 'find ... | sort | tail -n 1' inside a command substitution PICKS A FILENAME and judges nothing by exit status. Correct as written; recorded so a future sweep does not 'fix' it. It is the only status-masking-looking pipeline left in the file and it is benign.

NOT VERIFIED EITHER WAY, and not claimed: 'cargo build -p frankenmermaid-cli --target wasm32-wasip1' (ci.yml:365). Its package now resolves, but it fails on THIS host with 'can t find crate for std ... the wasm32-wasip1 target may not be installed' — rustup here has wasm32-unknown-unknown but not wasip1, while CI installs it via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly with 'targets: wasm32-wasip1'. So the spelling is fixed and the build outcome is untested by me. Not filed as a defect, because I have no evidence it fails anywhere the target exists.

NOT INVESTIGATED, as stated in the filing: whether CI was actually red on these jobs or something upstream marked them non-blocking. No CI run history is available to me. Either answer made the fix necessary.

ALSO STILL TRUE, not actioned: crates/fm-cli declares two binaries (frankenmermaid, fm-cli) from the SAME src/main.rs, which cargo warns about on every build. The Cargo.toml comment calls fm-cli a backwards-compatibility alias 'during transition', and repo policy says we do not keep compatibility shims — so removing it is probably right, but it changes the shipped binary set and ci.yml:368 consumes target/wasm32-wasip1/debug/fm-cli.wasm by name. Out of scope here; needs its own bead if anyone wants it.

GATES: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast EXIT=0 with 40/40 suites green; ci.yml still parses as YAML with 22 jobs; no source file touched so no golden can move. Pushed to main and master at b363bdba.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SECOND MECHANISM FOUND, and it is why this went unnoticed. Folding it into this bead rather than filing separately because fixing either defect alone leaves the gates still not gating.

FIVE CI GATE STEPS PIPE THEIR GATE COMMAND INTO tee WITH NO pipefail IN SCOPE, so the step's exit status is tee's — effectively always 0 — and the harness's failure is discarded:

  ci.yml:274/279  'Run invariant proof harness'                 ... | tee artifacts/evidence/slo/invariant-proof.log
  ci.yml:521/526  'Run degradation SLO harness'                  ... | tee artifacts/evidence/slo/degradation.log
  ci.yml:565/570  'Capture SVG golden evidence log'              ... | tee artifacts/evidence/logs/svg-golden.log
  ci.yml:572/576  'Capture layout golden evidence log'           ... | tee artifacts/evidence/logs/layout-golden.log
  ci.yml:578/582  'Capture determinism evidence log'             ... | tee artifacts/evidence/logs/determinism.log

Determined mechanically, not by eye: for each '- name:' step I checked whether its run block contains 'pipefail' and whether it contains a pipe into tee/tail/head. These five have the pipe and not the guard. GitHub Actions' default shell is 'bash -e {0}', which does NOT enable pipefail, so -e cannot save them — the pipeline as a whole succeeded. Note ci.yml DOES use 'set -euo pipefail' in other steps (lines 134, 155), so the idiom is known in this file; these five just missed it.

ONE MORE PIPE, CHECKED AND BENIGN: ci.yml:788-789 use '| sort | tail -n 1' inside a command substitution to PICK A FILENAME. Judging nothing by its status, so it is correct as written. Recording it so a future sweep does not 'fix' it.

THE TWO DEFECTS COMPOUND, which is the actual story here. 'cargo test -p fm-cli ...' fails immediately with 'package ID specification fm-cli did not match any packages'; the tee then reports success. So these gates have been REPORTING GREEN WHILE EXECUTING NOTHING. That is strictly worse than a red gate: a red gate gets fixed. This is the same family as the documented 'cargo check --all-targets without --workspace' incident.

FIX MUST BE ALL THREE PARTS TOGETHER or the gate stays broken:
  1. package spec: -p fm-cli -> -p frankenmermaid-cli (17 sites in ci.yml, 3 command strings in .ci/quality-gates.toml)
  2. bare 'cargo run -p ... --' sites need an unambiguous binary (default-run = "fm-cli" in crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml)
  3. 'set -euo pipefail' in the five steps above, so a failing harness fails its step

Part 3 is the one that turns the other two into a gate rather than a decoration. Landing 1+2 without 3 would make the commands run but still swallow their verdict.

title: EPIC: Project Foundation & Workspace Setup
description:

title: block-beta columns N span is not encoded: a 3-column block renders narrower than a 1-column one
description:
Fourth instance of the proportionality class, after bd-e69x (sankey widths), bd-h9gx (gantt bars) and bd-51tz (packet-beta bit ranges). block-beta declares an explicit grid with "columns N" and a per-block span; neither reaches the picture.

MEASURED, controlled input so label length is the only variable:

    block-beta
      columns 3
      block:wide:3
        W["x"]
      end
      N["a single column with a very long label indeed"]
      space
      M["y"]

  W, inside a block declaring a 3-COLUMN span, short label  -> width 100.00
  N, a SINGLE column, long label                            -> width 367.35
  M, a single column, short label                           -> width 100.00

So the 3-column span is 3.7x NARROWER than a 1-column cell. Width tracks label text, not the declared grid, exactly as in bd-51tz.

CONFIRMED ON THE COMMITTED FIXTURE TOO (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/block_basic.mmd, which declares columns 3 with header:3 and footer:3 blocks): A "Header spans 3 columns" w=234.52, D "Footer spans 3 columns" w=231.23, B "Left" w=100, C "Right" w=105. The two 3-span blocks are only ~2.3x a 1-column cell, and their widths differ from each other by 3.29px -- tracking their label strings, which differ by one word, rather than both being exactly three columns.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so nobody re-does it: B and C correctly share a row (both y=282.50), so row grouping works. And the `space` keyword is correctly invisible -- it carries class fm-node-block-beta-space, which the theme CSS gives opacity 0 and pointer-events none.

SECOND DEFECT: `space` does not occupy its grid CELL. In the fixture it renders at y=559.50, on its own row below the footer, rather than as the empty middle cell of the B/space/C row. In the controlled input above it lands at y=369 while N and M share y=92. So it consumes a row instead of a cell, which also means it does not create the gap it exists to create.

THIRD OBSERVATION, not yet confirmed as a defect: in the controlled input the declaration order and the row order disagree -- block:wide:3 is declared FIRST but renders at y=230.50, below N and M at y=92. The committed fixture does NOT show this (its header block is first and topmost), so it may be an artifact of a single-child block or of clusters sorting after plain nodes. Worth checking while fixing, not filed separately because I could not reproduce it on the real fixture.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. A block declaring a span of N columns is about N times a single column wide, regardless of label length.
2. Renaming a block changes no geometry -- the same invariant bd-h9gx needed, and the sharpest test of this defect.
3. Single-column cells in one row sit at consistent column x positions across rows.
4. `space` occupies a cell in its row, leaving a gap, rather than consuming a row of its own.
5. GOLDEN IMPACT: block_basic.svg and its layout checksum will move. Needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note naming the new grid geometry.

GUARD ALREADY WRITTEN AND WAITING: block_beta_span_width_is_proportional_to_declared_columns in crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs, #[ignore]d with a pointer to this bead. It fails today with "a 3-column span (100) must be much wider than a 1-column cell (367.35), independent of labels". UN-IGNORING IT IS THIS BEAD ACCEPTANCE GATE.

LABEL OVERFLOW WILL FOLLOW, and it is already solved twice in this repo -- reuse rather than reinvent: once a cell width is grid-derived, a long label will not fit. bd-h9gx placed gantt task names through a LayoutExtensions entry decided in layout so bounds could grow, reproducing mermaid inside-if-fits / outside-otherwise; bd-tm5p instead widened the container. Pick deliberately and say which in the code.

NO CERTIFIED RATIO AT RISK: block-beta is not in the head-to-head corpus.
close_reason:
CLOSED on its named gate. Layout fixes landed 95b2b700 (container spans reach the geometry, space holds its declared cell, container children positioned from the region centre so every row starts at column 0); the gate itself was blocked by bd-ukj2, which landed c64efaf0.

block_beta_span_width_is_proportional_to_declared_columns is now un-#[ignore]d and PASSING, with both assertions unchanged — neither was relaxed to whatever the fix produced. Assertion 1: the 3-column container dominates a 1-column cell regardless of label length. Assertion 2: space holds its cell, so A and C stay a full column-pitch apart with the declared gap between them.

Also proven at the layout level, independent of the SVG reader: block_beta_container_span_reaches_the_geometry (runs BOTH documents with the long label moved between the container and the single column, requiring the container to measure the same number of columns in each) and block_beta_space_holds_its_declared_cell, both in crates/fm-cli/tests/integration_test.rs.

Measured on golden/block_basic: A and D both exactly 863.57 wide (were 234.52 and 231.23, each tracking its own label and differing by 3.29px); B x=20 / space x=334.52 / C x=649.05 all on one row (space was alone on a row at y=559.5).

CRITERION 2 RESTATED, deliberately and recorded in the test's doc: 'renaming changes NO geometry' cannot hold literally, because a block grid's column PITCH is the widest cell's width in mermaid too (setBlockSizes takes maxWidth over the children). What is asserted is that the ENCODING is label-independent. GOLDEN-CHANGE for the layout is in 95b2b700; the a11y-only delta is in c64efaf0. cargo test --workspace 0 failures; clippy -D warnings clean.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION — I FILED THIS TOO BROADLY and the title is wrong. Correcting before anyone acts on it, because as written it would send someone to rewrite a grid layout that works.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS, measured: block-beta HAS a dedicated Grid algorithm, it DOES read the declared column count (fm-layout lib.rs:7385 reads ir.meta.block_beta_columns), and NODE-LEVEL spans work correctly. Control:

    block-beta / columns 3 / A["a"]:3 / B["b"] / C["c"] / D["d"]
    A  x=92   w=460      <- three cells wide, correct
    B  x=92   w=100
    C  x=272  w=100
    D  x=452  w=100      <- consistent 180px column pitch

So "columns N span is not encoded" is FALSE as a general statement. The grid, the column count and node spans are all implemented.

DEFECT 1, the real one: a span declared on a CONTAINER block is dropped. The parser applies the span as a class on a NODE (mermaid_parser.rs:6938 adds block-beta-span-{n} when span_cols > 1, and fm-layout block_beta_node_span reads exactly that class). For the container form `block:name:N` the container becomes a group, and its span is never transferred to anything that has a width, so its contents get span 1:

    block-beta / columns 3 / block:wide:3 / W["x"] / end / N["<long label>"] / space / M["y"]
    W   w=100.00     <- inside a block declaring a 3-column span
    N   w=367.35     <- a SINGLE column, wider only because its label is longer

That is why the committed fixture is wrong: block_basic.mmd uses the container form (block:header:3, block:footer:3), so A comes out 234.52 and D 231.23 — label-derived, differing from each other by 3.29px, when both should be exactly three columns.

DEFECT 2, and my earlier description of this was also imprecise: `space` is not "consuming a row". It gets a cell, but it is ordered LAST instead of at its declared position, which shifts every subsequent cell one place earlier. Measured with node-level syntax so no container is involved:

    declared: A, space, C, D, E, F   with columns 3
    row 1 (y=92):     A x=92, C x=318.25, D x=544.50      <- space skipped, no gap between A and C
    row 2 (y=230.50): E x=92, F x=318.25, space x=521.38  <- space appears at the END

So the gap the author asked for does not appear where they asked for it, and a phantom gap appears at the end of the grid. The `space` node itself is correctly invisible (class block-beta-space, opacity 0).

CORRECTED TITLE would be something like "block-beta drops container-level spans and mis-orders `space`". I am not renaming the bead unilaterally since its title is quoted in the committed guard and in bd-iicc; whoever picks it up should retitle or split it.

THE GUARD IS STILL CORRECT AND STILL FAILS FOR THE RIGHT REASON: block_beta_span_width_is_proportional_to_declared_columns uses the CONTAINER form, so it tests defect 1. Its doc comment has been corrected in the same commit as this note, and a second assertion added covering defect 2 so both sub-defects are specified by the same ignored guard.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG, recorded because the reasoning error is reusable: I inferred "no grid layout algorithm exists" from the symptom, then checked the layout dispatch and found DiagramType::BlockBeta -> LayoutAlgorithm::Grid. The predictor I proposed on bd-iicc last round ("declares a coordinate system that no layout algorithm implements") is therefore also wrong — block-beta, kanban and packet-beta ALL have dedicated algorithms. The accurate version is narrower: a dedicated algorithm exists but does not consume one specific declared quantity. That is only findable by measuring, not by reading the dispatch table, which makes the next round no cheaper to target than this one was. I have corrected that on bd-iicc too.

title: Deeply nested mindmap input overflows the stack and aborts the process
description:
Found by cc lane (LilacPike) while establishing whether a failing test was pre-existing.

crates/fm-cli/tests/test_tree_overflow.rs builds a mindmap with 10,000 levels of nesting (each line
indented two more spaces) and calls fm_parser::parse then fm_layout::layout_diagram. Result:

  thread 'test_tree_overflow' has overflowed its stack
  fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
  process didn't exit successfully (signal: 6, SIGABRT)

So a deep-but-small text input does not produce a diagnostic or a bounded error -- it ABORTS the
process. For a library that renders untrusted markup this is a robustness/DoS concern, not just a
failing test: no amount of caller error handling can catch a stack overflow abort.

PRE-EXISTING, not from this session's parser work. Two independent reasons:
1. It appeared identically in test runs at base 77c3a091 and earlier, before the inheritance change.
2. This session's edits are ArrowType/MarkerKind variants, marker dispatch, a11y phrase strings, and
   the state colon-label split. None touches mindmap parsing or tree-layout recursion. ArrowType grew
   from 31 to 37 variants, which stays a one-byte discriminant, so there is no struct-size change that
   could tip a borderline stack frame.

Note the test itself has NO assertions -- it parses, lays out, and prints timings. It looks like a
manual reproduction harness committed as a test, so it has presumably been red for a long time and
its failure is easy to dismiss as noise. It is not noise; it is an unbounded-recursion abort.

WANTED: a depth limit in the mindmap/tree path that returns a Diagnostic (the repo already bounds
input SIZE via core.max_input_bytes, cf. 894fdc1f, but not input DEPTH), or an explicitly heap-based
traversal. Then either give this test a real assertion or move it to the fuzz corpus.
close_reason:
Fixed: ParserConfig.max_nesting_depth (default 256) bounds recursive-descent nesting in parse_flowchart_document_items and parse_block_beta_document_items; surplus levels are flattened into the deepest accepted container with a warning, preserving nodes/edges and keeping end-matching balanced.

DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION: the bead named the mindmap/tree path. That case no longer aborts (verified: 10k-level mindmap parses + lays out in 3.0s; layout tree helpers compute_tree_subtree_spans/compute_all_tree_span_centers are already explicit-stack/BFS). The live unbounded recursion was the FLOWCHART subgraph document parser, plus the same pattern in block-beta.

REPRODUCTION (pre-fix, debug fm-cli): gdb backtrace on 50k nested 'subgraph' = 2965/3000 frames in fm_parser::mermaid_parser::parse_flowchart_document_items -> SIGSEGV. Depth bisect: subgraph ok@2000 FAIL@4000; block-beta ok@4000 FAIL@8000. Input was 966 KB -- well under core.max_input_bytes=5000000, and that limit is CLI-only, so the library API was fully exposed. Nesting is NOT bounded by input size: unindented 'subgraph S/end' costs ~14 bytes per level.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: with the cap temporarily raised to 1_000_000, crates/fm-cli/tests/test_tree_overflow.rs reproduces the exact bead symptom -- 'fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting ... (signal: 6, SIGABRT)'. With the cap at 256 both tests pass. The tests are therefore proven to catch the defect, not tautological.

TESTS (same bead): 3 new fm-parser unit tests (subgraph past-cap flattened / exactly-at-cap preserved boundary / block-beta past-cap flattened) asserting content preservation and end-balance as negative cases; deeply_nested_subgraphs_do_not_panic strengthened from a bare no-panic check to assert all 20 levels survive; test_tree_overflow.rs rewritten from an assertion-free timing harness into 2 asserting tests, both run on a 2 MiB worker-sized thread stack.

GATES: cargo check --all-targets clean (rch remote); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); fm-parser targeted tests 3/3 + 3/3 pass; fm-cli test_tree_overflow 2/2 pass; ubs exit 0.

title: WIN: skip SCC pass for acyclic graphs (layout +5-21% flowcharts)
description: Landed 28b271d. cycle_removal ran detect_cycle_components (Tarjan SCC) AND cycle_removal_dfs_back unconditionally. A graph is acyclic iff DFS finds no back edge; acyclic => no cyclic components + empty cycle summary => the SCC pass is waste. Reordered: dfs_back first; if empty (acyclic) use CycleDetection::default() instead of computing SCC. Output-identical (the extra singleton-component fields only feed MFAS-approx which reverses nothing without cyclic components). 426 tests pass single-threaded. Same-worker A/B: layout/small_10 +21.4%, medium_100 +5-12% (p<0.05); cyclic_50 n.s. (unchanged branch); Tree-path large unaffected (no cycle_removal). NOTE: layout/large_500 + full_pipeline use Tree algo (auto-select fallback) which does NOT call cycle_removal, so this only helps sugiyama-path (small/medium) flowcharts + cyclic graphs are on the else branch. Also: the tracing_dispatch test is a pre-existing parallel-capture flake (passes isolated).
close_reason: Landed 28b271d, pushed main+master, layout +5-21%

title: Update README FNX section to honestly reflect current integration status
description:
## Problem
README Section "Optional FNX Integration" describes FNX (franken_networkx) as if it's a simple optional feature flag you can toggle on. In reality:
- There are ~25 open P1 beads under the bd-ml2r epic covering architecture, adapter, diagnostics, cycle scoring, ordering enrichment, telemetry, runtime budgets, UX controls, comprehensive verification, and rollout.
- Only 2 of those 25 beads are in-progress (bd-ml2r.1 and bd-ml2r.1.1 — the very first sub-tasks).
- The feature flags exist in Cargo.toml but the actual integration code is not yet written.

This is the project's most ambitious unfinished initiative, and the README makes it sound like a toggle.

## Fix
Update the README FNX section to:
1. Keep the existing Cargo feature flag documentation (it's accurate for the BUILD story).
2. Add a clear status note: "FNX integration is currently in early development. The feature flags compile but the integration surface is not yet functional. See the project's issue tracker for the bd-ml2r epic tracking this work."
3. Optionally add a brief roadmap: Phase 1 (undirected graph intelligence + diagnostics) → Phase 2 (directed graph analysis + ordering enrichment).

## Why This Matters
Understating the gap between "feature flag exists" and "feature works" is a soft form of README dishonesty. Users or contributors who enable `--features fnx-integration` and find it does nothing will lose trust. Honest disclosure costs nothing and builds credibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README FNX section includes honest status disclosure.
- No false impression that enabling the feature flag gives you working functionality.
- Roadmap or link to issue tracker for follow-up.
close_reason: Added honest status disclosure (early development, feature flags compile but not functional), roadmap (Phase 1/2), and link to FNX_INTEGRATION.md ADR.

comments.text:
RETRACTION, mine. I filed 'the parse arm accepts zero revisions, therefore it parses nothing' and proposed gating parse rows on parse_accepted_revisions being nonzero. Both wrong.

parse_accepted_revisions is a parse-QUALITY counter, not a liveness counter. parse_results_reference
increments it only when a revision has no errors, did not recover, emitted no warnings, is not
'unknown', AND support_label() equals 'full'. In fm-core, Sequence maps to 'partial'.

Sequence is the ONLY type labelled partial, so the counter is identically ZERO for every sequence
diagram however completely the parse succeeded. sequence_20 was doing real work the whole time.

The proposed gate would have been worse than the thing it was meant to catch: it would have silently
refused EVERY sequence row forever, including sequence_20 -- the project's worst measured ratio and
the one workload we most need a number for -- while looking like a principled work proof. Same shape
as the uniform-verdict trap: a gate that refuses an entire class is a broken instrument, not a strict
one.

STILL OPEN, narrowly: 8 ns for a 1,257-byte parse is ~25 cycles and not plausible, reached by
batching 348,849 iterations into a ~3 ms integrated sample and dividing. Worth investigating on its
own merits. But it is NOT evidenced by accepted_revisions being zero, and 873,911x must not be quoted
while the timing is unexplained.

The banked 362.4x row is RENDER-scoped and unaffected: its work proof is emitted BYTES (43,368) and a
bytes/ns rate under the physics ceiling, both properties of the work rather than of its quality.

THE INTERFERENCE IS PERIODIC, AND EACH ARM IS FAR SHORTER THAN ITS PERIOD. This is a harness finding, not a host complaint, and it applies even in a window that passes a spot check.

Two sequences minutes apart show the same shape rather than random noise - roughly 3s quiet then 7s busy:

  frankenmermaid  100 reps x ~93us   = ~9 ms    ~1/1000 of one period
  mermaid-js       15 reps x ~35ms   = ~0.5 s   ~1/20 of one period

Each arm samples ONE INSTANTANEOUS PHASE of a slow oscillation rather than averaging over it, and A/B/B/A does not fix that: with arms 20x-1000x shorter than the period, the four arms are four point-samples of a slowly-varying signal.

WORSE, THE TWO ARMS ARE NOT COMPARABLY EXPOSED. The incumbent integrates over ~500ms and our arm over ~9ms, so the incumbent averages ~50x more of the interference than the arm it is compared against. Nothing in the current row records which phase either landed in.

Those are large for a pure timing repeat, and phase alignment accounts for them with no engine-side cause needed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
AUDITED MY OWN WAIT LOOPS AGAINST THE NEW DEADLINE RULE, AND CLOSED THE ONE HAZARD IT NAMES THAT I
HAD ACTUALLY HIT.

The rule: every wait needs a deadline, a pgrep loop can match its own cmdline and never exit, and a
file-sentinel loop can wait forever on a producer that already exited non-zero.

AUDIT of scripts/headtohead/measure_chain.sh, loop by loop:
  * three `while read` loops over `ps` output and /proc/stat — finite input, terminate naturally
  * `while true` window poll — exits on `$SECONDS >= window_deadline`. Not merely inspected: the
    `--wait 65` test polled three times and terminated on its own.
  * `while [ attempt -le ATTEMPTS ]` — counted, default 3
  * no file-sentinel loops at all, so the frankenlibc failure mode (waiting on a producer that
    already died) has no foothold here

⚠️ THE CMDLINE-SELF-MATCH HAZARD IS ONE I HIT LAST TICK, exactly as the rule describes. I ran
`pkill -f measure_chain.sh` to stop a background chain. The pattern appeared in the argv of the
pkill's own shell, so it killed ITSELF, returned 144, and left the chain running -- and the
follow-up `pgrep -f measure_chain` then reported the WATCHER as "still active". Anything looping on
that check never exits, and the thing it is waiting for may already be dead. I only noticed because
the exit code was strange; a polling loop would simply have hung.

FIXED AT THE SOURCE rather than in my habits: `--pidfile PATH` writes the chain's pid and removes
it on an EXIT trap, so a watcher uses

    kill -0 "$(cat PATH)"

which is liveness by pid, matches no pattern, and cannot match itself. The comment says plainly
that the watcher still needs its OWN deadline and must READ the chain's output when liveness
fails -- the chain exits non-zero for four distinct reasons (3 disk, 4 competing benchmark, 5 HEAD
kept moving, 6 disk-bound) and each is a different next step, so "it died" is not a diagnosis.

Verified by running it: pid recorded, and the file gone after exit.

ticks ago; still 0 verdicts in the last 30 CI runs. That is four and a half hours in which no gate
has produced a result, on a repo whose main receives a commit every ~272s.

evidence stands -- 900 admission samples, 0 clear, quietest sample 5 busy cpus -- so a retry with no
change to fleet serialisation would only reproduce it, which the script's own give-up message warns
against.

title: state hide empty description was drawn as a phantom state box
description:
`hide empty description` is a real state-diagram directive. It was in no filter in
parse_state_statements, so it fell through to the node parser and normalize_identifier turned it
into a state keyed `hide_empty_description` - a phantom box captioned with the author's own
directive, sitting in the rendered diagram.

Same family as bd-xfmm's subgraph phantom, and in the worse half of it: a dropped directive shows
nothing, this one shows the reader text nobody wrote.

FOUND by probing SYMBOLIC and multi-word state syntax, which the 137-token lexer diff (bd-hebu,
bd-lzhm) is structurally BLIND to - that diff only extracts /^(?:word\b)/ tokens, so `<<choice>>`,
the `--` concurrency separator and multi-word directives never appear in it. Of the forms probed,
`<<choice>>`, `<<fork>>`, `<<join>>` and `--` are all already supported; this was the one gap.

RECOGNISED AND IGNORED, and that is CORRECT here rather than a compromise: this renderer has no
state-description compartment at all - there is no state meta and nothing in fm-render-svg draws one
- so there is no empty description for the directive to hide. It is a genuine no-op for us.

DELIBERATELY NOT WARNED, for the same reason. A warning on valid input that changes nothing is a
false diagnostic, which is the trap the stale style-directive message was (bd-lvj3): it trains
readers to ignore the channel.

KEPT LOCAL to the state parser rather than added to is_non_node_directive_statement, which is shared
with the flowchart and other paths. Widening that predicate is exactly what bd-ij0f did when it ate
eight click tests.

Case-insensitive and spacing-tolerant, matching its `hide footbox` sibling in the sequence parser;
the probe confirms mermaid accepts `HIDE EMPTY DESCRIPTION`.

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Three tests added, none compiled. One is a CONTROL
that a state legitimately NAMED `hide` still exists - the filter is exactly three words, and a
broader `hide ...` guard would have swallowed it.
