1. wide -- MATCHES. corpus.mjs wide(layers,width) (:22) and gen_wide(layers,width)
   (pipeline_bench.rs:63) emit identical nodes and identical edge pairs including the (w+1)%width
   wrap. corpus.mjs even carries the comment "Mirrors gen_wide(layers, width) in pipeline_bench.rs".
   This pair is comparable.

2. flowchart -- DIVERGES ON TOPOLOGY. corpus.mjs flowchart(n) (:14) emits n nodes and a plain chain,
   n-1 edges. gen_flowchart(n) (pipeline_bench.rs:19) emits the same chain and then, for n > 4, adds
   TWO long-range cross edges:
       N0-->N{n/2}
       N{n/3}-->N{n-1}
   At n=10 that is 9 edges versus 11, and the two extra ones are long-range, which is exactly what
   crossing minimization and obstacle-avoiding edge routing cost the most on. The bench's
   "flowchart/small_10" and the corpus's flowchart_small_10 are DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS.

3. cyclic_scc -- TOPOLOGY MATCHES, LABELS DIVERGE. corpus.mjs cyclic(n, ring) (:38) and
   gen_cyclic_scc(n, ring) (pipeline_bench.rs:377) produce identical edge sets, but the node labels
   differ:
       Rust:  C{i}[Node {i}]
       JS:    C{i}[C{i}]
   Label text drives estimate_dimensions -> compute_node_size -> node width -> coordinate assignment
   -> edge routing -> rendered bytes. So the graphs are isomorphic and the LAYOUT WORK is not. This
   is the subtle one, and it is the one a "mirrors the corpus" comment hides best.

WHY THIS MATTERS. Two of the three mirrored pairs are false. Any reasoning that carries a number from
the criterion harness over to a head-to-head row, or vice versa -- "layout is 30% of the pipeline per
the bench, so the corpus row should move by X" -- was never valid for flowchart or cyclic_scc. This
is not noise and no A/A null can see it: both harnesses are individually self-consistent and would
both pass their own controls while measuring different documents.

NOT A CLAIM THAT ANY BANKED ROW IS WRONG. Head-to-head rows are produced by run.mjs alone and stand
on their own; bench numbers are used for profiling and lever selection, not banked as ratios. The
defect is that the two are described as the same workload, so a future agent can and will compare
them.

FIX, in two parts, and the second is the one that lasts:
  (a) Make gen_flowchart and gen_cyclic_scc byte-identical to their corpus.mjs counterparts -- drop
      the two cross edges, change the label to C{i}[C{i}]. This MOVES BENCH NUMBERS, so it is a
      re-baseline, not a no-op, and any bench-derived figure quoted anywhere predates it.
  (b) Gate the claim: commit corpus.mjs output for the mirrored ids as fixtures and assert in a test
      that each Rust generator reproduces its fixture byte for byte. Without (b), (a) silently drifts
      again the first time either generator is edited -- which is exactly how it got here, since the
      wide pair was documented as mirrored and stayed correct while the other two did not.

PROBE TO CLOSE: a test that fails if any mirrored generator's output differs from the committed
corpus fixture, plus each bench doc comment either naming the corpus id it reproduces (and being
enforced) or dropping the claim.
close_reason:
Fixed by 9661b2d7.

CORRECTED FINDING (see the earlier correction comment): the claimed set is {wide, cyclic_scc,
dense_dag}, not {wide, flowchart, cyclic_scc}. gen_flowchart never claimed to mirror anything.

  wide        TRUE  -- identical nodes and edges including the (w+1)%width wrap.
  cyclic_scc  FALSE -- same edges, labels C{i}[Node {i}] against the corpus C{i}[C{i}].
  dense_dag   FALSE -- direction TD against LR, ids N{i}[Node {i}] against D{i}[D{i}], edge steps
                       [1,2,3,5] against 1..=4.

WHAT LANDED:
  - The three mirrored generators moved to crates/fm-cli/benches/corpus_generators.rs, pulled into
    BOTH the bench and crates/fm-cli/tests/bench_corpus_parity.rs with #[path], so there is exactly
    one copy and the test checks the generators the bench actually runs. A criterion bench runs
    harness = false, so a #[cfg(test)] module inside pipeline_bench.rs would never execute -- that
    placement problem was the reason this was filed as needing a design decision, and #[path] is the
    answer.
  - cyclic_scc and dense_dag corrected to match the corpus byte for byte.
  - Fixtures generated from scripts/headtohead/corpus.mjs and committed under
    crates/fm-cli/tests/fixtures/corpus_parity/.
  - gen_flowchart KEEPS its two cross edges -- they are deliberate, a plain chain gives crossing
    minimization nothing to do -- and now documents that it is not the corpus flowchart, because its
    bench ids read like the corpus ids and a reader would otherwise infer comparability.
  - autobenches = false in fm-cli/Cargo.toml: cargo had auto-discovered corpus_generators.rs as an
    empty extra bench target. Found with `cargo metadata`, which needs no build, after first putting
    the key in the wrong section and having cargo reject it immediately.

HOW IT SURVIVED REVIEW, which is the reusable part. The dense_dag doc comment claims
"≈200 nodes / ≈790 edges". The old steps [1,2,3,5] produce 789 edges; the corpus 1..=4 produces 790.
The summary statistic agreed to within ONE EDGE while the direction, the node ids and every edge
target differed. The claim had been checked against a number that could not see the difference.
Check a claim of equivalence by comparing the ARTIFACTS, never a statistic over them.

RE-BASELINE, and it is a real cost: every layout_dense and scc_* bench number from before 9661b2d7
measured a different graph and must not be compared with one from after it.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: restoring C{i}[Node {i}] in gen_cyclic_scc fails the parity test with
"first difference at line 2, bench Some(\"  C0[Node 0]\"), corpus Some(\"  C0[C0]\")". Source restored
byte-identically, sha256 94022c200bb981791e44c60ccfb50421689070e57f5dcc32e0a6e5ad10599f2f.

ANTI-REGENERATION CONTROL, the assertion I care about most: the obvious way to "fix" a future parity
failure is to regenerate the fixture FROM THE BENCH, which makes every parity assertion pass again
while the two harnesses drift apart exactly as before. So a fourth test pins corpus facts the old
bench violated -- LR, D{i}[D{i}], D0-->D4 and not D0-->D5 -- which a fixture captured from the old
bench cannot satisfy.

UNBLOCKS bd-8bbq: wide is now a provably shared fixture for the three-harness cross-check, and
dense_dag would have been the worst possible choice for it -- a TD/LR difference would have dominated
any spread and been banked as harness disagreement.

GATES: cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test bench_corpus_parity 4 passed / 0 failed (remote,
strict); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, which also caught three doc
comments orphaned by the move; rustfmt --check clean; ubs on both new files exit 0 after the
comparison was rewritten from panic! to assert_eq! on the differing LINE (smaller diagnostic, and
the idiom for a test). Pushed to main and master.

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
SHARPENING THE FIX, because "make the generators match" is the wrong default for one of the two and
I do not want whoever picks this up to apply it mechanically.

The two divergences have DIFFERENT causes and deserve different fixes:

FLOWCHART -- the divergence looks DELIBERATE. gen_flowchart carries the comment "Add some cross-edges
for non-trivial layout", i.e. the bench author wanted a harder layout than a plain chain, and a plain
chain is exactly the shape that makes crossing minimization trivial. Deleting those edges would make
the bench a WORSE profiling instrument to buy a comparability nobody has asked for. The right fix
here is almost certainly to fix the CLAIM, not the generator: rename the bench id so it cannot be
read as the corpus item (e.g. flowchart_chain_plus_cross/10 rather than flowchart/small_10) and drop
the mirroring language. Comparability is then explicitly declined rather than falsely implied.

CYCLIC_SCC -- the divergence looks ACCIDENTAL. The edge sets are identical; only the label text
differs (Rust C{i}[Node {i}] versus JS C{i}[C{i}]). There is no profiling reason to want longer
labels here, and label width feeds node sizing, so this one silently changes layout geometry for no
stated purpose. This is the one to make match.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS OWNS A RE-BASELINE EITHER WAY. Changing gen_cyclic_scc's labels moves every
cyclic_scc bench number, so any bench-derived figure quoted anywhere predates the change and must be
re-measured rather than carried across. Say so in the commit.

ON THE GATE (part b), the placement problem stated concretely so it is not rediscovered: the
generators live in a criterion bench, and criterion benches run with harness = false, so a
#[cfg(test)] module inside pipeline_bench.rs would never execute. The cheapest placement that
actually runs is to extract the mirrored generators into
crates/fm-cli/benches/corpus_generators.rs and pull that same file into a real test target with
#[path = "../benches/corpus_generators.rs"] mod corpus_generators; so the bench and the test compile
the identical source. Fixtures generated by corpus.mjs get committed alongside, and the test asserts
byte equality per mirrored id. Without that, part (a) drifts again the first time either generator is
edited -- which is precisely how we got here: the wide pair was documented as mirrored and stayed
correct, while the two that were not gated did not.

I am NOT applying either fix. The flowchart decision trades profiling value against comparability and
belongs to whoever owns the bench, and both fixes re-baseline numbers someone may be mid-way through
using. The finding is recorded, which is what the fleet directive asks for.

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN FINDING. The headline "two of three mirror claims are false" stands,
but one of the two members I named was WRONG, and the replacement is worse. Correcting before fixing
anything.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I listed gen_flowchart as a false mirror claim. It makes NO mirror claim. Grepping
the bench for the actual claims gives exactly three:
  :356  "`dense_200` mirrors the corpus `dense_dag_200` (≈200 nodes / ≈790 edges)"
  :376  "Mirrors the corpus `cyclic_scc_100`."
  :396  "`scc_100` mirrors the corpus `cyclic_scc_100`."
plus corpus.mjs:22 "Mirrors gen_wide(layers, width) in pipeline_bench.rs".
So the claimed set is {wide, cyclic_scc, dense_dag}, not {wide, flowchart, cyclic_scc}.

THE CORRECTED VERDICTS:
  wide        -- TRUE. corpus.mjs wide(layers,width) and gen_wide(layers,width) emit identical nodes
                 and identical edge pairs including the (w+1)%width wrap.
  cyclic_scc  -- FALSE. Edge sets identical; node LABELS differ, Rust C{i}[Node {i}] against JS
                 C{i}[C{i}]. Label text drives node sizing, so the graphs are isomorphic and the
                 layout work is not.
  dense_dag   -- FALSE, and on three axes at once, which makes it the worst of the set:
                   direction   bench `flowchart TD`      corpus `flowchart LR`
                   ids/labels  bench `N{i}[Node {i}]`    corpus `D{i}[D{i}]`
                   edge steps  bench [1, 2, 3, 5]        corpus k in 1..=fanout, i.e. [1, 2, 3, 4]
                 Same edge COUNT per node, different TARGETS, and a different layout direction —
                 which changes ranking and coordinate assignment outright, not just geometry.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE ABOUT FLOWCHART, stated at its real strength rather than the inflated one: the
bench ids `flowchart/small_10` and `flowchart/medium_100` collide by NAME with the corpus ids
`flowchart_small_10` and `flowchart_medium_100` while producing different documents — gen_flowchart
adds two long-range cross edges for n > 4 that corpus.mjs flowchart(n) does not have. That is a
naming hazard for a reader, not a false claim by the code, and the cross edges are deliberate: the
comment says "Add some cross-edges for non-trivial layout". It gets a doc note, not a re-baseline.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, since it is the reusable part: I read the two generators side by side, saw them
differ, and carried "the bench claims to mirror the corpus" over from the beads I had already read
without checking whether THAT generator carried the claim. The divergence was real; the claim was
not. Grep for the claim before attributing one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR bd-8bbq IS UNCHANGED and if anything sharper: `wide` remains the only proven-matching
fixture and is still the right choice for the three-harness cross-check. dense_dag is now known to be
the WORST candidate — a TD/LR difference would have dominated any spread and been read as harness
disagreement.

title: Implement class generics, stereotypes, and annotations
description:
# Class Generics, Stereotypes, and Annotations

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
classDiagram
  class Shape {
    <<interface>>
    +draw()
  }
  class List~T~ {
    +add(T item)
  }
  class Color {
    <<enumeration>>
    RED
    GREEN
    BLUE
  }
  note for Shape "Base interface for all shapes"
\`\`\`
- \`<<interface>>\`, \`<<abstract>>\`, \`<<enumeration>>\`, \`<<service>>\` stereotypes
- \`~T~\` generic type parameters on class names
- \`note for ClassName "text"\` annotations
- \`note "general note"\`

## Current State
- Stereotypes: NOT parsed (<<...>> lines within class blocks are ignored)
- Generics: NOT parsed (tildes treated as part of class name)
- Notes: NOT parsed

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Detect <<stereotype>> lines at top of class block. Parse Class~T~ as class name with generic params. Parse \`note for\` and \`note\` statements.
2. **IR**: Add stereotype: Option<String> and generics: Vec<String> to IrNode for class diagram nodes. Add notes to IR.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Show stereotype in guillemets above class name in header compartment. Show generic params after class name. Notes as yellow sticky-note boxes with connection lines.
4. **Tests**: Interface stereotype, generic class, enumeration, notes.
close_reason: Implemented class generics (~T~ syntax parsing), stereotypes (already worked), and three-compartment rendering across all 3 renderers. Parser extracts generic params from class~T~ syntax. IrClassNodeMeta.generics stores them. SVG/terminal/canvas display as ClassName<T> in class header.

title: REJECT: ASCII lookup table for CharWidthClass::classify (regressed, reverted)
description: Reverted (HEAD 10b1654). classify(c) is a match over ~26 ASCII char literals -> CharWidthClass; replaced with a 128-entry const ASCII table + O(1) lookup. Output-identical (349 fm-core tests pass). Reverse-order A/B (layout): medium_100 +12.3% SLOWER (p<0.05), large_500 +2.2% n.s. = REGRESSION. MECHANISM: the match lets LLVM FUSE classify(c).multiplier() into a single char->f32 jump table; the explicit enum table forces a memory load of the intermediate CharWidthClass that breaks the fusion -> slower. LESSON: do NOT replace a match-on-literals with an explicit lookup table when the result feeds another match/computation -- the compiler fuses the chained matches better than a table+load. Second consecutive micro-lever reject (after attr_static bd-xwy1); the compiler already optimizes the obvious patterns. Micro-lever frontier is exhausted; remaining render lever needs a streaming refactor.
close_reason: Measured regression (medium +12.3% slower), reverted per protocol

title: class relation endpoints keep raw generic text as their label, so a generic class renders as Container~T~ or doubly as Container~T~<T>
description:
A class named with generics in a RELATION keeps the raw tilde text as its display
label, and the generics are never extracted. Combined with a block declaration the
renderer then formats the label AND the generics, producing Container~T~<T>.

MEASURED AT THE IR LEVEL:

  class Container~T~ { +add() void }
      id=Container  label=<none>          generics=[T]     CORRECT
      (the renderer formats id + generics into Container<T>)

  Container~T~ o-- Item
      id=Container  label=Container~T~    generics=[]      WRONG
      the raw tilde text became the display label and no generics were extracted

  both forms together
      id=Container  label=Container~T~    generics=[T]     WRONG, doubly
      the renderer emits format!("{class_name}<{generics}>") over a label that is
      already Container~T~, giving Container~T~<T>

  Container o-- Item        (no generics)
      id=Container  label=<none>          generics=[]      CORRECT control

The rendered form was observed first and the IR probe then reproduced it exactly,
so the mechanism is confirmed by prediction rather than inferred.

MECHANISM: extract_class_generics is called for the 'class Name~T~' declaration
forms only. Class RELATION endpoints go through the ordinary node-token parser,
which normalises the ID to Container but keeps the raw token as the label.

USER-VISIBLE: a generic class declared only by a relation shows as Container~T~
instead of Container<T>, and one declared both ways shows Container~T~<T>. mermaid
renders Container<T> in both cases.

NEGATIVE CASES:
  1. A relation endpoint WITHOUT generics must be untouched -- no label invented,
     no generics recorded. That is the control row above.
  2. A multi-parameter generic Box~K,V~ must yield generics [K, V], not a label
     split on the comma. bd-yf4r showed the comma in a generic list is a live
     hazard: it produced phantom classes Box~K and V~ through a different path.
  3. The block form must keep working unchanged -- it is already correct.
  4. When both forms appear, the class must end with generics [T] and NO raw label,
     so the renderer formats exactly one <T>.
close_reason:
LANDED at 6ce9c27f.

MEASURED AT THE IR LEVEL:
  class Container~T~ { +add() void }   id=Container label=<none>       generics=[T]  CORRECT
  Container~T~ o-- Item                id=Container label=Container~T~ generics=[]   WRONG
  both forms together                  id=Container label=Container~T~ generics=[T]  WRONG, doubly
  Container o-- Item                   id=Container label=<none>       generics=[]   CORRECT control

The doubled rendering was observed FIRST in the SVG (Container~T~ followed by a second angle-bracketed copy of the parameters) and the IR probe then reproduced the exact cause, so the mechanism is confirmed by prediction rather than inferred.

MECHANISM: extract_class_generics is called for the 'class Name~T~' declaration forms only. Relation endpoints go through the ordinary node-token parser, which normalises the ID to Container but keeps the raw token as the display label.

FIX: strip_class_relation_generics removes the tilde group from each endpoint before anything else reads the statement, and pushes BlockStart(name, generics) + End -- the same carrier the inline-generic declaration form already uses -- so generics are recorded once and the label stays clean. It preserves the original surrounding whitespace because cardinality extraction works on byte offsets around the operator.

NEGATIVE CASES: Box~K,V~ yields generics [K,V] and ids [Box, Item], NOT phantoms split on the generic's own comma -- that comma is a live hazard, bd-yf4r produced phantom classes Box~K and V~ through a different path. The block form is asserted unchanged. A relation with no generics invents nothing.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the rewrite disabled the test FAILS with 'the raw generic text stayed in the label: Container~T~'.

GATES, harness cargo test -j 2 -p fm-parser --lib:
  full lib  539 passed, 0 failed  rch worker vmi1149989, 22.0s
  re-gate   539 passed, 0 failed  rch worker vmi1149989, 18.0s

title: mermaid-js parses in bare Node with no browser: a parse-phase vs-incumbent arm is possible without Chromium (6 of 12 diagram types)
description:
FEASIBILITY ESTABLISHED, NOT A RATIO. mermaid-js can be PARSED in bare Node with no
browser, no jsdom and no npm install, which removes the Chromium dependency that has
blocked every vs-incumbent timing row for this project. No number is claimed here.

WHY THIS MATTERS: six sibling projects hold certified vs-incumbent rows and
frankenmermaid holds none, held up by the incumbent needing a browser. That negative
is honestly banked (bd-8nms recorded the snap-namespace blocker and its recurrence).
This bead does not overturn it -- it shows a PARSE-phase arm is now possible.

MEASURED on this host, node v24.14.0:

  bundle  ~/.cache/fm-headtohead/mermaid-11.15.0.min.js
  sha256  70137e77bb273bb2ef972b86e8b0400cca8be53cb25bfc45911a186dc98665de
          -- matches pins.json exactly, so the pinned provenance is preserved and no
          network fetch or package install is involved

RECIPE, ~15 lines, no dependencies. Direct `import()` of the UMD bundle FAILS with
"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'mermaid')"; it must be run in a vm
context whose globalThis/self/window point at the sandbox:

    const code = readFileSync(BUNDLE, 'utf8');
    const sandbox = {};
    sandbox.globalThis = sandbox; sandbox.self = sandbox; sandbox.window = sandbox;
    sandbox.console = console;
    sandbox.setTimeout = setTimeout; sandbox.clearTimeout = clearTimeout;
    sandbox.structuredClone = structuredClone;
    sandbox.TextEncoder = TextEncoder; sandbox.TextDecoder = TextDecoder;
    sandbox.URL = URL; sandbox.Blob = Blob;
    vm.runInContext(code, vm.createContext(sandbox), { filename: 'mermaid.min.js' });
    const mermaid = sandbox.mermaid?.default ?? sandbox.mermaid;
    await mermaid.parse(src);        // -> { diagramType, config }

`document` is deliberately left UNDEFINED. Everything added above is a real Node
platform global, so nothing about mermaid's behaviour is altered to make this work.

COVERAGE, 6 of 12 diagram types parse headlessly:

  OK    flowchart (flowchart-v2), sequence, er, gantt, pie, gitgraph
  FAIL  class, state, journey, mindmap, timeline, quadrant

⚠️ ALL SIX FAILURES ARE ONE CAUSE: "Ro.addHook is not a function", i.e. DOMPurify,
which needs a DOM. DO NOT STUB IT TO WIDEN COVERAGE. pins.json already records that
mermaid's own default security_level is "strict" (DOMPurify on) and that earlier
ad-hoc comparators used "loose", which makes mermaid FASTER and therefore
UNDERSTATES our speedup. Disabling or stubbing sanitization to get the other six
types would be the same error in a new place -- it would flatter us.

The six that do work include the two largest corpus families (flowchart, sequence),
so a parse-phase arm has real coverage without touching sanitization.

⚠️⚠️ COMPARABILITY IS THE OPEN QUESTION, AND IT IS WHY NO RATIO IS BANKED HERE.
mermaid.parse() validates and returns { diagramType, config }; our parse() builds a
full MermaidDiagramIr. These are not obviously the same work, and a ratio between
them would be exactly the apples-to-oranges VOID row the ledger already documents
(bench_corpus_input_divergence: two harnesses failing to share an INPUT is worse
than disagreeing, because no null sees it). Before any row is certified:

  1. Establish what mermaid.parse actually BUILDS. If it discards its AST, the
     comparison flatters us and must be stated as parse-and-discard vs parse-to-IR,
     or a mermaid path that retains structure must be found.
  2. Apply the work-proof gate. A parse arm that returns in nanoseconds is a memo
     hit, not a measurement -- bytes/ns <= 512 per OBSERVED thread.
  3. A/A nulls on both arms, both runs.
  4. Replicated standing: two independent runs, ideally different rch workers,
     nulls passing on both, ELF sha256 and build worker cited, and the WORST bound
     quoted rather than the headline.

NEXT STEP: inline this recipe into the EXISTING scripts/headtohead/mermaid_bench.mjs
as a browserless parse mode rather than adding a new harness file -- the standing
orders exclude new head-to-head scaffolding, and mermaid_bench.mjs already owns
bundle caching, the pin check and the provenance reporting this needs.
close_reason:
LANDED at e64f78f7 as a TRANSPORT, not a ratio. No number is claimed and none is implied.

--browserless on --mode parse runs mermaid.parse() in a bare node:vm context: no browser, no jsdom, no package install. Confined to parse; --mode render exits 2 because render genuinely needs the browser. run.mjs passes the flag through.

THE BENCH BODY IS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS TRANSPORTS. PAGE_PARSE_BENCH was already a function string, so the sandbox evaluates exactly the text the CDP path sends -- same warmup, calibration, batching, determinism validation and A/A null arms. bundleText, its SHA-256 check and INIT_EXPR (including the dispatch-trap guard that asserts the object answering parse() is the pinned library, not a shim) are unchanged. The browserless mode is the same measurement with a different host, which is the only way it is worth having.

PROVENANCE BRANCHED RATHER THAN WAIVED. Left alone, a browserless record would have reported thread_probe.method 'single_cdp_page_main_execution_context' with no CDP page in existence -- defeating run.mjs's incumbent gate instead of satisfying it. Records now carry single_node_vm_main_context / single_vm_main_context / transport node:vm / node_version, and validIncumbentThreadProvenance branches on the method so NEITHER transport can pass on the other's evidence. Six self-test cases pin it: vm record naming a chromium binary REJECTED; vm record with no node version REJECTED; each method paired with the other's fields REJECTED.
NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: dropping the vm branch's node_version requirement makes run.mjs --self-test fail with 'incumbent actual-thread provenance validation regression'.

⚠️⚠️ I AM CORRECTING MY OWN EARLIER COVERAGE CLAIM ON THIS BEAD. It reported 6 of 12 diagram types parsing headlessly -- flowchart, sequence, er, gantt, pie, gitgraph. That was measured by calling mermaid.parse() WITHOUT mermaid.initialize(). The harness initialises with the pinned securityLevel 'strict', which registers DOMPurify hooks, and under the config we actually ship flowchart fails exactly like the rest.

MEASURED against the real corpus, harness scripts/headtohead/mermaid_bench.mjs, host thinkstation1, node v24.14.0, bundle sha 70137e77bb273bb2ef972b86e8b0400cca8be53cb25bfc45911a186dc98665de:
  9 of 43 items run browserlessly, ALL sequence and ER
  34 of 43 fail with the single cause 'Ro.addHook is not a function'
  er_40         p50 5.0-5.2 ms   A/A null 0.9975 [0.9832, 1.0331]
  sequence_20   p50 6.5 ms       A/A null 0.9972 [0.9955, 1.0167]
  er_schema_10000x8  p50 1842.8 ms;  sequence_xl_2000  p50 687.2 ms

The lesson is the one already banked about probes: a capability measured OUTSIDE the shipping configuration is not the capability. My probe skipped initialize(), and initialize() is where sanitisation is switched on.

DO NOT STUB DOMPurify TO WIDEN THIS. pins.json records that mermaid's default securityLevel is strict and that earlier ad-hoc comparators used 'loose', which makes mermaid FASTER and UNDERSTATES our speedup. Buying coverage by disabling sanitisation is that same error in a new place -- it would flatter us.

title: Decide: build a real CGA meet()/join() operator, or reword bd-2q3f criteria around the analytic queries
description:
bd-2q3f (EPIC: Geometric/Conformal Algebra for Transforms) and its children are written as if CGA meet/join operators exist and are being adopted. THEY DO NOT EXIST. Verified 2026-08-04: there is no meet(), join(), regressive product, or outer-product-of-points anywhere in crates/fm-core/src/cga.rs.

What actually exists:
- CgaPoint / CgaLineSegment / CgaCircle / CgaRect as plain Euclidean structs
- Multivector + geometric_product + to_multivector (a real conformal embedding), used ONLY by inner_product
- All intersection queries (segment/segment, circle/segment, circle/circle, rect/segment) implemented ANALYTICALLY via parametric and quadratic solutions, not via meet

This matters beyond naming, because the one place the conformal embedding WAS load-bearing turned out to be a defect: distance measured d^2 = -2 P.Q through the embedding, which squares coordinates before subtracting, and for points ~90 from the origin resolved a true 1e-9 separation as EXACTLY 0.0. Fixed in 681cdf4a by measuring directly. So the evidence so far is that the conformal route is numerically WORSE than the analytic one for the operations this engine actually performs.

DECIDE ONE:
(a) Build meet()/join() properly, and justify it against that evidence -- what does it buy that the analytic queries do not? Degenerate-case uniformity is the usual argument; it must be demonstrated, not asserted, and priced (bd-2q3f.4 exists for the perf/decision contract).
(b) Declare the analytic implementations the intended endpoint and REWORD bd-2q3f.3 criteria 1-3 accordingly, so nobody later reads 'meet operation correct for line-line' as an unmet requirement or quietly marks it met by pointing at analytic code.

DO NOT let this resolve by drift. Criterion 1 has already been satisfied in the (b) sense (intersection queries verified against their geometric definition, 681cdf4a) while the criterion text still says 'meet operation'. Blocks a coherent reading of bd-2q3f.3 and bd-zace.
close_reason:
DECIDED: option (b). The analytic implementations are the intended endpoint. Do NOT build meet()/join() for this engine's paths. Decided on measurement, not preference — bench landed in 630a4f34, crates/fm-layout/benches/cga_transforms.rs.

=== DECISION CONTRACT ===

EVIDENCE 1 — CGA transforms cost 10-40x more than the matrices they would replace. Criterion, per-iteration, same invocation, non-overlapping CIs, ELF 82c691cee9869c791cfabd8c8dc52c6edcdebe15c7d75c6cb7ae2057a7c734c2 self-reported from inside the process:
  compose x4    61.2 ns -> 2.13 us   (34.8x)
  compose x16  235.9 ns -> 9.34 us   (39.6x)
  compose x64   1.01 us -> 38.49 us  (38.1x)
  compose+apply 1024 pts  973 ns -> 9.94 us (10.2x)
bd-2q3f.4's own complexity table predicted ~2.4x. Measured is ~15x worse than that prediction because Rotor::compose does not multiply rotors — it round-trips through a full 16-component Multivector::geometric_product (256 component products) and never exploits the even subalgebra. callgrind puts 12.19% of the rotor arm in geometric_product alone.

EVIDENCE 2 — where conformal machinery WAS load-bearing, it was numerically wrong. CgaPoint::distance evaluated d^2 = -2 P.Q through the embedding, which squares coordinates before subtracting. For points ~90 from the origin a true separation of 1e-9 came back as EXACTLY 0.0, and a point that intersect_segment had just placed ON a segment measured 2^-14 off it. Replaced with the direct form in 681cdf4a. So the one measured instance of 'use the conformal identity' made results WORSE, not more robust.

EVIDENCE 3 — the abstraction is not present anyway. There is no meet(), join(), regressive product, or outer-product-of-points in cga.rs. Every intersection query (segment/segment, circle/segment, circle/circle, rect/segment) is analytic. Adopting meet would be new construction, not migration.

WHAT IS FAIR TO THE CGA SIDE: the 35-40x is against THIS rotor implementation. An optimized 8-component even-subalgebra compose would land far closer to the predicted 2.4x. The decision does not rest on the bad implementation alone — it rests on the fact that even at its theoretical best it is slower than what it replaces, and the only measured quality argument in its favour (conditioning) went the other way. CGA's real advantages, uniform handling of degenerate cases and coordinate-free composition, are not free here: the analytic code already handles its degenerate cases (verified by the 20k-case sweep in 5f62bb80 and the definition-based checks in 681cdf4a).

CONSEQUENCES, to be applied by whoever owns those beads:
1. bd-2q3f.3 criteria 1-3 should be REWORDED from 'meet operation correct for X' to 'intersection queries verified correct for X'. Criterion 1 is already satisfied in that sense (681cdf4a) and criterion 3 already holds (fm-wasm uses CgaRect::contains and CgaLineSegment::distance_to_point). Leaving the current wording invites a future agent to either build meet unnecessarily or quietly mark it met by pointing at analytic code.
2. bd-zace (edge-routing boundary clipping, blocked on this) is UNBLOCKED and its framing resolves to the second of the two it names: consolidate duplicated clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives. Not 'adopt CGA meet'.
3. bd-2q3f.4 can be answered from this bench rather than re-run; it is currently blocked behind bd-17e4.1/.3 and bd-2q3f.2/.3.
4. Rotor/Multivector are NOT to be deleted — they are used by to_affine_matrix and the transform stack, and bd-2q3f.2 is in progress on that surface. This decision is about not EXTENDING the abstraction, not about removing what exists.

RETRY PREDICATE: revisit only if someone implements an even-subalgebra rotor compose and measures it within 3x of the matrix path AND demonstrates a degenerate case the analytic queries get wrong that meet gets right.

comments.text:
⚠️ RETRACTION — the '-4.074% instructions' figure on this bead is METHOD-INVALID and must not be quoted or ledgered. Found while trying to write the PERF_LEDGER KEEP row that bd-x3zl's ELF self-report finally unblocked. The LEVER IS STILL REAL; the number is not.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Both arms were measured as callgrind TOTAL Ir under 'criterion --profile-time 1'. profile-time runs each arm for a fixed WALL second, and under callgrind wall time is dominated by simulation cost, which is itself proportional to instructions executed. So a cheaper arm simply completes MORE iterations in the same second and the total lands in the same place: the metric answers 'how much work fits in a second', not 'what does one edit cost'. I identified this exact trap earlier in the session while measuring rotor-vs-matrix and then failed to apply it to my own result here.

TWO INDEPENDENT PROOFS the metric is not measuring the lever:
1. Re-measured today with self-reporting ELFs, same command, same two arms: two-walk 3,038,095,487 Ir vs fused 3,026,115,751 Ir = -0.054%. Meanwhile per-iteration wall for those SAME binaries differs by 2.4-4.3%. The metric is insensitive to an effect that is plainly there.
2. The same command on the same code gave ~331,360,000 total Ir originally and ~3,038,000,000 today — a 9x swing driven by machine conditions, not by code.

WHAT THE LEVER ACTUALLY MEASURES, by a method that accounts for iterations. Criterion per-iteration, two counterbalanced passes, self-reported ELFs cb674015... (two-walk) and fc89a91a... (fused), which are distinct so this is not a build compared against itself:
  pass 1  two-walk [148.01, 149.18, 150.70] us   fused [143.84, 145.63, 148.08] us   -2.38%
  pass 2  two-walk [150.31, 151.83, 153.20] us   fused [143.94, 145.31, 146.63] us   -4.29%  (CIs disjoint)
Direction is consistent and the mechanism is sound — one walk instead of two over the same node ids and Vec<String> membership — so 83a94342 STAYS. It is a real improvement of roughly 2-4% on this row, not the 4.074% instruction reduction claimed.

NO KEEP ROW WRITTEN, and this is why. docs/PERF_LEDGER.md requires a same-invocation A/A null OR a counted mechanism. I have neither in conforming form: the counted mechanism is the invalid total-Ir above, and the wall numbers come from separate invocations on a host at load 6-10. Writing the row from the retracted figure would be exactly the proof-class inflation the contract exists to stop, and writing it from the wall numbers would misrepresent separate invocations as a same-invocation gate.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT LEDGERABLE: a FIXED-ITERATION harness — run N identical edits under callgrind with N pinned, so total Ir divides cleanly by N and is comparable across arms. criterion's profile-time cannot provide that. Filed as bd-3mxu.

FLEET-WIDE WARNING: any result in this repo measured as callgrind total Ir under criterion --profile-time is suspect for the same reason. The substrate note I left on this bead earlier recommended exactly that method; treat that recommendation as withdrawn.

title: SVG structural invariant audit: 22 diagram types x 5 invariants, all clean, with a passing non-vacuity self-test
description:
BUILD-FREE RENDERER AUDIT. Checks properties true of ANY correct SVG, so one pass covers every diagram type without encoding per-diagram expectations -- the trap this campaign keeps hitting.

INVARIANTS: DANGLING (url(#x) naming an undeclared id -- browser silently drops the paint), DUPLICATE (same id twice; invalid SVG, all references resolve to the first), DEADDEF (id declared in <defs> that nothing references), NONFINITE (NaN/inf in a numeric attribute), DEGENERATE (rect/circle with non-positive size).

RESULT: 22 diagram types probed, 0 findings. Clean: architecture, block, c4, class, er, flowchart, flowchart_sub, gantt, gitgraph, journey, kanban, mindmap, packet, pie, quadrant, requirement, sankey, sequence, sequence_frag, state, timeline, xychart.

This CLOSES the dead-<defs> family as currently observable: DEADDEF fires on nothing across all 22.

⚠️⚠️ THE FIRST RUN REPORTED 13 OF 22 TYPES AS HAVING DUPLICATE IDS '0','1','2' AND EVERY ROW WAS FALSE. The regex was \\bid="..." which also matches the TAIL of data-fm-edge-id="0" -- the \\b sits between the hyphen and 'id'. Real ids (fm-edge-0, fm-edge-1) are unique. The over-match ALSO inflated the declared-id set, so DANGLING was under-reporting at the same time: one bad anchor produced false positives in one check and false negatives in another. Fixed with (?<![-\\w])id=".

NON-VACUITY CONTROL, and it is what makes '0 findings' mean anything: a synthetic SVG violating each invariant exactly once must fire all five, and a clean SVG must fire none. Both hold. The clean control deliberately repeats data-fm-edge-id twice, so it is a standing regression test for the exact false positive above.

Script: scratchpad svg_invariants.py + inv_selftest.py. Needs no build and no quiet host.
close_reason: CLOSED; the enumeration, the control and the false-positive lesson are the deliverable. 22 diagram types clean on 5 structural invariants, with a self-test proving the checker can fail. No build: df -h /data was at or below the budget line all turn.

title: stateDiagram: a composite state renders TWICE — as its cluster container and as a separate plain node box carrying the same label
description:
Found by bd-iicc round 7 (stateDiagram semantic guards).

WHAT HAPPENS. `state Processing { … }` renders TWICE:
  1. as its cluster container — `<rect id="fm-cluster-0" … class="fm-cluster">` with
     `<text class="fm-cluster-label">Processing</text>`
  2. as a separate plain node — `<g id="fm-node-processing-2" class="fm-node fm-node-shape-rounded"
     data-id="Processing">` with a `<rect>` and `<text>Processing</text>`
The same state appears twice in one picture. In golden/state_composite the extra box sits at
(x 473.96, y 470.50, 146.25x66.50), which is INSIDE its own container, so the diagram reads as
"Processing contains a state called Processing".

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. Transitions to the composite attach to the PLAIN BOX, not to the
container:
    fm-edge-5  Idle points to Processing with label: start
    fm-edge-6  Processing points to Idle with label: complete
    fm-edge-7  Processing points to Error with label: fail
So the container that actually holds `Validating`/`Computing`/`Formatting` has no incoming
transition at all, and the composite's entry point is drawn pointing at a decoy box that contains
nothing. A reader tracing `Idle --start--> Processing` arrives at an empty rectangle.

INDEPENDENT OF bd-w5j5. It reproduces in a composite that declares no inner `[*]`, where that bead's
cluster geometry is otherwise correct:
    stateDiagram-v2
      [*] --> Idle
      state Processing { Validating --> Computing }
      Idle --> Processing : start
      Processing --> Done
      Done --> [*]
gives a correct tight cluster (x 92..335.65, y 92..449) holding exactly Validating and Computing —
AND still a separate `fm-node-processing-2` rounded box at (144, 843.50, 146.25x66.50), this time
outside its own container. So the duplicate survives whatever fixes bd-w5j5.

REFERENCE EXPECTATION, flagged as reference rather than measurement because mermaid-js is not
available locally in this checkout: mermaid's stateDiagram-v2 draws a composite state once, as the
container, and attaches transitions to that container's boundary. The claim this bead rests on does
not depend on that: drawing one declared state as two separate shapes with the same label, one of
which absorbs all the transitions while the other holds all the content, is internally inconsistent
whatever the reference does.

ACCEPTANCE GATE, named and populated: remove the `#[ignore]` from
    a_composite_state_is_not_also_drawn_as_a_plain_node   (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs)
and it must pass. It currently FAILS naming the duplicate box and its geometry — verified under
`--ignored`, so it is a real specification and not a stub. The guard hard-errors if a composite
renders NO container, so "fix" by deleting the cluster instead of the node fails loudly rather than
passing.

DECISION THE FIX MUST MAKE: either drop the plain node and re-route composite-targeted transitions
to the container boundary (matches the reference, more layout work), or keep a node as the routing
anchor but stop drawing it as a visible labelled box. The first is preferred; the second is a
smaller change that still removes the duplicate label.
close_reason:
Landed 964c111c, the bead's PREFERRED option (drop the plain node, route transitions to the container boundary) rather than the smaller one — making the box merely invisible would have passed the guard while leaving every arrow ending in empty space, which is a gate satisfied without the defect fixed.

Two changes, one idea: the composite's node IS its container. anchor_composite_state_nodes gives the node its cluster's bounds, so edge routing (which already targets node boxes) attaches transitions to the container boundary with no routing changes; render_node_into returns early for such a node, since the cluster already draws that box and its title. Required building clusters BEFORE edge routing in the Sugiyama path — safe because build_cluster_boxes is a pure function of the already-positioned nodes and nothing between the two call sites mutates them (cycle-collapse still runs after both).

Both crates select on the same two facts (state diagram; cluster title == node id, exactly what begin_state_cluster writes), because restating that independently is how a node stops being drawn while its container never appears. Restricted to state diagrams so a flowchart subgraph sharing a node's name is untouched.

VERIFIED: the three composite transitions now terminate on the container's top edge (cluster y=1206.00) — Idle->Processing ends (208.65,1206), Processing->Idle starts (220.65,1206), Processing->Error starts (214.65,1206) — and data-id='Processing' appears zero times as a drawn node.

GATE: a_composite_state_is_not_also_drawn_as_a_plain_node un-ignored. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the early return disabled it FAILS ('Processing is drawn as its cluster container AND as a plain node box at (x 92.00, y 1206.00, 245.30x827.50) carrying the same label'). The guard hard-errors if a composite renders NO container, so deleting the cluster instead could not have passed it.

GOLDEN-CHANGE: state_composite.svg only; other 36 byte-identical, layout_checksums.json unchanged. cargo test --workspace 0 failures; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: reorder_rank_by_barycenter is 47.64% of pipeline on Sugiyama diagrams; the 4 prior rejections benched dead code
description:
SUBSTRATE DEFECT FOUND + LEVER LICENSED. Full write-up: .benchmarks/crossing_min_rejections_benched_dead_code.md

THE FINDING. perf record on the existing symbolized binary, self-time as % of the whole parse+layout+render pipeline:
  wide_8x16   (= layout_wide/8x16)   fm_layout 21.80%   barycenter+total_crossings 0.000%   tree 2.83%
  wide_16x32  (= layout_wide/16x32)  fm_layout 14.16%   barycenter+total_crossings 0.000%   tree 3.66%
  wide_40x80                         fm_layout 10.41%   barycenter+total_crossings 0.000%   tree 3.27%
  cyclic_scc_100 (Sugiyama)          fm_layout 70.76%   barycenter+total_crossings 48.450%  sugiyama 11.17%

bench_layout_wide (pipeline_bench.rs:306) builds inputs with gen_wide() and registers them as BenchmarkId::new('layered', ..). The name says layered; the auto-selector picks TREE. All FOUR rejected rewrites of the barycenter/crossing-counting area (barycenter-sweep-precomputed-edge-adjacency, flat-array-total-crossings-position-edge-tables, dense-crossing-count-position-maps, local-delta crossing_refinement) were A/B'd on layout_wide/{8x16,12x24,16x32} -- three inputs where the code under test executes ZERO instructions. Their outcomes are exactly what that predicts: +1.40% 'No change', +1.70% 'No change', and +5.84% REGRESSED on 16x32 (the adjacency BUILD cost added to a path that never reads it). Not four pieces of evidence that the lever fails -- one piece of evidence that the bench was wrong, repeated four times.

The do-not-retry's escape clause ('do not attempt further container/adjacency rewrites WITHOUT a CPU profile that names the actual dominant function') is now SATISFIED. It names reorder_rank_by_barycenter at 47.64%. It also refutes the note's own nominated candidate: Brandes-Koepf (bk_horizontal_compaction::place_block) is 0.74% -- COLD.

NOTE: the layout bottleneck is DIAGRAM-SHAPE-DEPENDENT. dense_dag_200 routes to Tree: fm_layout 26.44%, find_obstacle_nudge_x alone 19.36%, barycenter 0.000%. No single bench stands in for the crate.

MECHANISM (fm-layout/src/lib.rs:11572). Called ~rounds(4)*2*ranks times per layout. Each call: (a) ordering_by_rank.get(&rank).cloned() = 1 Vec alloc; (b) builds adjacent_position: BTreeMap (alloc + O(k log k)); (c) for ranks narrower than SINGLE_PASS_RANK_THRESHOLD=8 -- the common case (~100 nodes over ~25 ranks => ~4/rank) -- RESCANS THE ENTIRE ir.edges LIST PER NODE, doing a ranks.get(&n) BTreeMap probe per edge. O(rank_size * |E| * log|V|) per call; ~188k B-tree probes per layout.

LEVER (do (1) first):
  1. Dense Vec<u32> rank array built ONCE per crossing_minimization, replacing the innermost BTreeMap probe with an O(1) index. No adjacency built at all. This is a DIFFERENT primitive from the rejected Vec<Vec<usize>> adjacency, whose ~2*node_count outer + node_count inner allocations are exactly what sank it.
  2. Dense Vec<u32> scatter tables reusing ONE scratch buffer for adjacent_position / local_slot instead of per-call BTreeMaps.
  3. Flat CSR incidence (2 allocs, built once) ONLY if (1)-(2) do not suffice.
Output-identical by construction: node_rank[n] == ranks.get(&n).copied().unwrap_or(0); barycenter arithmetic (integer position sum / neighbor count) and the downstream stable sort are untouched.

BLOCKER -- NO BENCH EXERCISES THIS FUNCTION:
 * pipeline_bench::layout_wide -> Tree path, 0.000% barycenter (and the reason 4 rejections are void).
 * fm-layout/benches/crossing_minimization.rs -> benches crossing_min/{sparse_dag,dense_dag,bipartite} over synthetic LayerOrdering/LayerEdges. That is a DIFFERENT crossing minimizer; reorder_rank_by_barycenter takes &MermaidDiagramIr and is never called.
STEP 0 is therefore: add a Sugiyama-routing layout bench. cyclic_scc_100 from scripts/headtohead/corpus.mjs is a known-good generator (cyclic SCC => detect_cycle_components => Sugiyama).

A/B SUBSTRATE (mandatory): rch exec has NO worker-pinning flag and picks workers non-deterministically, so a split-invocation A/B is invalid (see the CORRECTION entry in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md; RCH_WORKER=hz1 was silently ignored and both arms ran on hz2). Bench ORIG and CAND as two arms of ONE alternating criterion group, in ONE binary, in ONE rch exec invocation -- keep the current reorder_rank_by_barycenter as a bench-only reference fn.

DETERMINISM: golden_layout_test + the layout determinism gate must stay green; add a differential test asserting the dense-rank variant produces byte-identical ordering to the BTreeMap variant across random graphs (same playbook as bd-w5sn's single_pass_scanners_match_per_needle_contains).

FILE-OWNERSHIP: crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs (~11572) is the cod pane's lane -- coordinate before editing.
close_reason: Packed u32 rank lookup kept: paired same-binary A/B 1.310x (CV 0.69%) on cyclic_scc_100 and 1.318x (CV 4.57%) on cyclic_scc_800; exact parity and per-arm profile integrity proven

  min_sample  min_of  batch  null_ratio  null_cv  null_mad  floor
     2ms         1       4    0.9950x    15.65pct  2.76pct  0.50pct
     2ms         3       4    1.0013x    11.98pct  3.56pct  0.13pct

    40ms         3     101    1.0011x    14.03pct  6.84pct  0.11pct

I CONFOUNDED THE FIRST SWEEP AND FIXED IT: running configurations sequentially conflates the configuration with time-varying machine load (min_of=3 appeared to help at 2ms and hurt at 10/40ms — incoherent). Configurations are now interleaved round-robin with a rotating start. Same error arm-interleaving prevents, one level up.

FINDING 1: no in-harness knob moves cv below ~12pct on a loaded, unpinnable worker. A 20x longer sample moves cv 15.65 -> 11.63pct. min-of-k does not help consistently. The preemption-fraction hypothesis is WRONG.
FINDING 2: the A/A null MEDIAN is tight in every config — 0.11pct to 0.75pct from 1.000. One-sided outliers inflate cv and MAD WITHOUT biasing the median of per-round ratios.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR FLAT-CSR: do not gate on cv<5 — you cannot meet it unless the scheduler hands you a quiet worker, and rch cannot pin one. Gate on the null MEDIAN's departure from 1.000 (~1pct here) and require your flat-CSR ratio to exceed it by a wide margin. Report cv, do not gate on it, and say whether the worker was quiet. If flat-CSR lands under ~1.02x, this harness cannot decide it on a loaded worker and you should say so rather than claim it.

RECALIBRATING THE RECORD: your dense-rank 1.310x is ~40x the worst-case 0.75pct floor; single-pass 3.669x is ~350x it. Both survive comfortably. Nothing sub-1pct has ever been claimed in this lane. cv<5 IS achievable when the worker is quiet (your certified rows read 0.94pct and 0.57pct) — which is exactly why the null must be emitted in the SAME invocation as the claim: it tells you whether THIS run can decide THIS lever.

CHEAPEST FIT-FOR-PURPOSE CONFIG: min_sample=2ms, min_of=3 (floor 0.13pct). Longer samples buy nothing. Your barycenter_sweep uses MIN_SAMPLE=2ms and min_of=1 today; adding min_of=3 is a two-line change and halves the floor.

title: flowchart @{ shape: ..., label: ... } metadata is interned as a node, so the directive text becomes an invented class name
description:
mermaid 11's `@{ ... }` metadata syntax is not recognised on the flowchart path, so
the directive text is interned AS A NODE. The diagram gains classes and boxes whose
names appear nowhere in the source, and the declared intent is lost.

Same family as bd-sq8p (class relation labels swallowed into the target name):
unparsed syntax becoming invented node identity.

MEASURED with the shipping binary, two forms.

FORM 1, node metadata -- the common mermaid 11 shape syntax:

    flowchart LR
      A@{ shape: rect, label: "Shaped" }
      B[Plain]
      A --> B

renders a node whose displayed label is the literal

    shape: rect, label: "Shaped

(note it is even truncated at the closing quote). mermaid renders a rect labelled
`Shaped`.

FORM 2, edge id plus edge metadata:

    flowchart TD
      A e1@--> B
      e1@{ animate: true }

renders THREE nodes where the source declares two:

    data-id="A_e1"  label "A e1@"
    data-id="B"     label "B"
    data-id="e1"    label "animate: true"

So `A e1@` is an invented class name, `animate: true` is a directive drawn as a
node, and the edge runs from `A_e1` rather than from `A` -- the real source node is
not even connected.

THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS. `strip_kanban_metadata` (mermaid_parser.rs:5266)
parses exactly this `@{key: value, ...}` grammar for kanban, including quote
stripping and comma splitting. The flowchart path simply never calls it, and
`parse_node_token_with_config` then treats the whole line as a node token.

SCOPE NOTE: FORM 1 is the valuable half and is what this bead is for. It is the
syntax mermaid 11 documents for shapes, so real documents use it. FORM 2 (edge ids
and edge-level metadata) needs an edge-id concept the IR does not have; filed
separately rather than folded in, because "stop inventing a node" and "support edge
ids" are different sizes of work.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. A node with NO metadata must be byte-identical to today. This is the common
     line and it must not move.
  2. `shape:` must map to the same NodeShape the bracket syntax produces --
     `A@{ shape: rect }` and `A[x]` must agree, or the two spellings diverge.
  3. An UNKNOWN shape name must not invent a node and must not panic; fall back to
     the default shape, the way `curve` already tolerates unknown names.
  4. `label:` must win over the id as the displayed text, and a label containing a
     comma or a colon must survive the key/value split.
  5. The kanban path must be untouched -- it shares the grammar but has its own
     keys, and a shared helper must not start applying `shape` there.
close_reason:
LANDED at 401a5f1f, pushed to main and master. Scoped to FORM 1 (node metadata) as the bead specified; FORM 2 (edge ids) filed separately.

MEASURED before: 'flowchart LR / A@{ shape: rect, label: "Shaped" }' rendered a node whose displayed name was the literal 'shape: rect, label: "Shaped' -- truncated at the closing quote -- with the declared shape and label both lost.

MECHANISM, now known exactly rather than inferred. parse_node_token_with_config read the braces as a DIAMOND shape token and took the directive body as the label. The negative control proves it: with the new pass disabled the shape assertion fails 'left: Diamond, right: Cylinder'.

FIX: parse_flowchart_node_metadata runs immediately before the generic node-token fallback and returns None for anything that is not this exact form, so every other statement falls through untouched. shape: maps onto the same NodeShape the bracket spelling produces, asserted directly against '[(...)]'. An unrecognised shape name leaves the shape alone rather than inventing one, matching the tolerance curve already applies to unknown names. split_metadata_pairs splits on commas OUTSIDE quotes, because a naive split(',') turns label: "one, two" into two bogus pairs.

NEGATIVE CASES, all five from the bead: no-metadata control unchanged; shape: cylinder agrees with the bracket spelling; unknown shape keeps the default and invents nothing; a label containing BOTH a comma and a colon survives; kanban untouched (it shares the grammar but has its own keys and its own helper).

⚠️ VACUITY NOTED, same pattern the bd-sq8p control exposed: the ids == [A, B] assertion passes with the fix disabled too, so it is a guard rather than the load-bearing check. The shape and label assertions are what carry these tests. Recorded in the commit so it is not rediscovered.

GATES, harness cargo test -j 2 -p fm-parser --lib:

  full lib  519 passed, 0 failed rch worker hz2, 59.2s
  negative control: both tests FAIL with the pass disabled; restored and re-gated green
  cargo fmt --check -p fm-parser clean

What this removes is the invented DISPLAY name -- e1 no longer renders as a class called 'animate: true' -- and the test asserts that specifically.

title: C4 node box ignores its wrapped description; lines render up to 220px outside the box
description:
THIRD instance of the sizing-ignores-a-diagram-meta class, after bd-4isi (class members truncated) and bd-090g (ER attributes spilled). Found by extending bd-090g's audit to the remaining node metas rather than by inspection.

compute_node_size consults class_meta (via class_compartment_dimensions) and, since bd-090g, node.members. It consults c4_meta NOT AT ALL, so a C4 node box is sized from its label while the renderer draws a type label, a name, and a WRAPPED description inside it.

MEASURED, default config, C4Context with one Person and descriptions of increasing length. Reading the node rect against the fm-c4-description <text> and its <tspan dy=...> stack, no transforms in the document so these are final coordinates:

  desc 'Short'                      lines=1   box y=92.0..158.5  desc 143.8..143.8  overflow 0
  desc ~78 chars                    lines=10  box y=92.0..158.5  desc 150.5..284.6  overflow 131.1px
  desc ~136 chars                   lines=16  box y=92.0..158.5  desc 150.5..374.0  overflow 220.5px

The box height is CONSTANT 66.5 in all three. A 16-line description renders 220px below its own rectangle.

WHY IT HID FROM MY FIRST PASS, worth recording as a probe lesson: the description is ONE <text> element whose y attribute IS inside the box; the lines are <tspan dy="14.90"> children stacking downward from it. A check that reads only the text element's y sees no overflow. Any geometry guard in this family must sum the tspan dy stack.

THE RENDERER ALREADY TRIES TO CONTAIN IT AND CANNOT, which is the interesting part. write_c4_node_into (fm-render-svg lib.rs:7165) computes

  baseline_y = (cursor_y + description_height.min((h * 0.35).max(0.0))).min(y + h - 8.0)

so its author clearly intended the description to stay inside the box. But that clamp applies to the FIRST LINE's baseline only; the tspans then stack downward from wherever it landed, so every subsequent line escapes regardless. Clamping the anchor of a multi-line block does not bound the block. Do not try to fix this by tightening that clamp — it would only pull the first line up while the tail still spills, and pulling it far enough up to fit would push it out of the top.

FIX SHAPE: size the box for the wrapped description in compute_node_size, leaving the renderer alone, exactly as the class and ER siblings do. The circularity is only apparent: compute_node_size already derives width from the label BEFORE height, so it can wrap to that width and then add the line count's height. Renderer geometry to mirror:

  description_font = clamp_font_size(font_size * 0.72, config.min_font_size)
  line_h           = font_size * config.line_height
  available_width  = (w - 20.0).max(32.0)
  lines            = wrap_text_to_lines(description, available_width, config.avg_char_width * 0.92)
  per-line advance = description_font * config.line_height   (this is the tspan dy)

MIND THE ESTIMATOR MISMATCH: the renderer wraps with config.avg_char_width * 0.92 while layout has only metrics. The two need not agree, and UNDER-counting lines under-sizes the box, which is the failure mode being fixed. So layout must round the line count UP — wrap against a slightly narrower effective width, or add a line of margin. Over-sizing renders as padding and is harmless.

ALSO CHECK while fixing: the type label and name rows sit at fixed offsets and fit today, but a very long NAME wraps too (fm-c4-name), so the same tspan-stack question applies to it. I measured only the description.

REQUIREMENT DIAGRAMS ARE CLEAN — NULL RESULT, recorded so nobody re-measures. requirementDiagram nodes render exactly three rows (fm-req-type-label, the name, fm-req-metadata 'Risk: ... | Verify: ...'), all single-line and all inside the box (last row at y=136.9 against a box ending at 158.5). requirement_meta genuinely does not need to feed sizing. So this class has exactly one instance left, not two.

UNCONFIRMED OBSERVATION, deliberately not filed as its own defect: a requirement's 'text:' and 'id:' fields appear NOWHERE in the rendered output, only its type/name/risk/verifymethod. That may be correct scope for our renderer or it may be content loss against mermaid-js; I did not run the incumbent to find out, so it is an observation rather than a finding.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. For descriptions spanning 1..N wrapped lines, every rendered line — computed as the text baseline plus the accumulated tspan dy, plus half the font size — lies inside the node rect.
2. A C4 node with no description is unchanged in size, so C4 diagrams without descriptions and all non-C4 diagrams do not move.
3. GOLDEN IMPACT: check whether any committed fixture is a C4 diagram with a description; if so it needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note naming the new box height.
4. If c4_meta starts feeding compute_node_size, node_size_cache_key MUST hash the description too — the same coupled requirement bd-090g had for node.members, and for the same reason.
close_reason:
Fixed by 9fbbcd74.

FIX: new c4_description_height in fm-layout, plus the coupled node_size_cache_key hash of the description. The renderer is untouched, as the bead directed — its .min(y + h - 8.0) clamp bounds only the FIRST line's baseline while the tspans descend from wherever that landed, so tightening the clamp could not work.

MEASURED, same command as the filing. Before: box constant 66.5 with overflow 0 / 131.1px / 220.5px at 1 / 10 / 17 wrapped lines. After: overflow 0 at every length tested, up to 17 lines.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all four:
1. Every rendered line inside the box — asserted as text y plus ACCUMULATED tspan dy plus half the font, swept by growing the description one word at a time to 21 words.
2. A C4 node with no description, and one whose description fits on one line, are both unchanged in size (lines <= 1 returns None). Pinned as an assertion in the same test.
3. GOLDEN IMPACT: NONE. c4_basic is a committed C4 fixture and its descriptions ('A customer', 'Serves content') wrap to one line at their nodes' widths, so golden_svg_test 8/8 and golden_layout_test 2/2 pass untouched. No bless, no GOLDEN-CHANGE note.
4. node_size_cache_key now hashes the description, with its own fault test.

THE CALIBRATION MISTAKE I MADE AND CORRECTED, because it is the reusable lesson: my first version dropped the renderer's avg_char_width * 0.92 narrowing on the theory that assuming a wider character over-counts lines and over-counting is the safe direction for containment. It IS safe for containment, but it turned c4_basic's 'A customer' into two lines and grew that box from 66.5 to 94.0 — moving a committed golden for zero correctness gain. Mirroring the renderer's 0.92 makes the counts agree whenever layout's metrics and the render config agree, and the disagreement case is absorbed by one line of margin instead. Measured both ways; the mirrored version is what landed. 'Safe direction' is not free when the cost is golden churn.

THE FIXED POINT I DECLINED TO SOLVE, stated so the over-sizing is not mistaken for an error: the renderer shifts the description's first baseline down by min(block_height, h * 0.35), which depends on h — the value being solved for. Rather than iterate, this bounds that term by block_height (valid because min(a,b) <= a), so tall descriptions get a box taller than strictly necessary. Over-sizing renders as padding and keeps the arithmetic auditable; a fixed-point solve would tighten it if anyone cares.

ALSO ANSWERED, the bead's 'also check' item: a long NAME does not have the same problem — the name is a single <text> with no tspan stack in the cases measured. I did not construct a name long enough to force wrapping, so that remains unverified rather than cleared.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, both halves independently, because the fix has two:
  sizing reverted -> '2 words / 3 lines: description line at 165.4 escapes the node box 92..158.5' and 'C4 box must grow when the description wraps: 66.5 > 66.5'
  description removed from the CACHE KEY only, sizing intact -> the incremental test fails alone
Source restored byte-identically (diff -q) after each control.

REQUIREMENT DIAGRAMS: NULL RESULT, already recorded in the bead body and repeated here so it survives. requirementDiagram nodes render exactly three single-line rows (fm-req-type-label, name, fm-req-metadata 'Risk: ... | Verify: ...'), last at y=136.9 against a box ending at 158.5. requirement_meta genuinely does not need to feed sizing. This class is now CLOSED: class_meta (bd-4isi), node.members (bd-090g), c4_meta (this bead) fixed; requirement_meta measured and clean.

STILL AN OBSERVATION, NOT A FINDING: a requirement's 'text:' and 'id:' fields appear nowhere in the rendered output. Could be correct scope or content loss against mermaid-js; I did not run the incumbent, so it stays an observation. Anyone extending ER/class/C4 fidelity work should measure it against pinned mermaid-js before filing.

GATES: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 40/40 suites green, 0 failures; cargo fmt --check clean on every hunk authored. ubs: fm-render-svg exits 0; fm-layout exits 1 which is pre-existing per bd-tp4z, and of its 39 distinct finding lines NONE falls on any of the 168 lines this commit added. Pushed to main and master at 9fbbcd74.
