title: Flowchart direct-CSS fast path skips marker/accent CSS pruning (perf regression; golden_svg_test red)
description:
Found by cc lane (RubyRidge). ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED. Supersedes this bead's original title/framing:
the goldens are not merely stale -- they are RED because a certified perf win silently regressed, and
the goldens caught it. Blessing them would bury the regression.

SYMPTOM: cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test golden_svg_test fails at case dense_flowchart_stress.
All 30 cases run in ONE test fn, so that first failure MASKS the rest; a full BLESS=1 run moves 18 of
them, so the drift is broad, not isolated.

ROOT CAUSE: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs, render_svg_with_layout_impl_reusing:

    let direct_minified_css = matches!(config.backend, SvgBackend::LegacyLayout)
        && config.embed_theme_css
        && ir.diagram_type == DiagramType::Flowchart;
    ...
    if direct_minified_css {
        return svg;                 // <-- skips apply_output_post_passes
    }
    apply_output_post_passes(&mut svg, use_post_pass_cache, known_live_marker_mask);

apply_output_post_passes is where strip_dead_marker_css (dead marker#arrow-* selectors) and
strip_unused_state_css (dead .fm-node-accent-N rules and their :root vars) run. The direct_minified_css
gate is true for EVERY flowchart with the LegacyLayout backend and embedded theme CSS, so on the most
common diagram type both prunings are now dead code.

MEASURED (dense_flowchart_stress, golden config, current HEAD vs committed golden):
  committed golden marker CSS: marker#arrow-end only            (pruning worked when it was blessed)
  current output marker CSS:   arrow-end, arrow-filled, arrow-open, arrow-circle, arrow-diamond,
                               arrow-cross                       (nothing pruned)
  +428 bytes on this one diagram; geometry (viewBox) and every <text> byte-identical.
Commit 0a083253 measured this same pruning at -17,125 B/corpus, so the regression gives that back.

INTRODUCED BY a2546282 'perf(svg): emit cached minified flowchart CSS' (2026-08-01), which added the
direct_minified_css fast path AFTER the last good bless (4798d977, 2026-07-31). That ordering is why
the goldens went red exactly then. Ruled out: 0f9efd49's 'if state_used { return; }' early return is
older than the last good bless and is not the cause.

SECOND, SEPARATE DELTA in the same golden set, and this one is a genuine FIX that does need blessing:
5bad0559 'fix(layout): preserve reciprocal rendered edges (bd-4b6s)' recovered edge labels that were
being collapsed into a literal 'x2' multiplicity badge. state_basic old->new: 'x2' -> 'stop';
state_composite: 'x2' -> 'complete'; flowchart_simple: a stray 'x2' badge removed with no label lost.
The old goldens were WRONG there (state_basic.mmd really does declare 'Running --> Idle : stop').

WHY THIS BEAD IS STILL OPEN: the obvious repair -- run apply_output_post_passes on the direct path too
-- re-adds the pass a2546282 deliberately removed, so it needs a measured A/B before landing, and the
host is at load ~23 with peer rustc saturating cores. Measuring now would produce an invalid verdict.
The better fix is probably to emit only live marker CSS at construction (theme.rs to_svg_style already
receives enough context, and flowchart_marker_mask(ir, layout) is already computed at the call site),
which is strictly less work than emit-then-strip -- but that also needs the same measurement.

DO NOT bulk-bless. Note e5925c1c 'test(golden): refresh SVG fixtures after class-shorthand parser work'
already refreshed goldens under an unrelated message and did NOT fix the failure -- the suite is still
red at HEAD. Correct sequence: (1) fix or measure-and-accept the marker/accent pruning regression,
(2) then bless ONCE with a GOLDEN-CHANGE note covering both deltas above.

Blocks bd-4e2k (class_basic.svg cannot be re-blessed cleanly until this is settled).
close_reason:
Closing on verified evidence. BOTH halves are fixed and the goldens are green; this bead body predates the commits that finished it, which is why it still read as open work.

I VERIFIED THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN TRUST EITHER NARRATIVE, because this bead exists precisely because a certified win had silently regressed.

MARKER HALF — pruning live. Rendered dense_flowchart_stress: marker CSS is marker#arrow-end ONLY. The regression symptom recorded in this bead was six selectors (arrow-end, arrow-filled, arrow-open, arrow-circle, arrow-diamond, arrow-cross). The committed golden agrees, so output matches the state that was blessed when pruning worked. Mechanism: flowchart_marker_mask(ir, layout) at lib.rs:633 feeds a live-marker mask into the CSS builder and prune_marker_selectors (lib.rs:1078) filters while the CSS is still pretty, BEFORE minify/cache — i.e. the fix this bead planned, not a re-add of the post-pass a2546282 removed.

ACCENT HALF — pruning live, and MEASURED with a control rather than asserted. A single-node flowchart emits exactly ONE accent rule (.fm-node-accent-5); the recorded symptom was 1 -> 8. Two nodes emit two; nine nodes emit all eight, which is correct because nine nodes span the palette.

  CONTROL (accent pruning disabled by forcing flowchart_accent_mask to all-live):
    single-node flowchart   pruning OFF 7,721 B  ->  pruning ON 6,295 B   = 1,426 B recovered, 18.5% of the document
    dense_flowchart_stress  25,669 B both ways   = unchanged, correctly: 16 nodes span all 8 accents so nothing is prunable
  The dense case being identical is the useful half of that control — it shows the mask is not over-pruning — and the single-node case shows it is genuinely consulted, not dead code. Load-independent byte counts, so no quiet host was needed and no timing claim is made.

The accent mask is built the way this bead planned it: flowchart_accent_mask (lib.rs:823) derives it from stable_accent_index(&node.id) over ir.nodes, a superset of what the body emits, over-approximating in the safe direction.

THE LATENT CACHE-KEY BUG THIS BEAD FLAGGED IS ALSO FIXED: accent_mask now participates in the CSS cache key (lib.rs:1255/1301/1312/1324/1337), so diagrams with different accent sets no longer share one entry.

THE AGREEMENT TEST THE PLAN REQUIRED EXISTS AND PASSES: strip_dead_marker_css_for_mask_matches_the_defs_scanning_twin — the mask-based pruner and the defs-scanning twin are asserted byte-identical.

GOLDENS: every case reports matched-golden and golden_svg_test passes 8/8 with golden_layout_test 2/2. The 18-then-14 moving cases recorded here are down to zero. The three legitimate deltas this bead identified were blessed with attribution rather than bulk-refreshed: bd-4b6s reciprocal edges (state_basic x2 -> stop, state_composite x2 -> complete, flowchart_simple stray badge) and bd-4e2k class shorthand (class_basic), per 93a6cd1d.

NO QUIET-HOST A/B WAS NEEDED, and that is worth recording because this bead originally required one: the landed fix prunes at CONSTRUCTION on already-pretty CSS instead of emitting-then-stripping, which is strictly less work than the pass a2546282 removed. So the original blocker ("measuring now would produce an invalid verdict at load ~23") was dissolved by choosing a cheaper mechanism rather than waiting for the host.

CREDIT: root cause and both plans by the cc lanes RubyRidge and PeachGorge (61b3c72d marker half, 6ab5a169 accent half, 93a6cd1d the attributed bless). My contribution here is verification and closure: I confirmed both prunings are live in current code, quantified the accent recovery with a disable-control, confirmed the cache-key fix and the agreement test, and confirmed zero moving goldens.

comments.text:
MARKER HALF FIXED AND LANDED in 61b3c72d. Bead stays open for the accent half.

MECHANISM (two compounding causes, both required to explain the symptom):
1. render_svg_with_layout_impl_reusing returns early on direct_minified_css (added by a2546282), so
   apply_output_post_passes -- which owns strip_dead_marker_css and strip_unused_state_css -- never

still pretty and before minify/cache. Strictly less work than emit-then-strip, so it does not re-add

required. Also fixes a latent cache-key bug: cached_minified_full_css keyed on the full stylesheet, so

now match their committed goldens again (18 moving cases -> 14). fm-render-svg 264/264; clippy
--workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; ubs no finding on changed lines.

REMAINING (accent half) -- the 14 cases still moving split cleanly, measured against HEAD:

title: schema_catalog_25 does not measure a render: our arm is a 16ns memo hit, so 412.8x and 401,800,000x are both artifacts of batching against a warm cache
description:
MEASURED TODAY, live, both arms in one invocation, on a quiet host (load1 7.93 on 64 cores). This is a negative result and it invalidates a headline, so it is filed rather than quietly dropped.

THE NUMBERS, from summary-08d27375-1786747598778.json:
  fm_p50_ns              16          <- sixteen NANOSECONDS
  fm_min_ns              16
  fm_batch               342682      <- iterations the harness needed to reach a measurable sample
  mjs_p50_ns             6428800000  <- 6.43 s, real
  speedup                401800000   <- 401.8 million x
  revisions              25
  fm_bytes / mjs_bytes   1663670 / 11866373
  ELF (self-reported)    0856d3b8043b472f0b98651944acfe813dcefc52f7894c69bd4bc8758ad91131
  rev                    08d27375 (dirty), mermaid 11.15.0 strict, Chrome/151.0.7922.108

Rendering 25 diagrams totalling 662 entities and 637 relationships cannot take 16 ns. Our arm is not rendering. The harness batches the job 342,682 times to reach its minimum integrated sample, and our engine memoises by revision key, so iteration 1 renders and iterations 2..342682 are cache hits. The reported p50 is the cost of a cache probe.

EVERY GATE PASSED, which is the uncomfortable part and the reason this needs a bead rather than a comment: output equivalence PASS (25/25 diagrams equivalent, 0 divergent, er 25/25, tier2_decided=11), fm bracket PASS, median-CI gate PASS, and the new balanced-square incumbent null PASS at 1.0120. A row can satisfy every statistical and semantic gate this harness has and still be measuring nothing, because no gate asserts that our arm did the WORK.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEDGER. The certified 412.825519x row for this workload (PERF_LEDGER.md:602, ELF a23cf867...) was produced by the same batching path, so it is very likely the same artifact at a smaller batch, not a render ratio. bd-hcw3 asked for this workload to be requalified because the ER geometry fix changed entity heights; the answer is worse than 'the number moved' -- the number was never measuring what its row says. I am not editing that row: it states its own ELF and stands as history. What must not happen is anyone quoting 412.8x, or today's 401,800,000x, as a render ratio.

WHAT A HONEST ROW NEEDS (the actual fix, and it is in the harness, not the engine):
1. The batch loop must defeat the memo, not feed it. Either force a distinct revision key per iteration, or reset the incremental engine between iterations, or measure ONE unbatched render and accept the wider CI.
2. A work-proof gate: assert the arm's reported bytes were PRODUCED in the timed region, e.g. that per-iteration allocation or instruction counts scale with the diagram, and refuse a row whose per-job time is below a floor that a render of N entities physically cannot beat. 16 ns for 662 entities should have been refused by the harness, not printed as a 401-million-x win.
3. Until 1 and 2 exist, this item cannot support a render claim at any batch size.

NOT A REGRESSION IN THE ENGINE. The memo is a real feature and the cache hit is genuinely 16 ns; the defect is that the measurement boundary lets the cache answer a question about rendering. The same trap is already known for the 214,830,232x revision-key elision row, which is why the campaign was told not to headline it -- this bead says the ER catalog row belongs in that same class.

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
ITEM 2 (the work-proof gate) LANDED: fcce5b11, scripts/headtohead/run.mjs.

Item 1 (defeat the memo inside the timed region) was already landed by peers before me:
43e3c3e3 time uncached render work, 21a182a7 prove timed render avoids memo, 0053504e keep timed
full-render samples off parse-plan reuse (TIMED_RENDER_REUSES_OUTPUT_SNAPSHOT /
TIMED_RENDER_REUSES_PARSE_PLAN both false, both stamped on every run record and fail-closed in JS).

THE GATE, stated as physics rather than a threshold so it cannot be tuned: a row claiming B result
bytes at P ns per job asserts a production rate of B/P bytes/ns. The widest cores retire at most 64
bytes of stores per cycle into L1; at 8 GHz -- above any shipping part -- that is 512 B/ns per
thread, before a byte of parse/layout/SVG work is paid for. Above the ceiling the bytes were not
produced inside the timed region. Threads scale it from the OBSERVED count only.

WIN/LOSE SPLIT, measured over every row this repo has stored (.benchmarks/headtohead + cert-v5,
137 rows, scored at the conservative threads=1 assumption):
  admitted 135 | refused 1 | unscoreable 1 (already failed host_wide_exclusivity_invalid, carries
  no bytes/p50).
The one refusal is this bead's own artifact, summary-08d27375-1786747598778.json: 1,663,670 bytes at
p50 16 ns = 103,979 B/ns, 203x over the ceiling. The FASTEST honest row ever recorded here runs at
1.30 B/ns, 393x BELOW the ceiling. So the gate has never had a chance to refuse honest work.

Checked on BOTH bracket arms before the bracket selects one -- refusing only the selected arm would
have let the defect choose which arm got audited. A record that cannot state bytes, p50 and observed
threads is refused as unstateable_production_rate; absence is not a passed check.

SELF-TESTS (both --mode render and --mode parse, exit 0): the 16 ns / 1.66 MB fixture refused; the
SAME job at its real 15.856699 ms cost admitted; a 300-byte job at 800 ns admitted -- that is the
negative case that kills any "refuse a p50 below N ns" phrasing, which is the naive fix; unstateable
records refused; ceiling boundary-exact; observed-thread scaling honoured while a merely-requested
count buys nothing.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: with workProofViolation() short-circuited to null, --self-test fails on the
memo-hit fixture in both modes. Source restored byte-identically, sha256
247ef39477412f9a2e42eb72b8577ffec4c1722c38a15f8f0585419856463df4.

NOT CLOSING THIS YET. Items 1 and 2 now exist, but this bead also says the workload cannot support a
render claim until schema_catalog_25 is re-measured under the fixed harness. That run needs a quiet
host and an admitting rch fleet (load1 was 13-27 and rch refused frankenmermaid jobs with
active_project_exclusion through this session). It is bd-hcw3's requalification and should close
both. What must not happen meanwhile is anyone quoting 412.8x or 401,800,000x as a render ratio --
and as of now the harness itself will refuse to print the second one.

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
CROSS-WORKER HAZARD CHECK (fleet-wide advisory 2026-08-15: same cell on two rch workers gave a 13.6x
swing with BOTH A/A nulls passing; a row that does not name its worker is incomparable).

CHECKED, not assumed. This harness is structurally immune, for three reasons already in the code:

1. rch NEVER TIMES ANYTHING HERE. It only compiles. Every measured phase runs on the local host
   under the host-wide quiescence gate, so there is no between-worker comparison to be poisoned.
2. BOTH ARMS ARE THE SAME BINARY, gated: run.mjs:2429-2430 requires
   binaryRecordBefore.elf_sha256 === binaryRecordAfter.elf_sha256 (and equal byte length) before the
   bracket may select an arm.
3. EVERY ROW ALREADY NAMES ITS HOST AND ITS BUILDER, separately: row.host{identity, cpu_model, isa,
   power_policy, physical_cores, logical_threads, ram_bytes, numa_nodes} (run.mjs:2737) and
   row.fm_build{tool, worker, base, clean_overlay} (:2730). So the advisory's requirement (3) is
   satisfied for build provenance as well as measurement provenance.

ALSO CHECKED: the 137-row audit backing the work-proof gate compares each row's result bytes against
that SAME row's own p50. It is a within-row physical bound, never a row-to-row or worker-to-worker
comparison, so the advisory does not touch its win/lose split.

No new gate added for this — adding one would be ceremony over a property the harness already
enforces. Recorded here so the next agent does not re-derive it.

title: Implement flowchart parallel edge syntax (A & B --> C & D)
description:
# Flowchart Parallel Edge Syntax

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
flowchart LR
  A & B --> C & D
\`\`\`
This creates 4 edges: A→C, A→D, B→C, B→D. The & operator allows declaring multiple source/target nodes in a single edge statement.

## Current State
- NOT parsed. The & character is not recognized in edge declarations.
- Mermaid parser's edge AST only supports single source → single target.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: In parse_edge_statement_asts(), before looking for arrow operators, split node references on '&'. If either side contains '&', expand to multiple FlowAst::Edge entries (cartesian product of sources × targets).
2. **Tests**: A & B --> C (2 edges), A --> B & C (2 edges), A & B --> C & D (4 edges), single node (no &, unchanged behavior).

## Considerations
- The & operator is only valid in flowchart, not other diagram types
- Must handle whitespace: 'A&B' vs 'A & B' vs 'A &B'
close_reason: Completed

title: click tooltips are parsed, diffed, and rendered by no backend
description:
MEASURED BY SOURCE-READING under the build freeze (/data 28G, no cargo run).

`click nodeId "url" "some tooltip"` populates IrNodeInteraction.tooltip, and NOTHING renders it:
  fm-render-svg     0 references
  fm-render-canvas  0 references
  fm-render-term    4 references, ALL in diff.rs

The terminal's four are the interesting part: diff.rs reports TooltipChanged and formats 'tooltip: old -> new'. So the engine can tell you a tooltip CHANGED while no backend has ever drawn one. That is the dead-IR-field class this project has already found twice - bd-jgco (gitGraph branch names) and bd-jerh (ER attribute comments) - both parsed, stored, drawn by nothing.

INCUMBENT: mermaid 11.15.0 does `t.tooltip && n.attr("title", t.tooltip)` - a title ATTRIBUTE on the node element, which is what a browser shows on hover. Note this is NOT the same as the `<title>Node: ...` CHILDREN fm-render-svg already emits; those are the a11y name for the shape, and a tooltip is the author's own text.

FIXED FOR SVG in this bead's commit. The emission goes on the same decoration path that already handles href, callback and menu-links. That path is only reached by nodes the streaming fast paths refuse, so all TEN fast-path gates that already carry `node.href().is_none() && node.callback().is_none()` gained `&& node.tooltip().is_none()`. Without that a tooltip-bearing node would take a streaming path and never reach the emission - which is plausibly how the field came to be dead.

STILL OPEN: fm-render-canvas has no way to express a hover tooltip (immediate-mode raster; there is no element to hang an attribute on), so it is arguably N/A there and should be recorded as such rather than left looking unfinished. fm-render-term likewise has no hover, but it could render the tooltip as visible text - that is a product decision, not an omission, and it is NOT taken here.

UNBUILT: no cargo ran. The change is 10 identical one-line gate additions plus one attribute emission.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE SVG HALF IS NOW VERIFIED, AND BOTH "STILL OPEN" ITEMS ARE RESOLVED AS DECISIONS — PINNED, NOT
JUST RECORDED.

1. THE UNBUILT SVG WORK COMPILES AND PASSES. This bead's fix landed under the freeze with "UNBUILT:
   no cargo ran" and ten identical gate additions. Run now: crates/fm-render-svg/tests/click_tooltip.rs
   5 passed, 0 failed — including `a_tooltip_survives_on_nodes_that_would_otherwise_take_a_fast_path`,
   which is the assertion that matters, since the ten `&& node.tooltip().is_none()` gates are what
   stop a tooltip-bearing node taking a streaming path and never reaching the emission. The bead
   guessed that was "plausibly how the field came to be dead"; the test now holds that door shut.

2. CANVAS IS N/A — CONFIRMED, AND FOR A BROADER REASON THAN THE BEAD GAVE. I checked rather than
   accepted it. `fm-render-canvas/src` contains ZERO references to `href`, `callback`, `tooltip`, or
   any hit-region export. So the canvas cannot express ANY of the three interaction features, not
   just tooltips. That reframes the item: it is a DESIGN BOUNDARY of an immediate-mode raster
   surface, not a missing tooltip. Giving the canvas tooltips means designing a hit-region export
   the embedding application consults — a WebGPU/host-integration item (bd-2u0.2 territory), not a
   renderer patch. Recorded so nobody opens it as a small fix.

3. TERMINAL: DECIDED, NOT DEFERRED. The bead left "render the tooltip as visible text" as an untaken
   product decision. Taking it: NO, and the reason is parity. The incumbent does
   `t.tooltip && n.attr("title", t.tooltip)` — a browser shows that ON HOVER. A terminal has no
   hover, so printing it unconditionally displays text mermaid NEVER shows, in every diagram using
   `click`, forever. That is a divergence dressed as a fix. The terminal diff legitimately keeps
   reporting TooltipChanged: comparing two IRs is not rendering one.

BOTH DECISIONS ARE NOW TESTS, because a decision recorded only in prose is one someone
"fixes" later in good faith:
  * fm-render-term/tests/plain_text_contract.rs — a click tooltip and its URL must not appear in the
    terminal body
  * fm-render-canvas/tests/interaction_is_not_drawable.rs — the same for the canvas, plus a CONTROL
    asserting the click declaration really reaches the IR. Without that control, a parser regression
    that dropped `click` entirely would make both assertions pass while the feature vanished
    upstream — which is the exact shape that let this field sit dead in three renderers until this
    bead measured it.

VERIFIED: fm-render-svg click_tooltip 5/5; fm-render-canvas interaction_is_not_drawable 3/3;
fm-render-term plain_text_contract 5/5; clippy -D warnings across both crates exit 0.

WHAT REMAINS on this bead, as far as I can see: nothing that is a defect. The SVG renders it, the
canvas cannot by construction, and the terminal deliberately does not. If someone disagrees with
the terminal decision it is now a one-line test to change and an argument to make, which is the
right shape for a product call.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
STATE TRANSITION GUARDS AND ACTIONS WERE BEING DROPPED FROM THE RENDERED LABEL. Found by sweeping
for the parsed-stored-drawn-by-nothing class this project has now hit four times (bd-jgco gitGraph
branch names, bd-jerh ER attribute comments, bd-bk7h tooltips, and this).

MEASURED. `stateDiagram-v2` with `A --> B: ZZEVENT [ZZGUARD] / ZZACTION`:

    before   svg  event=1 guard=0 action=0     term  event=1 guard=0 action=0
    after    svg  event=1 guard=1 action=1     term  event=1 guard=1 action=1

The IR held `guard: "ZZGUARD"` and `action: "ZZACTION"` the whole time. `IrEdge::guard()` and
`IrEdge::action()` have ZERO call sites in any renderer, so the parser was splitting the author's
description into three parts and drawing only one of them.

⚠️ THE INCUMBENT CHECK IS WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DIFFERENCE, and it nearly went the
other way. mermaid 11.15.0 has no guard/action concept for state diagrams at all: its only
`guardCondition` occurrences are Langium PARSER-GENERATOR internals (`subrule`, `rule.ref`,
`terminal`), not state semantics. So mermaid renders the whole post-`:` description verbatim, and
stripping it lost author text the reference shows. Had `guardCondition` turned out to be state
machinery, the split might have been the parity-correct behaviour.

FIXED at the parser: the edge label is now the author's full text, and the structured guard/action
are extracted AS WELL, not INSTEAD. They stay because they are the right shape for a consumer that
wants the parts — the defect was never that they exist, only that the label was cut down to feed
them.

ZERO GOLDEN CHURN, checked before editing: no golden .mmd contains a state transition with a guard.

title: gantt date axis is drawn on top unconditionally; mermaid defaults to bottom
description:
WE DRAW THE GANTT DATE AXIS ON TOP UNCONDITIONALLY. mermaid draws it at the BOTTOM by default - the
pinned bundle's gantt config reads `topAxis:!1` - and `topAxis` is the directive that moves it up.

So the divergence is INVERTED from what it looks like: a gantt chart WITHOUT `topAxis`, which is the
overwhelmingly common case, is the one that differs from the incumbent. A chart WITH it happens to
match us by accident.

Evidence:
  fm-render-svg   `let tick_y = layout.bounds.y + offset_y - 12.0;`  (above the diagram bounds)
  fm-render-term  the tick overlay writes on the row ABOVE the diagram body, by its own comment
  incumbent       gantt config default `topAxis:!1`, i.e. bottom

ALREADY DONE in the parser: `topAxis` is recognised and ignored rather than reported as
"unsupported gantt syntax". That warning was false on valid input, and ignoring the directive is
correct precisely BECAUSE we already draw what it asks for. What is NOT done is the default.

SCOPE: LayoutAxisTick carries only `label` and `position` (an x), so the y is chosen independently by
each renderer. Fixing the default therefore needs an axis-placement flag on IrGanttMeta plus
placement logic in fm-render-svg, fm-render-term and fm-render-canvas - three renderers and a new IR
field, which is not a parser change and should not be written unbuilt.

⚠️ EXPECT GOLDEN CHURN: moving the default axis position changes every gantt golden. Re-bless only
after diffing, and check that the terminal's band-label row scan (bd-039t) still finds a clear row -
that fix depends on the blank run between the tick row and the top of the chart box, which moving
the axis would relocate.

comments.author: BlackThrush
comments.text:
THIS BEAD'S PLANNED FIX IS WRONG IN ONE LOAD-BEARING WAY: `topAxis` ADDS an axis, it does not MOVE one. Read out of the pinned bundle (sha256 70137e77bb273bb2ef972b86e8b0400cca8be53cb25bfc45911a186dc98665de, verified against pins.json before reading), mermaid 11.15.0's gantt renderer does this:

  g.append("g").attr("class","grid").attr("transform","translate("+N+", "+(D-50)+")").call(L)...   <- ALWAYS
  if (i.db.topAxisEnabled() || n.topAxis) { ... g.append(...).attr("class","grid").attr("transform","translate("+N+", "+P+")").call($) }   <- ADDITIONAL

The bottom axis at `D-50` is unconditional. The `topAxis` branch appends a SECOND `g.grid` at the top padding `P`, built from a separate axis generator. The config default is `topAxis:!1`.

So the divergence is two defects, not one:
  1. a gantt WITHOUT `topAxis` (the common case) shows an axis on top where mermaid shows one on the bottom;
  2. a gantt WITH `topAxis` would show ONE axis where mermaid shows TWO.
A fix that reads the flag as "put the axis on top instead of the bottom" closes (1) and leaves (2) open, and would look correct on every chart that omits the directive.

WHERE THE GEOMETRY MUST LIVE, which changes the scope note on this bead. The bead says LayoutAxisTick carries only label and position "so the y is chosen independently by each renderer". That independence is already a live defect and must not be extended: fm-render-svg's gantt arm uses `layout.bounds.y + offset_y + 12.0` (render_gantt_svg, lib.rs:5903), while fm-render-canvas's draw_axis_ticks uses `layout.bounds.y + offset_y - 12.0` (renderer.rs, the `MINUS TWELVE, matching fm-render-svg` comment from 13fa861a). Those two cannot both be right. 13fa861a settled the sign against the generic loop at lib.rs:4056 in `render_layout_to_svg`, which gantt never reaches because the gantt arm early-returns before it, so the canvas was matched to the wrong sibling. NOT YET CONFIRMED by execution - both sites are read off source, and offset_y would have to differ between the two arms for them to agree, which I have not shown either way. Filed here rather than acted on.

Because of that, and because a bottom axis sits outside every node box `compute_bounds` measured, the placement belongs in fm-layout, published as rows the renderers merely draw - the precedent this codebase already set for gantt labels (bd-h9gx) and state notes: "only layout can grow the canvas to hold it. A renderer-only placement lands outside the viewBox and is clipped." `extend_bounds_for_gantt_labels` currently extends X only, so a bottom row also needs bounds.height grown by the tick line extent (label baseline y, line y+4..y+16) or it clips.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, DELIBERATELY. I wrote the IrGanttMeta.top_axis field and the parser read, then backed both out byte-clean rather than leave them in the tree: without the three renderer consumers the flag is parsed-stored-read-by-nothing, which is the exact class bd-jgco/bd-jerh/bd-bk7h are filed under, and this bead's own scope note says it "should not be written unbuilt". The rch fleet refused three times with `queue_timeout` (exit 103) while the wider suite held 3/29 slots, so I could not compile, and the change additionally needs a second build to re-bless the gantt goldens. Returned to open with the research banked rather than half-landed.

Also unchanged and still true: the terminal band-label row scan (bd-039t) depends on the blank run between the tick row and the top of the chart box, so moving the default axis must re-check it.

title: Print CSS neutralizes text fill and shape stroke but not node gradient fill
description:
Found by auditing bd-3gq's capability list against its five closed children. 'Print optimization' is the one capability with NO child bead, and it is only partly delivered. Filed as its own bead rather than reopening a closed child, per instruction.

CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not inspection. Rendered a single-node flowchart with print_optimized: true, node_gradients: true, glow_enabled: true and dumped the emitted @media print block verbatim. It contains exactly three rules:

  .fm-node text, .fm-edge-labeled text, .fm-cluster-label { font-size: 8.0px !important; fill: #111 !important; }
  .fm-node path, .fm-node rect, .fm-node circle, .fm-edge { stroke: #111 !important; }
  .fm-cluster { fill: #fff !important; stroke: #666 !important; }

The second rule targets .fm-node rect and sets ONLY stroke. Nothing sets node FILL. The body meanwhile emits:

  <rect x="92" y="92" width="148.73" height="66.50" rx="5.50" fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)"/>

so every node prints with its gradient intact. Clusters get fill: #fff for print; nodes do not. That asymmetry is the bug — print already decided flat white is correct for a container, then left the nodes gradient-filled.

WHY IT MATTERS: gradient fills waste ink and reproduce inconsistently across print pipelines, which is the entire reason a print stylesheet exists. It is also an internal incoherence: bd-3gq.1 added gradients, print optimization is on by DEFAULT (print_optimized defaults true and the CSS is embedded by default), so the default configuration ships a print mode that does not neutralize the default visual effect.

OBSERVABLE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Render with print_optimized + node_gradients. The @media print block must contain a rule whose selector matches node shapes and which sets fill to a flat print colour with !important, so it beats the inline fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)" presentation attribute. CSS beats presentation attributes, so a rule is sufficient and the body needs no change.
2. NEGATIVE CONTROL: with node_gradients FALSE, the print block must be unchanged from today — this fix must not alter output for diagrams that never had a gradient.
3. NEGATIVE CONTROL: the non-print CSS must be byte-identical before and after. Only the @media print block may move.
4. A test asserting the printed fill rule exists, that fails if the rule is removed. Assert on the print block specifically, bounded at its closing braces — do NOT substring-search the whole document. I made exactly that mistake while probing this: splitting on '@media print' and searching the remainder matched the <filter id="node-glow"> DEF further down the file and produced a false 'print handles filters' reading.

⚠️ GOLDEN IMPACT IS BROAD. print_optimized defaults to true and the print CSS is embedded by default, so changing print_css moves the <style> block of essentially EVERY SVG golden. That needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note and a semantic diff showing only the print block moved. That breadth is why this is filed rather than slipped in alongside the audit.

UNVERIFIED, do not treat as fact: in the same dump the <filter id="node-glow"> def was emitted while no element in the output referenced it, which would be dead output weight. That may be specific to the streaming path with embedded CSS — glow is applied via group.filter("url(#node-glow)") at lib.rs:9218, which that path may not reach. Worth a separate check; not filed as a defect because I did not confirm it across configurations.
close_reason:
Fixed in dcdefbb5.

FIX: print_css now emits, only when node_gradients is on, a rule neutralising the gradient's own stops:

  #fm-node-gradient stop { stop-color: #fff !important; stop-opacity: 1 !important; }

WHY THE STOPS AND NOT node FILL — this is the load-bearing design decision. The gradient reaches nodes as an inline fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)" presentation attribute, so ANY css fill rule beats it. But such a rule would equally beat classDef fills and solid shapes like FilledCircle, flattening colour an author chose deliberately. That collateral would have looked plausible, because print_css ALREADY overrides classDef stroke with !important, so 'print flattens user styling' is established precedent here. Restyling the paint server's stops changes exactly the one wrong thing and nothing else.

I WAS WRONG IN THIS BEAD'S OWN FILING, correcting for the record: I warned the fix would move nearly every golden because print CSS is embedded by default. It moves NONE. The fixtures pin node_gradients: false (golden_svg_test.rs:145), so they never take the new branch. golden_svg_test 3/3 and golden_layout_test 2/2 pass untouched — no bless, no GOLDEN-CHANGE note needed. Gating on the flag is what turned a broad-churn change into a zero-churn one.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all met:
1. Print block contains a rule flattening the gradient for print — yes, via stops.
2. Gradients-off print block unchanged — asserted as negative control 1; this is what keeps the goldens still.
3. Non-print CSS byte-identical — only the @media print branch is touched, and only when gradients are on.
4. Test fails if the rule is removed — verified by mutation: forcing the branch off fails with 'print block must flatten the gradient stops'. It reads the print block BOUNDED at its closing braces, per the warning in this bead, and negative control 2 asserts the fix does not reach for node fill.

Gates: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast RC=0 with all 40 binaries green; fm-render-svg 276 pass / 0 fail (up from 275); clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings RC=0; ubs exit 0.

STILL UNVERIFIED and deliberately not actioned: the same dump showed <filter id="node-glow"> emitted with nothing referencing it, which would be dead output weight. Glow is applied via group.filter("url(#node-glow)") at lib.rs:9218, which the streaming path with embedded CSS may not reach. Not filed as a defect because I confirmed it in only one configuration.

title: Identify the 64 B allocation that is 40% of dense-graph layout allocs at 0.75/node
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-oarm, which was REJECTED on measurement (see its comment and the ledger row at
docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md). The arena premise did not reproduce, but ONE bucket did, and it is a
real, small, well-localised target rather than a phase-wide refactor.

MEASURED (crates/fm-layout/tests/alloc_profile.rs, worker vmi1264463):
  dense_dag_200  200 nodes / 790 edges  -> 150 of 401 allocations are exactly 64 B  (37.4%)
  dense_dag_800  800 nodes / 3190 edges -> 600 of 1452 allocations are exactly 64 B (41.3%)
  chain_100 / chain_1000 / wide_8x16 / wide_16x32 -> 1, 1, 2, 4.

TWO PROPERTIES THAT SHOULD MAKE THIS EASY TO FIND:
  - Exactly 0.75 per node on BOTH dense fixtures. It scales with node count, not edge count.
  - It appears only at high fanout. chain (fanout 1) and wide (fanout 2) are ~0; dense_dag (fanout 4)
    is ~0.75/node. So something allocates per node only when that node's degree crosses a threshold,
    which smells like a spilled inline buffer -- 64 B is 8 usizes, or a SmallVec/ArrayVec spill, or a
    Vec grown to capacity 8.

ALREADY RULED OUT by reading: the obstacle spatial index. It is CSR (offsets: Vec<u32>, flat:
Vec<u32>) with no per-cell Vec, so it cannot be producing a per-node 64 B allocation.

HOW TO PIN IT: extend alloc_profile.rs to capture a backtrace when layout.size() == 64. Capturing a
backtrace inside a GlobalAlloc allocates, so it needs a reentrancy guard -- a thread_local Cell
initialised with `const { Cell::new(false) }` so the TLS itself never lazily allocates -- and the
captured frames must be pushed somewhere that is also guarded. Without the guard this recurses and
aborts.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WORTH LANDING: the honest headroom is small. dense_dag_800 does 1,452 allocations
for a 3,190-edge layout; removing 600 of them is a real work removal but on a base that is already
tiny, so gate it on INSTRUCTIONS with an A/A null and expect a low single-digit percentage at best.
Do NOT re-open the arena on the strength of this -- that is the lever the measurement just rejected.

title: Composite states always fail node_id_set: the container is not counted and its scoped pseudo-states are
description:
Every composite-state diagram failed `node_id_set_vs_input` against a CORRECT render. Two independent
causes in the same comparison, found by running the existing oracle over the committed goldens.

MEASURED on golden/state_composite:
  truth  (11): complete, computing, error, fork_state, formatting, idle, join_state, processing,
               taska, taskb, validating
  render (12): __state_end__state_processing, __state_start__state_processing, complete, computing,
               error, fork_state, formatting, idle, join_state, taska, taskb, validating

One id missing, two extra — and the render is right on both counts.

CAUSE 1, the missing one. `state Processing { … }` is a state you can BE IN: the source names it and
transitions point at it (`Idle --> Processing : start`), so `groundTruth` puts it in `node_ids`. The
renderer draws it — correctly, and like mermaid — as a cluster box with a label rather than a node
group, so it carries no `data-id` and `signature` never saw it:
  <rect id="fm-cluster-0" … class="fm-cluster"/><text class="fm-cluster-label">Processing</text>

CAUSE 2, the two extra ones. A `[*]` INSIDE a composite renders as `__state_start__state_Processing`
/ `__state_end__state_Processing`, one pair per composite. `isSyntheticNode` matched only the
diagram-level `__state_start` / `__state_end`, so the composite-scoped forms were counted as real
states that the source never declared.

Either cause alone fails the invariant, which is why both are fixed together and each is asserted
separately: a later change could repair one and silently reintroduce the other, and the totals would
still look wrong in the same way.

FIX. `isSyntheticNode` gains a trailing `(?:__.*)?` so scoped pseudo states are filtered; and for the
`state` family ONLY, `fm-cluster-label` texts join the rendered node set. Restricted to `state`
deliberately: a flowchart `subgraph` is a grouping, not a node you can transition to, and folding its
label into the node set there would admit output that had genuinely lost a node.

TESTS, four, including two that guard the fix against being too permissive:
  composite_scoped_pseudo_states_are_synthetic          — the scoped forms filter, the plain one still does
  a_real_state_named_like_a_pseudo_state_is_not_filtered — `started`, `endpoint`, `restart` are NOT synthetic
  composite_state_container_counts_as_its_state          — the container supplies the missing id
  composite_state_container_does_not_hide_a_dropped_state — delete a real state and it must STILL fail

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: removing the scoped-pseudo-state filter fails
`composite_scoped_pseudo_states_are_synthetic`, exit 1; source restored byte-identically, sha256
f9ece7b1984d1fa0ec6600676f721bb904ca96054ad8647ffd8fad9a41c8e8b9.

GATE: `svg_equivalence --self-test` 66 cases / 16 mutation controls / 4 negative controls exit 0;
`run.mjs --self-test` exit 0.

CORPUS EFFECT: state_composite moves DIVERGENT -> unverified, not -> verified. That is the honest
outcome and not a half-fix: the `state` family also requires `edge_topology_vs_input`, which stays
undecidable for this document, and an undecidable invariant is not a pass. Across the 37 golden pairs
the audit is now verified 15 / unverified 20 / divergent 2, down from divergent 4 at the start of
this sweep.

STILL DIVERGENT, and deliberately NOT claimed as defects here:
  malformed_recovery [flowchart] — a deliberately malformed fixture whose parser RECOVERS, so a naive
    source decode legitimately disagrees. Establish which side is right before touching either.
  sequence_advanced [sequence]   — `sequence_source_tokens_vs_output` fails; likely alt/loop/par
    syntax the token decoder does not model.
close_reason: Fixed in the same pass: isSyntheticNode gains a trailing (?:__.*)? for composite-scoped pseudo states, and fm-cluster-label texts join the rendered node set for the state family only. Four tests including two over-permissiveness guards (a real state named started/endpoint/restart is not filtered; a dropped state still fails despite the container id). Negative control run, byte-identical restore sha256 f9ece7b1…e8b9. Gate: svg_equivalence --self-test 66 cases exit 0, run.mjs --self-test exit 0. state_composite moves DIVERGENT -> unverified (edge_topology stays undecidable, and undecidable is not a pass)

title: Spacing hints in the IR: DOT nodesep/ranksep change the drawn gaps
description:
The one attribute pair bd-o1yq said needed IR SURFACE rather than wiring, now built. DOT `nodesep`
and `ranksep` change the drawn gaps.

WHY IT NEEDED NEW SURFACE. `LayoutSpacing` lives in `LayoutConfig`, which a parser cannot reach — the
parser produces IR. So this adds two hint fields to `MermaidDiagramMeta`, beside the existing
`block_beta_columns`, and fm-layout overlays them on the spacing it was configured with. The
precedent matters: layout already reads `ir.meta.block_beta_columns` and
`ir.meta.init.config.sequence_mirror_actors`, so a source-level hint reaching layout through meta is
the established pattern here, not a new one.

  DOT `nodesep=0.5`  -> meta.node_spacing = Some(36)
  DOT `ranksep=1.0`  -> meta.rank_spacing = Some(72)

UNITS ARE A DELIBERATE CHOICE, NOT AN ACCIDENT. graphviz measures both in INCHES; the layout works in
units. 72 per inch matches the points-per-inch convention the fontsize mapping already uses (bd-hc5y),
so the two conversions agree rather than each inventing a scale. Values are ROUNDED, not truncated: a
cast would turn nodesep=0.49 (35.28 units) into 35 by flooring every fractional request, and there is
a test at exactly that value.

WHOLE UNITS, and this is load-bearing rather than laziness. `MermaidDiagramMeta` derives `Eq` because
fm-layout's incremental memo compares `*meta == current.meta` by value; `Option<f32>` would break that
derive. Whole units also cost nothing observable, since layout coordinates are whole units anyway.

THE MEMO TRAP WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. `memo_ir_equal` destructures the IR and compares whole `meta`
by value, so the new fields enter the equality probe automatically — an edit that changes spacing
cannot reuse a cached layout. This is the failure mode a previous bead recorded (new IR fields must
reach the equality probe or the memo silently serves stale geometry), and here the whole-value
comparison handles it by construction.

BOTH LAYOUT PATHS were updated, which is the easy half to miss: the full path AND the incremental
recompute path resolve spacing through the same helper. Wiring only the full path would leave an
edited diagram silently re-laying part of itself at default gaps.

TESTS: 5 parser unit tests (inch conversion for both keys, the 0.49 rounding case, an absent-hint
control proving None is preserved so the layout keeps its own default, the `ranksep="0.75 equally"`
list form, non-numeric values warning) plus an end-to-end test asserting ranksep widens the RANK gap
and nodesep widens the IN-RANK gap between two siblings — the second needs two children to be
observable at all.

ONE OF MY OWN TESTS CORRECTLY FAILED AGAIN, for the second bead running: bd-mf4d's
unsupported-attribute list included nodesep and ranksep, which are now implemented, so warning about
them would be the false report. The list is down to ratio, size and splines, with a comment saying the
shrinking is the intended direction.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p fm-core --lib -> 0 (408 passed); cargo test -p fm-layout --lib -> 0 (471
passed); cargo test -p fm-parser --lib -> 0 (501 passed); cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli -> 0 (26
targets); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -> 0.

NO GOLDEN MOVED, and this one deserved the check more than the previous beads: the change touches
fm-layout, so a Mermaid diagram COULD have moved. It did not, because the hints are None for every
Mermaid source today — `spacing_with_source_hints` is an identity function when both are None. The
Mermaid golden suites pass unblessed, and the single dirty golden file (layout_checksums.json) is
another lane's pre-existing working-tree change from before this session (last commit a656acc4,
bd-f3tc), never staged by me.

FOLLOW-UP NOW CHEAP: Mermaid's own `%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 60, "rankSpacing": 90}}}%%`
is ALSO unsupported today — `rg nodeSpacing` finds nothing in fm-parser or fm-core. It sets exactly
these two meta fields, so it is now a small change in the init handling rather than new machinery.
That is the natural next increment and the reason the fields are named neutrally (`node_spacing`, not
`dot_nodesep`).

title: mindmap: default node and [square] node render identically; mermaid types them distinctly
description:
MEASURED by content hash: in a mindmap, `A` and `A[A]` produce BYTE-IDENTICAL SVG. Both parse to NodeShape::Rect.

Every OTHER mindmap shape is captured and rendered distinctly, so this is a single collision and not a broken feature:
  default  -> Rect      (svg 6202)
  square   -> Rect      (svg 6202)   <-- collides with default
  rounded  -> Rounded   (svg 6211)
  circle   -> Circle    (svg 6182)
  bang     -> Asymmetric(svg 6215)
  cloud    -> Cloud     (svg 6901)
  hexagon  -> Hexagon   (svg 6221)

INCUMBENT EVIDENCE, and its LIMIT stated honestly. mermaid 11.15.0's mindmap node-type enum has DEFAULT:0 and RECT:2 as DISTINCT values, alongside NO_BORDER, ROUNDED_RECT, CIRCLE:3, CLOUD:4, BANG:5, HEXAGON:6. An enum carrying separate values for default and rect strongly implies they draw differently. BUT I could NOT isolate mermaid's mindmap draw switch in the minified bundle to observe the visual difference directly - the `nodeType` hits in that bundle are DOMPurify's DOM nodeType, not the mindmap enum.

NOT ACTIONED, deliberately. Making the mindmap DEFAULT shape differ from Rect changes the appearance of EVERY mindmap that does not use explicit brackets - a wide blast radius - and I cannot state what it should look like without observing mermaid's actual output. Guessing a new default is worse than the current collision.

TO CLOSE THIS: render `mindmap / root((R)) / A` and `mindmap / root((R)) / A[A]` through mermaid (the head-to-head harness can dump SVG with --dump-svg) and compare. If DEFAULT draws without a border while RECT draws one, give mindmap a distinct default shape and keep Rect for the bracketed form. If they match, close as NOT A DEFECT and record it, because the collision then reflects the incumbent.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED. This bead was NOT ACTIONED because "I cannot state what it should look like without observing mermaid's actual output". I found that out by reading the pinned bundle, so the blocker is gone.

INCUMBENT, from mermaid 11.15.0's mindmap type switch:
    DEFAULT      -> "no-border"
    RECT         -> "rect"
    ROUNDED_RECT -> "rounded-rect"
    CIRCLE -> "circle"   CLOUD -> "cloud"   BANG -> "bang"   HEXAGON -> "hexgon" (their typo)
    default      -> "no-border"
with DEFAULT:0 and NO_BORDER:0 sharing a value. So mermaid's default mindmap node is BORDERLESS and a [square] one is a rectangle. The bead's earlier note could not isolate this because it searched `nodeType`, which in that bundle is DOMPurify's DOM nodeType; the mindmap switch is reachable via the shape-NAME strings instead.

Also observed, and it decided the implementation: mermaid draws the difference in CSS, not geometry. `defaultBkg` appends a path classed `node-bkg node-<type>` plus a separate bottom LINE, and the type reaches the output as a CSS class.

SO NO NEW NodeShape VARIANT. A default mindmap node now carries a `mindmap-no-border` marker class, with a stylesheet rule dropping the stroke. That mirrors the incumbent AND avoids auditing 172 `NodeShape::` sites in fm-render-svg alone (plus 41 in layout, 29 in term) - which is not something to do unbuilt. I checked that count before choosing, rather than assuming as I did last turn.

CLASS NAME CHOSEN AGAINST A KNOWN TRAP: the node-class emitter runs a SUBSTRING keyword scan (`active`, `dim`, `disabled`, `dashed-border`, `double-border`, ...) and this project has been bitten by `inactive` matching `active`. I checked `mindmap-no-border` against every trigger before using it - the border keywords are full hyphenated tokens, so "no-border" does not fire, and there is no "dim"/"active" substring hiding in "mindmap".

DISCRIMINATOR CANNOT DRIFT: `mindmap_token_is_default_shaped` and `parse_mindmap_node_token` now share one `mindmap_token_core` helper, so "took the default branch" and "has no delimiter" are the same question by construction. Two copies of the `:::` strip would have mislabelled any node whose class suffix contains a bracket.

TESTS (crates/fm-render-svg/tests/mindmap_default_shape.rs):
  * the two sources no longer render identically - the bead's own measurement, inverted
  * non-vacuity: the marker marks the DEFAULT node and not the square one
  * THE MARKER CLASS HAS A CSS RULE, asserted inside the <style> block, not merely present as a class attribute. A class with no rule changes bytes and not the picture; this project shipped semantic CSS behind a cosmetic gate once already (bd-w0f0)
  * control: rounded/circle/hexagon/bang/cloud stay unmarked, so a change that marked every node fails
  * control: `A:::cls` is still default-shaped, pinning the shared-core behaviour

⚠️ THE BLESSED GOLDEN WILL MOVE. crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/mindmap_basic.svg is entirely default-shaped nodes (`Branch A`, `Leaf 1`, ...), so every one gains the marker class and the stylesheet gains a rule. It CANNOT be re-blessed under the freeze. The first builder after the freeze must re-bless it and eyeball the diff: expected changes are the added class token on mindmap nodes and one added CSS rule, nothing geometric. If anything MOVES positionally, that is not this change and should be investigated.

⚠️ The mindmap_square KNOWN_GAP in feature_parity.rs is kept with corrected text and marked EXPECTED TO GO STALE - that list is checked in both directions, so the first build should fail naming it, and deleting it is the intended response.

title: state concurrency-region divider is drawn by the SVG only
description:
The `--` concurrency separator inside a composite state is drawn by fm-render-svg and by neither other surface.

`state Big { A --> B  --  C --> D }` declares two regions running in parallel. The layout records the boundary in extensions.cluster_dividers - built by build_state_cluster_dividers, keyed on the __state_region_ subgraphs the `--` creates - and fm-render-svg draws a dashed line per divider. fm-render-canvas and fm-render-term referenced that extension NOWHERE, so the two regions ran together into one box and a reader could not tell there were two. The separator is syntax the author wrote, not decoration.

FOUND BY DIFFING WHICH LAYOUT EXTENSIONS EACH RENDERER CONSUMES. That is the comparison that works. An earlier pass in the same session compared the CONFIG FIELD sequence_mirror_actors and wrongly flagged the canvas as missing mirrored headers - layout had already applied the flag, and the canvas consumes the derived sequence_mirror_headers instead. Compare what a renderer READS, not what it is configured by. Of thirteen layout extensions, exactly two are SVG-only: cluster_dividers (this bead) and node_centrality, which is an emphasis hint rather than declared content.

DONE: canvas. Draws a dashed line per divider, matching the SVG stroke-dasharray("6,4") that distinguishes a region boundary from an ordinary cluster edge, and resets the dash so nothing later inherits it.

REMAINING: fm-render-term. It has a character grid rather than coordinates, but a line primitive already exists there - the gantt today marker uses draw_line on the canvas layer - so this should reuse that rather than invent placement, the same way ER cardinality reused the class-cardinality placement (bd-2h3pp). Check first whether a dashed run is even legible at cell resolution; a solid rule may be the honest choice.

NO TEST YET - unbuilt. When builds return: a composite state with a `--` separator must produce a stroked path on the canvas that a state WITHOUT the separator does not.

comments.author: WindyRiver
comments.text:
TERMINAL HALF LANDED — the bead is now complete across all three surfaces, and its named probe passes on both of the ones that were missing it.

fm-render-term draws one dashed rule per entry in extensions.cluster_dividers, on the CANVAS layer rather than the text overlay for the reason the gantt today marker already gives in that file: the overlay carries state names, and a rule written there would erase one.

DASHED, not solid, and that is the load-bearing decision. render_cluster_canvas draws the composite state's own border with draw_rect, which is SOLID — so a solid divider is indistinguishable from a second box edge. The dash is the only channel at cell resolution that carries "region boundary", and it survives sub-cell quantisation: braille packs 2 pixels per column, so the 3-on/3-off cadence the sequence lifeline already uses on this canvas alternates set and clear cells rather than filling every one. The SVG carries the same distinction with stroke-dasharray(6,4).

The dash helper is written PARAMETRICALLY, not as a horizontal special case, even though every divider build_state_cluster_dividers emits today has start.y == end.y. A horizontal-only routine would silently place a future vertical divider at the wrong y instead of failing — the same shape as the state-note leader bug that cast a negative coordinate to usize and lost the line entirely.

THE BEAD SAID "NO TEST YET - unbuilt" AND NAMED THE PROBE IT WANTED. Both halves now have it:
  crates/fm-render-term/tests/state_concurrency_divider.rs      6 passed
  crates/fm-render-canvas/tests/state_concurrency_divider.rs    4 passed
The canvas half had landed under the freeze with no test at all; that gap is closed here too.

ISOLATED BY A MECHANISM CONTROL, which is the part worth reusing. Deleting the "--" from the source changes the region structure and therefore the whole placement, so a diff between two SOURCES would be dominated by relayout and would prove nothing about the divider. Every test instead renders the SAME ir and the SAME layout twice through render_term_with_layout_and_config / render_to_canvas_with_layout, differing only in whether extensions.cluster_dividers is populated. title: GPU plan omits clusters entirely: subgraph boxes and labels are absent, silently
description:
GpuRenderPlan carries node_instances, edge_segments, arrowheads, text_quads, text_runs and
glyph_atlas. There is no cluster primitive of any kind. So a diagram with subgraphs renders on the
GPU path with its NODES AND EDGES BUT NO CONTAINERS -- no box, no border, no cluster label -- and
nothing in the type, the docs or the tests says so.

BIGGER THAN THE STYLING FAMILY it sits next to. Those five (stroke width a3157251, label colour
58564713, opacity a2b268c5, font size 54d5f637, dash bd-l3nsf) are a declared PROPERTY reaching one
surface and not the other. This is missing GEOMETRY: the subgraph a user drew is not there at all.

FIVE RESOLVERS ALREADY EXIST AND ARE UNREACHABLE FROM THE GPU PATH -- resolve_cluster_colors,
resolve_cluster_dash_array, resolve_cluster_opacity, resolve_cluster_stroke_width,
resolve_cluster_text_color, all pub(crate) in renderer.rs and all consumed only by the Canvas2D
pass. That is the same asymmetric-sibling shape one level up, and note the structural gate added in
16ffa88f DOES NOT COVER IT: that gate scans `resolve_node_*` names only, so it is green today while
this gap is wide open. A gate that covers one level and reads as covering the family is its own
hazard -- extending it to `resolve_cluster_*` should happen WITH the fix, not before, or it just
fails loudly with nothing to consume.

⚠️ THE TEST FIXTURE CANNOT NOTICE. The only two occurrences of "cluster" in gpu_plan.rs are
`clusters: Vec::new()` and `cycle_clusters: Vec::new()` in a test layout builder. Every GPU plan
test runs against a diagram with ZERO subgraphs, so no existing test could fail on this and adding
per-property tests would not help either. A fixture that cannot express the case is the same defect
class as the kanban fix that passed its own hand-built fixture while being unreachable from parser
output (bd-u3fo).

WHAT A FIX NEEDS, in dependency order:
  1. A GpuClusterInstance (bounds, fill, stroke, stroke width, opacity) plus its vertex attributes
     and a WGSL struct -- the ABI guard from d1d9b587 makes that edit safe and will fail if the
     three descriptions drift.
  2. Cluster labels through the existing text pass, which already resolves per-run font size and
     colour; cluster label colour has its own resolver.
  3. DRAW ORDER. Clusters must be emitted BEHIND their contents or the container paints over the
     nodes inside it. The Canvas2D pass draws clusters first for exactly this reason, and the
     cluster-opacity work landed by a peer notes that globalAlpha had to be restored so it did not
     fade the nodes drawn afterwards.
  4. A fixture with a real subgraph, added FIRST -- otherwise the tests cannot distinguish
     "implemented" from "still empty".

NOT A REGRESSION: the GPU pass has never drawn clusters. This is filed because it is SILENT, not
because it broke.
close_reason: done

title: CI cargo fmt --check is red on main: 17 pre-existing diffs across six files
description:
MEASURED. CI ci.yml:107 runs `cargo fmt --check`. On main it exits 1 with 17 diffs across six
files, none of them in code added this session (my own four violations are fixed in a0a625b2):

  crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs   371, 445, 518, 538
  crates/fm-core/src/cga.rs                2711, 2721
  crates/fm-core/src/lib.rs                1105, 5655
  crates/fm-layout/benches/cga_transforms.rs      44
  crates/fm-layout/benches/incremental_layout.rs  17, 26
  crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs              1682, 9484, 14853, 16654, 16680
  crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs          15891

All 17 are pure layout: a match arm rustfmt wants collapsed onto one line, an `assert_eq!` it wants
split across three, a tuple it wants exploded. No semantic content.

SECOND RED GATE OF THE SAME CLASS as bd-wra5 (the default-feature clippy break, fixed in db5e254c).
Both were red on committed main while nobody was looking, and both are cheap to fix — the reason
they sat is that a red gate nobody watches stops being a signal.

WHY I DID NOT JUST RUN `cargo fmt`, which is the obvious one-command fix. Four of the six files are
under active edit by other lanes in this shared checkout (fm-layout/src/lib.rs above all, plus
fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs which changed twice today). A repo-wide reformat rewrites regions
those lanes have in flight, and formatting churn is the worst kind of conflict to resolve because
every hunk looks equally plausible. It is a coordination action, not a lane action.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE, for whoever owns fleet coordination:
1. Announce a short freeze on the six files, or wait for a moment when `git status` shows them clean.
2. Run `cargo fmt` once, at the root, unmodified.
3. Commit it alone, touching nothing else, so the diff is verifiably formatting-only —
   `git show --stat` should list exactly those six files and no others.
4. Confirm `cargo fmt --check` exits 0 before landing.
Do NOT let lanes fix these piecemeal: two lanes formatting overlapping regions of
fm-layout/src/lib.rs at once produces exactly the conflict this is trying to avoid.

NOTE ON WHY THIS DRIFTED, worth keeping. A local `rustfmt <file>` is NOT equivalent to `cargo fmt`
for a file with submodules: running rustfmt on crates/fm-core/src/lib.rs also reformats cga.rs and
lens_tests.rs because it follows `mod` declarations. That is why I hand-formatted my own fm-core
hunks instead — and it is a plausible route by which a lane "formatted its file" and still left the
gate red, or reformatted a peer's file without meaning to.
close_reason: Fixed in 487a0918: single unmodified root cargo fmt during the clean-tree window the bead specified. cargo fmt --check exits 0 (was 1); workspace clippy -D warnings clean; fm-core 408 / fm-render-svg 283 / golden_svg_test 39 all pass. Formatting-only commit verified by pathspec; peer WIP untouched.

title: A byte golden cannot see that its own output is structurally broken: add a corpus health check
description: MOTIVATED BY A DEFECT THE GOLDENS COULD NOT SEE. gantt_basic.svg referenced marker-end=url(#arrowhead) against an empty <defs> in EVERY committed revision, so every gantt arrowhead silently failed to draw and every byte comparison passed - the snapshot pinned that the output does not CHANGE and was blind to it being wrong in a way it had always been wrong (bd-8zo0). scripts/golden_svg_health.mjs adds the four checks a byte golden cannot make for itself, each a distinct failure mode rather than a style preference: dangling_reference (points at an id it never defines, so the marker/gradient/clip simply does not apply); duplicate_id (invalid SVG, and url(#id) resolves to whichever element the viewer picks); non_finite_number (a NaN coordinate does not misplace an element, it REMOVES it, so content loss reads as a rendering that looks fine); bare_ampersand (not well-formed XML, a strict consumer refuses the whole document); bad_viewbox (missing or degenerate, so the diagram is unscalable or invisible). It reads what is COMMITTED rather than re-rendering, so it also catches a golden re-blessed from a broken build. TEN SELF-TEST CASES, one per check plus a healthy-document case (without which every other case is meaningless) and an escaped-entity case proving &/'/' are not flagged. CI: the self-test is wired into the ledger-integrity-guard job now and passes. THE CORPUS SCAN IS DELIBERATELY NOT ARMED YET - it exits 1 on the two committed gantt_basic.svg copies, and arming it before bd-8zo0's fix and re-blessed golden land together would put main red on a defect main already has. bd-8zo0 adds that line in the same commit as the golden, so the fix cannot land without its regression net and the net cannot land without the fix. GATE: node scripts/golden_svg_health.mjs --self-test exit 0 (10 cases); the scan reports scanned=74 violations=2 exit 1, which is the correct verdict today; workflow parses (yaml.safe_load) and the full CI step body runs exit 0.

Corpus scan intentionally left unarmed until bd-8zo0's fix and golden land together (it correctly exits 1 on the two gantt_basic copies today), so the fix and its regression net must land in one commit. title: render on a nonexistent file silently renders the FILENAME as a diagram instead of erroring
description:
FOUND while gating bd-2f5y, by a control that asserted a missing input file must not exit 0. It does exit 0.

MEASURED: 'frankenmermaid render definitely-not-a-file.mmd' exits 0 and renders successfully. open_input_path (fm-cli/src/main.rs:3984) returns Ok(None) when std::fs::File::open hits NotFound, and load_input then treats the argument as INLINE diagram text. So a typo in a filename does not produce 'file not found' — it produces a diagram whose content is the mistyped filename.

THE FALLTHROUGH IS DELIBERATE and the comment says so ('Missing path: exists() was false, so the old code fell through to inline text'), because the CLI accepts inline source as a positional argument. So this is not an accidental bug; it is an ambiguity in the argument grammar with a bad default. The question is which reading wins when the argument LOOKS like a path.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING: should_treat_input_as_path already distinguishes the cases — it returns true when the argument contains a path separator, and there is more logic after that. An argument that took the path branch and then failed to open with NotFound is a user who meant a FILE, not a user who meant a diagram called 'definitely-not-a-file.mmd'. Falling back to inline text there is the wrong default: inline mermaid source essentially never looks like a path, and a mistyped path essentially always does.

SAME FAMILY AS bd-ec1t / bd-yrxu: input the engine cannot interpret is silently reinterpreted as content instead of being reported. mermaid-cli errors on a missing input file.

NEGATIVE CASES: (1) genuine inline source must still work — 'render "flowchart LR\n A --> B"' has no separator and must keep rendering; (2) a real file must still render; (3) an argument WITH a path separator that does not exist should error, since nothing that looks like a path is plausible inline source; (4) '-' must still mean stdin; (5) the error must name the path and exit nonzero.

⚠️ DO NOT FIX BY MAKING EVERY MISSING PATH AN ERROR without checking should_treat_input_as_path's other branches — an extensionless bare word may legitimately be inline source, and tightening that would break the inline form the fallthrough exists to support.
close_reason: Fixed: open_input_path fails closed on NotFound when the argument states a path (separator or file extension); bare words still fall through to inline source. All five negative cases verified end to end. Bug-encoding test replaced with contract plus two controls; mechanism control run.

This is a correctness admission primitive, not a performance claim or an incumbent ratio.

title: Head-to-head harness does not compile: the run record blew rustc's recursion limit, and behind it the memo path went dead
description:
TWO DEFECTS, both introduced by 0053504e (2026-08-15 09:04) and both invisible until the first was
cleared. The first is FIXED in this commit; the second is filed, not fixed.

== 1. FIXED: crates/fm-cli/examples/headtohead.rs did not compile at all ==

  error: recursion limit reached while expanding `$crate::json_internal!`
      --> crates/fm-cli/examples/headtohead.rs:1889:13
  error: could not compile `frankenmermaid-cli` (example "headtohead")

The per-item run record is one `serde_json::json!` literal. 0053504e added
timed_render_reuses_output_snapshot and timed_render_reuses_parse_plan to "every run record", which
pushed macro expansion past rustc's default 128.

This is a hard front-end error, not a lint, so it takes down `cargo build --example headtohead`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and CI with it -- AND THE ENTIRE MEASUREMENT CAPABILITY,
because that example IS the frankenmermaid arm of the head-to-head harness. Every requalification
queued behind a quiet host (bd-hcw3, bd-bh7d item 3, bd-ln6n, bd-zxxw) was blocked on a binary that
could not be produced, on top of the host conditions.

FIX: `#![recursion_limit = "512"]` on the example, raised rather than splitting the literal because
the record is one object and reads best as one. VERIFIED: `cargo build --release -p
frankenmermaid-cli --example headtohead` finishes clean on the remote fleet (8m 41s).

== 2. FILED, NOT FIXED: with the recursion error cleared, clippy shows the memo path is DEAD ==

  error: fields `texts`, `config`, `revision_key`, and `output` are never read      (:377)
  error: methods `same_texts`, `same_batch`, `matches`, `matches_revision` never used (:384)
  error: field `render_snapshot_cache` is never read                                (:625)
  error: methods `render_all_cached`, `render_all_versioned`,
         `render_all_with_revision` are never used                                  (:850)

So `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is still RED, and this is a design
question rather than a lint to silence.

REACHABILITY, traced rather than assumed:
  - the example binary reaches rendering through ONE call, `render_all_uncached` (:1448).
  - `render_all_versioned` / `render_snapshot_cache` appear only at :2183 and :2206, inside the
    crate's own #[cfg(test)] block.
0053504e set TIMED_RENDER_REUSES_OUTPUT_SNAPSHOT = false and TIMED_RENDER_REUSES_PARSE_PLAN = false,
which was the correct fix for bd-bh7d item 1 -- the batch loop must not feed the memo. Its commit
message says "Incremental/product snapshot paths still pass true", but no such caller survives in
the example.

WHY THIS MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT A LINT: the memo is the mechanism the incremental-edit workload
is supposed to MEASURE (bd-1buv.3, "incremental edit rerender dominance vs mermaid-js"; the
214,830,232x revision-key elision row is the same vein). Deleting the machinery would remove the
harness's ability to measure that workload honestly; #[allow(dead_code)] would be gate
self-weakening and would hide the fact that the capability is gone. The right resolution is a
decision by whoever owns the incremental measurement lane:
  (a) give the incremental workload a caller that legitimately passes reuse = true, so the memo path
      is exercised where reuse is the thing under test and never in a timed full-render sample; or
  (b) remove the machinery and record that this harness measures cold renders only, so nobody
      later quotes a memo-reuse ratio it cannot produce.

⭐ THE STANDING RULE THIS INSTANTIATES: keep the slow path REACHABLE. A fast path gated to a
constant `false` is not a disabled optimization, it is dead code that stops being tested.

PROBE TO CLOSE: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 without any new
allow(dead_code), and whichever of (a)/(b) is chosen is stated in the code.
close_reason: clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings EXIT=0 on rch worker vmi1149989; example compiles; memo path retained under a self-deleting expect() with its three invariants already tested; the (a)/(b) capability decision belongs to bd-1buv.3

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
A THIRD DEFECT IN THE SAME HARNESS, found the moment the binary could finally be built, and it is
the worst of the three: the DRIVER never ran either.

  ReferenceError: Cannot access 'provenanceBinary' before initialization
      at scripts/headtohead/run.mjs:2130:65

Every invocation of run.mjs — every mode, including --host-admission-only — died during module

  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fnx-integration -- -D warnings -> clean (13m 07s)

comments.text:
GATE IS GREEN. Verified remotely, not locally, not by inspection:

  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  EXIT=0, 0 error lines, "Finished dev profile in 3m 04s"
  rch WORKER: vmi1149989 (196.2s wall)   HARNESS: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings

  #[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "incremental-edit memo, no caller until bd-1buv.3"))]

title: Parse and render sequence diagram interaction fragments (loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break)
description:
# Sequence Interaction Fragments

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
sequenceDiagram
  Alice->>Bob: Request
  loop Every minute
    Bob->>Alice: Heartbeat
  end
  alt Success
    Bob->>Alice: 200 OK
  else Failure
    Bob->>Alice: 500 Error
  end
  opt Optional
    Alice->>Carol: Forward
  end
  par Parallel
    Alice->>Bob: Task 1
  and
    Alice->>Carol: Task 2
  end
  critical Critical Section
    Alice->>Bob: Important
  option Timeout
    Alice->>Bob: Retry
  end
  break When error
    Alice->>Bob: Abort
  end
  rect rgb(200, 220, 240)
    Alice->>Bob: Highlighted
  end
\`\`\`

Fragment types: loop, alt/else, opt, par/and, critical/option, break, rect (colored background).
Each fragment is a labeled box spanning the involved participants, enclosing the messages within.
Fragments can be nested.

## Current State
- NOT parsed. Fragment keywords produce warnings.
- No layout support for fragment regions.
- No SVG rendering of fragment boxes.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Add SequenceStatement::FragmentStart { kind, label }, FragmentElse { label }, FragmentEnd. Track nesting depth. Kind enum: Loop, Alt, Opt, Par, Critical, Break, Rect.
2. **IR**: Store as Vec<IrSequenceFragment> with kind, label, start_message_index, end_message_index, participant_range, and nested children.
3. **Layout**: Fragments add padding around their contained messages. Compute fragment box bounds from the first/last message y-positions and the leftmost/rightmost participant x-positions. Nested fragments get progressively larger bounds.
4. **SVG Renderer**: Draw fragment boxes as dashed-border rectangles with a label tab in the top-left corner. Fragment kind shown in bold in the tab. 'else'/'and'/'option' dividers shown as dashed horizontal lines within the fragment.
5. **Tests**: loop, alt/else, opt, par/and, nested fragments, rect with color.

## Complexity
This is the single most complex sequence diagram feature. Fragment nesting requires a stack-based parser and recursive layout. Budget 2-3x the effort of a simple task.
close_reason: Implemented sequence interaction fragment parsing (loop, alt, opt, par, critical, break, rect). Stack-based parser tracks nesting depth. Fragments store kind, label, start/end edge indices, alternatives (for else/and/option dividers), and nested child indices. 'end' keyword dispatches to close either fragments or box groups. 6 tests added covering all fragment types, alt/else alternatives, nested fragments, rect with color, and warning-free parsing.
