comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
INSTRUMENTED AS THIS BEAD ASKED. Two facts established, one suspect eliminated, and one methodological trap that would have produced a wrong answer.

FACT 1 - THE RENDERER IS EXONERATED. This bead's open question was whether layout already holds two points or whether something between layout and SVG replaces the routed path. Dumping LayoutEdgePath.points directly out of layout_diagram:

  cycle_ladder   edge8  reversed=false  npts=2  [(138.68, 352.72), (278.68, 347.27)]
  cycle_feedback edge2  reversed=true   npts=4  [(168.51,1119.0), (215.81,1119.0), (215.81,66.5), (168.51,66.5)]

Layout ALREADY holds two points for the failing edge. So the fault is in fm-layout, not in a renderer-side path rewrite, and suspect 2 from the earlier comment ('a renderer-side path rewrite, not yet examined') is ELIMINATED. The emitted d= differs from these only by the render offset (padding - bounds), which accounts for the +78/+72 seen in the SVG.

FACT 2 - NEITHER ROUTER CAN PRODUCE TWO POINTS FROM NON-ALIGNED ANCHORS. Read end to end:
  - route_edge_points_with_obstacle_index returns [source, target] ONLY in the two ALIGNED branches (|dy| < 0.001 horizontal, |dx| < 0.001 vertical) AND only when the obstacle nudge returns None. Every else branch emits four points.
  - simplify_polyline cannot collapse those four: is_axis_aligned_collinear uses epsilon 0.001, and the staircase (sx,sy),(sx,mid),(tx,mid),(tx,ty) is neither x- nor y-collinear at the measured dy of 5.45.
  - route_edge_points_spline_with_obstacle_index DELEGATES to the orthogonal router and returns early when len() <= 2; it only chamfers. It cannot reduce four to two either.
So the final two points imply the anchors handed to the router were ALIGNED and the nudge found nothing — i.e. at the ORIGINAL anchor y the straight line was clear — and the slant (dy 5.45) was introduced AFTERWARDS. apply_parallel_offset runs after routing (lib.rs ~15000) and mutates points in place with no re-check. That remains the strongest hypothesis and it now has a mechanism: avoidance is computed, then the offset moves the line off the cleared path and into the obstacle.

⚠️ THE TRAP, and it nearly gave me a wrong attribution. My probe printed the routed anchors to STDERR from inside fm-layout and the final points to STDOUT from the test. The two streams INTERLEAVE, so the H2ZE line appearing next to a PROBE line does NOT belong to the same fixture. I initially read 'H2ZE edge8 anchors=(160.26,1305.50)->(591.31,66.50)' as cycle_ladder's, which contradicted everything; it is cycle_feedback's. Whoever continues must tag each instrumentation line with the fixture id, or print both through the same stream.

NEXT STEP, unchanged in kind but now narrowed: instrument with the fixture id attached and capture, for cycle_ladder edge 8 specifically, (a) the anchors passed to the router, (b) which branch was taken, (c) parallel_offset, and (d) the points immediately before and after apply_parallel_offset. If the before-offset points are two ALIGNED points and the after-offset points are the slanted pair, the fix is that avoidance must be the LAST word — either apply the offset before routing, or re-run the obstacle check after it.

NOT FIXED THIS TURN. I did not land a repair, because the mechanism is one instrumented run short of confirmed and a guess here would be tested against the very fixtures it was fitted to.

title: Gantt bars encode neither start date nor duration: label width inflates them and they are centred on their start day
description:
A gantt bar position and length ARE the diagram semantics. Right now neither is encoded correctly. Same family as bd-e69x (sankey flow widths had to be scaled by value) and bd-5wbp (gitGraph branches drawn collinear -- "it is just not a gitGraph").

THE CODE, fm-layout lib.rs:6540-6546:

    node_sizes[node_index].0 = node_sizes[node_index].0            // LABEL-derived width
        .max(duration_days * base_col_width)                        // duration-derived width
        .max(if milestones[task_idx] { 72.0 } else { 156.0 });      // hard floor

    let x = start_offset_days * base_col_width;
    centers[node_index] = (x, y);                                   // x is a CENTRE, not a left edge

with base_col_width = 48.0.

DEFECT 1 -- LABEL WIDTH INFLATES THE BAR. Because the label-derived node width is the first max() operand, a long task name lengthens the bar. Measured, dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD, one section:

    T1 :a1, 2024-01-01, 1d   (short name)  -> bar w=156.00
    T2 :a2, 2024-01-02, 10d  (short name)  -> bar w=480.00     = 10 * 48, correct

    rename T1 to "A deliberately long gantt task name that far exceeds its one day bar":
    T1 (still 1 day)                       -> bar w=524.10
    T2 (still 10 days)                     -> bar w=480.00

So a ONE-DAY task renders a LONGER bar than a TEN-DAY task, purely because its name is long. The duration ordering inverts. A reader comparing bar lengths -- which is the only thing a gantt chart asks them to do -- gets the wrong answer.

DEFECT 2 -- THE BAR IS CENTRED ON ITS START DAY. `centers[node_index] = (x, y)` with `x = start_offset_days * base_col_width` makes the bar straddle its start, so its left edge sits half a bar-width BEFORE the date it starts on. With the 156px floor a 1-day task spans about +/-1.6 days around its start. Left-edge ordering therefore does not track start dates, and the chart origin is dragged left by whichever bar is widest.

DEFECT 3 -- the 156px floor (72 for milestones) alone breaks proportionality for anything under 3.25 days, independent of labels. That one may well be deliberate for readability; I am recording it because combined with 1 and 2 it means SHORT tasks are systematically misencoded, and any fix has to decide about it explicitly.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY PREDICTION, not by reading alone. I modelled "width = max(label_w, duration*48, 156), bar centred at start_offset*48, then global shift = padding - min_left" and it reproduces both measured cases to 0.01px:

    control          predicted T1 206.00..362.00 w=156.00 | T2 92.00..572.00 w=480.00
                     observed  T1 206.00..362.00 w=156.00 | T2 92.00..572.00 w=480.00
    long T1 label    predicted T1 92.00..616.10 w=524.10 | T2 162.05..642.05 w=480.00
                     observed  T1 92.00..616.10 w=524.10 | T2 162.05..642.05 w=480.00

That also RETRACTS a wrong reading I had mid-investigation: I first thought start positions were inverted (T1 starting Jan 1 drawn right of T2 starting Jan 2). They are not inverted in the sense of a comparison bug -- it is exactly the centring in defect 2 plus the global left-shift. Same wrong picture, different cause; the cause matters for the fix.

THE FIX REQUIRES A RENDERING-POLICY DECISION, which is why I am filing rather than landing it. Making the bar encode its data means:
    left  = start_offset_days * base_col_width
    width = duration_days * base_col_width
and the label can then no longer set the width. But our renderer centres the task label INSIDE the bar, so decoupling width from label makes long labels overflow the bar -- the same containment class as bd-090g/bd-9xjy/bd-tm5p. mermaid-js avoids this by giving task names their own column beside the timeline rather than fitting the bar to the text. So the options are:
  (a) keep the label inside and ellipsize it to the bar, as edge labels ALREADY do in this engine (an edge label renders as "...that wil<ellipsis>" inside a box sized to the truncated text) -- cheapest, consistent with existing behaviour, but loses text;
  (b) give task names a left-hand column and let bars be pure duration -- matches mermaid-js, biggest change;
  (c) keep the bar duration-true and allow the label to overhang it deliberately.
I am not choosing between these unilaterally: (b) changes the diagram layout, and this is a shipped diagram type.

NO CERTIFIED OR PUBLISHED RATIO IS AFFECTED, checked: `grep -c "gen: 'gantt" scripts/headtohead/corpus.mjs` is 0 -- gantt is not in the head-to-head corpus at all. So unlike bd-hcw3 this needs no requalification.

COLLISION WARNING: bd-0nr2 is IN_PROGRESS on the stale gantt_basic SVG golden. Any fix here moves that same golden, so whoever lands this must coordinate with that bead rather than blessing over it. Noted on bd-0nr2 too.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Bar width is proportional to duration: for two tasks whose durations differ by a factor k, their bar widths differ by k (within the chosen floor policy), REGARDLESS of label length. The 1d-long-name vs 10d-short-name case above must stop inverting.
2. A bar left edge corresponds to its start date: two tasks starting one day apart have left edges exactly base_col_width apart, and an earlier task never has a greater left edge than a later one.
3. Renaming a task must not change ANY bar geometry. This is the single sharpest test, because it isolates the defect from the floor policy.
4. Whatever is decided about the floor and about labels is stated in the code, not left implicit.
5. GOLDEN IMPACT: gantt_basic.svg and its layout checksum will move, needing a GOLDEN-CHANGE note naming the new bar geometry -- coordinated with bd-0nr2.

FOUND by continuing the containment sweep to the surfaces I listed on bd-tm5p (sequence lifelines, gantt bars, edge labels). Edge labels came back CLEAN -- the renderer ellipsizes them and sizes the box to the truncated text, verified on a 62-character label. Gantt is where it bit.
close_reason:
Fixed by 094b4065.

DECISION, and it is a CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF I was given. I was asked for option (b), "task-name column in LayoutExtensions matching mermaid-js", with the reason "this is a port; where the incumbent has settled behavior we reproduce it rather than invent our own truncation policy". I checked what mermaid-js actually does before building, and IT DOES NOT USE A NAME COLUMN. Deminified from the pinned 11.15.0 bundle its gantt renderer selects among three CSS classes:

    textWidth > barWidth ? (barX + textWidth + 1.5*leftPadding > chartWidth ? "taskTextOutsideLeft" : "taskTextOutsideRight") : "taskText"

i.e. inside the bar when the name fits, otherwise immediately outside it, preferring the right and going left only when right would run off its fixed-width chart — and never truncating in any branch. So I implemented that, because the REASON I was given (reproduce the incumbent) points there even though the option LABEL pointed at a column. Recorded here as instructed, and flagged in the handoff.

WHAT LANDED. Bars are purely temporal: width = duration_days * 48, centre offset by half the width so the LEFT EDGE lands on the start day. Milestones keep a fixed marker width centred ON their day, correct for an instant. The 156px floor is gone. Task-name placement is decided in fm-layout and carried through LayoutExtensions as gantt_task_labels, beside the existing bands and axis_ticks.

WHY LAYOUT AND NOT THE RENDERER, which is the load-bearing design point: only layout can grow the diagram bounds to hold a label outside its bar. My earlier geometry-only attempt (recorded above) proved that — it put a 60-character name at x = -68 against a viewBox starting at 0, clipped. extend_bounds_for_gantt_labels grows the canvas for whichever side was chosen. An empty extension preserves the old centred behaviour, so no other diagram type is affected.

MEASURED, T1 :a1, 2024-01-01, Nd beside T2 :a2, 2024-01-02, 10d:
  N=1   bar 1.00 cols; 60-char name -> anchor=start at bar_right+8, spans 292..652 inside a 712 canvas, FULL 60 chars, no ellipsis
  N=4   bar 4.00 cols; same, outside-right
  N=10  bar 10.00 cols; the name now fits, anchor=middle inside the bar
Renaming T1 between 2 and 60 characters leaves bars byte-identical at [(92,192),(140,480)].

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all five:
1. Width proportional to duration regardless of label -- asserted at three durations; the 1d-vs-10d inversion is gone.
2. Left edge corresponds to the start date -- Build now starts exactly where Design ends in the golden, see below.
3. Renaming changes NO bar geometry -- the sharpest criterion, asserted directly and controlled.
4. Floor and label policy are stated in the code, not implicit.
5. Golden moved with a GOLDEN-CHANGE note and a semantic diff.

THE GOLDEN DIFF IS THE BEST EVIDENCE. Fixture is Design 3d then Build 4d "after a1":
  Design w 156 -> 144 = exactly 3 x 48 (floor removed)
  Build  x 218 -> 236, and 236 - 92 = 144 = exactly 3 days
so Build now begins precisely where Design ends. BEFORE, Build started at 218 while Design ran to 248 — the "after a1" dependency was rendering BACKWARDS. Nobody had noticed because the bars still looked like bars. Build width unchanged at 192 = 4 x 48; both labels still fit inside and stay anchor=middle; no task lost or reordered; viewBox 502 -> 520 wide with height unchanged; layout_width 422 -> 440. Only gantt_basic moved of 19 SVG and 22 layout cases.

AN EXISTING ASSERTION CHANGED, and I want it on the record as strengthened rather than relaxed: gantt_layout_groups_tasks_by_section_and_orders_slots_horizontally read assert!(task_1.bounds.width >= 156.0), pinning the very floor that was part of this defect. It now reads assert_eq!(task_1.bounds.width, 96.0) because task_1 declares DurationDays(2) = two columns. An exact value replaces a lower bound that accepted anything above 156.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, one per half, because the fix has two: label width restored into the bar width -> "1d: renaming the task changed the bar geometry"; placement extension emptied -> "1d: a name too wide for a 48px bar must be placed outside it". Source restored byte-identically after each.

NO REQUALIFICATION: gantt is not in the head-to-head corpus (grep -c "gen: 'gantt" = 0), so no certified ratio is touched. bd-0nr2 was warned before this landed and its gantt_basic golden has now moved as predicted.

GATES: clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast EXIT=0 with 40/40 suites green; cargo fmt --check clean on every hunk authored; ubs fm-render-svg exits 0 and fm-layout exits 1 pre-existing per bd-tp4z with none of its findings on my lines. Pushed to main and master at 094b4065.

comments.author: ubuntu
ubuntu
comments.text:
ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED -- reporting the loss, with the blocker it exposed. Nothing landed; fm-layout/src/lib.rs is byte-identical to HEAD (git diff empty) and goldens are green 8/8 + 2/2.

WHAT I TRIED (option c, "keep the bar duration-true and let the label overhang"). Replaced the width/centre computation with:
    milestone: width 72.0, centre = start_offset_days * col          (an instant, correctly centred on its day)
    task:      width = duration_days * col, centre = start*col + width/2   (left edge ON the start day)
dropping the 156px floor, since durations are already clamped to >= 1 so the narrowest bar is one 48px column.

IT WORKED, exactly as the acceptance criteria asked. Measured after the change:
    T1 1d Jan-1  left offset 0.00 cols, width 1.00 cols
    T2 10d Jan-2 left offset 1.00 cols, width 10.00 cols
and critically, criterion 3: renaming T1 to the 68-character name changed NOTHING -- identical left and width. Duration and start are both encoded correctly.

WHY I REVERTED IT ANYWAY. compute_bounds derives the canvas from NODE BOXES, and the node box is now the bar. The task label is still drawn centred on the bar, so on a 48px bar it extends far outside it and off the canvas:

    viewBox 0 0 712 332.1
    long label centred at x=116.0, font 12.0 -> spans about -68 to 300 at ratio 0.45, or -88 to 320 at 0.50
    => CLIPPED LEFT by the viewBox at x=0

So the change trades wrong bar lengths for LOST TEXT. That is not an improvement, and shipping it would have swapped one wrong picture for another. Option (c) as written is not viable, which retires it -- that is the useful result here.

WHAT THIS TELLS US ABOUT THE REMAINING OPTIONS. Both surviving options need the LAYOUT to account for label space, because the renderer cannot: only layout knows the day arithmetic, and only node boxes reach compute_bounds.
  (a) ellipsize to the bar -- viable with the existing fit_node_label_text helper and needs no bounds work, since the label stays inside the bar. But a 1-day bar is 48px, which shows roughly three characters, so the names become useless. Honest geometry, unusable text.
  (b) task-name column -- the right answer, and it needs the name gutter to participate in bounds, not just in rendering. A gutter drawn left of every bar is outside bounds for exactly the same reason the overhang was.

CONCRETE ARCHITECTURE FOR (b), which is what I would do next and why I did not do it in this pass: gantt ALREADY ships non-node geometry through LayoutExtensions -- layout.extensions.bands carries section bands and layout.extensions.axis_ticks carries date labels, and the renderer streams both. A gantt name gutter (and/or explicit per-task bar geometry) belongs in that same channel, so bounds and the renderer agree by construction instead of the node box doing double duty as both "the bar" and "the thing bounds measures". That is a real design change to a shipped diagram type across two crates plus goldens, and it also has to be sequenced against in-progress bd-0nr2 on the gantt golden.

Also worth recording for whoever does it: write_gantt_label_into hardcodes text-anchor="middle" and its doc contract says it must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL to an Element::text() slow path, so any placement change has to move both emitters in lockstep -- the same sibling-gate discipline that bd-678053a and bd-a6uk both turned on.

The attempt is preserved outside the repo for reference rather than committed, since a reverted experiment does not belong in history.

title: DOT: penwidth and font attributes into style refs; fontcolor proven unmappable
description:
The next increment bd-6fvi named, and it stayed small as predicted: penwidth, fontsize and fontname
now cross over on the same resolve-then-emit path the colors use, for BOTH nodes and edges, with
defaults and subgraph scoping inherited from bd-9yjo.

  penwidth=N  -> stroke-width:N      (bare number: SVG user units)
  fontsize=N  -> font-size:Npt       (DOT measures in POINTS, so the unit is pt)
  fontname=F  -> font-family:F

Edges now resolve their whole visual set the same way nodes do, replacing the color-only path from
bd-6fvi, and one test pins that an EDGE ignores `style=filled`: an edge has no interior, so the node
rule (where style=filled turns `color` into the fill) must not leak to it.

FONTCOLOR IS DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPORTED, and this is the finding worth keeping. I implemented it as
`color:<value>`, which passes fm-core's style-property allowlist, and the end-to-end test then FAILED:
the property reaches the IR and the renderer drops it. This renderer colors text with `fill` on the
text element, and `fill` in a node-level style ref already means the SHAPE fill, so the two cannot
coexist in one declaration. Rather than ship a mapping that produces CSS nothing consumes, I removed
it and added a test asserting that `a [fontcolor=green]` produces NO style entry — so a future attempt
gets a red test explaining why instead of rediscovering it.

That is the second time in two beads that an end-to-end assertion on rendered output caught something
IR-level tests could not: bd-6fvi's control caught meaningless colour-name needles, and this one
caught a silently-dropped property. Parser tests alone would have called both of these done.

TESTS: 6 new parser unit tests (node attributes, edge attributes, edge-ignores-style-filled, the
fontcolor non-emission, default merge keeping an inherited font across a width override, and edge
defaults reverting at a subgraph brace) plus an end-to-end SVG test with its own negative control
proving an unstyled graph carries none of the three needles.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p fm-parser --lib -> 0 (486 passed); cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli -> 0;
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -> 0; rustfmt clean. No golden moved.

STILL NOT SUPPORTED: fontcolor (above, with reason), bgcolor, and cluster-level attributes —
IrStyleTarget has no Cluster variant, so cluster styling needs IR surface rather than a parser change.
close_reason: Landed; fontcolor left unsupported with a test recording why

title: Requalify schema_catalog_25 (412.8x, worst certified ratio): bd-090g changed ER entity geometry
description:
SELF-REPORTED CONSEQUENCE of my own correctness fix. Filing because staying quiet would leave the worst certified ratio quotable against code that no longer produces the measured output.

WHAT CHANGED. bd-090g (9f0e6cad) made ER entity boxes tall enough to hold their attribute rows; before it, rows from the 4th attribute onward rendered OUTSIDE the box. bd-9xjy (9fbbcd74) did the equivalent for C4 descriptions.

WHY IT REACHES THIS ROW. PERF_LEDGER.md:602 carries 'Database-catalog publish | 25 schemas; 662 entities / 637 relationships total | 15.856699 ms / 6,546.050 ms | 412.825519x', campaign result class incumbent-win, ELF a23cf867fd18608c0c3d6a75671dc57573847fb4db6724bc87942944a74cbd6a, workload id schema_catalog_25. Its generator is schemaCatalog -> docEr (scripts/headtohead/corpus.mjs:297), and docEr DOES emit attribute blocks:

  E{i} {
    int id PK
    string field0 ... field{attrs-1}      // attrs = 1 + floor(r()*5)
  }

so every entity carries 'int id PK' plus 1-5 fields = 2 to 6 rows, roughly uniform. Measured entity box heights at exactly those counts, current code:

  2 rows -> 66.50   (unchanged; 2 rows already fitted)
  3 rows -> 80.10   (+13.60)
  4 rows -> 95.70   (+29.20)
  5 rows -> 111.30  (+44.80)
  6 rows -> 126.90  (+60.40)

Four of the five reachable row counts grow, so on the order of 80% of the 662 entities have a different box height than when 412.825519x was measured. Layout height, output bytes and the output SHA-256 all move. The row's ELF is superseded.

THE ROW IS NOT WRONG AND IS NOT BEING RETRACTED. It states its own ELF and remains valid history for that ELF; that is how this ledger works, and every landed change supersedes prior output hashes. What is NOT valid is quoting 412.825519x for current code, and this is specifically the number the campaign has been told to attack ('attack the LOWEST certified ratio; WORST = ER 412.8x, LAYOUT-bound'), so it will be quoted unless this is recorded.

DIRECTION OF THE EFFECT IS UNKNOWN AND I AM NOT GUESSING. Taller boxes mean more layout extent and more output bytes, which argues slower. But the fix also moves our ER rendering TOWARD mermaid-js, which draws attribute rows inside the entity box, so the cross-engine output-equivalence verdict for this workload should improve. Whether the ratio rises or falls is an empirical question and needs the harness, not an argument.

ALSO AFFECTED, same cause: the er_schema_* items (er_schema_2500x8, er_schema_10000x8 in .benchmarks/cert-v5/) whose recorded output_sha256 values no longer match current code. The pinned 'er' generator (corpus.mjs:90) is NOT affected -- it emits relationships only, no attribute blocks, so anything measured on 'er' alone stands.

NO PUBLIC CLAIM IS AFFECTED, checked rather than assumed: README quotes ratios for the shared-subgraph and docs workloads (851.99x, 10,201.63x, 27,419.82x, 24,893.41x, 17,060.38x) and mentions ER only as a supported diagram type, in the Sugiyama dispatch table, and in IR comments. It states no ER or catalog ratio. So this is an internal-ledger requalification, not a public correction.

WHAT THIS BEAD NEEDS:
1. Rebuild the headtohead example at current HEAD per the harness README route (strict remote, --base/--clean-overlay, self-reported ELF).
2. Re-run schema_catalog_25 with the live mermaid-js arm in the SAME invocation, on a quiet host (load < 8), at jobs=1 -- the last is not optional here, because this repo has a documented defect where output bytes depend on measured wall time and can manufacture false byte-divergence.
3. Re-run cross-engine output equivalence for the item; record whether the verdict improved, since the fix should bring us closer to mermaid's geometry.
4. Add a fresh row with its own ELF and A/A null, and annotate the 2026-07-27 row as superseded-by rather than editing its numbers.
5. If the ratio moved materially, say so plainly in either direction. A correctness fix that costs ratio is still the right change and should be reported as a cost, not hidden.

I did not attempt steps 1-4 myself: this is a full certification run needing a predeclared quiet window, and re-publishing a peer lane's incumbent-win row is not a call I should make unilaterally alongside a same-session correctness change of my own.

title: C4 long-form direction macros and Node aliases were dropped as unsupported
description:
mermaid's C4 lexer accepts BOTH spellings of every direction macro - /^(?:Rel_Up\b)/ sits directly
beside /^(?:Rel_U\b)/, and likewise Down/D, Left/L, Right/R - and it accepts Node, Node_L and Node_R
as short spellings of Deployment_Node. We listed only one spelling of each, so the others fell to
the default arm, warned "unsupported C4 directive" and drew NOTHING.

Cost of the omission:
  Rel_Up/Rel_Down/Rel_Left/Rel_Right  the relationship was dropped entirely - no edge at all.
  Node/Node_L/Node_R                  the BLOCK never opened, so the container and everything
                                      nested inside it were lost, not just the one line.

FOUND SYSTEMATICALLY, not by guessing. I extracted the full 43-macro token list from the pinned
bundle's C4 lexer and diffed every one against our dispatch. That is what turned up 11 names we do
not accept; four of the remaining ones are a separate concern (below).

PURE ALIASES for us, which is why the fix is only a match arm: direction is never consumed - every
relationship arm except BiRel and Rel_Back falls through to the same (from, to, Arrow) - and the
_L/_R suffix on Node is a layout hint we do not read either. So the long spelling can only ever
mean what the short one already means. Nothing downstream needed changing, which is exactly why the
omission stayed invisible.

STILL UNSUPPORTED, deliberately left warning rather than half-implemented: RelIndex,
UpdateElementStyle, UpdateRelStyle, UpdateLayoutConfig. These are not aliases - they mutate element
and relationship STYLING and layout config, so each needs a real consumer, and the default arm's
warning is honest about them today.

VERIFIED the incumbent accepts the forms with scripts/headtohead/parse_probe.mjs: Rel_Up(a,b,"x"),
Node(n,"N") { ... } and UpdateElementStyle(...) all report the grammar ACCEPTING the input (C4
render needs a DOM, so the probe's runtime-error class is expected here and is not a syntax verdict).

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Four tests added, none compiled. Each new form has a
CONTROL asserting the pre-existing spelling still works, because a change that swapped one spelling
for the other would otherwise pass.
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build

title: LayoutConfig::edge_routing is inert: requesting Spline produces byte-identical geometry
description:
MEASURED DEAD OPTION. `LayoutConfig::edge_routing` has two variants, Orthogonal (default) and
Spline, and requesting Spline changes NOTHING for a flowchart. Not "changes little" — byte-identical
geometry:

  source                                             orthogonal_pts  spline_pts  coords_differ
  flowchart TB  a-->b  a-->c  b-->d  c-->d                       16          16          false
  flowchart TB  a-->b  b-->c  c-->a                               8           8          false
  flowchart LR  a-->b  a-->c  b-->d  c-->d  a-->d                18          18          false

`coords_differ` compares the full (x, y) sequence of every routed edge point, so this is not a
point-count artifact — I checked count first, then coordinates, precisely because equal counts can
hide different geometry. Both runs go through `layout_diagram_with_config` with only `edge_routing`
differing.

WHY, as far as I traced it. `route_edge_points_spline_with_obstacle_index` returns the orthogonal path
untouched when it has <= 2 points ("nothing to curve", correct), but these fixtures have 4-point routes
and still do not change, so the spline router is evidently not being reached on the path a flowchart
takes. There are SIX hardcoded `EdgeRouting::default()` call sites in fm-layout — at lib.rs 4966, 4968,
5090, 7978, 8374, and two more in tests — several inside specialized layout paths that receive no
`LayoutConfig` at all. I confirmed one of them (`build_directed_path_edge_paths` / `build_edge_paths`
around 4966) cannot see a config: passing `config.edge_routing` there does not compile, because the
enclosing function has no config parameter. I did NOT finish identifying which specific path each of
these fixtures takes.

WHAT I DID AND THEN REVERTED, and why the revert is the point. I built the natural feature on top of
this: Mermaid's `flowchart.curve` (which is parsed, stored in init.config, and read by NOBODY) and
DOT's `splines` both mapping onto a `meta.edge_routing` hint that fm-layout resolves into
`EdgeRouting`. Parser side worked and was tested — 511 fm-parser tests green, both dialects mapping
their spelling vocabularies correctly, unknown names still tolerated rather than newly rejected.

Then the end-to-end test failed, and kept failing after I widened the fixture and after I wired an
additional call site. The measurement above is why: the hint feeds an option that does nothing, so the
feature would have been unreachable work — a new IR field, a new core enum, two parser mappings and a
layout resolver, all so a user's `curve=basis` could change no pixel. That is exactly the trap the
last several beads have been unpicking (bd-mf4d's phantom nodes, bd-hc5y's dropped `fontcolor`,
`flowchart_curve` itself), so shipping it would have contradicted the standard those set. Everything
was reverted; the working tree is back at HEAD and nothing was committed.

THE ORDER OF WORK IS THE LESSON. I should have probed whether `EdgeRouting::Spline` does anything
BEFORE building a parser feature to select it. Two of the previous beads got this right by accident —
they asserted on rendered output early and caught dropped properties — and here the end-to-end
assertion caught it again, just later than it should have.

WHAT SOMEONE SHOULD DO, in order:
1. Determine which layout path each diagram shape actually takes, and which of the six hardcoded
   `EdgeRouting::default()` sites is on it.
2. Decide whether `Spline` is meant to be reachable at all. If yes, thread the routing choice into the
   specialized paths (some need a config parameter they do not currently take). If no, delete the
   variant and the spline router rather than leaving an option that silently does nothing — a config
   knob with no effect is worse than an absent one, because callers write it and believe it.
3. Only then wire `flowchart.curve` and DOT `splines` to it. The parser-side mapping is
   straightforward and is described above; the blocker is entirely downstream.

Note `flowchart_curve` remains today what it has been: parsed, recorded in `init.config`, read by
nothing. This bead is the reason it stays that way for now rather than being wired to an inert target.
close_reason: Root cause fixed: midpoints were cancelled by simplify_polyline; chamfer survives. Hardcoded default sites and source-side selection recorded as separate follow-ups

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED. Last turn measured that `EdgeRouting::Spline` produced byte-identical
geometry and left the mechanism open. It is a two-line self-cancellation:

  route_edge_points_spline_with_obstacle_index inserted the MIDPOINT of every orthogonal segment,
  then called simplify_polyline, which drops axis-aligned-collinear middle points.

A midpoint of an axis-aligned segment is collinear with its neighbours BY DEFINITION, so every
inserted point was removed again and the function returned its input unchanged. That is not "inert on
some shapes" — it was provably a no-op for EVERY input, which is exactly what the three measured
fixtures showed. The suspicion I recorded last turn (that some hardcoded `EdgeRouting::default()` call
site was to blame) was WRONG, and it is worth saying so plainly: those six hardcoded sites exist and
are a separate smell, but they were not the reason Spline did nothing.

THE FIX replaces each right-angle corner with a CHAMFER: step back a quarter of the shorter adjacent
leg, step forward the same amount on the other leg, and drop the corner. The two points sit on
different axes, so the segment between them is DIAGONAL and simplify_polyline cannot collapse it. The
cut is a quarter of the SHORTER leg so a chamfer can never overshoot into the next corner and invert
the path on a short segment.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, stated so the variant is not oversold: it is not a cubic Bezier, which is what the
variant's doc comment claims. A true Bezier needs curve commands in the SVG writer — the renderer
emits straight `L` segments only — and control points the IR has no room for. A chamfer is the honest
approximation reachable without changing the IR or the renderer, and it is visibly different: right
angles become bevelled. Whoever wants real curves should read this as the remaining work, and may want
to correct the variant's doc comment at that point.

EVIDENCE: three shapes (TB diamond, LR diamond with a skip edge, the DOT equivalent) now differ
between Orthogonal and Spline on the full (x, y) sequence of every routed point, gain points, and
contain at least one diagonal segment. A second test pins that `layout_diagram`'s default output is
byte-identical to an explicit Orthogonal request — the control that matters, because every golden
fixture uses the default and none can select Spline from source today.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p fm-layout --lib -> 0 (471 passed); cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli -> 0 (26
targets, both golden suites among them); cargo test -p fm-wasm -> 0; cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets -- -D warnings -> 0.

NO GOLDEN MOVED, which is the load-bearing check for a routing change: the default path is untouched
(asserted, not assumed), so no fixture's geometry moves. Both golden suites pass unblessed. The one
dirty golden file (layout_checksums.json) is another lane's pre-existing working-tree change from
before this session, last committed in a656acc4 (bd-f3tc), and has never been staged by me.

STILL OPEN, and now separable from this bug:
1. Six hardcoded `EdgeRouting::default()` sites in fm-layout, several in specialized paths that
   receive no LayoutConfig. A caller's routing choice cannot reach those paths. Now that Spline
   demonstrably does something, this is a real gap rather than a moot one.
2. No SOURCE can request Spline. Mermaid's `flowchart.curve` and DOT's `splines` map onto it naturally
   — the parser-side mapping I built and reverted last turn is described in this bead's first comment
   and can now be rebuilt against a target that works.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
LAST OPEN ITEM PROBED AND CLOSED AS NOT-A-DEFECT.

The concern recorded here was that six hardcoded `EdgeRouting::default()` call sites in fm-layout make the
effective routing depend on which algorithm the dispatcher chose. Measured: it does not, for any
flowchart shape I could construct.

  wide flowchart (one root, eight children -> dispatches away from Sugiyama): honors curve=basis
  tree-shaped flowchart:                                                     honors curve=basis
  diamonds (general path, already covered):                                   honor curve=basis

Both new probes PASSED before any change, which is the evidence — I wrote them expecting red.

The remaining hardcoded sites belong to diagram types whose edges are not orthogonally routed at all:
gitGraph lane connectors and the specialized-layout finalizer used by sequence/gantt-style diagrams.
Curving those would be wrong, not missing, so hardcoding the default there is appropriate.

The wide-shape probe is kept as a regression guard in crates/fm-cli/tests/dot_rank_layout_test.rs —
it is the assertion that would fail if someone re-hardcoded routing on that dispatch path. No
behaviour changed and no feature was claimed for it.

title: Cross-engine ratios are unguarded against a 2.7x CPU frequency spread: only one arm is pinned, and it is pinned to the slowest core by construction
description:
MEASUREMENT-INTEGRITY DEFECT affecting every certified cross-engine row. Filed after reproducing the fleet-wide 2.879x cross-core spread report on this host.

OBSERVED LIVE on thinkstation1: cpu10/15/24/27/28 at 1429 MHz while cpu34 ran at 3914 MHz — 2.739x at the same instant, later 2.750x. The harness's own power-policy gate reports scaling_min_khz 1429008 / scaling_max_khz 4561833, a 3.19x hardware range, so idle cores sit exactly at the floor.

THREE DEFECTS, confirmed by reading scripts/headtohead/run.mjs:
1. ONLY THE FRANKENMERMAID ARM IS PINNED. taskset appears at exactly one site. The mermaid-js arm runs under Chromium unpinned across all 64 cores.
2. THE PINNED CORE IS CHOSEN FOR IDLENESS. pickIdleCpu() sorts by busy fraction and takes the minimum. On per-core DVFS the least-busy core is the one parked at the 1429 MHz floor, so the selection rule actively prefers the SLOWEST clock for our arm while the unpinned incumbent runs on cores its own load has boosted.
3. FREQUENCY WAS RECORDED NOWHERE. grep for scaling_cur_freq/cpu_mhz/MHz over the driver returned 0.

WHY NO EXISTING GATE CATCHES IT: busy fraction is occupancy, not speed — a core at 5% busy and 1429 MHz passes the 20% quiescence veto comfortably. And each engine's A/A null is measured entirely inside its own phase at that phase's frequency, so a null of 0.998891 proves self-consistency, not comparable clocks. The two gates that look like they should cover this are both blind to it by construction.

SCOPE: every certified cross-engine ratio in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md was produced under these conditions. That is NOT a claim any specific row is wrong — the bias direction depends where Chromium actually ran — it is a claim the rows carry no evidence either way, because the quantity that can move a ratio by up to 2.7x was never recorded.

PARTIALLY FIXED (see the commit): per-phase CPU MHz capture landed. cpuMhz() reads scaling_cur_freq per core; cpuMhzSummary() gives cores/min/max/mean/spread_ratio plus the pinned core's own frequency; phaseLoad now carries cpu_mhz_before and cpu_mhz_after per phase, so each arm records the clock it ran at. Harness self-test green. ⚠️ The emission path is NOT yet exercised by a real measured phase, because no certification run has been admissible; first successful run should be checked for sane cpu_mhz_* values before its row is trusted.

⚠️ NOT FIXED, and it needs an owner rather than me: making both arms run on comparable cores. Pinning Chromium is not symmetric with pinning a single-threaded Rust process — a browser is multi-process and multi-threaded, so taskset on it changes its PARALLELISM, not just its clock. The choice between 'pin both and accept a different Chromium execution model' and 'pin neither and record the spread' changes what the comparison MEANS. It must not be decided by the person whose row it unblocks.

NEGATIVE CASES for whoever takes the remaining half: (1) whatever is chosen, the ROW must show both arms' observed MHz so a reader can see whether they were comparable; (2) pinning Chromium must not silently reduce it to one core, which would measure a different program than users run; (3) a fix that equalises clocks by BUSY-WAITING to boost the pinned core is not acceptable — it changes the thing being measured; (4) re-check whether pickIdleCpu should prefer an idle core at all, given idle now means slow.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DEFECT 2 RETRACTED - MEASURED FALSE. I claimed pickIdleCpu() "actively prefers the SLOWEST clock for our arm" because the least-busy core sits at the 1429 MHz floor. That was inferred from scaling_cur_freq AT REST and does not survive measurement.

Two independent trials, replicating the selection rule then pinning a CPU-bound child to the chosen core exactly as taskset -c does:
  cpu6 (0.0% busy)  at rest 2090 MHz  ->  under load 4217-4292, mean 4282
  cpu1 (0.0% busy)  at rest 3433 MHz  ->  under load 4289-4292, mean 4291

The governor reaches within 0.1% of the host maximum inside the first 0.5s sample and holds. An idle core is slow at rest and fast under load - that is what DVFS is for. So the 2.7-3.0x spread is overwhelmingly IDLE-versus-BUSY, not fast-arm-versus-slow-arm, and both arms are busy while being measured.

PRIORITY DROPPED P0 -> P2 accordingly. I filed it P0 substantially on the retracted claim.

WHAT SURVIVES: only one arm is pinned (taskset at exactly one site) - true; CPU frequency recorded nowhere - true, and the per-phase capture is written and parked behind ScarletMeadow's run.mjs lease.

WHAT REPLACES IT, POINTING THE OPPOSITE WAY: the residual asymmetry is all-core versus single-core boost. Our arm pinned to ONE core can hold single-core boost (~4292 MHz) while Chromium spread across many cores runs at the lower all-core sustained clock. That biases in OUR favour, is far smaller than 2.7x, and is the opposite sign to what I originally asserted. Anyone auditing rows should look for that, not for a slow pinned arm.

ALSO RETRACTED, my own probe artifact: an earlier sampler appeared to show SMT siblings at different clocks (cpu19 3093 vs cpu51 4121, same physical core 19/51). Frequency is per physical core so siblings cannot differ; the gap was an averaging artifact, each mean taken only over samples where THAT cpu exceeded 50% busy, so the two means covered different windows. No sibling frequency split was observed.

STILL UNANSWERED: which cores each arm actually runs on during a CERTIFICATION run. equivalence.mjs pins neither arm (only run.mjs pins), and per-core busy sampling cannot attribute cores to processes while 31 cores are above 50% from sibling projects. It needs per-process /proc/<pid>/stat attribution during an admitted run.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DEFECTS 2 AND 3 FIXED. Defect 2 confirmed live, and the magnitude is larger than the bead estimated.

MEASURED ON THIS HOST just now, comparing the two rules on the SAME observation of all 64 cores:

  OLD rule (least busy): cpu0   busy 0.0%  1429 MHz   <- the exact DVFS floor
  NEW rule             : cpu14  busy 0.0%  4164 MHz
  clock ratio new/old  : 2.914x
  host spread          : 1429-4164 MHz = 2.914x, 18 cores tied at 0.0% busy

Both cores were EQUALLY IDLE at 0.0%. The old rule was not making a tradeoff; it was picking the
frequency floor for free, because on per-core DVFS the least-busy core is the parked one. So the
frankenmermaid arm ran at roughly a third of available clock while the unpinned mermaid-js arm ran
on cores its own load had boosted.

FIX: idleness stays a REQUIREMENT (a co-tenant makes the measurement meaningless), but among cores
already acceptable on occupancy the FASTEST clock is chosen. The band is anchored to the quietest
core actually observed, +5 points, so this can never start preferring a loaded core: if every core
sits at 40% the band is 40-45% and the quiescence gate refuses the run anyway.

Extracted as scripts/headtohead/cpu_selection.mjs because run.mjs parses argv at import, so nothing
inside it is reachable from a check. Five properties asserted, including the two that matter: a BUSY
fast core is never chosen (speed only breaks ties inside the band), and a NON-VACUITY case proving
the new rule actually disagrees with the old one on the measured spread rather than being a no-op.
A host without cpufreq falls back to the old rule unchanged.

DEFECT 3 also fixed: the chosen core's MHz, the host min/max/mean/spread, the band size and the
selection rule are now recorded in the pinned_cpu provenance and printed at pin time. grep for
scaling_cur_freq over the driver previously returned 0.

DEFECT 1 NOT FIXED: the mermaid-js arm is still unpinned under Chromium. Pinning a browser with
multiple processes is a different problem and I am not claiming it here.

IMPLICATION FOR THE BANKED STANDING (bd-8557, 362.4x worst bound): that row was produced with the
OLD rule, so our arm was very likely clocked at the floor while the incumbent was not. The bias runs
AGAINST us, so the true ratio is probably higher -- but the honest statement is the one this bead
already makes: the row carries no evidence either way, because the quantity was never recorded. It
is recorded now.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DEFECT 1 NOW FIXED TOO. The mermaid-js arm is pinned to a cpuset chosen by the SAME rule as ours, so both arms are drawn from the same population instead of one being pinned to the floor and the other running free.

SIZING ERRS UPWARD ON PURPOSE, and this is the part worth reviewing. Chromium is multi-process, so
too small a set would slow the INCUMBENT and inflate our ratio -- an over-claim in our own favour,
which is a worse failure than the under-claim the old code produced. Default is 8 cores, raisable
with --incumbent-cpus, and a set that could not be filled is reported as starved=true and printed at
pin time rather than left to be inferred from a row.

Six properties asserted on the pure selector, including the two that matter: a BUSY fast core is
excluded from the incumbent set as well, and a short set is FLAGGED (that is the over-claim
direction). A control asserts the single-core and set selectors agree on which core is fastest, so
the two arms cannot drift onto different notions of 'fastest'.

Verified rather than assumed: taskset -c 2,3,4 gives a node child affinity 2-4 and
availableParallelism 3, and affinity is inherited by descendants, which is what makes it reach
Chromium's renderer and GPU processes.

Also caught in review: my first version called argValue(), which does not exist in run.mjs -- the
helper is arg(name, fallback). node --check cannot see an undefined identifier on a branch it never
executes, so I verified every referenced symbol is present in the file by name.

NO MEASUREMENT WAS RUN. The host is under external I/O load and this is code plus pure-function
tests only. The first certified row taken after this lands will be the first with both arms on
comparable clocks; every row before it, including the 362.4x standing, carries the qualification
recorded in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
OPEN ITEM FOUND BY USING THE FIX: selectPinnedCpuSet picks by RANK, so the incumbent's set straddles a wide clock range while our single-core arm takes only the top.

First both-arms-pinned measurement (sequence_20, ELF c99c2857 at rev 07768c81):

  fm         cpu45 @ 3433 MHz  (fastest_clock_among_idle, N=1)
  incumbent  8 cpus, SLOWEST member 1916 MHz  (fastest_clocks_in_idle_band, N=8)

Taking the fastest N necessarily reaches down into slower cores as N grows. With N=1 our arm gets the
top of the band; with N=8 the incumbent's set spans 1916-4292 MHz, a 1.79x internal range. If
Chromium schedules onto the slow member it runs slower than it would UNPINNED, which inflates the
ratio IN OUR FAVOUR -- the exact direction selectPinnedCpuSet's own doc comment names as the worse
error.

So defect 1 is fixed in the sense that matters (the incumbent can no longer roam onto boosted cores
while ours is parked at the floor) but the replacement is not symmetric.

PROPOSED, not implemented: constrain the incumbent's set to cores within a tolerance of the measured
arm's clock rather than to the fastest N. Selecting by rank is what let the set straddle the range. A
tolerance also gives an honest 'starved' signal when the host cannot supply N comparable cores, which
rank-selection silently papers over.

I am not implementing it in the same turn I found it, because the right tolerance is a judgement
about how much clock spread is acceptable between arms and that belongs in the row's provenance, not
in a value I pick unilaterally.

Measured row banked in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md: worst bound 368.2x, inside the existing 362-403
band, standing unchanged at 362.4x.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RANK-SELECTION REPLACED BY CLOCK-MATCHING, and a deeper limit surfaced that I am NOT claiming to have fixed.

selectPinnedCpuSet now takes an optional targetMhz and picks the cores CLOSEST to it rather than the
fastest N. No free parameter: the objective is 'cores like the one our arm got', not 'cores above a
threshold I chose' -- which is why I could implement this after saying the tolerance judgement was not
mine to make. pick_pins passes the measured arm's clock.

Synthetic, on the band shape that exposed the defect (arm at 3433):
  rank-selected : 4292,4207,4092,3600   internal spread 1.192x
  match-selected: 3433,3500,3333,3600   internal spread 1.080x

The set also now REPORTS incumbent_spread, so a row states how comparable its incumbent cores
actually were instead of leaving it to be inferred from a rule name.

THE LIMIT, measured live and worth more than the fix: fm cpu32 at 2397 MHz, incumbent slowest 1429
MHz, internal spread still 1.677x, host range 1429-4217.

Two things follow, neither of them solved here:

1. This host's clocks are BIMODAL -- a mass parked at 1429 and a boosted tail -- so an 8-core set
   drawn from the idle band straddles regardless of the criterion. Matching narrows the choice; it
   cannot conjure eight comparable idle cores that do not exist.

2. More important: our arm is pinned to an IDLE core, and on per-core DVFS idle cores are BY
   DEFINITION the parked ones. 2397 MHz against a host max of 4217 is not an accident of this sample
   -- it is structural. So the measured arm systematically runs below the clock a busy, boosted core
   would give it, and every ratio we quote UNDERSTATES our engine. That is the conservative
   direction, so no banked row is threatened, but it means 'pin to the fastest idle core' has a
   ceiling that pinning cannot lift.

Recorded rather than acted on: fixing (2) means either warming the target core before measuring or
accepting the floor and saying so in the row. Both are judgements about method, not code.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PIN FIX VERIFIED WORKING, and a second unread guard found in the same place.

The pin fix (52b72e34) does what it claims. Observed live this tick via pick_pins.mjs: fm_cpu chosen by 'fastest_clock_among_idle' at 4204/4181/3945 MHz across three selections -- never the 1429 MHz floor the old least-busy rule selected -- and the incumbent set chosen by 'clocks_closest_to_measured_arm' at 4192 MHz slowest in the best selection, spread 1.007. One selection reported clock_headroom {ratio: 0.999, at_peak: true}. The cpu_mhz_* emission path this bead flagged as UNEXERCISED is now exercised by real measured phases and the values are sane (per-arm min/max/mean/spread, 64 cores, plausible 1429-4267 range).

SECOND DEFECT, same class as the one this bead is about. pick_pins computes incumbent_starved; abba_render.py PRINTED it and quoted the ratio anyway. A guard computed and never read is the same as no guard. Fixed in 55493656: the script now refuses, with --allow-starved-incumbent as a stamped override.

IT MATTERS, MEASURED. Same ELF ed83ad60, same input sha 31c0dd6b, same window, minutes apart:
  6 cpus, starved=True  -> 447.8x
  8 cpus, starved=False -> 373.1x
Starvation inflated the bound 1.20x IN OUR FAVOUR. This is direct evidence for the open question at the bottom of this bead ('pin both and accept a different Chromium execution model' vs 'pin neither and record the spread'): pinning the incumbent to a set that is TOO SMALL measurably changes the answer, so whichever policy is chosen must carry a starvation check. I have not decided the policy -- the bead says it must not be decided by the person whose row it unblocks, and that is still me.

NO ROW BANKED. scripts/window_check.sh (bd-8557, landed this tick) returned NOT MEASURABLE for every attempt: cpus over 20% busy sampled 64 64 64 17 17 13 14 15 64 64 64 64, spread 51 vs threshold 4, idle 24.0-86.8% within one window, load rising monotonically through each bracket. The standing 362.4x is unchanged. Full detail in the REFUSED entry in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIRST EVIDENCE ON THIS BEAD'S OPEN POLICY QUESTION: single-core pinning of the measured arm is itself a noise source, and on this host it is the LARGER term.

Measured in the best window I have had (loadavg 11.9, idle 69.6-86.5%, iowait 0.00%, and crucially loadavg FLAT across all four arms - 15.85/15.85/15.85/15.7 - so the same-window requirement was actually met for once). Same ELF 105c52ba (rev dd19948f, verified inside the ELF), same input sha 31c0dd6b.

PINNED to one core, via the A/B/B/A bracket:
  run A  fm 149,974 / 92,576 ns   drift 1.6200x   bound 223.4x
  run B  fm 138,338 / 145,397 ns  drift 1.0510x   bound 242.1x

UNPINNED, same binary, six runs, same window:
  87,406  94,995  93,196  102,803  91,735  103,985 ns   spread 1.19x

So the PINNED arm's spread (1.62x within a single invocation) is worse than the UNPINNED spread (1.19x across six runs). Pinning buys clock comparability and pays scheduling fragility: on one core an interloping thread cannot be migrated away from, and 13-14 of 64 cpus were busy.

THE TELL IS THE CALIBRATED BATCH, and it is a signal the harness already records but does not read. Every slow observation carries batch 21-25; every fast one carries batch 37-39 - including run A's own A2 at 92,576 ns with batch 37, in the same invocation as its 149,974 ns A1 at batch 23. The batch is calibrated to a 3 ms target, so a contended core shrinks the batch and raises per-op time together. A batch far below the unpinned norm is therefore direct evidence the pinned core was contended during that arm.

I checked my own code first rather than blaming the host: bd-rrvr had just added a per-label byte scan to the parse path, which is exactly what a 1.5x parse slowdown would look like. The unpinned distribution above is the old baseline on the SAME binary, so the parse change is exonerated.

NOT DECIDING THE POLICY. This bead says the pin-both-vs-pin-neither choice must not be made by the person whose row it unblocks, and that is still me. Handing over the evidence instead.

NOTHING BANKED. Run A fails the bracket's own drift control; run B's bound (242.1x) sits below the standing 362.4x for the same reason. The standing row is unchanged.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
A/B/A ON THE PINNING POLICY ITSELF. This is the like-for-like experiment my last comment did not have, and it is decisive.

Last time I compared a PINNED bracket against UNPINNED single-arm runs - not like-for-like. This is three FULL brackets, same window, same ELF 105c52ba, same input sha 31c0dd6b, with unpinned brackets on BOTH SIDES of the pinned one so drift in the comparison itself is controlled. Loadavg flat across all twelve arms (11.66 -> 11.38); idle 68.2-85.2%; iowait 0.00%; host spread 2.85-3.00x throughout.

  bracket        fm A1      fm A2     drift      bound
  no-pin (1st)   96,557     94,654    1.0201x    366.6x
  PINNED        156,370     91,043    1.7175x    227.7x
  no-pin (2nd)   92,143     91,060    1.0119x    382.0x

The pinned bracket is the ONLY one that fails the harness's own drift control, and it sits between two that pass it comfortably, under flat load. The calibrated batch agrees exactly: pinned A1 at batch 20, every other observation at 37-39 - the tell I flagged last comment, now confirmed in a controlled design.

All six incumbent A/A nulls contain 1.0 (no-pin 1st 1.0242 / 0.9467; pinned 1.0028 / 1.0167; no-pin 2nd 0.9625 / 0.9718), so the incumbent arm was self-consistent in every configuration - the instability is OURS, and specifically it is the pinning.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It settles the empirical half: on this host, single-core pinning of the measured arm costs more in scheduling fragility than it buys in clock comparability. It does NOT settle the policy, because 'pin neither and record the spread' leaves the ~3x cross-core clock spread unquantified in the ratio, which is the exact confounder this bead was opened for. Both options are still live; one of them now has a price tag.

I AM STILL NOT DECIDING IT, and the reason is sharper this time: unpinned gives the HIGHER ratio (366.6x and 382.0x vs 227.7x). An agent who wanted a bigger number would adopt 'pin neither' on this evidence. That is exactly why the person whose row it unblocks should not be the one to choose, and this bead already says so.

STANDING FIGURE UNCHANGED at 362.4x. Both unpinned bounds land above it at a NEW revision (dd19948f) with a different pinning policy, which CORROBORATES the standing row rather than replacing it. Raising it would require dismissing the pinned bracket's 227.7x, and the convention quotes the worst bound observed.

Full detail in the third addendum to the REFUSED entry in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

title: Set up CI auto-publish for WASM npm package on tagged releases
description:
## Problem
Even after the initial npm publish (bd-w9id), future releases need automated publishing. Currently the CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml, 40KB) handles build+test+deploy but does NOT include an npm publish step for the WASM package.

## Scope
1. Add a new CI job (or step in existing workflow) that triggers on version-tagged pushes (e.g., `v*`).
2. The job should: run build-wasm.sh, verify the pkg/ output, run `npm publish --access public` using a stored NPM_TOKEN secret.
3. Add the NPM_TOKEN secret to the GitHub repo settings.
4. Guard against accidental re-publish: check if the version already exists on npm before attempting publish.
5. Consider: should the version in pkg/package.json be auto-bumped from Cargo.toml version, or maintained independently?

## Dependencies

title: Replace hardcoded quadrant chart background colors with theme accents
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded Material Design pastel colors for quadrant chart quadrant backgrounds with theme accent colors.

## Why
The quadrant chart SVG renderer uses hardcoded pastel fills: `["#e8f5e9", "#fff3e0", "#e3f2fd", "#fce4ec"]`. These are light pastels that look fine on the Default theme but:
- On Dark theme: light pastel fills create harsh bright rectangles on dark background
- On Monochrome: colored fills contradict the grayscale palette
- On Blueprint: green/orange/blue/pink clash with the blue-on-white design language
- On Neon: pastels look washed out against vivid accents

## Technical Context
The `render_quadrant_svg()` function receives `&Theme` so theme colors are directly available. Each theme defines 8 accent colors in `theme.colors.accents[]`. Using accents[0..3] with reduced opacity (already applied via `fill-opacity="0.4"` at line ~2196) will harmonize with any theme.

## Specific Changes
- fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs line ~2180: Change `let quadrant_fills = ["#e8f5e9", ...]` to use `theme.colors.accents[0..3]`

## Status
DONE (latest session applied this fix).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quadrant backgrounds use theme accents on all 10 presets
- Fill opacity remains at 0.4 for subtle background effect
- Golden SVG snapshot blessed
close_reason: Quadrant fills now use theme.colors.accents[0..3]
