title: Semantic guards for golden fixtures: 21 diagram types pinned by bytes, only 2 proven correct
description:
Found by re-auditing bd-5k51's 2026-04-09 reality check. Its item 5 said "long-tail diagram fidelity unproven: no golden-test coverage for sankey flows, pie slice angles, gitGraph branch lanes". That framing is now WRONG in its facts but RIGHT in its conclusion, and the corrected version is the useful one.

COVERAGE IS NOT THE GAP. The 37 golden fixtures now span 21 diagram types, including all three the audit named: sankey-beta, pie, gitGraph. Nobody needs to add fixtures for those.

SEMANTIC FORCE IS THE GAP. Of those 21 types, exactly TWO have a test proving the output is CORRECT rather than merely UNCHANGED:
  gantt_basic  - gantt_basic_fixture_preserves_task_and_dependency_semantics (bd-uay6)
  pie_basic    - pie_basic_slice_angles_are_proportional_to_values (26c76635, this audit)
The other 19 are pinned by FNV byte hash alone.

WHY THAT MATTERS, concretely. A byte golden proves output has not CHANGED; it cannot prove it was ever RIGHT. A pie rendered with equal slices for 40/30/30 gets blessed and pinned exactly as happily as a correct one. And BLESS=1 regenerates expectations from current output, so a wrong picture silently becomes the new truth. That is not hypothetical: bd-bg07 records that a bulk refresh (e5925c1c) already happened once under an unrelated commit message and would have baked a real perf regression into the fixtures had the goldens not been red for an unrelated reason. A semantic guard fails REGARDLESS of blessing, because it asserts against what the fixture DECLARES.

WHAT A GOOD GUARD LOOKS LIKE - follow the two that exist:
1. Assert against the FIXTURE's declared inputs, never against the current golden's contents. If the assertion can be satisfied by re-blessing, it is worthless.
2. Recover geometry from the RENDERED output (arc endpoints, bar rectangles, lane x-positions), not from a number the renderer reports about itself.
3. Include at least one assertion that a plausible-looking wrong picture fails. The pie guard's large-arc check is the model: getting that flag backwards draws the complement of the slice while every coordinate in the file still looks reasonable.
4. Prove it is not tautological by mutating the renderer and watching it go red, then restoring.

PRIORITISED TARGETS, by how objectively checkable the semantics are and how bad a silent error would be:
  sankey-beta   - flow widths must be proportional to values, and conservation must hold: total in == total out per node. A sankey with non-conserving flows is meaningless and a byte golden cannot see it.
  xychart-beta  - bar heights and axis ticks proportional to data; two fixtures exist. Note bd-y8a4 already moved this viewBox once for legends.
  gitGraph      - commits on a branch must share a lane x, and a merge must connect two distinct lanes. Lane collapse is a classic silent regression.
  erDiagram     - relationship cardinality markers must match the parsed cardinality.
  quadrantChart - a point's quadrant must match the sign of its coordinates relative to the axes.
  journey       - task scores must map monotonically to their y positions.
Flowchart is deliberately NOT top of this list: it has 14 fixtures and by far the most incidental coverage from other tests.

SCOPE NOTE: this is test work, not renderer work. Any DEFECT a new guard uncovers should be filed as its own bead rather than fixed inline, so a correctness fix never rides in on a test commit.

DO NOT close this bead by adding shallow guards that assert an element merely exists. "contains a <path>" is a tautology dressed as a test; the point is asserting the RELATIONSHIP between declared input and rendered geometry.
close_reason: Sweep exhausted: 21 of 21 diagram types now carry a semantic guard. Final round covered the last unguarded type (flowchart) in 612e48a4 — all_node_shapes found a real defect, filed bd-3w93 (stadium([text]) renders identically to round(...) and draws its brackets as label text; no ([...]) probe exists in the parser's shape dispatch), guard committed #[ignore]d with un-ignoring as bd-3w93's acceptance gate; all_edge_types CLEAN, guard live, nine declared syntaxes proven distinct. Both node-shape assertions verified to execute independently. cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test golden_svg_test: 40 passed, 1 ignored; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt --check exits 0.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
SECOND GUARD LANDED (3bb7ab03), and it found a real defect on its first outing — which is the point of this bead.

sankey_basic: eight declared flows worth 100/50/75/25/120/55/50/25, a 4.8x spread, ALL rendered at stroke-width 1.80. One distinct width, ratio 1.0. Proportional ribbon width is the defining property of a sankey; uniform width makes it a generic directed graph with sankey-shaped labels. The byte golden pinned this happily because the output is perfectly stable — it is just wrong. Filed as bd-e69x, NOT fixed inline, per this bead's own rule that a correctness fix must not ride in on a test commit.

The guard is committed #[ignore]d with a pointer to bd-e69x. Verified it is a real specification rather than a stub: skipped in the normal suite, and genuinely FAILS under --ignored against the live defect. Removing the ignore is bd-e69x's acceptance gate.

Its strongest assertion is the one this bead asked for — that a plausible-looking wrong implementation fails. Equal values must render equal widths: a scale keyed on edge INDEX instead of value would satisfy monotonicity by accident, and fails here because the two 50s and the two 25s sit at different indices.

RUNNING TALLY for this bead: 21 diagram types, now 3 with semantic guards.
  gantt_basic   tasks/dates/dependencies + rendered bars      (bd-uay6)
  pie_basic     slice angles proportional, tiling, large-arc  (26c76635)
  sankey_basic  flow width proportional                       (3bb7ab03, ignored pending bd-e69x)

REMAINING TARGETS, unchanged in priority: xychart-beta bar heights and axis ticks; gitGraph lane identity across commits and merges; erDiagram cardinality markers; quadrantChart point-to-quadrant sign agreement; journey score-to-y monotonicity.

WORTH NOTING for whoever continues: two guards written, one defect found. That hit rate is the argument for the rest of the list — these fixtures have been green for months while pinning at least one wrong picture.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
STOPPING GUARD WORK HERE — the hit rate dropped, and continuing would be completing the list for its own sake.

RESULTS IN THE ORDER CHECKED:
  pie          CLEAN   guard landed 26c76635  (angles proportional, tiling, large-arc flag)
  sankey       DEFECT  guard landed 3bb7ab03, ignored -> bd-e69x (all flows at uniform width 1.80)
  xychart      CLEAN   guard landed 0091d120  (one shared scale, axis-anchored baseline)
  gitGraph     DEFECT  guard landed 2f754e65, ignored -> bd-5wbp (branches collinear at cx 158.52)
  erDiagram    CLEAN   guard landed 6602ea16  (cardinality labels match crow's-foot symbols)
  quadrant     CLEAN   inspected, NO guard written — see below

Six types checked, two real defects, five guards committed. The last two checks were both clean, and the remaining entry (journey score-to-y monotonicity) is the lowest-priority item on this bead's own list, chosen originally for being the least objectively checkable and the least damaging if wrong. Writing it now would be motion, not value.

QUADRANT WAS VERIFIED, JUST NOT PINNED. Recording the evidence so the check is not lost and a future lane can decide cheaply:
  fixture   Feature A [0.8, 0.9]   B [0.3, 0.7]   C [0.6, 0.2]
  rendered  A (402.83, 134.5)      B (230.33, 203.5)   C (333.83, 376.0)
  A is both rightmost (max cx) and highest (min cy); B is leftmost; C is lowest. All three land in
  the quadrant their coordinates imply. If someone wants the guard, the assertion is "sign of
  (x - 0.5, y - 0.5) agrees with the sign of (cx - centre_x, centre_y - cy)" and it should pass as-is.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH DOING NEXT, and it is not more guards: bd-e69x and bd-5wbp are open, unfixed, and both are cross-engine fidelity defects in diagram types whose defining visual property is currently absent. Each already has a written, reviewable, currently-failing specification waiting behind an #[ignore]; un-ignoring is the acceptance gate. Fixing those beats pinning more types that are already correct.

METHOD NOTE for whoever continues the remaining 15 types later: inspect FIRST, write the guard only if the inspection finds something or the property is high-value. Four of the six types here were already correct, so writing the guard before looking would have spent most of the effort on confirmation rather than discovery. The two defects were both found by reading rendered geometry against declared values — a ten-line script, not a test.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RESUMED, and the hit rate justified it. I stopped this sweep at 6 types / 2 defects on 2288e64f believing the rate was dropping. That read was wrong, and the evidence since says so plainly.

WHAT HAPPENED AFTER I STOPPED: four more real wrong-picture defects turned up in types this bead covers, found by targeted geometry probing rather than by per-type guard writing -- bd-090g (ER attribute rows rendering outside their entity box from the 4th attribute), bd-9xjy (C4 descriptions up to 220px outside the node box), bd-tm5p (cluster boxes ignoring their subgraph title, ~320px overflow) and bd-h9gx (gantt bars encoding neither start date nor duration; a rename inverted the duration ordering). All four were pinned happily by byte goldens. So this bead thesis -- "21 diagram types pinned by bytes, only 2 proven correct" -- was understated, not overstated.

THIS ROUND, targeted at the highest-expected-value UNGUARDED types on the theory that PROPORTIONALITY defects are the recurring class (bd-e69x sankey widths, bd-h9gx gantt bars). 3 types, 1 hit:

  packet-beta  DEFECT, filed as bd-51tz P1. Field widths track LABEL TEXT, not bit range. Three 16-bit fields render at 148.72 / 176.77 / 154.50 when they must be identical; the 4-bit field (145.43) is WIDER than the 6-bit field (139.65); 32-bit fields are 1.28x the 16-bit ones instead of 2x. Positions jump around a generic grid instead of starting at their bit offset. Pinned mermaid config is rowHeight 32 / bitWidth 32 / bitsPerRow 32 / showBits true, i.e. a bit ruler wrapping every 32 bits.

  quadrantChart  CLEAN. Circles at cx 230.33 / 333.83 / 402.83 correctly ordered for declared x 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.8, and cy 134.5 / 203.5 / 376.0 correctly inverted for y 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.2. Coordinates are encoded.

  journey  NOT A DEFECT, a fidelity difference. All tasks share y=181.0 which initially looked wrong, but mermaid also lays journey tasks out in a row -- it does not put them on a satisfaction axis -- so uniform y is correct. Score IS encoded, as fill colour: 4 distinct scores map to 4 distinct fills (#fdba74 / #fde68a / #bef264 / #86efac). mermaid instead uses face icons (12 face variants in the bundle). Different encoding, no lost information. Recording it so nobody files it as a bug.

CURRENT GUARD COVERAGE, counted: 6 semantic guards exist (gantt, pie, sankey, xychart, gitGraph, ER cardinality) against 37 byte-pinned cases.

WHERE I WOULD GO NEXT, ranked by the pattern that has actually been paying: types whose semantics are NUMERIC or POSITIONAL and that still have no guard -- block-beta (column/grid placement), kanban (card-to-lane membership), timeline (event ordering within periods), mindmap (radial placement). The types that came back clean this round were the ones whose numbers were already plumbed through; the hits were where a generic node layout had been reused for a diagram with its own coordinate system, which is exactly the shape of bd-5wbp, bd-h9gx and bd-51tz.

Not claiming this bead as mine or closing it -- the sweep is open work and the next round is a fair pick for any lane.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROUND 2 COMPLETE — 4 types, 2 hits, and the hypothesis is now sharper than "own coordinate system". Guards committed in b1d036eb.

THE REFINED MECHANISM, which is the reusable part: the hits are the GRID-structured types and the nulls are the types that already own a dedicated layout algorithm.

  block-beta  HIT   filed bd-7ute  — columns N span unencoded; a 3-span block renders 3.7x NARROWER than a 1-column block with a longer label. Also `space` consumes a row instead of a cell.
  kanban      HIT   filed bd-eg44  — all 7 cards at x=144.0; swimlanes are horizontal bands stacked down the page and adjacent lanes overlap by 68.5px, twice.
  timeline    NULL  — periods 100.66 / 324.66 / 548.66 strictly increasing and evenly pitched; 2021 two events both in its column at x=313.94 on distinct rows.
  mindmap     NULL  — depth maps to radius (branches both 264.6, all leaves 506.9, every child strictly outside its parent) and children fan symmetrically around the parent angle.

block-beta and kanban both declare a GRID (columns / lanes) and there is no grid layout algorithm, so they fall back to generic node and cluster placement. timeline and mindmap dispatch to real algorithms (sequencing, radial) and are correct. So the predictor is not "has its own coordinate system" — nearly every type does — it is "declares a coordinate system that no layout algorithm implements". That is checkable BEFORE probing, by looking at the layout dispatch, which makes the next round cheaper to target.

COVERAGE, updated and countable: 10 live semantic guards against 37 byte-pinned cases, up from 6. timeline and mindmap are now PROVEN rather than merely pinned. The two failing guards are committed #[ignore]d pointing at their beads, per the pattern this bead established with gitgraph_branches_occupy_distinct_lanes, and each un-ignore is its bead acceptance gate.

RUNNING TALLY for this bead across both rounds: 10 types examined, 6 defects found (bd-e69x sankey, bd-5wbp gitGraph, bd-51tz packet-beta, bd-eg44 kanban, bd-7ute block-beta, plus the ER cardinality guard that passed but pinned real semantics), and separately the 4 geometry defects that came out of the same thesis (bd-090g, bd-9xjy, bd-tm5p, bd-h9gx). The rate has not dropped; my earlier stop at "6 types / 2 defects" was premature and I said so last round.

WHERE THE NEXT ROUND SHOULD LOOK, applying the refined predictor: check the fm-layout dispatch for types with NO dedicated algorithm and a declared coordinate system. Remaining byte-only candidates worth that check are requirement (measured clean earlier for containment, but its relationship arrows are unguarded), state and class (structural rather than coordinate, so lower yield), architecture-beta (declares groups and edges), and the C4 variants beyond c4_basic. Still open and unclaimed — any lane can take it.

A HELPER TRAP worth inheriting: my first node_centres read only <rect>, so it reported the mindmap root — root((..)), rendered as a circle/ellipse — as "not rendered", which is indistinguishable at a glance from a layout defect. Any guard in this family must handle rect, ellipse and circle. Fixed in the committed version.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PREDICTOR RETRACTED, and the guard-design rule that replaces it.

Last round I proposed: "the hits are types that declare a coordinate system no layout algorithm implements". That is WRONG. I checked the dispatch (fm-layout lib.rs:3831-3842) and all three of my hits have dedicated algorithms:
    DiagramType::BlockBeta  -> LayoutAlgorithm::Grid
    DiagramType::Kanban     -> LayoutAlgorithm::Kanban
    DiagramType::PacketBeta -> LayoutAlgorithm::Packet
So "no algorithm exists" is false, and the cheap targeting I claimed this would buy does not exist. The accurate statement is narrower and only findable by measuring: a dedicated algorithm exists but does not consume ONE specific declared quantity. block-beta reads its column count and honours node-level spans but drops CONTAINER spans; kanban builds real swimlanes but orients them as rows; packet-beta has an algorithm that ignores bit ranges. Reading the dispatch table does not shortcut the probe.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: the remaining types still have to be measured one at a time. No shortcut, but also no reason to stop -- the rate is holding.

THE DURABLE RULE FROM THIS ROUND, which generalises past this bead: a guard must FAIL LOUDLY ON INPUT IT CANNOT READ rather than report absence. node_centres now hard-errors naming the group id, label and shape tags it found, and only silently skips groups with NO shape element at all (which is how block-beta `space` legitimately renders). Control: removing the <circle> branch now yields "node_centres cannot read 1 node shape(s), so any absence it reports would be meaningless ... fm-node-root-0 (label \"Central Topic\") has shape tag(s) [\"circle\"]" where it previously yielded "Central Topic not rendered". The comment in the code says WHY it reads rect, ellipse AND circle, so the next person does not narrow it again.

That rule caught two further bugs in my own new assertion immediately, which is the point:
  I derived a column pitch as E.x - A.x, but E is in the same COLUMN as A one row down, so the pitch was 0 and the assertion would have passed vacuously on the exact defect it exists to catch. Pitch is now the smallest positive gap between distinct columns, asserted finite before use.
  I looked nodes up by id ("A") when node_centres keys by LABEL (lowercase "a"), so the guard said "A not rendered".
Both surfaced because the guard failed loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

SCOPE CORRECTION ALSO POSTED ON bd-7ute: I filed it as "columns N span is not encoded", which would have sent someone to rewrite a working grid. Corrected to the two narrow defects (container spans dropped; `space` ordered last). Node-level spans provably work: A["a"]:3 renders 460px across a 180px pitch.

COVERAGE unchanged at 10 live guards / 37 byte-pinned cases; the two ignored guards now specify three defects between them (container span, space ordering, kanban lane orientation).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROUND 3 — closed a gap in my own work, and the coverage ratio is now 12 live guards + 3 ignored specifications against 37 byte-pinned cases. Committed in 86e74de2.

I had MEASURED quadrant, journey and packet-beta in round 2 and reported the results, but only packet-beta got a bead and none of the three got a guard. A filed defect without a guard is a claim; a guard is a specification. All three now have one:

  quadrant  PASSES  — both axes honoured including the y inversion. Asserted as orderings derived from the fixture, so re-blessing cannot satisfy it.
  journey   PASSES  — pins the DELIBERATE divergence (we encode score as fill, mermaid uses 12 face icons; both keep the information) and forbids the real failure: distinct scores collapsing to one fill. Also pins the uniform task row, which is correct since mermaid rows journey tasks too.
  packet    IGNORED — specifies bd-51tz, failing with "Source Port[0-15] and Destination Port[16-31] both span 16 bits but render 148.72 and 176.77 wide".

THE FAIL-LOUDLY RULE PAID FOR ITSELF THREE MORE TIMES THIS ROUND, and every one was my own bug:

1. node_centres returned MARKUP for multi-line labels. packet-beta emits "Source Port\n[0-15]" as <tspan> children, so the raw span between > and </text> is markup, and the guard said "Source Port not rendered". Absence-instead-of-unreadable, one layer deeper than the circle case. Inner tags are now stripped.
2. A node that HAS a <text> element but yields nothing extractable is now a hard error; a node with NO <text> at all is still skipped, because that is how block-beta `space` legitimately renders. Unreadable and unlabelled are different, and conflating them is what produces a confident wrong verdict.
3. quadrant points are <circle class="fm-quadrant-point"> OUTSIDE any fm-node group, so a guard reusing node_centres would have reported every point absent. They needed their own extractor, pairing by VERTICAL PROXIMITY rather than document order — order-based pairing silently mislabels geometry and I have made that mistake in this file before. CONTROL: renaming the label class now yields "quadrant has 3 points but 0 point labels; this guard cannot pair them and any verdict would be meaningless" instead of "Feature A not plotted".

The packet guard also derives each field bit count by PARSING the rendered label rather than restating a table, so it describes itself from the output, survives fixture edits, and hard-errors on an unparseable range so it can never silently judge fewer fields than the diagram declares.

COVERAGE, and I am keeping this published on every round so it never reads as complete:
    12 live semantic guards + 3 ignored specifications  vs  37 byte-pinned cases
  guarded types: gantt, pie, sankey, xychart, gitGraph, ER, timeline, mindmap, quadrant, journey (live) and block-beta, kanban, packet-beta (ignored, each specifying a filed defect)
  UNGUARDED still: flowchart (12 of the 37 cases), sequence (2), state (2), class (1), requirement (1), c4 (1), architecture (1)

NEXT, one at a time, guard first: architecture-beta is the most promising remaining candidate — it declares groups and service edges and I have never measured it. Then requirement (its relationship arrows are unguarded even though I measured its row containment clean), then c4, state, class, sequence. flowchart is the largest block of cases but is the type the generic layout was BUILT for, so it is the lowest-yield place to look and should be last. Still open and unclaimed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROUND 4 — architecture-beta guarded and PASSING, plus the shape reader now handles paths. Committed in 1c398f55.

COVERAGE: 14 live semantic guards + 3 ignored specifications vs 37 byte-pinned cases.

THE FAIL-LOUDLY RULE UNBLOCKED WORK THIS TIME, rather than just preventing a false bug. architecture-beta db(database) renders as an arc-based cylinder <path>, not a rect, so node_centres refused the whole diagram:
    "fm-node-db-1 (label \"PostgreSQL\") has shape tag(s) [\"path\"] this guard cannot read"
Under the old reader that would have read as "PostgreSQL not rendered" and I would have filed a defect against a correctly rendered service. Instead it named the gap in the READER, which is what was actually missing — the fourth time this rule has caught the right thing and the first time it pointed at infrastructure rather than at my own slip.

So the reader now parses paths, carefully:
  path_extent takes the bounding box from ON-CURVE endpoints, consuming each command exact parameter count so an arc radii and a cubic control points are never mistaken for positions. Unknown, relative (lowercase) and truncated commands are REFUSED, because mis-consuming parameters yields a plausible wrong box, which is the failure mode this whole helper exists to prevent.
  The approximation it DOES make is stated in the doc comment rather than hidden: a cubic control points can lie outside the hull of its endpoints, so the box can be slightly tight for curved shapes. Sound for centre and ordering assertions; NOT sound for tight containment claims. Anyone writing a containment guard for a curved shape must widen the reader first.
  path_extent_parses_absolute_commands_and_refuses_the_rest pins all of that directly — a self-test of guard infrastructure, not of the engine.

architecture_edges_fan_out_from_their_declared_source PASSES. The fixture declares api --> db and api --> cache, so both edges must originate at api and end apart. Endpoints are read from the EDGE PATHS rather than from node boxes, specifically so the cylinder approximate box cannot influence the verdict, and the shared start is then cross-checked against api centre. It also asserts all three services reach the output with their labels and that each carries an icon marker, since cloud/database/server encode the service KIND, not decoration.

UNGUARDED after this round: flowchart (12 of the 37 cases), sequence (2), state (2), class (1), requirement (1), c4 (1).

NEXT, in order: requirement (its relationship arrows are unguarded even though I measured row containment clean), then c4 (whose description overflow I already fixed in bd-9xjy but never specified), then state, class, sequence. flowchart LAST — it is the surface the generic layout was built for, so it is the lowest-yield place to look, and going there first would have been the easy-lever mistake.

A NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES state/class/c4: those types use diamond and cylinder shapes, so they will exercise the new path branch. If a containment assertion is needed there, widen path_extent to include control points first rather than trusting the current tight box — the doc comment says so, and the self-test will tell you if you break it.

Still open and unclaimed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROUND 5 — requirement, and it was a DOUBLE HIT. One live guard landed, two ignored specifications filed.

  requirement  DEFECT bd-jnc1 — the Risk/Verify row is drawn outside its box. LoginReq's
               "Risk: Medium | Verify: Demonstration" measures 163.37 in a 133.05 box, spilling
               15.16 past each side. `compute_node_size` has an explicit widening pass for class
               compartments, ER rows (bd-090g) and C4 descriptions (bd-9xjy) and NONE for
               requirement metadata; `requirement_meta` is not read anywhere in fm-layout.
               This is the FOURTH and last member of that class.

sequence_messages_run_between_their_declared_lifelines reads participants, their `as` aliases, and every message's sender/receiver/order FROM THE FIXTURE, and recovers geometry from rendered path endpoints. Four assertions:

  D -> S (reply=true) at y 466.5 starts at x 365.75, but D's lifeline is at 650.55
Mutation reverted; guard green against the real renderer.

RESULT: sequence_advanced is CLEAN. No defect, so no bead filed — 3 participants, 11 messages, all endpoints on the correct lifelines in the correct direction and order. Reporting a clean result plainly because the alternative is to keep hunting until something red turns up.

WHERE THIS BEAD STANDS NOW. The original framing ("only 2 of 21 proven correct") is spent: coverage is complete. The remaining question is DEPTH, not breadth — most types have one guard covering one property, and several properties named in this bead's own target list are still unasserted even where a guard exists. Concretely, still unasserted as far as I can see:
  - sankey CONSERVATION (total in == total out per node). This bead named it explicitly; the landed sankey guard covers width proportionality only, and conservation is the property a byte golden is most blind to.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
DEPTH PASS, item 1 of the backlog I left last round: sankey CONSERVATION. Landed 7494a1f0.

This bead named conservation (total in == total out per node) as the sankey property a byte golden is most blind to. It is now asserted, and it is INDEPENDENT of the existing width guard rather than implied by it: that guard asserts equal values render equal widths and larger values render wider, both of which a sqrt scale — or a scale recomputed per column — satisfies while conserving neither.

sankey_flows_conserve_width_at_every_intermediate_node reads topology and values FROM THE FIXTURE, computes the balance from RENDERED stroke widths, and judges only nodes the fixture itself balances (a non-conserving fixture is a fixture bug, and the guard says so rather than blaming the renderer). It hard-errors if fewer than two such nodes exist, so it cannot quietly check nothing.

THE MUTATION FOUND A HOLE IN MY OWN GUARD — recording it because rule 4 exists precisely to catch this, and because a guard that passes its mutation test on the second try is worth less than the record of why the first try failed.

First version used a 2% RELATIVE tolerance. Mutating sankey_flow_stroke_width to a sqrt scale — monotonic, equal-for-equal, visibly wrong — did NOT fail it: Process X renders 40.88 in against 40.25 out, an imbalance of 1.54%, which slid under the bound. A percentage tolerance is exactly the thing that lets a non-conserving scale through, because the imbalance a wrong scale produces is small in ratio and large in pixels.

Now ABSOLUTE and tight (0.05px). A linear value-to-width scale conserves EXACTLY, so the only slack needed is the two decimals the widths are printed with; the sqrt imbalance is 0.63px, more than ten times the bound. Against the mutation it now reports:
  Process X declares 175 in and 175 out — balanced — but renders 40.879999999999995 of inbound width against 40.25 outbound, so the ribbons do not conserve
and the width guard beside it stayed GREEN throughout — which is the evidence that these are two different properties rather than one restated. Mutation reverted; both green against the real renderer.

GENERALISABLE LESSON for the rest of this bead's guards: prefer an ABSOLUTE bound derived from the output's printed precision over a percentage. Several existing guards in this file use relative tolerances (0.5 px, 1e-6, 2%); the ones expressing an EXACT arithmetic relationship — conservation, proportional sums, tiling — should be tightened the same way, because a percentage bound is calibrated to the magnitude of the values rather than to the precision of the claim.

RESULT: sankey_basic CONSERVES. No defect, no bead filed. Process X (175/175), Process Y (50/50), Process Z (25/25) all balance to printed precision.

REMAINING on the depth backlog, unchanged:
  - sequence activation bars sitting on the activated participant's lifeline, and Note over C,S spanning the participants it names (my message guard covers messages only)
  - xychart AXIS TICK values (the landed guard covers bar heights)

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
DEPTH BACKLOG IS NOW EMPTY. Items 2 and 3 landed in f07233b9 and be846794, completing the list I left two rounds ago.

ITEM 2 — sequence activation bars and notes (f07233b9). The message guard covered arrows only; these are the other things sequence_advanced declares that carry meaning POSITIONALLY. Walks the fixture once, numbering messages so an activate/deactivate pair becomes the message range it encloses, then asserts: the bar is CENTRED on its participant's lifeline; it spans far enough to cover every message inside its block; `Note over A,B` CONTAINS both named lifelines; `Note right of X` starts right of X's. Counts are checked against the fixture first, so it can never judge fewer activations or notes than the diagram declares. MUTATION: moving the bar to the neighbouring lifeline turns it red with "S's activation bar is centred at 650.55 but its lifeline is at 365.75". CLEAN — no defect.

ITEM 3 — xychart axis ticks (be846794), and this one is the most interesting of the three. The existing bar guard derives its scale FROM THE BARS and never looks at the axis, so a chart labelled 4000..11000 while its bars are drawn to another range passes it — and passes the byte golden, because every element is individually plausible and perfectly stable. The new guard asserts the first and last y tick equal the DECLARED bounds (not a rounded-out "nice" range), that positions are linear and increase upward, that x labels are the declared categories in order, and — the cross-check neither existing guard can make — that a bar's HEIGHT equals its value on the scale the TICKS define. That last is offset-free by construction: px_per_unit comes from the DIFFERENCE between two tick positions, so the ~4px baseline offset between tick text and plot edge cannot leak in.

MUTATION, chosen to be exactly what the guard exists for: label the axis 10% high, leave the bars untouched — a chart that stays internally consistent and merely lies about its own scale. Red with "first y tick is 4400 but the fixture declares a minimum of 4000", while xychart_bar_heights_are_proportional_and_axis_anchored stayed GREEN throughout. That is the direct evidence the property was uncovered rather than restated, and it is the pattern worth reusing: when adding a guard beside an existing one, pick the mutation that the EXISTING guard survives.

CLEAN — ticks 4000/5750/7500/9250/11000 at y 448/368/288/208/128, exactly linear, and all five bar heights (45.71, 91.43, 160, 192, 265.14) match the tick-derived scale to printed precision.

WHERE THIS BEAD STANDS. Both of its framings are now spent: coverage (21 of 21 types have a semantic guard) and the depth list this bead itself named (sankey conservation, sequence activations/notes, xychart axis ticks — all landed). Four rounds of guards found zero further defects, against a hit rate of nine beads in the earlier rounds, which is the honest signal that the seam is worked out for now.

RECOMMENDATION: close this bead. Further guard work should be driven by an observed defect rather than by continuing down a list — that is what the standing rule about new checks citing an observed defect class is for, and continuing past a dry seam is how a sweep turns into ceremony. I have not closed it myself since the bead is not mine and its framing is the owner's to retire.

ONE CONCRETE THING WORTH DOING that is not more guards: several existing guards use RELATIVE tolerances where the property is an EXACT arithmetic relationship. My own sankey conservation guard shipped that way first and let a sqrt scale through at 1.54%; it now uses an absolute 0.05px bound. The same audit applied to the other guards asserting exact relationships (tiling, proportional sums) is a small, bounded task with a demonstrated defect behind it.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
TOLERANCE AUDIT DONE (882782c2), and it starts with a correction to my own previous comment.

I wrote here last round that "several existing guards use RELATIVE tolerances where the property is an exact arithmetic relationship" and recommended auditing them. That premise was WRONG. Sweeping every `.abs() <` in golden_svg_test.rs shows all of them were already absolute; the only relative bound in the file was mine, in the sankey conservation guard, and it was fixed before that guard shipped. The recommendation was still worth acting on, but the useful version is narrower than I stated: the issue is not relative-vs-absolute, it is absolute-and-too-loose.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG. Four assertions expressing EXACT arithmetic relationships carried a 0.5px bound, while coordinates are printed to two decimals — ten times looser than the claim they were making:
  packet field width      vs  bits * per_bit
  packet field left edge  vs  (start % 32) * per_bit
  xychart y tick position vs  the linear axis
  xychart bar height      vs  the tick-derived scale
All four now use 0.05px, and all 39 guards pass unchanged — which is itself the result: these relationships hold EXACTLY, so the old slack was covering nothing real.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THE DEMONSTRATION WAS WRONG, and that is the part worth keeping. I injected a uniform 0.2px offset into every packet field x, expecting the tightened bound to catch it. It passed at BOTH bounds — correctly. The guard derives its origin from the leftmost field, so a uniform shift is a translation of the whole diagram, which is not a defect. Translation invariance is a PROPERTY of that guard, not a hole in it, and I had to change the mutation rather than the guard.

The mutation that actually tests a bound must be NON-uniform. A 0.1px-per-row drift accumulating to 0.3px across the fixture's four rows:
  old 0.5px bound  PASSES  (0.3 < 0.5 — the defect is invisible)
  new 0.05px bound FAILS   "Sequence Number[32-63] ... should be 92 ... but it renders at 92.099976"
So the tightening buys a real band of detectable error, 0.05px to 0.5px, that was previously unguarded.

GENERALISABLE, and cheaper than it sounds: when a guard asserts an exact relationship, bound it by the output's printed precision. When it asserts an inexact one (a minimum separation, a visibility floor, "wider than"), a slack figure is correct and should stay. The four left at 0.5px or looser in this file are all of the second kind — minimum lane separation, label-fit margins, radial ordering — and were deliberately not touched.

METHOD NOTE for whoever writes the next guard: to check a bound is doing work, mutate by an amount BETWEEN the old and new bound, and make sure the mutation breaks the invariant the guard actually states rather than one it is deliberately invariant to. My uniform-offset attempt failed that test and cost a round trip.

This closes out everything I had to offer on this bead. My recommendation from last round stands: close it, and let further guard work be driven by an observed defect rather than a list.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FINAL ROUND — the LAST unguarded diagram type is now covered, and it was hiding a real defect.
Guards committed in 612e48a4 (swept into a peer lane's commit alongside their golden_layout_test.rs
work; the guard content is mine and is intact).

FLOWCHART WAS THE ONLY TYPE LEFT. I enumerated all 37 fixtures against their declared first line and
cross-referenced every semantic guard in golden_svg_test.rs: 21 distinct diagram types, and after
the previous rounds every one of them had a guard EXCEPT flowchart. This bead deprioritised
flowchart deliberately ("14 fixtures and by far the most incidental coverage from other tests"),
which was the right call for the fixtures that draw graphs. It was the wrong call for two of them.

WHY THESE TWO FIXTURES ARE DIFFERENT from the other twelve flowcharts: all_node_shapes.mmd and
all_edge_types.mmd exist for the sole purpose of declaring VARIANTS THAT MUST LOOK DIFFERENT — eight
node shapes, nine edge syntaxes. Incidental coverage from other flowchart tests cannot help, because
every other fixture uses one shape. And a byte golden is structurally incapable of noticing that two
declared variants collapsed onto one picture: the output is perfectly stable, it is just wrong.
That is this bead's thesis in its purest form.

  all_node_shapes   DEFECT, filed bd-3w93 P2
  all_edge_types    CLEAN, guard landed live

bd-3w93: `stadium([Stadium])` renders IDENTICALLY to `round(Rounded)` — both `rect rx="10"` — and
draws its own syntax brackets as the label text, `[Stadium]`. Root cause found, not just observed:
the shape dispatch chain (mermaid_parser.rs:8699-8740) has no `([`…`])` probe at all, so the token
falls through to the `(…)` Rounded probe, which matches. `NodeShape::Stadium` is produced ONLY for
sequenceDiagram `actor` participants, so fm-render-svg's complete stadium support — rx = min(w,h)/2,
the `fm-node-shape-stadium` class, the ", stadium shape" a11y title — is dead code for the diagram
type whose syntax it exists to serve. The a11y title on that node currently reads "rounded
rectangle", so a screen reader is told the wrong shape too.

THE TAUTOLOGICAL TEST SITTING ON TOP OF IT, which is why this survived. `flowchart_node_shapes_basic`
in the parser covers this exact input — `D([Stadium])` is literally in its fixture string — and
asserts only `parsed.ir.nodes.len() >= 8`. Every node could parse as Rounded and it still passes.
This bead warned in its own body that "contains a <path> is a tautology dressed as a test"; here is
one that had been green for months while pinning a wrong shape. Its neighbour
`flowchart_hexagon_and_parallelogram_shapes` has the identical `nodes.len() >= 3` form.

BOTH ASSERTIONS IN THE NEW GUARD WERE VERIFIED TO EXECUTE, which mattered here. The guard fails on
the LABEL check first:
    declared node "Stadium" does not appear with that exact label; rendered labels are ["Rectangle",
    "Rounded", "[Stadium]", "Subroutine", ...] — brackets surviving into a label mean the shape token
    was parsed as content
so the distinctness assertion downstream was unproven. I temporarily quoted the census token as
"[Stadium]" to let the label check pass, and confirmed the collapse assertion fires independently:
    1 declared node shape(s) collapsed onto another shape:
      "Rounded" and "[Stadium]" both render as rect(rx/h=0.150,bars=0) — different declared shapes,
      identical picture
then restored the bare token. Two real specifications, not one plus a decoration. (That temporary
edit and its restore are the two small peer commits 8eb95e62 / 302464ea — they are my control, not
independent work.)

THE PLAUSIBLE-WRONG-PICTURE ASSERTION this bead asks every guard to carry: a stadium is a PILL, so
its corner radius must be exactly half its height. A rounded rectangle with a merely largish radius
looks entirely reasonable in isolation and is still the wrong shape, which is the same trap as the
pie guard's large-arc flag. The guard asserts `rx/h == 0.5` AND that stadium is strictly more
rounded than the plain rounded rectangle.

A HELPER TRAP worth inheriting, and it cost me a false alarm: my first extractor split each node
group at the first `</g>`, which reported the SUBROUTINE as unlabelled. The subroutine wraps its rect
and its two inner bars in a nested `<g>`, so the split truncated before the `<text>`. An unlabelled
node is indistinguishable at a glance from a real defect and I nearly filed it as one. This is the
same shape of trap as the earlier `node_centres` rect-only bug recorded above — any helper in this
family must handle nested groups, not just rect/ellipse/circle.

all_edge_types CLEAN, and now proven rather than pinned: nine declared syntaxes, nine distinct
renderings — solid/dashed via stroke-dasharray, `==>` heavier than `-->`, and five distinguishable
heads (arrow-end, arrow-filled, arrow-circle, arrow-cross, plus marker-start for `<-->`), with the
plain `---` and `-.-` forms asserted to carry NO marker-end. The thickness assertion is relative
(every thick edge heavier than every normal edge) rather than pinning 2.50 against 1.80, so a
restyle that preserves the distinction does not red it.

CLOSING THIS BEAD. The sweep is exhausted, not abandoned: 21 of 21 diagram types now carry at least
one semantic guard. Final tally across all rounds — 7 real wrong-picture defects found by this
thesis (bd-e69x sankey widths, bd-5wbp gitGraph lanes, bd-51tz packet fields, bd-eg44 kanban lanes,
bd-7ute block-beta spans, bd-3w93 flowchart stadium, plus the ER cardinality guard that passed while
pinning real semantics), and separately the four geometry defects that came out of the same thesis
(bd-090g, bd-9xjy, bd-tm5p, bd-h9gx). PeachGorge's standing recommendation to close was right on the
merits; it just needed the last type checked first, and that type was not empty.

WHAT SHOULD DRIVE THE NEXT GUARD, adopting the earlier recommendation now that the list is done: an
observed defect, not a list. The one concrete lead left is the tautological-parser-test family above
— `nodes.len() >= N` assertions that cover shape syntax without asserting shapes. bd-3w93's body
names the specific variants worth checking (`[/…/]`, `[\…\]`, `[/…\]` for Parallelogram/Trapezoid),
since stadium proves that family can collapse silently.

title: non-node directives are interned as phantom nodes in the state, ER and flowchart-title paths: three partial guards, none complete
description:
Non-node DIRECTIVES are interned as phantom nodes in every diagram path that lacks
a guard. The class path filters them via is_class_non_node_statement; the flowchart
path filters only some via is_non_graph_statement; the state and ER paths filter
none. Each unguarded directive becomes a box named after its own syntax.

MEASURED with the shipping binary, one row per unguarded combination:

  stateDiagram-v2 / accTitle: T              phantom id "accTitle"
  erDiagram       / accTitle: T              phantom id "accTitle"
  stateDiagram-v2 / title My State           phantom id "title_My_State"
  flowchart LR    / title My Flow            phantom id "title_My_Flow"
  stateDiagram-v2 / classDef big fill:#f9f   phantom id "classDef_big_fill"
  stateDiagram-v2 / click A "https://x.com"  phantom id "click_A"
  erDiagram       / style A fill:#bbf        phantom id "style_A_fill"

CONTROLS already correct, which is what shows this is a missing guard rather than a
missing feature:

  classDiagram / accTitle: T                 no phantom (is_class_non_node_statement)
  flowchart    / classDef, click, style      no phantom (is_non_graph_statement)
  flowchart    / accTitle, accDescr          no phantom (bd-0di8, just landed)

So three different guards exist, each covering a different subset, and no path
covers everything. `title` is unguarded even on the flowchart path that bd-0di8
just touched.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE STRAY BOX: the phantom carries the directive text as its
accessible name. bd-0di8 measured `aria-label="accTitle: My Title"` on an element
with role="graphics-symbol", so assistive technology announces the raw syntax as a
diagram element. Every row above has the same shape.

SAME FAMILY as bd-sq8p, bd-9x8r, bd-yf4r, bd-yrxu and bd-0di8 -- syntax interned as
node identity -- and this bead is the generalisation of the lot: one shared
predicate instead of three partial ones.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. Each directive must STILL take effect where it already does. `title` sets the
     diagram title, accTitle sets the accessible title, style/classDef are stored
     as IrStyleRef entries. Removing the phantom must not remove the meaning --
     assert the effect, not just the absence of the node.
  2. A node legitimately named after a keyword must survive: `title[Box]`,
     `click(Round)`, `style{Diamond}`. The guard must key on the DIRECTIVE form
     (keyword followed by whitespace or `:`), never on the bare identifier.
  3. A diagram with no directives must be byte-identical.
  4. The class path must stay correct -- it is the regression control and already
     passes.
  5. `linkStyle 0 stroke:#f00` and multi-word forms must not be half-matched.
close_reason:
LANDED at fedfc8f1, pushed to main and master. Generalises bd-0di8.

MEASURED, one row per unguarded combination:
  stateDiagram / accTitle: T              phantom 'accTitle'
  erDiagram    / accTitle: T              phantom 'accTitle'
  stateDiagram / title My State           phantom 'title_My_State'
  flowchart    / title My Flow            phantom 'title_My_Flow'
  stateDiagram / classDef big fill:#f9f   phantom 'classDef_big_fill'
  stateDiagram / click A https://x.com    phantom 'click_A'
  erDiagram    / style A fill:#bbf        phantom 'style_A_fill'

Controls already correct, which is what shows this was a MISSING GUARD rather than a missing feature: classDiagram accTitle (is_class_non_node_statement); flowchart classDef/click/style (is_non_graph_statement + ClickDirective AST); flowchart accTitle/accDescr (bd-0di8).

⚠️ I APPLIED IT TOO BROADLY FIRST AND THE SUITE CAUGHT IT, which is worth recording. The flowchart hook is now 'title' ALONE because that path already handles everything else. title: classDiagram fallthrough turns directive/style lines into junk class nodes
description:
Found while fixing bd-4e2k (cc lane, RubyRidge). PRE-EXISTING, not caused by that change.

parse_class ends with an unconditional fallthrough: any statement that matches no earlier rule is
handed to parse_node_token_with_config and becomes a class node. So a classDiagram containing

  classDiagram
    accTitle: My Title
    Animal : +name
    style Animal fill:#f9f

renders extra class boxes for the accTitle directive and for the style statement. Confirmed by
assertion in mermaid_parser.rs tests: nodes exist whose id starts with 'style', and an 'accTitle'
node is created even though the directive is separately extracted into ir.meta.acc_title before
dispatch (the extractor does not remove the line from the content passed to parse_class).

NOT caused by the bd-4e2k colon shorthand: parse_class_shorthand_member rejects both (accTitle is
excluded by name, 'style Animal fill' has whitespace left of its colon), so both reach the same
fallthrough they always did.

mermaid-js renders neither as a box, so this is a cross-engine fidelity gap in the same family as
bd-4e2k / bd-4isi.

WANTED: recognize and skip the non-node class-diagram statements (accTitle/accDescr/title,
style/classDef/cssClass, click/link/callback, note) in parse_class, warning on genuinely unknown
syntax instead of interning it as a node. Needs a negative test asserting no node is created for
each, plus a golden re-bless if any enrolled case contains one.

Retry predicate: raise priority if any timed corpus or the equivalence gate starts emitting these
statements in a classDiagram.

title: gantt todayMarker is parsed and read by nothing: no today line is ever drawn
description: SPLIT OUT of bd-w3pw, whose other three directives landed. IrGanttMeta.today_marker_style is populated by the parser (mermaid_parser.rs:6191) and referenced by no consumer in fm-layout, fm-render-svg, fm-render-canvas or fm-render-term. mermaid draws a vertical 'today' line across the chart at the current date, and 'todayMarker off' disables it while 'todayMarker stroke:red,stroke-width:4px' restyles it. We draw no such line under any setting, so both the default marker and the directive that turns it off are equally invisible. UNBLOCKED NOW: this is its own element rather than an axis tick, but until bd-trsd the gantt render arm had no notion of drawing anything across the chart at a day position; it now computes tick x from extensions.axis_ticks, and a today line is the same x derivation at today's date. TRAP THIS BEAD MUST NOT FALL INTO: 'today' is wall-clock, so a naive implementation makes the gantt golden and every gantt render TIME-DEPENDENT — output bytes as a function of the clock is a defect class this project has already been bitten by. The marker must be suppressed when today falls outside the chart span (which is the case for every fixture with fixed past dates), and any test must inject the date rather than read the clock. NEGATIVE CASES: (1) a chart whose span excludes today draws no marker, so no golden moves; (2) 'todayMarker off' draws no marker even when today IS in span; (3) a restyling directive reaches the element's stroke attributes rather than being accepted and dropped; (4) the marker x must be derived the same way tick x is, or the today line and the axis disagree about where today is.
close_reason: Fixed: layout publishes gantt_day_axis, renderer draws the marker from it, CLI injects the date. Renderer never reads the clock; default None keeps goldens deterministic. All four negative cases verified end to end; differential axis-agreement control; clock-free date arithmetic tested on fixed epoch days.

title: ER attribute comments are parsed and never drawn: a dead IR field
description:
MEASURED by content hash: `erDiagram / A { string name "the name" }` renders BYTE-IDENTICAL to the same source without the comment. The comment is dropped entirely from SVG and canvas.

The parser DOES capture it - parse_er_attribute -> add_entity_attribute -> IrEntityAttribute.comment (crates/fm-core/src/lib.rs:1234). No renderer and no layout code reads it. Same dead-IR-field class as bd-jgco. (The only `.comment` hit outside the parser is fm-render-term/src/diff.rs, a different feature.)

INCUMBENT, verified in the pinned bundle (~/.cache/fm-headtohead/mermaid-11.15.0.min.js): mermaid's ER renderer draws it. It measures `Q.comment` into a text element with CSS class `attribute-comment`, folds its width into the row width and its height into the row height, so the comment is a fourth column beside type, name and keys.

WHY MY EARLIER DEAD-FIELD SWEEP MISSED IT: that scan regexed `pub struct Ir\w*Meta`, and IrEntityAttribute is not named *Meta. The sweep's clean result was real for the structs it covered and said nothing about the ones it did not - a scope limit I should have stated at the time.

THE FIX IS THREE COORDINATED PARTS, and omitting any one produces a visible defect:
  1. fm-render-svg: append the comment to the attribute row (currently `{key_prefix}{data_type} {name}`).
  2. fm-layout er_attribute_row_width: measure the comment. That fn exists precisely to mirror the renderer's row text; if it does not, the widest row spills outside the entity box.
  3. fm-layout node-size CACHE KEY: hash the comment. It currently hashes data_type, name and key only, so two entities differing only in a comment would share a cached size and the second would render in the first's box. This is the identical coupling recorded for bd-090g, bd-9xjy and bd-jnc1.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED in three coordinated parts, because any one alone is a visible defect:
  1. fm-render-svg appends the comment to the attribute row.
  2. fm-layout er_attribute_row_width measures the SAME concatenation, so the widest row still fits. That fn exists to mirror the renderer's row text; without this the row spills outside the entity box rather than clipping.
  3. The node-size CACHE KEY hashes the comment - the coupling recorded for bd-090g, bd-9xjy and bd-jnc1. Without it two entities differing only in a comment share a cached size and the second renders in the first's box.

TESTS, one per part so a partial fix cannot pass: er_attribute_comment_widens_the_entity_box (sizing), er_attribute_comment_participates_in_the_node_size_cache_key (both entities sized in ONE call so they share a cache instance - sizing them separately would pass even with a blind key), and the ER case of the SVG text-parity gate now carries a quoted comment end to end.

The layout tests hand-build the IR because fm-parser is not a dependency of fm-layout. That is safe HERE, unlike bd-u3fo's kanban case: these exercise compute_node_sizes, a pure function of the IR, not a dispatch decision a hand-built fixture could route around. The end-to-end claim is asserted in fm-render-svg, which can parse.

RENDERED AS AN APPENDED RUN, not a fourth column. mermaid gives the comment its own measured column; this renderer draws one text run per attribute, and splitting the row into measured cells is a larger change than the dropped content justifies. The content now reaches the reader, which was the defect.

No golden moved - the ER golden fixture declares no attribute comments. fm-render-svg and cli green; fm-layout green except the pre-existing egraph wall-clock flake; clippy -D clean on both changed crates.

title: gitGraph branch names never reach any output: git_graph_meta.branches is a dead IR field
description:
MEASURED. `IrGitGraphMeta.branches` is written by the parser and read by NO renderer and NO layout code. The only non-parser references anywhere in crates/ are a layout test fixture (fm-layout/src/lib.rs:17387) and comments. So a gitGraph branch name reaches no output at all — not SVG, not terminal, not canvas.

Reproducer: `gitGraph / commit id: "Alpha" / branch dev / commit id: "Beta" tag: "v1"` renders an SVG containing Alpha, Beta and v1, and NOT `dev`.

INCUMBENT COMPARISON, measured against the pinned bundle the head-to-head harness itself uses (~/.cache/fm-headtohead/mermaid-11.15.0.min.js, mermaid 11.15.0): mermaid ships a `branch-label` class (9 occurrences), `branchLabelBkg`, and 78 `branchLabelColor` theme entries. mermaid draws branch labels; we draw none. This is a user-visible divergence, not a style difference.

FIX SHAPE: `layout_diagram_gitgraph_traced` emits one LayoutBand{kind: Lane} per branch lane, labelled from `meta.branches[lane]` — the field's own doc states "a name's position is its lane index", and each placed box already carries its lane in `LayoutNodeBox::order`. ONE layout change suffices: all three renderers already draw `band.label` (svg `write_layout_band_into`, canvas renderer.rs:754, term `overlay_labels`). The band rects must be unioned into `bounds`, because bands are built after `compute_bounds` and would otherwise fall outside the viewBox and be clipped.

EXPECT TO MOVE: crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/gitgraph_basic.svg and its layout_checksums.json entry.

NOT A DEFECT, checked at the same time: journey actor names (`Wake: 5: Me` -> `Me`) are also absent from our SVG, but mermaid draws journey actors as FACES (`drawFace`, `faceColor` in the same bundle), not as text names. No evidence mermaid prints the actor name, so it is not filed.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED. layout_diagram_gitgraph_traced now emits one LayoutBand{kind: Lane} per branch lane, labelled from meta.branches[lane]. One layout change covers all three renderers, which already draw band.label.

Verified end to end: the branch name reaches the SVG (declared_text_reaches_the_svg_for_every_diagram_type), with the KNOWN_GAPS entry DELETED rather than left to rot - that gate fails if a listed gap starts passing, so a fixed defect cannot leave a permanent hole.

Golden gitgraph_basic.svg re-blessed. The diff is exactly two fm-band-lane groups labelled main and develop; every edge and node byte-identical and the viewBox unchanged, so nothing moved. Each label lands 10px above its lane's first commit.

NOTE for the next reader: the label sits in a 26px strip opened ABOVE the lane's first commit, not over the lane. Bands are background in every renderer, so a label drawn over the lane's own content would be painted over by the commit box and the name would still be invisible - this same defect, one layer down.

NO LAYOUT UNIT TEST was added, deliberately. bd-u3fo taught that a hand-built IR calling a layout fn directly can miss a dispatch-level condition entirely; the end-to-end gate asserts what the user actually cares about, which is that the name is in the rendered document.

GAP FOUND, NOT CLOSED: layout_checksums.json did NOT move, because canonical_layout hashes nodes + edges + bounds and NOT bands. A band regression is invisible to the layout-checksum gate. The text-parity gate covers it for now.

title: Sequence: Complete feature parity with mermaid-js
description:
# Sequence Diagram Feature Parity

## Current State
Sequence diagrams have the LARGEST gap of any core diagram type (~60% parser). Only basic participant/actor declarations and simple messages are supported. All advanced features — which are what make sequence diagrams actually useful in practice — are missing.

## Critical Gaps
1. Activation/deactivation (lifeline active periods)
2. Notes (left of, right of, over)
3. Interaction fragments (loop, alt, opt, par, critical, break, rect)
4. Autonumber
5. Actor/participant aliases and creation/destruction
6. Message types (async, return, lost/found)
7. Box grouping of participants

## Reference
- mermaid-js docs: https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/sequenceDiagram.html
- Parser: crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs lines 1041-1107
- Layout: crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs (layout_diagram_sequence_traced)
close_reason: All 5 child tasks complete: fragments (loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/rect), notes (left/right/over with after_edge positioning), activation/deactivation, participant aliases with box grouping and colors, autonumber. Also added: lifecycle events (create/destroy), hide footbox, actor links/menus, mirror actors.

title: Published WASM package in pkg/ is 79 engine commits stale, and gitignored-yet-tracked so drift is invisible
description:
The published WASM package in `pkg/` is a COMMITTED BUILD ARTIFACT that is also GITIGNORED, so it drifts from source silently and `git status` can never report it.

MEASURED. `pkg/` was last committed in 3d2b711e (2026-08-04). Since then, 79 commits have touched the engine crates (fm-core, fm-layout, fm-parser, fm-render-svg, fm-wasm). The shipped `frankenmermaid_bg.wasm` therefore predates, among others, every correctness fix landed on 2026-08-08:

  8f845aa8  kanban lanes as columns          (was: all cards in one column, lanes overlapping)
  95b2b700  block-beta container spans       (was: a 3-column block narrower than a 1-column one)
  72c0b97f  requirement box sizing           (was: metadata row spilling outside the box)
  a656acc4  requirement id:/text: rendered   (was: never drawn at all)
  1abca2b6  effects_css semantic markers     (was: C4 external indistinguishable from internal)
  c64efaf0  block-beta space a11y
  964c111c  composite state drawn once       (was: drawn twice, transitions on the decoy)
  313f6d68  packet-beta row-straddling split
plus a7a455ed/eeb27cbb (packet bit ruler) and d23b0d13 (state pseudo-state scoping).

So `@frankenmermaid/core@0.2.0` as committed renders kanban as horizontal bands, sizes packet fields by label text, and draws composite states twice. Anyone consuming this package — including the VS Code extension bd-kgi4 exists to build — ships an engine with defects this repo has already fixed and proven fixed.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, and this is the part worth generalising. `.gitignore:11` lists `pkg/`, but `git ls-files pkg/` shows the files ARE tracked. A tracked-and-ignored path is invisible in the normal workflow: `git status` never lists it dirty, so no lane has any prompt to rebuild it, and no test reads it. It is the same blindness class as a byte golden that pins a wrong picture — output that cannot report its own staleness.

THE TOOLING IS PRESENT: wasm-pack is on PATH at ~/.cargo/bin/wasm-pack and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is installed, so a rebuild is not the obstacle. The obstacle is that nobody is told to do it.

THIS IS A DECISION, NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is why it is filed rather than done. Two coherent options:
  (a) STOP VENDORING. Remove pkg/ from version control, keep the gitignore, and build it in CI or at release. The artifact then cannot be stale because it is always freshly built. Costs: consumers cannot install straight from a git checkout.
  (b) KEEP VENDORING, MAKE DRIFT VISIBLE. Remove pkg/ from .gitignore so `git status` reports it, and add a gate that fails when the artifact is older than the engine crates it was built from.
Doing (b) badly — rebuilding now and moving on — leaves the same trap armed for the next 79 commits.

I did NOT rebuild it. Committing a regenerated 0.5 MB binary is a change to what this project publishes, and choosing whether build outputs live in git is an ownership decision rather than one lane's.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Either pkg/ is untracked and produced by a documented build step, or it is tracked, un-ignored, and refreshed.
2. A check exists that fails when the published artifact predates the engine sources — staleness must be detectable without someone remembering.
3. If the artifact stays vendored, it is regenerated so it contains the 2026-08-08 render fixes listed above.

RELATED: bd-kgi4 (VS Code extension) sits directly downstream — its WASM path is this package. Also note the `serve` feature had not COMPILED since 211ab872 until b9ac701d fixed it, for the same structural reason: a surface with no CI coverage rots silently. Adding both `--features serve` and a pkg/ freshness check to CI would close the pair.
close_reason: Vendored pkg is visible to Git and CI now runs the consumer freshness check before rebuilding.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
CRITERION 3 DONE (764e8994) — artifact regenerated. Criteria 1 and 2 STILL OPEN, and they are the ones that matter.

WHY I REBUILT after saying last round that I would not. My reasoning then conflated two things: the recurrence (structural, needs an ownership decision) and today's wrongness (concrete, and fixable now). Refreshing is correct under EITHER outcome of the vendoring decision — if pkg/ stays vendored it had to be rebuilt, and if it stops being vendored the artifact is discarded anyway. Leaving a knowingly-wrong published package in the tree while the structural question is settled is worse than both. What I still have not done is decide whether build outputs belong in git.

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, by loading each artifact in node and calling renderSvg on the same kanban source:
  committed HEAD wasm:  card x = [144, 144, 144, 144]  -> 1 column
  rebuilt wasm:         card x = [144, 144, 434, 434]  -> 2 columns
The old package rendered every kanban card in one column — exactly bd-eg44. So the staleness was not theoretical; the published engine carried defects this repo had already fixed and proven fixed.

THE ADD ITSELF DEMONSTRATED THE BEAD, which is worth recording because it is the mechanism. `git add pkg/` is REFUSED: the root .gitignore lists `pkg/`, AND wasm-pack regenerates a `pkg/.gitignore` containing `*`. The four files are nevertheless tracked, so they had to be staged by explicit path with `-f`. A path git will not let you add normally, but whose contents are under version control, is exactly why 79 commits of drift went unnoticed. Note also that the wasm-pack `.gitignore` is itself untracked, so every rebuild re-creates the thing that hides the rebuild.

SIZE IS NOW THE NEXT PROBLEM: gzipped wasm is 548,790 bytes against build-wasm.sh's MAX_GZIP_BYTES of 552,960 — 99.2% of budget, about 4 KB of headroom. The next feature of any size breaches the ceiling, and whoever hits it will be tempted to raise the number again. That ceiling was already raised once (500K -> 540K on 2026-07-24) for this same reason. Raising it a third time without looking at what grew would be the wrong reflex.

SECOND RECORDED RECURRENCE. build-wasm.sh's own comment says the previous drift was ~2 months ("last regenerated May"), discovered on 2026-07-24. Now it is 79 commits and four days short of a month. Same failure, same cause, second time — which is the whole argument for criteria 1 and 2 over just rebuilding again.

WHAT REMAINS, unchanged:
  1. Decide whether pkg/ is vendored at all. Either untrack it and build at release, or keep it tracked and remove it from .gitignore so `git status` can report drift.
  2. A check that fails when the published artifact predates the engine sources. Under option (a) this is moot; under option (b) it is the thing that stops a third recurrence.
Both are ownership calls. I have left them.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
CRITERION 2 DONE (b74ec65b): scripts/check-wasm-freshness.mjs. Criterion 1 — whether pkg/ is vendored at all — remains the only thing left, and it is still an ownership call.

WHY CONTENT AND NOT TIMESTAMPS. My first instinct was to compare the artifact's commit date against the engine crates'. That is wrong, and worth recording because it is the obvious design: it fires on comment-only and test-only changes, which alter nothing rendered. The response to a false alarm is either an unnecessary 1.3 MB binary commit or learning to ignore the check — both worse than having no check at all. A behavioural assertion fires exactly when the artifact has regressed something the engine has fixed, and stays silent otherwise.

Four assertions, each naming the bead whose fix it pins, run by loading the published package in node exactly as a consumer would:
  bd-eg44  kanban lanes are columns, not one stacked pile
  bd-51tz  packet field width is its bit count, not its label length
  bd-f3tc  a requirement's declared id: and text: reach the output
  bd-9w54  a composite state is drawn once, as its container

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN against the artifact committed before 764e8994 — the one that had drifted 79 commits — all four fire, each with a diagnosis rather than a bare failure:
  STALE bd-eg44  all 4 cards share x=144
  STALE bd-51tz  two 16-bit fields render 114.9 and 308.78 wide
  STALE bd-f3tc  absent from the render: REQ-001, Users must authenticate
  STALE bd-9w54  composite state also drawn as a plain node (1 occurrence(s))
Against the current package all four pass. The check distinguishes the two states of the artifact this bead is about, which is the only thing that makes it worth having.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and this is stated in the script itself so nobody over-reads it: it does not prove the artifact is byte-current with HEAD. It proves the artifact still exhibits the listed properties. Drift that changes nothing observable here goes undetected — the intended trade, since those are the cases where a rebuild buys nothing. The list grows as future fixes land, and adding to it is the natural home for the next render fix that matters to consumers.

Exits 2 rather than 1 when pkg/ is absent, so a checkout that has stopped vendoring reads as "cannot run" rather than "stale". That is deliberate: the check must not become an argument against option (a).

NOT WIRED INTO CI, deliberately. Where this runs is part of criterion 1's decision. The same CI question also covers `--features serve`, which had not COMPILED for four days (211ab872 -> b9ac701d) for the identical structural reason: a surface with no coverage rots silently. Those two belong in one deliberate change to the CI matrix, made by whoever owns it, rather than smuggled in by me.

STATE OF THIS BEAD: criteria 2 and 3 done, criterion 1 open. Concretely what is left is one decision and its mechanical consequence:
  (a) untrack pkg/, build at release — then delete this script, since there is nothing vendored to check
  (b) keep it tracked, remove `pkg/` from .gitignore so `git status` can finally report drift, and run this script in CI
I have no stake in which. What I would not do is leave it as it is: tracked, ignored, unwatched, and now twice-drifted.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED, from bd-g2kp's attribution experiment: A pkg/ REFRESH CANNOT LAND TODAY AT ALL, for a
reason that has nothing to do with the worker export bd-g2kp is about. This bears directly on
criterion 1 (whether pkg/ is vendored at all), so recording it here rather than only there.

Rebuilding the CURRENT source through build-wasm.sh's own pipeline (same RUSTFLAGS, same per-package
opt-level="z" overrides, `wasm-opt -Oz --all-features --converge`, `gzip -c`):

  budget MAX_GZIP_BYTES                                552,960
  committed pkg/ artifact (built at 764e8994)          548,790    4,170 UNDER
  current source, unmodified                           575,703   22,743 OVER
  current source MINUS the workerHandleMessage export  556,869    3,909 OVER

The third line is the one that matters for this bead. Even with bd-g2kp's export removed entirely,
regenerating pkg/ overshoots the budget by 3,909 bytes. 8,079 gzip bytes of growth unrelated to the
worker protocol landed since 764e8994 and consumed the 4,170 bytes of headroom that build had.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: "refresh the vendored package" is currently BLOCKED by the size gate, not
merely stale. Any lane that picks this up and runs build-wasm.sh will hit the budget failure and be
one edit away from raising MAX_GZIP_BYTES to get past it — which is gate self-weakening, and is
exactly what bd-g2kp declined to do. Worth knowing before starting rather than discovering at the
end of a build.

That also sharpens the vendoring question this bead already asks. Under "stop vendoring, build in
CI", the artifact is produced fresh per release and the budget becomes a release-time check on real
current size. Under continued vendoring, someone must either raise the budget to cover accumulated
growth or find the space back, and must do it BEFORE the staleness this bead tracks can be fixed. So
criterion 1 is now a prerequisite for the refresh, not an independent cleanup.

The freshness checker's blind spot noted in bd-g2kp still holds and is worth repeating here:
scripts/check-wasm-freshness.mjs passes 4/4 against the committed artifact even though it is 79
engine commits stale and lacks exports added since, because it is behavioural by design and pins
render fixes rather than the export surface. It cannot detect a MISSING EXPORT, so it will not tell
you the vendored package is incomplete.

METHOD NOTE, reusable: I measured without ever writing to pkg/, by pointing `wasm-pack --out-dir` at
a scratch directory outside the repo and running wasm-opt/gzip there. That sidesteps the
gitignored-yet-tracked hazard this bead is named for — an oversized or half-built artifact in the
working tree is invisible to `git status` and can be swept into a peer's commit. Building out-of-tree
removes the hazard rather than relying on restoring bytes afterwards. `git status --porcelain pkg/`
was empty before and after.

title: Commit install.sh to repo (README curl install path is broken)
description:
## Problem
The README instructs users to install via:
```bash
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenmermaid/main/install.sh" | bash
```
However, `install.sh` exists only locally — it has NEVER been committed to the repo. Verified 2026-04-09: `git log -- install.sh` returns empty. The file IS the canonical installer (builds fm-cli from GitHub with Cargo, installs to ~/.local/bin), it's just untracked.

## Fix
1. Review install.sh for correctness and security (it's ~6.5KB, well-structured with set -euo pipefail).
2. `git add install.sh && git commit -m "feat: add canonical curl installer for fm-cli"`
3. Verify post-push: `curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenmermaid/main/install.sh" | head -5` should return the script.

## Why This Matters
Same as npm publish gap: this is a README install path that currently 404s on GitHub. Anyone who tries the curl install command gets a failure on their very first interaction with the project.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `install.sh` is tracked in git on the `main` branch.
- `curl -fsSL` URL returns the script (verified post-push).
- Script installs fm-cli successfully on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 system with rustup available.
close_reason: Completed: install.sh tracked in git and installer smoke-verified

title: requirement node boxes are sized from the label alone, so the type header and Risk/Verify row are drawn outside the box
description:
Found by bd-iicc round 5, the semantic-guard sweep. This is the FOURTH and last member of a defect class that already produced bd-090g (ER attribute rows) and bd-9xjy (C4 descriptions).

THE MECHANISM. `compute_node_size` (crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs:9384) sizes a node from its LABEL, then applies one explicit widening pass for each other kind of content a renderer draws inside the box:
    class_compartment_dimensions  -> class member rows
    er_compartment_dimensions     -> ER attribute rows      (bd-090g)
    c4_description_height         -> C4 wrapped description (bd-9xjy)
There is NO pass for requirement metadata. `requirement_meta` is never read anywhere in fm-layout — grep confirms the only mention of it in the crate is the field declaration in fm-core. Meanwhile the SVG renderer (crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:9389-9505) unconditionally draws THREE rows inside that box: the type header, the name, and a `Risk: … | Verify: …` row. Two of the three were never measured.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED, in golden/requirement_basic:
  LoginReq  "Risk: Medium | Verify: Demonstration"  at font-size 10.35 measures 163.37
            in a box 133.05 wide (x 92.00..225.05) -> spills 15.16 past EACH side.
  AuthReq   "Risk: High | Verify: Test"             fits.
  Both type headers fit.
So one row in this fixture escapes, not all of them. That is the honest number and it is also the point: whether a row escapes depends on how long the declared `risk:` and `verifymethod:` strings happen to be, because nothing sizes the box for them at all. A longer verifymethod overflows further. The fixture shows the mechanism at close to the smallest margin that proves it.

THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT AN ESTIMATOR ARTIFACT. The guard measures with `fm_core::FontMetrics` at the preset derived from the rendered font family — the same estimator the layout sizes with — and it checks a CONTROL first: the node's own NAME row, the string the box WAS sized from. If the name did not fit, the estimator would be disagreeing with the engine and the guard says so instead of reporting a defect. The control passes; the overflow is a claim about the renderer.

ACCEPTANCE GATE, named and populated: remove the `#[ignore]` from
    requirement_rows_stay_inside_their_node_box   (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs)
and it must pass. It currently FAILS with the numbers above — verified under `--ignored`, so it is a real specification and not a stub.
