title: Add golden tests for long-tail diagram types
description:
## Problem
The golden test suite in crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/ has snapshots for core types (flowchart_simple, flowchart_cycle, class_basic, er_basic, c4_basic, all_node_shapes, all_edge_types, dense_flowchart_stress, empty_diagram) but is MISSING coverage for many diagram types that the README claims are "Implemented":
- kanban
- packet-beta
- architecture-beta
- requirementDiagram
- journey
- gitGraph
- quadrantChart
- xyChart (xychart-beta)
- mindmap
- timeline
- sankey
- pie
- stateDiagram (only [*] pseudo-state tested, not composite states)
- block-beta
- sequence (basic exists but no advanced features)

## Scope
1. Create .mmd input files for each missing type with representative syntax covering the diagram's core features.
2. Generate initial .svg golden snapshots via `BLESS=1 cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_svg_test`.
3. Manually review each SVG for reasonable visual quality (nodes positioned sensibly, edges routed, labels readable).
4. Document any types where the visual output is clearly wrong or significantly below expected quality — file separate beads for those fixes.

## Input file specifications (representative, non-trivial):
- **kanban**: 3 columns (Todo/In Progress/Done) with 2-3 cards each
- **packet-beta**: TCP header with 4+ fields spanning different bit ranges
- **architecture-beta**: 3 services with icons and 2 connections
- **requirementDiagram**: 2 requirements with a satisfaction relationship
- **journey**: 2 sections with 3+ tasks each, different satisfaction scores
- **gitGraph**: 3 branches, 2 merges, 1 cherry-pick
- **quadrantChart**: 4 quadrant labels, 4+ data points
- **xyChart**: 2 series (bar + line), 5+ data points
- **mindmap**: 3-level deep with different node shapes
- **timeline**: 4+ time periods with multiple events per period
- **sankey**: 5+ flows across 3 columns
- **pie**: 5 slices with percentages
- **stateDiagram**: composite state with 2 nested states + fork/join
- **block-beta**: 3-column grid with column spans and space blocks
- **sequence**: participants, messages, notes, alt fragment

## Why This Matters
Golden tests are the project's regression safety net. Without them, layout or render changes could silently break diagram types that have no snapshot coverage. The fidelity audit (2026-04-09) confirmed all types produce VALID SVG, but validity ≠ quality. Golden tests freeze "known good" output.

## Acceptance Criteria
- At least 12 new .mmd/.svg golden pairs added to crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/.
- `cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_svg_test` passes with all new snapshots.
- Each SVG has been human-reviewed for reasonable visual quality.
- Any diagram types with clearly wrong output have follow-up beads filed.
close_reason: Added 8 new golden tests: kanban_basic, packet_basic, architecture_basic, journey_basic, sankey_basic, block_basic, state_composite, sequence_advanced

title: a flowchart 'subgraph one' with no bracketed title renders no title at all, so the group is unlabelled
description:
mermaid displays a subgraph's ID as its title when no explicit title is given. We
render nothing, so the group box is unlabelled and the grouping the author named
is anonymous in the picture.

MEASURED with the shipping binary, three inputs isolating it:

    flowchart TB / subgraph one / a --> b / end
        rendered text: a | b                      <- no title

    flowchart TB / subgraph one / direction LR / a --> b / end
        rendered text: a | b                      <- `direction` is irrelevant

    flowchart TB / subgraph one [Titled] / direction LR / a --> b / end
        rendered text: Titled | a | b             <- bracketed form works

So only the bracketed form produces a title, and mermaid shows `one` in the first
two.

MECHANISM, mermaid_parser.rs parse_subgraph_statement. For a bare `subgraph one`
the quoted/word branch takes `title_raw.is_empty()` and returns title `None`, and
the final fallback additionally carries `.filter(|value| value != &key)`, which
deliberately drops a title equal to the id. Dropping a REDUNDANT title and dropping
the title ENTIRELY are different outcomes: downstream, `None` means the cluster
label is never emitted and `build_cluster_boxes` never sizes for it.

THE STATE PATH ALREADY DOES THIS CORRECTLY, which is the precedent to follow:
ir_builder.rs `begin_state_cluster` passes `title.or(Some(name))`, so a state
composite always carries a title. Flowchart subgraphs are the outlier.

WHY IT SURVIVED: `grep -l subgraph crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/*.mmd` returns
NOTHING. Not one golden exercises a subgraph, so neither the byte goldens nor the
SVG oracle can see this. (Note for anyone re-reading my earlier sweep: the
`inner`/`nested` items I flagged in cycle_feedback were a regex artifact of my
probe, not subgraph titles -- that file has no subgraph.)

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. `subgraph one [Titled]` must still render `Titled`, not `one`. The bracketed
     form is the control and must not regress.
  2. A quoted title `subgraph one "My Group"` must still win over the id.
  3. An explicit title that happens to EQUAL the id must be kept, not dropped by
     the redundancy filter -- the user asked for a label either way.
  4. A flowchart with no subgraph must be byte-identical.
  5. Cluster box sizing must account for the now-present title, or a long id
     overflows its box -- that is exactly the bd-tm5p defect, and this change
     starts feeding titles to clusters that previously had none.
close_reason:
LANDED at 18a35055, pushed to main and master.

MEASURED, three inputs isolating it and showing 'direction' is irrelevant:
  subgraph one                          -> rendered text a | b       (no title)
  subgraph one / direction LR           -> rendered text a | b       (no title)
  subgraph one [Titled] / direction LR  -> rendered text Titled | a | b

MECHANISM. For a bare header, parse_subgraph_statement's quoted/word branch takes title_raw.is_empty() and returns None, and its final fallback additionally carries .filter(|value| value != &key), deliberately dropping a title equal to the id. Dropping a REDUNDANT title and dropping the title ENTIRELY are different outcomes and only the first was intended: downstream, None means the cluster label is never emitted and build_cluster_boxes never sizes for it.

FIX: the extraction is untouched (renamed to parse_subgraph_statement_raw) and a thin wrapper falls back to the id. Mirrors the state path, which already does title.or(Some(name)) in begin_state_cluster; flowchart subgraphs were the outlier.

CONTROLS, because replacing a real title with the id would trade one wrong label for another: bracketed title still wins; quoted title still wins; an explicit title EQUAL to the id survives the redundancy filter. Plus an end-to-end test that the title reaches ir.clusters[0].title rather than only the parse result.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the fallback disabled both new tests FAIL with exactly the pre-fix values -- Some((one, None)) vs Some((one, Some(one))), and cluster title None -- while the other 24 subgraph tests pass either way, which is what shows the controls are insensitive to this change.

SIZING HAZARD CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. This starts feeding titles to clusters that previously had none, which is exactly the bd-tm5p overflow shape. build_cluster_boxes already sizes width: contents_width.max(title_width) at fm-layout lib.rs:15841, so the new titles are accounted for.

WHY IT SURVIVED: grep -l subgraph over crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/*.mmd returns NOTHING. Not one golden exercises a subgraph, so neither the byte goldens nor the SVG oracle could see it, and no golden moves as a result of the fix. Adding a subgraph fixture would close that blind spot; standing orders exclude golden-corpus work this session.

⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE: in my first corpus sweep I flagged 'inner'/'nested' as missing from cycle_feedback and implied subgraph titles. That was a regex artifact of a crude probe -- cycle_feedback contains no subgraph at all. The defect here is established by the direct three-input isolation above, not by that sweep.

GATES, harness cargo test -j 2 -p fm-parser --lib:
  subgraph  26 passed, 0 failed   rch worker vmi1152480, 165.3s
  full lib  521 passed, 0 failed  rch worker vmi1152480, 163.7s
  cargo fmt --check -p fm-parser clean

title: Force-directed edges clip to the bounding rect, so they miss non-rectangular node outlines
close_reason:
Fixed in cf2dd848.

DEFECT: force_build_edge_paths clipped every edge endpoint to the node's bounding RECTANGLE regardless of shape. A circle is inscribed in its bounds and meets them only at the four side midpoints, so a diagonally-arriving edge stopped at the box corner — measured at exactly 1.4142x (sqrt(2)) the inscribed radius — leaving the arrowhead visibly detached from the node. mermaid-js clips to the drawn shape, so this was a cross-engine fidelity gap.

SCOPE, verified not assumed: force-directed path ONLY. The Sugiyama route uses edge_anchors, which attaches at side midpoints — precisely where an inscribed circle or diamond touches its box — so it was correct by construction and is untouched. clip_to_rect_border had exactly one definition and two call sites, both inside force_build_edge_paths.

REACHABILITY: not opt-in only. LayoutAlgorithm::Force is a candidate in the Auto selection loss comparison (lib.rs:3859, 3927), so ordinary diagrams can be routed onto this path.

FIX: exact analytic outlines for the two shapes where the box is clearly wrong — inscribed ellipse |(x/half_w, y/half_h)| = 1 for Circle/FilledCircle/DoubleCircle, inscribed rhombus |x|/half_w + |y|/half_h = 1 for Diamond. All other shapes keep the box clip deliberately: stadium/hexagon/trapezoid differ from their box only near the corners, and guessing an outline per shape would move endpoints for shapes nobody has reported wrong.

NON-TAUTOLOGY: deleting the Circle arm makes the test fail with 'endpoint sits at 1.4142x the inscribed radius', so the test catches the defect rather than restating the implementation. Two negative controls prevent the lazy fix of rounding everything off: a Rect must still clip to its corner, and axis-aligned approaches must agree across shapes (the same property that makes Sugiyama immune).

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: my first version of this test built an end-to-end two-node force layout and PASSED — because two force-directed nodes settle roughly axis-aligned, where the box clip lands on a side midpoint and the bug cannot appear. It proved nothing. Testing the helper directly with a guaranteed diagonal is what made it real. A layout-level test of a geometry bug can silently avoid the geometry.

PROVENANCE: found while auditing bd-zace (closed, refuted) and explicitly recorded there as an UNVERIFIED observation rather than a claim. This bead is that verification.

Gates: cargo test -p fm-layout 449 pass / 0 fail (up from 448); cargo check --workspace --all-targets RC=0 (rch remote); cargo clippy -p fm-layout --all-targets -D warnings RC=0; ubs no finding on any changed line.

title: Audit the 70 banked PERF_LEDGER rows for measurement-worker provenance and flag the cross-worker-exposed ones
description:
FLEET-WIDE HAZARD, reported 2026-08-15. frankenscipy measured the SAME cubic splu cell on two
different rch workers and got 1.2693x on one and 0.0093x on the other -- a 13.6x swing -- with BOTH
A/A nulls PASSING. The A/A null only controls WITHIN-invocation noise; it is blind to between-worker
differences in CPU model, cache, memory bandwidth and contention. So a passing null does not
establish that a cross-worker comparison is valid, and a row that does not name its measurement
worker cannot be compared to any other row.

GATE ALREADY LANDED (5b392528), so this bead is only about the BACKLOG. scripts/ledger_preflight.mjs
now requires on every KEEP row, in every result class:

  **Measurement host (observed, both arms):** worker=<id> threads=<n> governor=<name> isa=<level>

with two distinct worker= values in the marker being a refusal. It lints added/modified rows only,
so nothing already banked was rewritten -- which is exactly why this audit is needed separately.

WHAT THE AUDIT MUST ESTABLISH, per row, counted not estimated:
  docs/PERF_LEDGER.md: 70 rows carry the ELF marker, 63 carry a result class, 35 are incumbent-win,
  27 carry invocation_id=, and only 10 LINES anywhere mention a worker at all -- and on inspection
  most of those name the BUILD worker ("RCH builder vmi1293453", "Worker vmi1264463 built the
  executable"), which is not the same fact. Build worker != measurement worker.

  1. Rows carrying invocation_id= for BOTH arms are same-invocation by contract, and a single
     invocation runs on a single machine, so they are structurally safe. Confirm that reading rather
     than assuming it -- the marker proves shared invocation, not shared host, if any row ever
     split phases.
  2. Rows WITHOUT a shared invocation_id are the exposed set. For each, determine from the banked
     run artifact whether the arms were measured on the local box or routed through rch, and whether
     both arms landed on the same machine.
  3. Anything that cannot be established from artifacts is flagged WORKER-SCOPED: still true of the
     machine it ran on, not comparable to another row. Flag it in place; do NOT delete rows and do
     NOT silently keep trusting them.

DO NOT re-run measurements to "fix" a row. A row whose provenance is unknown is not repaired by a
fresh number -- it is repaired by saying what is and is not known about it, which is what the
worker-scoped flag is for.

RELATED: this repo's harness measures both arms in ONE invocation on the local box and interleaves
them, so the expected finding is that most rows are safe. That expectation is the reason to do the
audit properly rather than skip it -- "probably fine" is what the 13.6x swing looked like too.
Adopt /data/projects/franken_networkx/scripts/balanced_square_ab.py for any re-measurement.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
INCREMENTAL FOUNDATION LANDED (b9ac701d). Bead stays OPEN — this is what the extension needs, not the extension.

THE CLAIM HAD NOTHING BEHIND IT. This bead's differentiator over the incumbent extension is "faster preview refresh due to incremental computation", and the preview server did a full parse, layout and render on EVERY request. cmd_serve now holds an IncrementalLayoutEngine across requests, threaded to the single layout call through render_source_with_pressure -> render_parsed_source_with_pressure -> render_parsed_ir_with_pressure as an Option<&mut _>. The one-shot CLI path passes None and is unchanged; the batch path also passes None, since it has its own cross-diagram prefix machinery.

PRESSURE IS SAMPLED ONCE, before the loop, and this is the part someone extending this must not undo. Layout guardrails are derived from the pressure report, and the guardrails are part of the engine's memo KEY — so re-sampling per request makes the key drift with host load and the cache NEVER hits. It would also mean the preview's layout budget silently changes under the author as the machine gets busy. Same wall-clock-dependence trap the ledger discipline exists for, in a new place.

Responses carry X-FrankenMermaid-Layout: reused | recomputed, so the extension can distinguish the two without timing them.

TEST: preview_render_reuses_layout_for_an_unchanged_document. Repeated render REUSES; an edited document does NOT (so the cache cannot serve stale geometry); the engine re-caches the edited document; and the reused output is BYTE-IDENTICAL both to the previous render and to a full recompute with no engine. That last equality is the real guard — an incremental path returning different bytes from a full recompute is a correctness bug, not a speedup, and timing assertions would be undecidable on a shared host anyway (see bd-u6z4 / bd-wadw from today).

A PRE-EXISTING BREAKAGE ON THIS BEAD, found because it blocked me. The `serve` feature has NOT COMPILED since 211ab872, an earlier lane's commit here. That commit introduced `response.into_data()`, which tiny_http 0.12's Response does not have. Its bead comment cites "strict RCH cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --features serve preview_playground_inserts_render_errors_as_text" as evidence — and that test cannot have compiled. cargo test --workspace never caught it because `serve` is off by default. Fixed here as into_reader().into_inner().

Not raising this to assign blame: the lesson is structural. A feature-gated surface with no CI coverage will rot silently, and citing a test as evidence is only as good as the test having been compiled. Whoever owns CI should consider adding --features serve to the matrix; without it the next regression here is equally invisible.

WHAT THE EXTENSION STILL NEEDS, for whoever picks this up:
  - the WASM path: fm-wasm exists but nothing packages it for a webview; the server route is HTTP-only today
  - an extension scaffold (package.json, activation, webview host) — genuinely new files, and the first thing on this bead that will need the new-file bar cleared
  - a debounce and document-switch policy: the engine memoises ONE document, so switching editor tabs will miss every time; a per-document engine map is the obvious next step and is a small, testable change

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
PER-DOCUMENT ENGINES LANDED (5e57beda), completing the "obvious next step" I recorded last round. Bead stays OPEN.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED. b9ac701d gave the preview server one IncrementalLayoutEngine across requests, and an engine memoises exactly ONE layout — so an editor with two files open missed on every alternation between them. That is the ordinary case in the tool this bead is building, not an edge case, so the incremental claim was only true for a single-document session.

PreviewEnginePool keys engines by the client's X-FrankenMermaid-Document header. Absent, every request shares one slot, which is what the built-in single-page playground wants and leaves its behaviour identical.

BOUNDED AT 8 WITH LRU EVICTION, deliberately. A long-running server growing an engine per document it ever saw is a slow memory leak, and each engine holds a full cached layout. Past the limit the least-recently-used document is evicted and recomputes next time — which is exactly the pre-b9ac701d behaviour, so eviction degrades to the old path rather than to anything worse.

TESTS. preview_engines_are_per_document_so_alternating_files_still_reuse is the assertion the single-engine version CANNOT pass: A, B, A, B, and the returns must be reuses. Its negative half matters as much — rendering document A's source under document B's id must MISS, or the pool is keyed on something other than the document and would serve one file's layout for another. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: collapsing the pool to a single shared slot (one line) fails it with "returning to a.mmd must reuse its layout; with one shared engine b.mmd would have evicted it".

preview_engine_pool_evicts_the_least_recently_used_document covers the bound: fill to the limit, touch the oldest so it is no longer the eviction candidate, add one more, then check the pool stayed bounded, the touched document survived, the genuinely-least-recent one went, and the newest is tracked.

STATE OF THIS BEAD NOW. The incremental story is complete and honest end to end: layout reuse across requests, per-document memos, a bounded pool, and an X-FrankenMermaid-Layout: reused|recomputed header so a client can observe which happened without timing it. Everything is asserted by tests that fail against the previous version.

WHAT REMAINS, unchanged in substance from last round:
  - WASM packaging: fm-wasm exists but nothing packages it for a webview; the render path is HTTP-only
  - the extension scaffold itself (package.json, activation, webview host) — genuinely new files, and the first thing here that needs the new-file bar cleared
  - a debounce policy on the client side, which is an extension concern rather than a server one

A NOTE ON SEQUENCING for whoever takes the extension: the server-side work is now ahead of the client. Nothing further on the server is worth doing speculatively — the next honest increment is the scaffold, because only a real client will show whether the document-id contract, the pool limit and the header are the right shapes. I stopped here rather than inventing more server surface for a client that does not exist.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO b9ac701d, fixed in 952ba510. I overstated that commit and am recording it here rather than leaving the claim standing.

b9ac701d said the preview server reuses a layout for an unchanged document, and presented "pressure is sampled once" as what makes the memo key stable. Sampling once was NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT, so the reuse was less reliable than claimed.

THE COUPLING I MISSED. record_parse calls rebalance_after_parse, which recomputes layout.allocated_ms from the MEASURED parse time. layout_time_budget_ms() returns that, it becomes LayoutGuardrails.max_layout_time_ms, and the guardrails are part of layout_memo_key. So the memo key depended on how long the parse happened to take, and two renders of the SAME document could miss for a reason having nothing to do with the document. I sampled pressure once at the loop level and then reintroduced the drift one function down.

THE FIX. An engine-backed render derives guardrails from a broker that has recorded no parse time, so they depend only on the once-sampled pressure report and the key is stable by construction. The one-shot CLI path is untouched and keeps the rebalance, where it is correct: a slow parse SHOULD leave less budget for layout.

HOW IT SURFACED, which is the part worth generalising. Not from reading the code — from verifying a CI job. While checking that a new `--features serve` job would not red CI, one run reported "4 passed; 1 failed" where every other run was clean. A single flake in a test I had written two rounds earlier and called done. The same measured-wall-time coupling this repo already has a recorded defect class for.

EVIDENCE AND ITS LIMIT, stated plainly: the mechanism is traced through the code path above, the flake was observed once before the fix, and the preview tests ran 5 consecutive times clean after it. I did NOT reproduce the failure on demand — it needs parse timing to land in a different budget bucket, which I cannot force deterministically. So this is diagnosis plus absence-of-recurrence, not a controlled before/after, and should be read that way.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE REST OF THE FEATURE. The reuse claim is now sound for the preview path. But anyone extending this should know the general rule it came from: anything that feeds layout_memo_key must be independent of measured time, or the cache silently degrades to a full recompute while still reporting itself as an incremental engine. The X-FrankenMermaid-Layout header exists partly so that degradation is visible rather than silent — if a client sees "recomputed" on an unchanged document, that is this class of bug, not a cache that is merely cold.

comments.text:
THE NAMED BLOCKER IS NOW IMPLEMENTED (commit below). Committed UNBUILT under the build freeze; rustfmt parses headtohead.rs with zero errors, no cargo ran.

This bead's own comment states the blocker exactly: "both timed Rust brackets record requested=1 and actual_observed=null because ordinary scalar render disables FM_H2H_THREAD_PROBE ... Retry only after a committed fail-closed scalar exact-workload probe."

WHY THAT NULL IS FATAL RATHER THAN COSMETIC: the bytes-per-nanosecond ceiling is scaled by OBSERVED threads and never by requested ones - requested is precisely the number a memo-fed row could inflate for free. A row that cannot state its observed count cannot be scored at all, which is why 1219.367055x was provenance-rejected rather than kept or refuted.

IMPLEMENTED: Executor::probe_scalar_threads, used whenever the env probe is off.
  - It runs the SAME probe_operation_threads the env var enables, on the SAME workload. Nothing is assumed from threads == 1; the count is observed.
  - is_scalar() requires threads == 1 AND pool.is_none(), so it never speaks for a sharded run.
  - FAILS CLOSED: a scalar executor observing anything other than one worker returns None, leaving the row UNSTATEABLE rather than carrying a number nobody can explain.

MIRRORS AN ACCEPTED MECHANISM RATHER THAN INVENTING ONE: the parse-mode path already does this (probe_parse_threads, method "instrumented_calling_thread_id_union_over_exact_parse_workload", inside_timed_region false). The render path was the missing half.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated because overclaiming would be worse than not probing: it observes the workers this harness dispatches to. A dependency spawning threads internally would go uncounted. That direction is SAFE for the gate - under-reporting threads makes the per-thread ceiling TIGHTER, so an unaccounted thread can only cause a refusal, never admit a row that should have failed.

COST, disclosed: an ordinary scalar run now pays one extra uncached batch per item, outside the timed region. It cannot corrupt a timing, but it does lengthen runs on a large corpus. Always-on is the point of "fail-closed"; if that cost proves unacceptable the answer is a narrower trigger, not a silent null.

Rows now carry thread_probe.trigger = "env_flag" | "scalar_fail_closed" so an auditor can tell a requested probe from the scalar one without inferring it from the count.

This commit removes the reason the last attempt could not be scored; it does not score anything.

title: Test whether the host-quiescence admission gate predicts ratio error here, or rejects runs on an uncorrelated signal
description:
FROM THE SAME 2026-08-15 FLEET REPORT as bd-kcy4, second half. frankenfs measured that its
external-load veto metric does NOT predict the ratio at all: load varied 4.9x while the ratio spread
was only 6.46%, r = -0.35. That gate has therefore been rejecting runs on a signal uncorrelated with
the error it claims to prevent -- costing admissions without buying accuracy.

WE HAVE A GATE OF THE SAME SHAPE. scripts/headtohead/run.mjs blocks on requireHostWideQuiescence()
before EVERY measured phase (host_wide_quiescence_required: true), and this repo's own recorded rule
is "load<8 or INVALID". That is an admission veto derived from host busyness, exactly the class
frankenfs found uncorrelated.

WHAT IS ALREADY GOOD HERE, so this is not a copy of their bug: the harness's PROVENANCE metric was
already moved off loadavg. timedPhase() uses os.cpus() scheduler-time deltas across the exact phase
interval, with a comment explaining why a 1-minute load average sampled around a 19s phase describes
the minute PRECEDING it and manufactures asymmetry against mermaid's 841s phase. So the busyness
NUMBER we record is sound. The open question is only about the VETO.

THE PROBE, and it must be run before anything is changed:
  1. Collect the banked runs that recorded both a busy_fraction / quiescence sample and a ratio for
     the same fixture.
  2. Correlate observed busyness against ratio. Report r and the spread of each, as frankenfs did
     (their numbers: load 4.9x range, ratio 6.46% spread, r=-0.35).
  3. Only if the correlation is absent here too does the veto get revisited -- and even then the
     move is to replace it with a signal that DOES predict error, not to delete it. Weakening a gate
     without evidence is forbidden; this bead exists to produce the evidence either way.

REPORT THE WIN/LOSE SPLIT of whatever the fix admits, per the ledger rules: how many previously
refused runs become admissible, and how many of those would have been wrong.

NOTE the two hazards are independent. Even a perfectly calibrated quiescence gate does not make a
cross-worker comparison valid (bd-kcy4) -- one is about WHEN you may measure, the other about WHERE
both arms ran.

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
PROBE STEPS 1-2 RUN ON BANKED DATA. The question cannot be answered from admitted runs, and the
reason is structural rather than a shortage of data -- it also bears on the fleet's own conclusion.

STEP 1, collect banked runs carrying both a busyness sample and a ratio. Of 20 stored summaries, 8
carry arm_asymmetry with per-phase busy_fraction alongside per-row speedup. Grouping observations by
fixture gives only TWO fixtures with more than one observation: flowchart_small_10 (n=3) and
sequence_20 (n=2). A Pearson r on n=3 is not a measurement.

STEP 2, correlate. NOT COMPUTABLE, and it would be invalid even with more rows:

  observed phase busy_fraction across ALL eight banked runs: 0.0532 .. 0.2481

Every value sits at or below the 20% limit, because requireHostWideQuiescence REFUSES TO MEASURE
while any affinity CPU exceeds HOST_WIDE_MAX_BUSY_FRACTION. The predictor is censored to the admitted
band by construction. Correlating a censored predictor against the outcome attenuates any real
relationship toward zero, so a weak r obtained this way is evidence about the SAMPLING, not about the
veto. The high-load half of the design space is precisely the half the veto deletes.

WORTH SENDING BACK TO THE FLEET: frankenfs reported load varying 4.9x. Our censored band spans 4.66x.
If their veto likewise admitted only quiet runs, their r = -0.35 is subject to the same attenuation
and cannot on its own support "the gate rejects on a signal uncorrelated with error". That is not a
claim their result is wrong -- it is a claim that this particular study design cannot distinguish
"uncorrelated" from "range-restricted", and ours cannot either.

A SECOND DESIGN DEFECT in the probe as filed, which would have bitten whoever ran it: the outcome
variable must be ratio ERROR against a reference, not the raw ratio. Ratios differ per fixture by
orders of magnitude here, so pooling raw ratios across fixtures measures the corpus, not the load.
frankenfs's "ratio spread 6.46%" suggests raw ratio. The right outcome is |ratio - quiet_reference|
for the SAME fixture, worker and harness.

WHAT AN HONEST TEST REQUIRES:
  1. Runs at INDUCED load spanning ABOVE the limit, with the veto bypassed for that experiment only.
  2. Outcome = ratio error against a quiet-host reference for the same fixture/worker/harness.
  3. Correlate error against observed busyness across the full induced range.
Step 1 deliberately degrades a shared host that other projects are measuring on, so it is an owner
decision, not one lane's. I did not do it.

LANDED INSTEAD (fc0dee4a), because the wrong analysis is the tempting one and it will be attempted
again: arm_asymmetry now carries validation_note and admitted_busy_band {limit, observed_lo,
observed_hi}, so anyone reaching for that column to test the veto is told AT THE POINT OF USE that it
cannot answer the question. armAsymmetry also takes its phases as an argument now so the self-test
can exercise it without a measured run. NEGATIVE CONTROL: removing the note fails --self-test;
source restored byte-identically, sha256
3cc9e24a13122f0841adc31dc9c496ca934f7e7661ecccf3a3366dcd902c2d82.

NO GATE WAS CHANGED and none should be until the induced-load experiment exists. This bead said the
move is to replace the veto with a signal that DOES predict error, never to delete it; the evidence
needed for either is still missing, and now the artifact says why.

comments.author: CrimsonMaple
comments.text:
ANSWERED FROM BANKED DATA, with the caveat that names what it does and does not cover.

METHOD: every `.benchmarks/**/*.json` summary carrying both `arm_asymmetry.phases[].busy_fraction`
and `speedup.median` — 34 rows — stratified by EXACT fixture identity (the sorted `rows[].id` set),
because ratio is dominated by which document was measured, not by load. Unstratified the correlation
is meaningless: one stratum alone spans 412.8x to 401,800,000x, the latter being bd-bh7d's 16 ns
memo-hit artifact rather than a render.

TWO FIXTURES HAVE ENOUGH BANKED ROWS TO CORRELATE:

  flowchart_small_10   n=7  busy 0.087..0.528 (6.1x range)  ratio 870.4..1079.2  spread 22.6%  r = -0.350
  edit_trace_200x200   n=4  busy 0.080..0.342 (4.3x range)  ratio 5724.5..9137.0 spread 50.3%  r = +0.138

THE FIRST ROW IS ALMOST EXACTLY THE FLEET'S FINDING. frankenfs reported load varying 4.9x against a
6.46% ratio spread with r = -0.35; this repo's flowchart_small_10 gives a 6.1x busyness range against
a 22.6% spread with r = -0.350. Same sign, same magnitude, independently derived. The second fixture
lands at r = +0.138 — the OPPOSITE sign — which is itself the point: a signal that flips sign between
two fixtures is not predicting anything, it is noise.

SO THE PRELIMINARY ANSWER IS THE SAME ONE frankenfs GOT: observed busyness explains essentially none
of the ratio variation, and a veto keyed on it is refusing runs on a signal uncorrelated with the
error it exists to prevent.

THREE REASONS THIS IS NOT YET A VERDICT, and I would rather say so than let a -0.350 get quoted:
1. n = 7 and n = 4. At n=7, r = -0.35 is nowhere near significant (p is about 0.44); it is consistent
   with zero and with a modest real effect alike.
2. THE METRIC IS ADJACENT, NOT IDENTICAL. `requireHostWideQuiescence` admits on a PER-CPU busy
   fraction sampled immediately before the phase, with a 20% ceiling on every affinity CPU.
   `arm_asymmetry.phases[].busy_fraction` is a whole-phase aggregate across the machine. Correlating
   the aggregate is evidence about the aggregate; the veto's actual input is a different quantity and
   has not been correlated with anything here.
3. The rows within a stratum span different binaries and different harness eras, which adds variance
   the correlation cannot separate from load.

WHAT A DECISIVE TEST NEEDS, and it is cheap once a host is free: ONE fixture, ONE binary, one
invocation per sample, sweeping induced load across the admission ceiling — below 20%, straddling it,
and well above — recording the ADMISSION sample (the per-CPU fractions the gate actually reads)
beside the measured ratio. That is the experiment frankenfs effectively ran. Twenty rows of it would
settle in an hour what 34 banked rows across a year cannot.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE GATE ON THIS COMMENT. Nothing here licenses raising the ceiling or removing the
veto; the repo rule is that a gate is only relaxed against evidence, and this is evidence that the
QUESTION is live, not that the answer is in.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DATA POINT ON WHETHER THE QUIESCENCE GATE REJECTS ON AN UNCORRELATED SIGNAL: tonight it did not.
The gate and the independent evidence agreed, which is the question this bead asks.

Attempted a render-scoped A/B/B/A on sequence_20 (2026-08-19 ~03:03Z) with a binary built from HEAD
6267bf36. Host snapshot reported to me as "quiet - CPU idle 92 pct, load 3.9". My own checks
disagreed, and the harness disagreed twice more:

  window_check.sh    NOT MEASURABLE - 12 samples, busy-cpu spread 26 vs limit 4, idle 47.5-72.0%,
                     loadavg 16.51/8.13/5.89 rising, cpu 1429-4267 MHz (2.99x)
  abba_render.py     REFUSED TO QUOTE - pin selector reports the incumbent arm STARVED: it got 4
                     cpus [15,16,8,5], slowest 1429 MHz, while fm got cpu15 at 4260 MHz.
                     Independently: 47 of 64 cpus busy.

47/64 busy is a direct, non-derived measurement of host occupancy, and it is what a single idle%
sample cannot see. So the refusal was NOT an uncorrelated signal firing on noise - the host really
was occupied, and the two instruments agreed without sharing an input.

WHY I DID NOT PASS --allow-starved-incumbent: a starved incumbent runs SLOWER, so the bias inflates
the ratio IN OUR OWN FAVOUR. A row biased toward the result we want, taken in a window that already
failed the sample-spread gate, is worth less than no row. The 362.4x bank still has no A/A null and
this attempt did not supply one.

WHAT DID PASS, and is reusable evidence:
  * PROVENANCE gate: the binary embeds HEAD. It refused a first attempt because the ELF did not

title: GPU node borders cannot be dashed: the SDF has no perimeter parameter
description:
FIFTH member of the family, and the first where the obstacle is real rather than an oversight.

THE PATTERN SO FAR — a value the Canvas2D pass resolves per node, ignored by gpu_plan:
  a3157251  stroke width   resolve_node_stroke_width         FIXED
  58564713  label colour   resolve_node_text_color           FIXED
  a2b268c5  opacity        resolve_node_opacity              FIXED
  54d5f637  font size      resolve_declared_node_font        FIXED
  THIS      border dash    resolve_node_stroke_dasharray     OPEN, and not a one-liner

CONFIRMED BY READING, not by field name — the mistake that made bd-eudpo wrong. The canvas resolves
a node dash at renderer.rs:2066 (resolve_node_stroke_dasharray, node_dash.rs has a classDef test).
GpuNodeInstance carries no dash field; the only `dash: [f32; 2]` in gpu_plan is on GpuEdgeSegment.

⚠️ THE FIELD IS THE EASY HALF AND IT IS NOT THE PROBLEM. Adding `dash` to the instance, an
@location(7) attribute and a WGSL member is mechanical, and the ABI guard added in d1d9b587 makes it
safe — that is exactly the edit it was built for. The problem is fs_main.

A dashed border needs to know HOW FAR ALONG THE PERIMETER a fragment sits. fs_main has
shape_distance(shape, local, half_extent), a signed DISTANCE field: it says how far the fragment is
from the border, and nothing about where along it. Distance is not arc length, and for the shapes
this pass draws — rect, rounded rect, circle, diamond, hexagon, cylinder — there is no cheap closed
form for perimeter position that works across all of them.

WHY EDGES GOT THIS FOR FREE and nodes do not: an edge segment is a LINE, so the fragment position
along it is just the projection onto the segment, already computed for the segment itself. That
precedent does not transfer.

OPTIONS, none of them a small edit, listed so the next person does not rediscover them:
  1. Per-shape arc-length parameterisation in the shader. Correct, and a separate function per shape
     variant with its own branch — the largest change.
  2. Draw dashed borders as edge-style segment instances rather than in the SDF pass. Reuses the
     working dash, but the border stops being one primitive and the join handling has to be right.
  3. Screen-space dashing keyed on the fragment coordinate rather than the perimeter. Cheap, and
     WRONG in the way that matters — the pattern would not follow the border, it would look like a
     hatch showing through it, and it would pass a test that only asserts "some dash is present".

⚠️ DO NOT TAKE OPTION 3 TO GET A GREEN TEST. That is the knowingly-partial correctness this campaign
has rejected twice already; a border whose dashes do not follow it is worse than a solid border,
because a solid border is honestly undashed.

NOT BLOCKING bd-2u0.2: the GPU pass draws solid node borders today, which is what it has always done
and is a visible-but-honest gap rather than a wrong picture.

title: Snapshot immutable batch parse signatures by revision
description: Retain the complete public parse-mode batch signature behind the stable corpus revision key so repeated 512-document parse jobs return in O(1); isolate with a same-ELF disable arm and compare against live mermaid.parse.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
READ THE SOURCE BEFORE IMPLEMENTING THIS, AND IT CHANGES THE TASK. What this bead asks for is the mechanism that was REMOVED for producing this project's worst measurement artifact, and the codebase carries an enforced tripwire against re-adding it.

EVIDENCE, from crates/fm-cli/examples/headtohead.rs:

  line 59-70, on BatchRevisionKey: "No TIMED arm reads it any more (bd-8557). It keyed parse_all_versioned's memo, which the parse arm STOPPED CONSULTING once it was found to be measuring the cache rather than the parse; the field is kept because it is part of the corpus item's deserialized shape and the memo's semantics tests still exercise it." It carries #[expect(dead_code)] with that reason.

  line 392-403, on the render-snapshot memo: "bd-bh7d removed the only production caller: feeding this memo inside a calibrated batch turned iterations 2..N into O(1) probes and produced a 16 ns 'render'." And: "`expect` rather than `allow`, and `not(test)` rather than unconditional, so this annotation is enforced in BOTH directions: it FAILS THE BUILD the moment a real caller appears."

So: (a) the revision-keyed memo existed, (b) it was removed because the parse arm was measuring the cache, (c) adding a caller now fails the build BY DESIGN, and (d) bd-dqkg already holds the (a) reinstate / (b) remove decision this bead would pre-empt.

THE BEAD'S OWN DESIGN IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. A same-ELF disable arm is the right control, but bd-bh7d passed EVERY gate the harness had: output equivalence 25/25, the fm bracket, the median CI, and a balanced-square incumbent null at 1.0120. A statistical control cannot distinguish a fast engine from a memo; only a COUNT can.

AND THE RATE GATE CANNOT ADMIT THE HONEST VERSION EITHER. A memo hit legitimately returns a document it did not recompute, so a truthful reuse row lands orders of magnitude above the bytes/ns ceiling and is refused for looking exactly like the defect. Raising the ceiling would delete the gate. This is recorded in the ledger already; it is why reuse needs a counted proof rather than a threshold.

WHAT I IMPLEMENTED INSTEAD, as the missing prerequisite: fm_core::reuse_proof (commit below). ReuseProof { requested, computed } classifies a batch as FullComputation / Reuse / NothingComputed / Impossible, and admits_throughput_claim() is true ONLY for a full computation. The historical artifact is a test case: requested 342,682, computed 25 -> Reuse, claim refused. Controls: an honest full batch DOES admit a claim (a type that refused everything would be safe and useless), one reused document out of 512 is enough to disqualify, and impossible counts are refused rather than read generously -- treating computed > requested as a full computation would let a corrupt count launder a reuse row into a throughput row.

CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH THIS BEAD COULD BE DONE SAFELY:
  1. The memo is reachable ONLY from an incremental/reuse lane, never from the parse arm's timed loop.
  2. Its rows carry ReuseProof and are read as reuse measurements, never compared against full-computation rows in either direction.
  3. The #[expect(dead_code)] tripwire is DELETED deliberately as part of that change, not worked around.
  4. bd-dqkg's reinstate/remove decision is settled first, since this bead assumes one answer to it.

Recommend this bead be blocked on bd-dqkg rather than implemented as written.

title: mermaid 11 shape names we do not know render as the wrong shape, silently
description:
MEASURED against the pinned mermaid 11.15.0 bundle, by enumerating our accepted alias set against the incumbent's.

WE ACCEPT (crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs, flowchart_metadata_shape, ~line 2244):
  box circ circle cyl cylinder database db dbl-circ decision diam diamond double-circle
  doublecircle event fr-rect framed-rectangle hex hexagon in-out lean-r parallelogram pill
  priority proc process question rect rectangle round rounded stadium subprocess subroutine
  terminal trap-b trapezoid

PRESENT IN THE INCUMBENT AND ABSENT FROM THAT LIST (each verified in the bundle):
  notch-rect  curv-trap  bow-rect  lin-cyl  div-rect  sl-rect  tag-rect  hourglass  bolt
  brace  flag  delay

THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, not the missing shapes. flowchart_metadata_shape returns None for an
unrecognised name and its own doc says the caller then "keeps the node's existing shape rather than
invent one". So `A@{ shape: notch-rect }` renders as a plain rectangle with NO warning: the author
wrote valid mermaid 11, got a different shape, and has nothing pointing at why.

That is the same class as bd-rrvr (unrecognised operator surviving as a node label) and the
`style` target that resolved to nothing before bd-xfmm. Every other unrecognised-input path in this
parser now warns - sequence, class, state and ER each emit "unsupported <kind> syntax: <line>" - so
shape names are the remaining silent one.

SMALLEST HONEST FIX, and it does not require implementing any shape: warn when a `shape:` name is
unrecognised, naming the name. "shape 'notch-rect' is not implemented; the node kept its previous
shape" turns a silently wrong diagram into an actionable message. Implementing the twelve shapes is
a separate, larger piece of work.

CONTROL THE FIX WILL NEED: a recognised name must NOT warn, and an unrecognised one must not change
the shape it falls back to. A warning that fired on `rounded` would train readers to ignore the
channel.

NOT IMPLEMENTED BY ME: crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs is under an exclusive agent-mail
reservation held by CalmOriole (expires 2026-08-18T23:39Z), and /data is at 43G against a 42G hard
brake with a build throttle in force, so this was filed rather than written.

title: Measure the seven new XL corpus items: does mermaid-js render 2000+ nodes in wide/cyclic/dense_dag/sequence/class/state/er at all?
description:
The corpus items exist and are pinned (this bead is the RUN, not the authoring). Seven syntax families had no XL tier: their largest pinned sizes were 20 participants, 40 states, 40 ER entities, 50 classes, 100 cyclic nodes, 200 dense-DAG nodes, 512 wide-layout nodes. The XL block only ever reached thousands of nodes through flowchart / architecture / er_schema / edit_trace / doc_build.

ADDED (all dnf_allowed, js_budget_ms 600000, reps_js 1, reps_rs 40), with pins.json extended by exactly 7 keys and zero existing hashes touched:
  wide_xl_50x50       2500 nodes   127352 bytes  9cfef3ff...
  cyclic_scc_xl_2500  2500 nodes   110787 bytes  127e6986...
  dense_dag_xl_2000   2000 nodes   146782 bytes  8269f6d2...
  sequence_xl_2000    2000 parts   156189 bytes  ca71cd41...
  class_xl_2000       2000 classes 156446 bytes  1790d245...
  state_xl_2000       2000 states   54688 bytes  b76e7fa8...
  er_xl_2000          2000 ents     51765 bytes  6ddd0830...

WHAT THIS BEAD CLOSES ON: a run.mjs invocation over --only these seven ids, on a quiet host, with the live mermaid-js arm, recording for each item whether mermaid produced a render. A dnf with kind='failed' is the structural result (mermaid does not render this at all -- no waiting changes it); a dnf with kind='timeout' is a lower bound only; a completed mermaid render means the family does NOT fail at this size and the item becomes an ordinary ratio row that must then pass cross-engine equivalence.

DO NOT pre-suppose the failure. The reason to run this is that the answer is unknown per family: mermaid's own maxEdges/maxTextSize are already raised in pins.json, so a family may well render where another RangeErrors. Reporting 'mermaid handled 3 of the 7' is exactly as valuable as reporting 7 failures, and cheaper to believe.

BLOCKED ON HOST: this needs the same quiet window bd-hcw3 needs (load < 8; the host has been 22-40 on 64 cores all session) and a built ELF (rch fleet has been refusing test-sized jobs: 'no admissible workers ... insufficient_total_slots').

NOT A RATIO CLAIM UNTIL RUN. The items are admitted-but-unmeasured, the same status er_schema_5000x8 and er_schema_10000x8 carried when they were added.

comments.text:
INCUMBENT ARM MEASURED, live on this host, mermaid@11.15.0 (bundle sha256 70137e77bb273bb2ef972b86e8b0400cca8be53cb25bfc45911a186dc98665de, securityLevel=strict) in Chrome/151.0.7922.108, --mode render --render-once, budget 600000 ms per item.

  item                 status  kind    failure_class  wall      error
  wide_xl_50x50        dnf     failed  range_error     8758 ms  render failed after parse accepted: Maximum call stack size exceeded
  cyclic_scc_xl_2500   dnf     failed  range_error     8719 ms  same
  dense_dag_xl_2000    dnf     failed  range_error    46482 ms  same
  class_xl_2000        dnf     failed  range_error    20689 ms  same
  state_xl_2000        dnf     failed  range_error     7608 ms  same
  er_xl_2000           dnf     failed  range_error     7573 ms  same
  sequence_xl_2000     ok      -       -              12460 ms  rendered successfully

SIX OF SEVEN, NOT SEVEN. The campaign brief said mermaid-js crashes on all seven of these families at >=2000 nodes. Measured, sequence_xl_2000 RENDERS -- 2,000 participants and 3,998 messages complete in 12.46 s. Correcting that here rather than repeating the round number: the structural claim covers six families, and sequence is an ordinary (slow) ratio row, not a cannot-run row.

THE FAILURE IS IN RENDER, NOT PARSE. Every failing item carries probe_parse_accepted: true, so mermaid ACCEPTS the document and then exhausts the JS call stack while rendering. This matters for how the result is described: it is not "mermaid rejects diagrams this large", it is "mermaid accepts them and then cannot draw them". kind=failed (not timeout) means no budget increase changes the outcome -- there is nothing to wait for, so these bound no ratio and belong out of the ratio aggregate, which is exactly what run.mjs already does with dnf rows.

NOTE ON dense_dag_xl_2000: 46.5 s before failing, the slowest failure by 2x. It has the highest edge density (~8,000 edges over 2,000 nodes), so mermaid does substantial work before the stack gives out.

OUR ARM is covered by crates/fm-cli/tests/xl_scale_classes_test.rs, which drives parse -> layout -> render for all seven at these exact shapes and asserts every declared node reaches layout, the LAST declared node survives, the shared geometry-invariant checker reports nothing, the SVG closes, and two independent runs agree byte for byte.

This bead's question is answered for the incumbent side. It stays open until our side's test run is green and both halves are committed.

title: Canvas renderer ignores ALL user styling: style, classDef and sequence rect colours
description:
MEASURED SVG vs canvas on the same IR, reading the canvas's recorded SetFillStyle operations:

  style_stmt        style a fill:#ff0000        svg=true canvas=FALSE
  classdef          classDef hot fill:#ff0000   svg=true canvas=FALSE
  classdef_stroke   classDef hot stroke:#00ff00 svg=true canvas=FALSE
  seq_rect_color    rect rgb(255,0,0)           svg=true canvas=FALSE

The canvas emits only 3-4 distinct fills for an ENTIRE diagram - the uniform config colours - regardless of what the author declared.

COUNTED, which makes the cause unambiguous rather than inferred:
  fm-render-svg     inline_style 30   classes 19   style_refs 11
  fm-render-canvas   inline_style  0   classes  0   style_refs  0
  fm-render-term     inline_style  0   classes  4   style_refs  0

The canvas reads NONE of the three styling channels. The parser and IR carry them (fm-render-svg consumes all three), so this is a renderer gap, not a parse gap.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COLOUR: the canvas path is what fm-wasm ships to a browser. A user who colours their diagram sees it uncoloured in the browser preview and correctly coloured in exported SVG - the two outputs disagree about the document.

IT ALSO BLOCKS bd-2u0.2. That bead's architecture item 1 wants per-instance fill and stroke colours on GpuNodeInstance. There is nothing per-node to carry while the canvas resolves no styling at all; I recorded that as the blocker on that bead and this is it.

THE TERMINAL IS A PARTIAL CASE, not a clean one: it reads `classes` (4 references) but neither inline_style nor style_refs. Worth its own measurement rather than assuming it is either fine or equally broken.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED for node fill and stroke. resolve_node_colors merges the three channels in mermaid's order - classDef definitions named by node.classes, then style directives targeting the node, then the node's own inline_style - and returns None per channel when nothing was declared, so an unstyled diagram keeps the theme default rather than a colour the resolver invented.

THE SVG HELPER COULD NOT BE REUSED, which is worth knowing before someone tries: resolve_node_inline_styles returns CSS STRINGS, and fm-render-svg gets classDef support for free by emitting a CSS class and letting the BROWSER cascade it. A canvas has no cascade, so the class has to be resolved in the renderer and the values returned as colours.

FOUR TESTS, two of them controls that would catch the obvious wrong implementations: an unstyled diagram must keep #ffffff and must NOT acquire a colour from nowhere (catches a resolver that always returns something), and 'class a hot' must leave b at the default (catches a resolver that ignores the target and paints every node).

STILL OPEN in this bead: edge styling (linkStyle) and text colour, neither of which this touches; and the terminal's partial case - it reads classes (4 references) but neither inline_style nor style_refs, which deserves its own measurement rather than an assumption.

THIS ALSO UNBLOCKS bd-2u0.2's per-instance colours. I recorded there that GpuNodeInstance had nothing per-node to carry because the canvas resolved no styling; resolve_node_colors is now that source.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TERMINAL HALF IS MIS-SCOPED, and it is not a small follow-up to the canvas fix.

The canvas fix worked by RESOLVING style/classDef/inline_style into a stroke and fill the renderer already had. The terminal has no such channel to resolve them into.

MEASURED, not inferred:
  * crates/fm-render-term/src/renderer.rs emits NO ANSI anywhere. Its only \u{1b} is the INPUT of strips_terminal_control_characters_from_labels.
  * TermRenderConfig has no colour field at all - tier, render_mode, glyph_mode, sizes, label caps, show_selection, show_clusters, diagonal_edges, padding, show_minimap, gantt_today. Nothing else.
  * The sole ANSI emitter in the crate is minimap.rs, behind an explicit opt-in MinimapConfig::use_color, default false.

⚠️ I NEARLY FILED A WRONG REASON FOR THE RIGHT CONCLUSION, and it is worth recording because it is the same substring-vs-semantics trap this project keeps hitting. My first reading was 'the terminal asserts it emits no ESC, so it is deliberately monochrome' - citing strips_terminal_control_characters_from_labels. That test sanitises USER-SUPPLIED escapes in a label; it says nothing about the renderer's own output. The conclusion survives, but on the evidence above rather than on that test.

WHAT 'reads classes only' ACTUALLY MEANS: the single classes reader in this crate is is_block_beta_space_node, which matches the STRUCTURAL marker class block-beta-space. That is a layout probe, not partial styling support. Describing it as a partial case overstates what is there.

SO THE REMAINING ITEM IS A NEW CAPABILITY: terminal colour output. It must be OPT-IN, because -f term is routinely piped to a file where escape bytes are corruption rather than colour, and MinimapConfig::use_color is the in-repo precedent for exactly that shape. Sizing it as 'finish the styling fix' would understate it considerably.

I have NOT built it - that is a feature decision about the terminal's output contract, not a leftover. Recorded at the top of TermRenderConfig, where a reader asking 'why is there no colour option' will actually look.

Gate: fm-render-term tests pass, clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0 (doc-comment change only).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
LAST MEASURED ROW CLOSED: seq_rect_color now reaches the canvas.

`rect rgb(255,0,0)` in a sequence diagram is a FRAGMENT, not a cluster - draw_sequence_fragments hardcoded `rgba(226,232,240,0.2)` while `fragment.color` sat unread on the very struct the loop iterates (LayoutSequenceFragment.color, fm-layout lib.rs:2161). One line of plumbing; the value was already there.

MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND THE TEST CAUGHT IT. I assumed the sequence rect was a cluster and wired cluster_box.color first. That test failed with fill rgba(226,232,240,0.2) - a DIFFERENT alpha from the cluster theme 0.44 - which is what pointed at a separate code path. Kept the cluster change anyway: it is correct and live for the group path (fm-layout:6249 populates color from group.color).

Also added sanitize_canvas_paint. This is not injection defence - a canvas fillStyle is not markup. It is that a browser IGNORES an unparsable fillStyle and keeps the PREVIOUS colour, so forwarding junk paints the shape with whatever was drawn last: a silent, position-dependent wrong colour. Refusing early and falling back to the theme is the visible failure instead. Accepts hex/rgb()/rgba()/hsl()/hsla()/bare keyword; refuses quotes, semicolons, backslashes, angle brackets, control chars, and anything over 64 bytes.

13/13 pass in fm-render-canvas::node_styling, with controls: uncoloured cluster keeps the theme, malformed colour falls back and is never forwarded verbatim.

SPLIT OUT AS bd-xfmm: a flowchart subgraph + `style one fill:` still does not colour, because fm-layout hardcodes LayoutClusterBox.color=None at 16484 and 16848 - the colour never arrives. A renderer test for it would fail for a reason in another crate, so it is a note in the test file and a bead of its own, not an assertion here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TEXT COLOUR NOW REACHES THE CANVAS - the remaining half of this bead's canvas side.

The fill/stroke half landed earlier; the TEXT half had the same shape one channel later. Every label was drawn in config.label_color whatever the author wrote, so `style a color:#f00`, a classDef carrying `color:`, and an inline style were all discarded for text.

REFERENCE BEHAVIOUR: fm-render-svg honours it by mapping `color` onto the text element's `fill` - in split_style_properties, `color` is the single TEXT_STYLE_PROPERTIES entry that is RENAMED rather than passed through. A canvas has no cascade, so the same declaration has to be resolved in Rust and handed to set_fill_style before the text is drawn. That is why porting the SVG helper would not work: it returns CSS strings, not colours - the same reason the peer's fill/stroke half needed its own resolver.

IMPLEMENTATION: the merge chain (classDef, then style directives, then inline_style, later wins) is factored out of resolve_node_colors into merged_node_style, so a second property reads off the SAME chain rather than a second copy of it. resolve_node_colors keeps its exact signature, which matters because gpu_plan.rs calls it too. resolve_node_text_color reads `color` from the same merge and returns None when nothing was declared, so the caller keeps the theme default instead of a colour the function invented.

THE EDIT WAS LINE-RANGE BOUNDED, and that is the part worth recording. `ctx.set_fill_style(&self.config.label_color);` appears at indent 16 in TEN places, and only FOUR are inside the node loop where the resolved value is in scope. A global replace - which is what I first wrote - would have produced six out-of-scope references, and under the build freeze I cannot compile to find that out. I counted the indents, bounded the rewrite to the loop's line range, and asserted exactly four replacements; the other seventeen label_color sites are untouched.

The four share ONE binding rather than resolving per site: plain label, class compartments, ER entity rows and requirement rows all draw text belonging to the same node, so they must agree about its colour. Resolving per site is how one branch silently keeps the default.

TESTS (crates/fm-render-canvas/tests/node_text_color.rs) pair each drawn text with the fill in force when it was drawn - a bare list of fills cannot say which label got which colour, which is the whole defect. Five cases: style directive, classDef, an UNSTYLED node in the SAME diagram keeping the theme colour (the discriminating control; without it, colouring every label with the first declared colour passes), an unstyled diagram unchanged, and a control that a TEXT colour never fills a SHAPE (a resolver reading the wrong key would colour the box and satisfy everything else).

Ops are read from the Debug form as node_styling.rs does: DrawOperation is not exported from the crate, so a test cannot name it. My first draft imported it and would not have compiled.

NO GOLDEN MOVES: canvas output is not goldened (the goldens are SVG), so nothing needs re-blessing for this one.

UNBUILT: /data 28G under freeze, no cargo ran.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE TERMINAL'S "PARTIAL CASE" IS CLOSED, AND IT IS NOT THE CANVAS DEFECT. Measured with this
bead's own method rather than assumed, which is what the open item asked for.

Same IR, both renderers, a fixture declaring all three channels
(`style a fill:#ff0000,color:#00ff00`, `classDef hot fill:#0000ff`, `class b hot`):

  arm    #ff0000  #0000ff  #00ff00   escape bytes
  svg    yes      yes      yes       --            <- control: the colours ARE in the IR
  term   no       no       no        0

The SVG arm is the control that makes the terminal row mean something: the declarations survive
parsing and reach a renderer that honours them, so the terminal's plain output is a choice about
real data, not the absence of data.

WHY IT IS A CHOICE, three independent pieces of evidence:

1. The `classes 4` count that made the terminal look half-implemented is reading a DIFFERENT
   FEATURE. Every `classes` read in renderer.rs is `is_block_beta_space_node`, which asks whether a
   node is a block-beta SPACER. That is structure, not style. The terminal reads none of the three
   styling channels, so it is not a partial case at all -- the census just landed on a homonym.

2. config.rs states the policy outright: colour output "must be OPT-IN because `-f term` is
   routinely piped to a file and escape bytes there are corruption, not colour".
   `MinimapConfig::use_color` defaults to false, and colour is confined to the minimap and the diff
   summary -- neither of which is the diagram body.

3. renderer.rs:3611 already tests that a label carrying `\u{1b}[31m` renders with no `\u{1b}` in
   the output. That is an INJECTION DEFENCE, not an oversight: a label is attacker-controlled in
   any tool that renders a diagram someone else wrote, and an unfiltered CSI or OSC sequence
   retitles the window or moves the cursor.

CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this needed pinning rather than just recording: the fix that was
correct for the canvas -- resolve the declared colour, paint with it -- would be a REGRESSION here.
It corrupts every piped `-f term` capture. Anyone closing "the terminal half of bd-lvj3" by
symmetry with the canvas half would be introducing the bug the renderer already avoids.

LANDED: crates/fm-render-term/tests/plain_text_contract.rs, four tests. There was no end-to-end
escape gate before this -- the existing check is a unit test on a constructed label, and a future
styling change would land on the public path instead. Tests: the fixture really declares styling
(the control above, asserted on the IR so a parser regression cannot make the others pass more
easily); a styled diagram emits zero escape bytes AND never writes `ff0000` as literal text either
(stripping the escape while printing the hex would satisfy a naive escape scan); an escape inside a
node label does not survive to the output; and styled vs unstyled render BYTE-IDENTICALLY, which
separates "ignores styling" from "chokes on styling" -- if a declaration perturbed geometry or
truncated a label, neither of the other scans would notice.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p fm-render-term exit 0, 6 suites, 161 passed, 0 failed; clippy -D warnings
exit 0.

SEPARATELY, in the same session: the canvas text-colour work recorded here on 2026-08-18 as
"UNBUILT: /data 28G under freeze, no cargo ran" now COMPILES AND PASSES -- cargo test
-p fm-render-canvas, 9 suites, 129 tests, 0 failed, including node_text_color.rs (5) and
subgraph_style.rs (3). The unbuilt caveat on that comment can be dropped.

WHAT REMAINS on this bead is the canvas edge/text work already recorded, not the terminal. I make

  classdef         classDef hot fill:#ff0000  -> node_styling.rs::a_classdef_colours_the_nodes_that_name_it
  classdef_stroke  classDef hot stroke:#00ff00 -> the same test's stroke assertion
  seq_rect_color   rect rgb(255,0,0)          -> cluster_styling.rs::a_sequence_rect_colour_reaches_the_canvas

⚠️ THE CENSUS IS NOT THE EVIDENCE, and re-running it is how I nearly misread this. Today's counts
read fm-render-canvas inline_style 9, classes 5, style_refs 7 (was 0/0/0), which looks like proof
the channels are read. But fm-render-term now reports inline_style 1, and that single hit is a
COMMENT in config.rs referring to this bead. A grep counts prose. The rows above are behavioural,
which is why they are the evidence and the census is only a pointer.

TWO CHANNELS STILL MISSING, measured the same way with the SVG arm as control:

  channel                                        svg                          canvas
  edge label colour  linkStyle 0 color:#ff00ff   emits ff00ff                 FALSE
  node dash          style a stroke-dasharray:5 5 emits stroke-dasharray:5 5  FALSE

Also probed and already WORKING, recorded so nobody re-derives them: cluster/subgraph border
colour, classDef text colour, `style` on a stateDiagram-v2 node, `style` on a classDiagram node.

NODE DASH IS FIXED in this commit; edge label colour is NOT and remains open on this bead.

`resolve_node_stroke_dasharray` reads the same merge chain as the other three properties, so this
is the fourth property off one chain rather than a fourth copy of it. Same asymmetric-sibling shape
as stroke-width: the EDGE path has drawn dashes since the edge half landed, and the node path never
learned the property.

THE PART WORTH KNOWING BEFORE TOUCHING THIS: `lineDash` is canvas STATE, not a draw argument. It
persists until something sets it again, so setting a dash and not clearing it dashes every shape
drawn afterwards — a worse defect than the one being fixed, and invisible to any test that renders
a single node. It is set only when declared and cleared immediately after, so an undeclared node is
drawn under exactly the state it was drawn under before. The control asserts this structurally: the
LAST dash-affecting op must be the reset, not the pattern. Counting occurrences cannot express it,
because the correct implementation legitimately emits the pattern once per dashed node.

`parse_dash_array` refuses what it cannot use rather than forwarding it: unparsable, negative, and
ALL-ZERO. The last is the interesting one — `[0, 0]` is not a no-op on a canvas, so forwarding a
junk declaration is strictly worse than ignoring it, the same reason `parse_stroke_width` refuses.
Both separators are accepted because SVG accepts both (`5 5`, `5,5`).

Six tests: style directive, classDef, comma form, the leak control above, an undeclared node
keeping a solid border (guards the None arm against a resolver that invents a default), and a
malformed/degenerate case covering all three refusals.

-D warnings exit 0.

probed six channels rather than enumerating every property mermaid accepts.

equivalent to setting no font at all. Pinned by a test asserting the exact composition

`font-family` cannot use a closed set, so it is a CHARACTER ALLOWLIST plus a 128-byte bound:
letters, digits, space, `,`, `-`, `_`, `.` and quotes, which covers real stacks like
`'Fira Code', monospace`. Measured refusals: `Courier{}`, `Courier<b>`, `Courier()`, `Courier!`,

a value ever exists — `font-family:Courier;` yields the family `Courier`, an ordinary declaration.

sanitiser. I kept that as its own test rather than deleting the case, so if the style grammar ever
changes such that a raw `;` survives into a value, it flips to failing and says so.

refusal test fails, establish whether the sanitiser is weak or the PREMISE is wrong. Last time a
disarm control proved the sanitiser was load-bearing; this time a probe proved the input never

title: requirement verifyMethod and any capitalised field were dropped at parse time
description:
`verifyMethod:` - the spelling mermaid's own grammar and documentation use - was DROPPED. The
requirement field match ran against the RAW field text with a lowercase-only `"verifymethod"` arm,
so the camelCase form every author is told to write fell through and the value never reached the IR.
The same trap hit any capitalised field: `Text:`, `Risk:`, `ID:`.

THIS IS THE HALF bd-qdmn LEFT OPEN. That bead hit exactly this problem for `docRef` and fixed it by
listing BOTH spellings in the pattern - which closed one field and left the mechanism armed for the
other five. An enumeration of casings can only ever be as complete as the next author's shift key.

MEASURED against the pinned bundle with scripts/headtohead/parse_probe.mjs - all three PARSE:

    verifyMethod: test    PARSED
    verifymethod: test    PARSED
    VerifyMethod: test    PARSED

so mermaid's requirement lexer is case-insensitive and matching a single casing was never right for
any of these fields.

FOUND SYSTEMATICALLY. I extracted all 137 `/^(?:word\b)/` keyword tokens from the bundle's lexers
and diffed them against our parser sources; `verifyMethod` came out of that list. The first two runs
of that diff were BROKEN - they reported every keyword missing, including ones I could see in the
source - because my sed left a trailing `)` and then a literal `\b` on each token. A uniform verdict
is a broken instrument, not a discovery; the third run is the one with a file-content control on it.

FIXED: a `requirement_field_key` helper canonicalises the name case-insensitively and returns the
lowercase key, so the caller's match stays plain arms. It allocates nothing - `eq_ignore_ascii_case`
compares in place, where `to_ascii_lowercase()` would have put a String on the parse path for every
field line inside a requirement block.

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Three tests added, none compiled. One is a CONTROL
that `notafield:` is still ignored - case-insensitive matching must not slide into matching
anything, or the block would start absorbing arbitrary lines.
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build

title: ER relationship operators encode cardinality as arrowheads: 12 of 14 draw a head, 2 draw none, and the table contradicts itself twice
description:
FOUND BY THE ARROW-EXPECTATION AUDIT, the same sweep that produced bd-e29r, bd-8yj9 and bd-gp82. This one is provable from the table alone -- it does not need a mermaid reference, because ER_OPERATORS contradicts ITSELF twice.

ER_OPERATORS (crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs:95), all 14 entries:

    ("||--o{", Arrow)   ("||--|{", Arrow)   ("}|--||", Arrow)   ("}o--||", Arrow)
    ("|o--o|", Arrow)   ("o|--|{", Arrow)   ("}|--|{", Arrow)   ("|o--||", Arrow)
    ("}o--o{", Arrow)
    ("}|..|{", DottedArrow)   ("||..||", DottedArrow)   ("..", DottedArrow)
    ("||--||", Line)          ("--", Line)

CONTRADICTION 1 -- LINE STYLE ALONE ADDS AN ARROWHEAD.
  ("||--||", Line)   vs  ("||..||", DottedArrow)
  ("--",     Line)   vs  ("..",     DottedArrow)
Each pair is the SAME cardinality with only the dash pattern changed. In mermaid, `..` is the
non-identifying relationship: same terminators, dashed instead of solid. It cannot acquire an
arrowhead by being dashed. One member of each pair is wrong.

CONTRADICTION 2 -- CARDINALITY ALONE ADDS AN ARROWHEAD.
  ("||--||", Line)   vs  ("}|--|{", Arrow)
Identical line style, identical `--`, and the only difference is which cardinality glyphs sit at the
ends -- yet one draws no head and the other draws one. Cardinality is not direction.

BOTH CONTRADICTIONS REACH THE OUTPUT. Verified by reading the marker mapping, not assumed:
  fm-render-svg:3300  ArrowType::Line | ThickLine | DottedLine => 0            (no marker)
  fm-render-svg:3301  ArrowType::Arrow | DottedArrow           => MARKER_END
  fm-render-svg:12209 ArrowType::Arrow      => marker-end="url(#arrow-end)"
  fm-render-svg:12232 ArrowType::DottedArrow => dasharray "5,5" + url(#arrow-end)
So 12 of the 14 ER operators draw an arrowhead at the target end and 2 draw none, on the same
diagram, decided by cardinality and dash pattern rather than by anything directional.

WHY AN ARROWHEAD IS WRONG FOR EVERY ONE OF THEM, not just for the inconsistent ones. An ER
relationship is not directed. mermaid draws crow's-foot / bar / circle terminators at each end and
NO arrowhead. This engine does not draw those glyphs at all -- it renders cardinality as TEXT near
the endpoints (write_er_cardinality_labels_into, fm-render-svg:4607 and :4773). Given that model the
faithful mapping is line style only: every `--` operator to Line, every `..` operator to DottedLine,
with the cardinality carried by the labels that are already drawn. The arrowhead adds direction
information the notation does not have, and it is the ONLY thing distinguishing `||--||` from
`}|--|{` in the drawn edge, which is backwards -- those two differ in cardinality, which the labels
already say, and not in direction.

TWO REASONS NOTHING CAUGHT THIS.
1. GOLDEN BLIND SPOT. grep over crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/*.mmd finds exactly two ER relationships,
   both in er_basic.mmd:
       USER ||--o{ ORDER : places
       ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
   Both map to Arrow. Neither `||--||`, nor any `..` form, nor any of the other ten operators
   appears anywhere in the corpus, so no golden distinguishes the two branches and NO GOLDEN MOVES
   when this is fixed.
2. ORACLE BLIND SPOT, structural. scripts/headtohead/svg_equivalence.mjs models class-diagram
   operators as marker roles -- markerRoles at :930 maps '<|--' to ['inheritance','none'] and so on
   -- but its erDiagram branch (:984) matches the operator with a bare `[^\s]+` and throws it away,
   recording only `from>to`. The ER operator's meaning is invisible to the cross-engine equivalence
   gate by construction, so that gate cannot ever report this.

THE ONLY EXISTING TEST OVER THESE TABLES CHECKS ORDER, NOT MEANING.
operator_tables_are_longest_prefix_first (mermaid_parser.rs:11514) asserts that no operator is
preceded by its own prefix -- a real invariant, and the one bd-92b6 was about -- but it says nothing
about which ArrowType any entry maps to. Every semantic defect in these five tables is outside what
it can see. That is the gap this bead sits in.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
1. The two committed golden relationships (`||--o{`, `||--|{`) must keep rendering, with their
   cardinality labels unchanged -- the labels are the notation, and a fix that removes the arrowhead
   must not disturb them. Assert the label text is still present and still positioned at the
   endpoints.
2. `||--||` and `}|--|{` must render the same edge decoration as each other. Asserting one in
   isolation passes while the inconsistency survives in the other.
3. `--` and `..` must differ ONLY in dash pattern: same marker set, different stroke-dasharray.
   A fix that maps both to Line loses the non-identifying distinction entirely, which is a
   different defect in the same place.
4. Flowchart, class and sequence edges must be untouched. ArrowType::Arrow is shared vocabulary;
   this is a change to which ArrowType the ER table SELECTS, not to what any ArrowType means.
5. A fixture per operator family would close the golden blind spot, but the corpus currently has no
   way to tell any of this apart -- note that adding one is the only way a golden can defend the fix.

SIBLING FOUND IN THE SAME SWEEP, filed separately: PACKET_OPERATORS maps bare `==` to ThickArrow
while FLOW_OPERATORS maps the same token to ThickLine.
close_reason:
LANDED. All 14 ER operators now map on line style alone: every -- form to Line, every .. form to DottedLine. Cardinality is carried by the endpoint labels that were already drawn.

VERIFIED ON REAL OUTPUT, not only the table: rendering the committed er_basic.mmd with the fixed binary gives 0 marker-end usages, down from 2, while the cardinality labels 'places' and 'contains' are still drawn. The relationship keeps its meaning and stops asserting a direction the notation does not have.

TESTS: every entry must be DottedLine if it contains .. and Line otherwise, so a new operator cannot be introduced with a head; both original contradictions are pinned by name so a regression reads as the same bug; -- and .. must still DIFFER, so the fix cannot collapse identifying and non-identifying into one style; and a control asserts the parsed cardinality survives, because removing the heads is only correct while the labels carry it.

GATES: cargo test -j 2 -p fm-parser 553 passed 0 failed (551 before these two tests); -p fm-render-svg 297 passed 0 failed. Observed loadavg 14.68/20.30/25.97.

⚠️ crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/er_basic.svg still contains the pre-fix marker-end and is now stale, although golden_svg_test passes. I deliberately did NOT run BLESS=1: a wholesale re-bless would also absorb the cycle_braid position change that bd-38wq is tracking, and mask an open defect that is not mine.

comments.text:
⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN FILING, same session, before anyone acts on it. This bead says "no golden distinguishes the two branches and NO GOLDEN MOVES when this is fixed." The first half is true and the second half is FALSE, and they are not the same claim.

neither catch the inconsistency nor defend the fix. "The corpus is blind to the defect" does not
imply "the corpus is unaffected by the fix", and I conflated the two.

for a golden bless with an element-by-element diff, and expect exactly two changed <path> elements

⚠️ SECOND THING TO SETTLE BEFORE CHANGING ANY ENTRY, which I did not settle. I established the
table contradicts ITSELF -- that part needs no external reference and stands. I did NOT measure what
mermaid-js actually draws for these operators; I reasoned from its documented notation. The
direction of the fix depends on that:

  - If mermaid draws crow's-foot terminators and no arrowhead, mapping `--` to Line and `..` to
    DottedLine is faithful, and the cardinality text this engine already draws
    (write_er_cardinality_labels_into) carries what the glyphs would have.
  - If instead the intended reading is that the arrowhead stands in for the crow's foot on the
    "many" end, then the fix is the opposite: make ALL of them carry a head consistently, and
    `||--||` and `--` are the wrong two rather than the right two.

Both readings resolve the self-contradiction; they resolve it in opposite directions, and the
committed golden's two edges land on opposite sides. Render the operators through the pinned
mermaid-js harness and look before choosing. Do not take my recommendation of Line / DottedLine as
settled -- it is the reading I find better supported, not a measurement.
