title: Unrecognised operators are swallowed into a node label as raw source, with no warning
description:
MEASURED. An unrecognised edge operator does not fail, does not warn, and does not drop the line - it collapses the WHOLE LINE into a single node whose label is a raw source fragment.

  source                        nodes declared / got   warning   resulting label
  flowchart  a[A] ~~> b[B]              2 / 1            none     "A] ~~> b[B"
  class      Alpha ~~ Beta              2 / 1            none     "Alpha ~~ Beta"
  flowchart  a[Unclosed --> b[B]        2 / 1            none     "Unclosed --> b[B"

CONTROL, so the instrument is not simply reporting everything: the well-formed a[A] --> b[B] yields 2 nodes labelled ["A", "B"] with no warning, and state_bad_arrow yields the sensible label "B".

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A PARSE FAILURE: the user gets a box containing the characters "A] ~~> b[B" and NO signal that anything was misread. A dropped line or an error would be honest; rendering a fragment of the user's own syntax as if it were their content is not. It also defeats the eye: the diagram looks like it rendered.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT from bd-64h3 (duplicate branch declared silently). That was a semantic duplicate accepted without comment; this is a SYNTAX error rendered as content.

NOT FIXED HERE: crates/fm-parser is under another agent's exclusive lease. Also, the obvious fix - warn when a line looks like it contains an unrecognised arrow - is a HEURISTIC, and a bad one could warn on legitimate labels containing ~ or >. It deserves a considered rule (e.g. warn only when the collapsed label contains a bracket that the node-token parser did not consume), not a rushed pattern match.

ACCEPTANCE GATE landed as an #[ignore]d reproducer in crates/fm-render-svg/tests: it asserts the two-node source produces two nodes, and that no node label contains a raw operator fragment. Un-ignoring it closes this bead.
close_reason:
SECOND HALF CLOSED. The unrecognised-operator fragment is no longer drawn as content: the node is DROPPED and the warning says so. Both #[ignore]d reproducers are un-ignored and pass; malformed_input is 7 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored.

GROUNDED ON THE INCUMBENT, NOT ON TASTE. I evaluated the pinned mermaid 11.15.0 bundle in the SAME browserless node:vm sandbox mermaid_bench.mjs uses and asked it directly:
  flowchart TD / a[Unclosed --> b[B]   -> THREW 'Parse error on line 2'
  classDiagram / Alpha ~~ Beta         -> parsed ok
So on the unmatched-bracket shape the incumbent REFUSES the line outright while we drew it as a box containing the user's own syntax. Dropping + warning moves us toward mermaid and is strictly more honest than a box full of syntax.

⚠️ HONEST LIMIT ON THAT EVIDENCE, stated rather than papered over: the flowchart '~~>' case could NOT be settled this way. mermaid's flowchart parse path reaches DOMPurify, which needs a DOM that sandbox deliberately withholds, so it reports DNF. Stubbing a DOM to get an answer is exactly the trade mermaid_bench.mjs's own comment warns against ('it would flatter us'), and I did not do it. Both cases take the SAME unmatched-bracket rule, so the policy rests on the case that was actually measured, and the test says so in its docstring.

MECHANISM CONTROL RUN. I left the warning intact and disarmed ONLY the drop (returned false instead of true). Result: the 3 drop-asserting tests FAIL and all 4 controls still PASS --
  FAILED an_unrecognised_operator_does_not_become_a_node_label
  FAILED an_unclosed_bracket_is_dropped_rather_than_drawn
  FAILED a_malformed_line_does_not_drop_its_well_formed_neighbours
  ok     an_unrecognised_operator_is_no_longer_silent
  ok     the_warning_identifies_the_line_and_the_label
  ok     a_balanced_bracket_in_a_label_does_not_warn
  ok     a_well_formed_flowchart_edge_yields_two_clean_nodes
That separates my half from the peer's cleanly: the warning is theirs and survives the disarm, the drop is mine and is what the new assertions carry. Restored and verified (zero disarm residue).

THE ASSERTION THAT STOPS THIS BEING 'DROP EVERYTHING': a_malformed_line_does_not_drop_its_well_formed_neighbours. A rule that refused the whole diagram would satisfy every other assertion here while trading a garbage label for a blank page. A/B/E/F must survive alongside a malformed c ~~> d line, and they do.

THE NARROW RULE IS UNCHANGED: unmatched bracket only. The balanced-bracket control (a["x [y] z"]) still does not warn, with its non-vacuity check that the source really produced two nodes.

Gate: cargo test --workspace exit 0, 57 test-result groups ok / 0 FAILED; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. (First clippy run returned 143 = SIGTERM, killed by the host, not a lint failure; re-run clean.)

NOT A PERF CLAIM. No ratio measured, none claimed. Host was not measurable this tick anyway - window_check.sh refused every window.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
HALF FIXED, and the bead stays OPEN for the other half.

FIXED: the silence. intern_node_token and intern_flow_ast_node now warn when a node label holds an UNMATCHED bracket, naming the line and quoting the label. Both funnels are covered, so every diagram type gets one rule.

STILL OPEN: the garbage. a[A] ~~> b[B] still yields ONE node labelled 'A] ~~> b[B'. Warning is strictly better than silence, but showing a fragment of the user's syntax AS THEIR CONTENT remains wrong.

MY OWN GATE CAUGHT THE OVERCLAIM. I had written one assertion accepting 'parsed cleanly OR warned' plus a second forbidding a raw fragment in any label. After the warning landed, the first was satisfied and the second still failed - so the test refused to go green on a half-fix. I split it into a passing test for the silence and a separate #[ignore]d reproducer for the label, rather than relaxing the assertion. A single either/or assertion would have let the remaining half vanish from view the moment the warning landed, which is exactly what nearly happened.

THE RULE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: unmatched bracket only. Controls prove it: a legitimate a["x [y] z"] label does NOT warn (with a non-vacuity check that the source really produced two nodes), and the full 562-test parser suite produces no new warnings. The tempting rule - warn when the label looks like it contains an arrow - would fire on legitimate labels containing ~ or >, and a false warning on correct input is worse than the silence it replaces.

title: Flaky: tracing_dispatch_event_contains_mandatory_fields fails only under concurrent workspace load
description:
fm-layout's tests::tracing_dispatch_event_contains_mandatory_fields intermittently reds main:

  panicked at crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs:22511
  Should emit a layout.dispatch event

REPRODUCTION PROFILE, measured not guessed:
  cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast   -> FAILED (449 passed, 1 failed)
  cargo test -p fm-layout, 6 consecutive runs -> 450 passed every time
  that test alone -> passes
So it fails only when many test binaries run concurrently and saturate cores. It is not order-within-binary alone, or the isolated runs would have caught it in six tries.

TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS. The second is the one worth worrying about:

(a) BENIGN — the test installs its capture subscriber with tracing::subscriber::with_default, which is THREAD-LOCAL. Any event emitted from a worker thread inside layout_diagram_traced is invisible to it. If the layout takes a parallel path under load, the dispatch event is emitted somewhere the subscriber cannot see and the assertion fails even though the engine behaved correctly. That is a test-harness defect: the fix is a global subscriber for the duration, or asserting on a channel the workers also write to.

(b) CONCERNING — the dispatch DECISION is itself load-sensitive. This repo has a documented defect where output depends on MEASURED WALL TIME through record_parse -> budget ledger -> layout guardrail, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes a loaded host choose a different algorithm and therefore emit a different event. If that is what is happening here, the flake is not a test bug at all — it is the guardrail silently changing layout strategy under contention, and the test is correctly reporting it.

DO NOT fix by loosening the assertion or by adding a retry until (a) vs (b) is settled. If it is (b), the assertion is the only thing currently detecting a real behavioural nondeterminism, and muting it removes the detector. Distinguishing them is cheap: capture WHICH algorithm the dispatch chose in both the passing and failing runs — if the algorithm differs, it is (b).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TEST: an intermittently red test makes 'main is green' unverifiable. I hit exactly this today — a workspace run reported a failure that six isolated runs could not reproduce, which is indistinguishable at a glance from a real regression I had just introduced.

Found while bringing the workspace green in f805c8d3. Everything else passes: 39 of 40 test binaries green, and this one is green in isolation.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION — mechanism (a) is RULED OUT, and the reproduction envelope is now characterised. Not solved; recording so the next lane does not repeat 15 runs.

(a) THREAD-LOCAL SUBSCRIBER MISSING WORKER-THREAD EVENTS — ELIMINATED. fm-layout has no rayon, no thread::spawn and no par_iter anywhere (grepped src/lib.rs and Cargo.toml). layout_diagram_traced is single-threaded, so there is no worker thread whose events a with_default thread-local subscriber could miss. The hypothesis I filed as most likely is simply wrong.

REPRODUCTION ENVELOPE, all measured:
  isolated, that test alone                  PASS
  cargo test -p fm-layout, 6 consecutive     6/6 PASS
  cargo test -p fm-layout --test-threads=64, 8 runs   8/8 PASS
  cargo test -p fm-layout --test-threads=1            PASS
  cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast               FAILED once
So it is NOT intra-binary scheduling — neither maximal parallelism nor forced serialisation provokes it. It needs whole-machine load, i.e. many test binaries running at once. That is a much narrower target than 'flaky'.

WHAT THE FAILURE MODE TELLS US: the earlier assertion ('Layout should emit at least one tracing event') PASSED, so capture was working and events were recorded; only the layout.dispatch event was absent. The info!(event = "layout.dispatch", ..) at lib.rs:3741 is UNCONDITIONAL within its function, so the only explanations left are that the function was not reached, or that this one event was lost from an otherwise-working capture.

STILL OPEN, and now the leading candidate: an early return before line 3741 taking the call down a memo/incremental fast path that never dispatches. There are returns at 3159, 3214 and 3426 ahead of it. Those sit in IncrementalLayoutEngine methods rather than the free function the test calls, so the link is NOT established — confirming or excluding it is the next step, and it matters because a cache path taken under load and not otherwise is the (b)-shaped answer.

MY EARLIER FRAMING WAS TOO BINARY: I filed this as (a) benign vs (b) concerning. With (a) dead, a third possibility is in play — thread-local incremental state surviving across tests via libtest worker-thread reuse. --test-threads=1 does not disprove it (that also serialises the state), so it stays live.

The standing instruction not to mute the assertion or add a retry is unchanged, and is stronger now: the benign explanation is the one that has been eliminated.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
SECOND HYPOTHESIS ELIMINATED, and a real event-loss hole closed in e946dbc7 — but the bead STAYS OPEN because the fix is not proven to be the cause.

(b) EARLY RETURN ONTO A MEMO/INCREMENTAL FAST PATH — ELIMINATED. I named this the leading candidate last time; it is dead. layout_diagram_traced_with_config_and_guardrails (lib.rs:3024) calls compute_traced_layout_with_config_and_guardrails UNCONDITIONALLY — no cache consult, no early return — and that reaches dispatch_layout_algorithm_with_config (lib.rs:3713), whose info! event = layout.dispatch is unconditional. The returns at 3159/3214 that I flagged are IncrementalLayoutEngine METHODS, which this test's call path never enters. So the dispatch event IS emitted on every run; nothing skips it.

That reframing is what mattered: if the event is always emitted and the test says it is absent, the CAPTURE is what loses it. So I audited the capture.

REAL DEFECT FOUND: CaptureWriter had flush() draining its residual buffer but NO Drop. with_writer builds a new writer per event, so each is dropped as soon as its event is written — and any event whose bytes arrived without a terminating newline, with no flush() call, was silently discarded. "Other events present, one specific event missing" is exactly that shape. Fixed by implementing Drop, which is strictly additive: it can only surface a line already written and lost, never drop or duplicate one the newline path committed.

WHY THIS DOES NOT CLOSE THE BEAD — measured, not assumed. I instrumented Drop to report rescued bytes and ran the test: ZERO events rescued in a passing run. The fmt layer does terminate events with a newline normally, so the hole exists but is not taken on the happy path. Whether the rare failing run takes it is unknown, and I still cannot reproduce on demand: 6 isolated runs, 8 at --test-threads=64, 1 at --test-threads=1 all green; only whole-workspace concurrency ever reproduced it, once.

So: two hypotheses dead, one real hole closed, cause still unproven. If it never recurs, this was probably it. If it recurs, the next lane starts from "the event is definitely emitted and the capture definitely has a Drop", which is a much narrower search than where this bead began.

NEXT LEAD if it does recur: the write() path uses "if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(buf)" and SILENTLY DISCARDS the chunk when decoding fails, which happens if a multi-byte character straddles a write boundary. The dispatch event's fields are ASCII, so it should not apply — but that is reasoning, not measurement, and it is the last silent-drop path left in the writer.

comments.author: IvoryPrairie
comments.text:
CONTINUED from PeachGorge's investigation. Landed 3322e9a3. NOT CLOSING — see the last paragraph.

MECHANISM (b) IS RULED OUT, by construction rather than by repro. This bead named settling (a) vs (b) as the thing that must happen before any fix, and flagged (b) — the guardrail changing layout strategy under load — as the concerning one. It cannot be (b): the `layout.dispatch` event is emitted unconditionally at the end of dispatch_layout_algorithm_with_config (lib.rs:3782), on the caller's own thread, with no early return before it, and BEFORE evaluate_layout_guardrails runs. A load-sensitive decision changes the `selected` FIELD; it can never change whether the event exists. The failing assertion is "no event contains layout.dispatch", so a different algorithm choice cannot produce it. Both mechanisms this bead named are now dead.

THE LAST SILENT-DROP PATH IS CLOSED, and it was reachable. Your comment named it and was explicit that the case for its harmlessness was reasoning rather than measurement:
  "the write() path uses `if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(buf)` and SILENTLY DISCARDS the chunk when decoding fails … the dispatch event's fields are ASCII, so it should not apply — but that is reasoning, not measurement"
Measured. capture_writer_keeps_a_line_split_mid_character feeds one JSON line containing a multi-byte character across two write() calls, cut so the split lands INSIDE the character. Against the old chunk decode the first half is invalid UTF-8 alone, the whole chunk including `layout.dispatch` was discarded, and the capture came back EMPTY:
  assertion `left == right` failed: expected exactly the one written line, got []
That is exactly the reported failure shape — other events present, one specific event missing. The ASCII argument was correct about the dispatch event's own FIELDS, but the split boundary is chosen by the writer's chunking, not by the field contents, so ASCII-ness of the payload does not protect it.

CaptureWriter now buffers bytes and decodes only at line boundaries, with from_utf8_lossy, so no chunk can be discarded and even malformed output surfaces as a line the assertion can report on. The test asserts the character is reassembled, not merely that something arrived.

I did NOT loosen the assertion or add a retry, per this bead's explicit instruction.

WHY THIS DOES NOT CLOSE IT, same standard you applied: the original flake reproduced exactly once, under whole-workspace concurrency, and I did not reproduce it today. So I cannot claim this was the cause — only that the writer can no longer lose a line without saying so. If it recurs, the next lane starts from "the event is definitely emitted, the capture has a Drop, and the writer cannot discard bytes", and the search moves off the writer entirely — most likely to the fmt layer or the subscriber registry itself.

IT IS NOT THIS FLAKE. `dispatch_layout_algorithm_with_config` emits `layout.dispatch` UNCONDITIONALLY, after the match, on every path — including the guardrail-fallback path. comments.text:
MECHANISM FOUND AND FIXED, with a controlled experiment. The cause is the one I refuted last tick —
my refutation was wrong because my probe was SEQUENTIAL and the mechanism is a RACE.

THE MECHANISM. `tracing` caches a callsite's `Interest` GLOBALLY. This binary runs 300+ tests in
parallel and many call `layout_diagram_traced` with NO subscriber on their thread, so the
`layout.dispatch` callsite gets evaluated against a subscriber-less thread and cached as
`Interest::never`. A test that then installs a thread-local capturing subscriber finds the callsite
already disabled and captures NOTHING.

⚠️ THE DECISIVE OBSERVATION was not the missing dispatch event — it was that on EVERY miss the
capture held ZERO events while the engine-side trace read `cache_hit=false
query=layout_full_recompute`. The layout really did run and really did dispatch; the callsite was
simply off. "No events at all" says something different from "this one event is missing", and it is
what pointed at interest rather than at the layout.

CONTROLLED, three runs per arm, 4000 capture attempts per run against 8 threads laying out
concurrently (~2M unsubscribed layouts per run):

    arm                                          misses / 12000
    as-is                                             3
    rebuild_interest_cache() inside the closure       2      <- loses the same race
    global always-enabled subscriber                  0      <- fix

FIXED by `install_global_always_enabled_subscriber()`, a `Once` that installs a process-global
always-enabled registry with no layers. No thread is ever subscriber-less, so `never` is never
cached; the per-test `with_default` still overrides it on the capturing thread, and the global one
drops everything after a filter check.

⚠️ MY REFUTATION LAST TICK WAS WRONG, AND THE REASON IS INSTRUCTIVE. I tested the interest-cache
theory with two SEQUENTIAL probes — hit the callsite unsubscribed, then capture — and both captured
the event, so I recorded it refuted. A sequential probe cannot see a race. The rate is about 1 in
4000 even with 8 threads hammering it, which is exactly why it only ever showed up under
whole-workspace load. When a probe refutes a race hypothesis, the probe has to CONTAIN the race.

Bead mechanism (a) stays refuted, and for the original reason: fm-layout has no rayon, par_iter,
thread::spawn or scope, so the event is never emitted off the calling thread. Mechanism (b) —
load-sensitive dispatch — is also not it: `cache_hit=false query=layout_full_recompute` on every
observed miss shows the engine took the full path and dispatched.

VERIFIED: fm-layout 5 suites, 525 passed, 0 failed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0.

⚠️ TWO CLIPPY FAILURES CAME FROM MY OWN DOC COMMENTS, both `doc_lazy_continuation`: my helper's doc
spliced into the middle of the test's existing doc block (so that block documented my helper), and
the refutations note I added last tick continued a bullet list. Last tick I only ran
`clippy -p fm-layout --lib`; `--all-targets` is what caught them. A narrower clippy scope than CI
uses is a gate that passes for the wrong reason.

title: Make sequence note width content-adaptive
description:
## What
Replace the hardcoded `note_width = 120.0` in build_sequence_note_geometry() with a value computed from the note text content using FontMetrics.

## Why
The sequence diagram layout uses a fixed 120px width for ALL notes regardless of content. This means:
- Short notes ("OK") waste space with a 120px box
- Long notes ("This is a detailed explanation of the process flow") truncate or overflow
- Multi-participant "Over" notes that span wide participants also use the same 120px base

## Proposed Approach
1. Compute note width from `FontMetrics::estimate_dimensions(note.text)` + padding
2. Clamp to a reasonable range: `min(80.0, max(text_width + 24.0, 200.0))`
3. For "Over" notes spanning multiple participants, use `max(computed_width, participant_span + padding)`
4. Similarly, `note_line_height = 16.0` and `note_vertical_padding = 12.0` should derive from font metrics

## Dependencies
This requires FontMetrics to be passed to build_sequence_note_geometry(). Currently the function receives `message_y_positions`, `participant_x_centers`, and `node_sizes` but NOT FontMetrics. The signature needs extending.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Short notes render compact
- Long notes expand to fit text
- Multi-line notes properly sized for all lines
- "Over" notes spanning participants are at least as wide as the span
close_reason: Note width now computed from content: widest_line * avg_char_w + 24, clamped [80, 300]. Short notes compact, long notes expand. Multi-line notes size to widest line.

title: Flaky: wall_clock_valve_never_silently_reshapes_the_ordering fails under whole-machine load, because its own control is a wall-clock assertion
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE, once in three runs. cargo test -p fm-layout --lib -- --test-threads=64 at loadavg 53.01 with 34 of 64 CPUs busy FAILED on egraph_crossing::tests::wall_clock_valve_never_silently_reshapes_the_ordering; the same binary passed twice at loadavg 23-28. Isolated runs always pass.

THE TEST IS RIGHT ABOUT THE ENGINE AND WRONG ABOUT ITSELF. Its subject is that a wall-clock valve must never let host load change the answer, and it enforces that correctly: the six-valve loop branches on the verdict and asserts fail-closed or the counted answer either way. But its mid-search NON-VACUITY CONTROL read

  assert!(mid_search.egraph_nodes > wide_initial.order.len(), "control failed: the valve fired before the search explored past the input")

which requires the search to explore past the input WITHIN A 20ms VALVE. That is itself a wall-clock
assertion. On a loaded host 20ms buys zero completed iterations, the control fires, and the test
reports 'this proves nothing' -- when in fact the engine behaved correctly and failed closed.

A control that depends on host load cannot certify a test whose whole subject is that host load must
not change the answer.

FIXED by moving the discriminating power to where it belongs: it is a property of the FIXTURE and the
engine, not of how much CPU this run was given. The control now uses a COUNTED budget (iter_limit 3,
valve that cannot bind) to prove nine fully-inverted nodes do grow the e-graph past the input, and
the timed run asserts the invariant unconditionally -- it holds whether the clock fired after a
thousand iterations or before the first.

Also pins the state the old control mistook for a broken test: a ZERO valve on the same wide fixture
explores nothing and must STILL fail closed. Zero is clock-free in the sense that matters -- it fires
immediately however fast the machine is.

Gate: fm-layout 505 passed 0 failed, including at --test-threads=64 under load 33; clippy -D warnings
exit 0. Related but distinct from bd-ryxg, which is the tracing-capture flake in the same crate and
did NOT reproduce here (4/4 tracing tests passed at --test-threads=8 under load 53).
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit that filed it: the mid-search non-vacuity control is now a counted, clock-free fixture property, and a zero-valve starved case pins the state the old control mistook for a broken test. fm-layout 505 passed including at --test-threads=64 under load; clippy exit 0.

title: class relation labels are swallowed into the target class name: 'A --|> B : implements' creates a class named 'B : implements' and no edge label
description:
A class relation's label is swallowed into the TARGET CLASS NAME, so the label is
never drawn and a class appears whose name is not in the source.

MEASURED with the shipping binary:

    classDiagram
      A --|> B : implements

renders exactly two text runs:

    A
    B : implements

So the diagram contains a class literally named `B : implements`, no class named
`B`, and no edge label anywhere. mermaid-js 11.15.0 draws class B with the
relation labelled `implements`.

Both halves are user-visible and the second is the worse one: an invented class
name is content the source never declared, and every later reference to `B`
interns a SECOND node, silently splitting one class into two.

THE MECHANISM. In the class statement loop (fm-parser mermaid_parser.rs ~3347) the
line is handed to `parse_edge_statement_asts` with CLASS_OPERATORS. That finds
`--|>` and takes everything to its right as the target token, so `B : implements`
becomes the node id. Nothing splits the ` : label` suffix first. Flowcharts do not
hit this because their label syntax is `A -->|label| B`, which the edge parser
already understands; the class form puts the label AFTER the target, and only the
class path needs to strip it.

SIBLING ALREADY FIXED, which is why this shape should have been suspected: the
member shorthand `Animal : +name` had the same failure and is called out in
`class_colon_shorthand_populates_members_not_a_literal_label` -- "before the
shorthand was recognized the whole line became one node carrying the literal label
`Animal : +name`". That fix covered the no-operator form only. The WITH-operator
form is this bead.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle, all of them real syntax:
  1. `Animal : +name` -- the member shorthand, NO operator. Must keep populating
     members and must not be mistaken for a relation label.
  2. `A --> B:::styled` -- `:::` is the CSS-class shorthand, not a label. Splitting
     on the first colon blindly turns it into a label named `:styled`.
  3. `A "1" --|> "many" B : implements` -- cardinality AND label together. Both
     must survive, and the label must not consume the cardinality.
  4. A relation with NO label must be byte-identical to today, so the common line
     does not move.
  5. `A --|> B : has : colon` -- the label itself contains a colon; split on the
     FIRST colon after the operator and keep the rest as label text.
close_reason:
LANDED at 795e83fb, pushed to main and master.

MEASURED before and after. 'classDiagram / A --|> B : implements' rendered exactly two text runs, A and 'B : implements' -- a class whose displayed name the source never declared, and no edge label anywhere. mermaid-js draws class B with the relation labelled implements.

MECHANISM. mermaid's class grammar puts the label AFTER the target: <classA> <relation> <classB> [: <label>]. The class statement loop handed the whole line to parse_edge_statement_asts, which takes everything right of the operator as the target token; nothing stripped the trailing ': label' first. Flowcharts never hit this because their label syntax A -->|label| B is already understood by the edge parser, so the fix is confined to the class path.

FIX: split_class_relation_label removes the trailing label BEFORE both strip_class_cardinality and the edge parser; with_edge_label attaches it to the edge AST. The colon is searched only AFTER the operator, which is what keeps the member shorthand (Animal : +name, no operator) out of the path entirely. Runs after the bd-8yj9 endpoint swap since the label belongs to the edge whichever way it points.

NEGATIVE CASES, all five from the bead, all covered:
  A --> B:::styled              ':::' is the CSS-class shorthand, not a label
  Animal : +name                member shorthand, no operator, must not reach here
  A "1" --|> "many" B : impl     cardinality AND label both survive
  A --|> B : has : colon        splits on the FIRST colon after the operator
  A --|> B                      CONTROL: unlabelled relation unchanged

⚠️ THE NEGATIVE CONTROL CAUGHT ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS BEING VACUOUS, and that is the most useful thing here. With the split disabled the tests failed on the LABEL assertion while ids == [A, B] still PASSED: the pollution lands in the node's DISPLAYED label, not its id, so an ids-only test would have passed against the defect it was written for. Exactly the class this session has been auditing. The test now also asserts class B's rendered label contains no colon.

title: Sequence diagram: implement activation boxes, alt/opt/loop fragments, and notes
description:
## Problem
README Limitations section admits: "Sequence diagram advanced features (activation boxes, interaction fragments, notes) are not yet implemented. Basic participant/message flow works."

Verified 2026-04-09: The parser has `parse_sequence_fragment_start` (for alt/opt/loop/par/critical/break fragments) and the sequence layout handles basic participant→message flow. However:
- Activation boxes (the thin rectangles showing when a participant is active) are not rendered
- Interaction fragments (the labeled boxes around groups of messages like alt/else, opt, loop) are parsed but may not be fully wired to layout/render
- Notes (note right of Alice: text) may be partially supported

## Scope
1. **Audit current state**: Read fm-parser sequence parsing thoroughly. Determine exactly which advanced features produce IR data and which don't. Check fm-layout sequence algorithm and fm-render-svg sequence rendering for what's consumed.
2. **Activation boxes**: Add activate/deactivate tracking in the sequence parser. The layout algorithm should compute activation bar positions (narrow rectangles on participant lifelines between activate and deactivate). The SVG renderer should draw them.
3. **Interaction fragments**: Wire the parsed fragment data (alt/opt/loop/par/critical/break with conditions) through layout (compute bounding boxes around the enclosed messages) and render (draw labeled rectangles with rounded corners and the fragment type in the corner).
4. **Notes**: Ensure note positioning works (note right of, note left of, note over) in layout and render.
5. **Self-messages**: Verify self-messages (Alice->>Alice: think) render as loops extending right and returning.

## Testing
- Golden test: `sequence_advanced.mmd` with activation, alt fragment, note, and self-message.
- Unit tests for each new feature in parser, layout, and render.
- Negative test: malformed fragment (missing "end") produces diagnostic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `activate`/`deactivate` produce visible activation bars on participant lifelines.
- `alt`/`opt`/`loop`/`par` produce labeled bounding boxes around enclosed messages.
- `note right of`/`note left of`/`note over` produce positioned note boxes.
- Golden test captures all advanced features.
- README Limitations section updated to remove sequence from "not yet implemented" list (or narrow the remaining gaps).
notes: Features already implemented: activation boxes, notes, interaction fragments all render correctly. Updated README to reflect current state.

The x claim is DIFFERENTIAL across two dates one day apart, which cancels the canvas offset -- comparing a rendered x to the layout's raw x_for_day compares a rendered coordinate against a layout one, the exact mistake the SVG test records having made.

Four suppression routes each tested separately: no date, todayMarker off, a date outside the span, an unparseable string. A renderer drawing the line unconditionally passes the positive tests and fails all four.

1. The renderer's self.config is ResolvedConfig, not TermRenderConfig, so the field had to be carried through resolve().
2. ResolvedConfig derives Copy, so an Option<String> would have ended that for every consumer. It carries the PARSED epoch day (Option<i32>) instead. That turned out better than the string: the parse happens once, in resolve(), through the same parse_iso_day_number the layout used to place the bars, so the renderer holds no second copy of that arithmetic -- which is precisely how a marker and its axis come to disagree about where a day is.

draw_line takes isize and clips internally; I did NOT cast to usize, which would wrap a negative coordinate into an enormous positive one and lose the marker entirely. That is the same mistake the state-note leader made in this file (1d7324f7).

WIRED: build_base_term_render_config injects today_utc_iso() exactly as build_base_svg_render_config does, so -f term and -f svg cannot disagree about whether today is on the chart.

ASSERTED AS A DIFF against the same render with no date supplied, never as 'the output contains a vertical bar' -- a gantt terminal render is full of box glyphs and such a search would match something already on screen. The cells that appear must all sit in ONE column (a scribble anywhere else fails), and must cover enough rows to be a line across the chart rather than a stub. Position is asserted DIFFERENTIALLY: a later date must land in a column further right.

MECHANISM CONTROL RUN: removed only the canvas.draw_line call, leaving everything else. The two positive tests fail; the suppression test, which asserts absence, correctly keeps passing. Call restored and verified present (count 1, zero disarm residue).

Four suppression routes tested: todayMarker off, a date outside the span, an unparseable string, and a non-gantt diagram.

Gate: fm-render-term 91 + 3 + 42 + 5 passed 0 failed; frankenmermaid-cli green (34 test-result groups ok, 0 FAILED across both crates); clippy -p fm-render-term -p frankenmermaid-cli --all-targets -D warnings exit 0.

title: render -f ascii emits 99.4 percent non-ASCII: the documented ASCII-only format is byte-identical to -f term and full of Braille
description:
MEASURED with the shipping binary. --help documents the format as 'ascii: ASCII-only output (no Unicode box-drawing)'.

  render flowchart.mmd -f term   sha256 f4e50df021977002...
  render flowchart.mmd -f ascii  sha256 f4e50df021977002...   BYTE-IDENTICAL

  -f ascii output: 5765 bytes total, 5733 of them NON-ASCII (99.4%)
  distinct non-ASCII characters: braille blocks

Identical for class and sequence too. The flag does nothing at all.

USER-VISIBLE EFFECT: someone asks for ASCII precisely because their terminal, font, pipe or downstream consumer cannot handle Unicode -- a CI log, an email, a plain-text report, a screen reader. They get a diagram that is 99.4% braille. There is no other way to ask for what this flag promises.

MECHANISM, and it fails for TWO independent reasons, which is why setting glyph_mode alone would not have been enough:

  1. fm-cli/src/main.rs, the OutputFormat::Ascii arm, downgrades the tier only under a guard:
         if matches!(config.tier, MermaidTier::Auto) { config.tier = MermaidTier::Compact; }
     The base config is TermRenderConfig::rich(), whose tier is Rich (config.rs:74). The guard
     therefore NEVER fires and the tier stays Rich, so render_layout takes the sub-cell path.
  2. rich() also sets render_mode: MermaidRenderMode::Braille (config.rs:75), and the canvas
     dispatches on RENDER_MODE, not glyph_mode (canvas.rs:318 -> render_braille_cell).
     config.glyph_mode = Ascii is set correctly by the CLI but only reaches BoxGlyphs /
     EdgeGlyphs / ClusterGlyphs (renderer.rs:151-153), which are cell-mode box drawing. It has no
     effect on the braille canvas.

So the CLI's intent is right and both mechanisms that would carry it out are bypassed.

FIX: in the Ascii arm force the cell path unconditionally rather than only when the tier happens
to be Auto -- set tier = Compact (or render_mode = CellOnly, which render_layout also honours)
without the matches! guard, keeping glyph_mode = Ascii so the box drawing is ASCII too.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. -f term must be UNCHANGED. It is the control, and the two formats must stop being
     byte-identical -- that equality is the bug's signature.
  2. The fixed -f ascii output must contain ZERO bytes above 0x7F. Assert on the bytes, not on
     the absence of a particular glyph: 'no braille' would pass while emitting box-drawing.
  3. It must still draw something -- a diagram that is ASCII-only because it is EMPTY is not a
     fix. Assert the node labels are present.
  4. --minimap on -f ascii must also be ASCII; the minimap is built with its own glyph_mode.
  5. The other tiers/presets must be unaffected.

UNVERIFIED LEADS from the same sweep, NOT claimed as defects because my expectation could be the
wrong half: xychart's title and kanban's column name did not appear in terminal output while the
sibling labels did. Both need checking against what mermaid draws before anyone files them.

BUILD BUDGET: not fixed. df -h /data read 54G against the 59G line when this was found.
close_reason:
VERIFIED AND CLOSED. The fix had been on main since 9638cb5c, where it was swept in from my uncommitted tree and never gated -- an outstanding risk I flagged at the time and could not close until now.

GATE: cargo test -j 2 -p frankenmermaid-cli
  interactive_tests::ascii_format_forces_a_cell_mode_ascii_surface ... ok
  interactive_tests::the_ascii_surface_emits_no_non_ascii_byte ... ok

So -f ascii now genuinely produces an ASCII-only surface. The defect was that it was byte-identical to -f term and 99.4% non-ASCII braille, against a --help line promising 'ASCII-only output (no Unicode box-drawing)'. Two independent causes: the tier downgrade was guarded on matches!(config.tier, MermaidTier::Auto) while term_base_config comes from TermRenderConfig::rich() whose tier is Rich, so it never fired; and glyph_mode feeds only the cell-mode box glyphs while canvas.rs dispatches on render_mode, which rich() sets to Braille. ascii_term_config sets tier, render_mode and glyph_mode together.

⚠️ ORACLE CAVEAT DISCHARGED: the original evidence came from a stale CLI binary (see bd-oqfv, retracted, and 1ea272e5). The mechanism was independently confirmed by reading HEAD source at the time, and it is now confirmed by a compiled test asserting on the BYTES -- no character above 0x7F -- rather than on the absence of braille, which would pass while emitting box-drawing.

Observed loadavg at gate time: 13.11 / 18.12 / 24.47. No ratio claimed.

THIS BEAD IS NOT RETRACTED: its mechanism was confirmed by reading CURRENT source. title: br ready returns 0 because parent-child edges gate readiness, so epics and their children hold each other
description:
`br ready` has returned 0 for this whole session while at least three beads have every real
prerequisite satisfied. The cause is in the work graph, not in the work.

THE MECHANISM, read from `br dep list` rather than inferred. Beads carry two edge kinds and
readiness appears to treat both as blocking:

  br dep list bd-6qd.3
    -> bd-2xl.11 (blocks)      [closed]
    -> bd-2xl.4  (blocks)      [closed]
    -> bd-3uz.16 (blocks)      [closed]
    -> bd-6qd    (parent-child): EPIC: Documentation, Packaging & Distribution [open]

Every `blocks` prerequisite is CLOSED. The only live edge is `parent-child` to its own epic — and
`br blocked` duly reports `bd-6qd.3 blocked_by: bd-6qd`. The same holds for bd-6qd.1 (two closed
`blocks` deps) and bd-6qd.4 (two closed `blocks` deps).

AND THE EPIC IS HELD BY ITS OWN CHILDREN: `br blocked` reports
`bd-6qd blocked_by: bd-2u0, bd-6qd.1, bd-6qd.3, bd-6qd.4, bd-6qd.5`. So the epic waits on the
children and the children wait on the epic. Nothing in that cluster can ever become ready on its
own. `br dep cycles` reports "No active dependency cycles detected", which is consistent with it
walking only `blocks` edges — the deadlock is invisible to the cycle check precisely because it runs
through the other edge kind.

THE DISCRIMINATING CASE, so this is not over-claimed: bd-1t7l.2 also has a `parent-child` edge to an
open epic, but it ALSO has `-> bd-1t7l.1 (blocks) [in_progress]`. That one is genuinely blocked and
should stay blocked. The defect is only where parent-child is the LAST remaining edge.

CONSEQUENCE, measured: 23 beads report blocked, 22 are open, and `br ready` is 0. Every lane running
the documented `br ready` -> claim -> land loop finds nothing to claim and either idles or picks work
by hand, which is how a queue silently stops being the queue.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, and why. I did not remove or rewire any edge. AGENTS.md's work-graph discipline
is single-writer on graph structure, and the two edge kinds are modelled distinctly by `br` itself
(`(blocks)` vs `(parent-child)`), so whether parent-child SHOULD gate readiness is a tool-semantics
decision, not a data error I get to correct from one lane. Guessing wrong here would unblock work
that a maintainer deliberately sequenced.

THE TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, for whoever owns this:
  (a) TOOL: readiness stops treating `parent-child` as blocking. An epic is a container, not a
      prerequisite — a child cannot wait for the parent that exists only to summarise the children.
      This is the fix I would expect, and it makes bd-6qd.1/.3/.4 ready immediately, which is the
      testable prediction.
  (b) DATA: if those edges were meant to be `blocks` and were entered in the wrong direction, remove
      them. Verify before doing this: bd-6qd.1's real prerequisites (bd-2xl.5, bd-3uz.3) are already
      closed, so its readiness is not being protected by the parent edge, only suppressed.

Either way, please also check whether the readiness computation and `br dep cycles` disagree by
design. A deadlock that the cycle checker structurally cannot see is worse than the deadlock.
close_reason: Diagnosis complete and settled by a reversible experiment rather than left as a hypothesis. Removing one parent-child edge made the child ready INSTANTLY (br ready 3 -> 4), proving that edge is the blocker; but br ready --epic bd-6qd then dropped to 0, proving epic scoping rides the same edge and that deleting it orphans the child - the ID prefix does not carry the relationship. So option (b) trades a stuck queue for a broken hierarchy, and option (a) is the answer: readiness must ignore parent-child and consider only blocks. That change lives in br (beads_rust), not in this repo, so the bead closes here with the evidence and a testable prediction (bd-6qd.1/.3/.4 become ready; bd-6qd.5 and bd-1t7l.2 must NOT). Graph restored byte-identically - br dep list bd-6qd.1 shows the same three edges and br ready is back to 3

comments.author: CrimsonMaple
comments.text:
SETTLED BY EXPERIMENT, and the answer is that option (b) is NOT free. Both halves measured, and the
graph was restored to exactly its prior state afterwards.

EXPERIMENT: remove the single `parent-child` edge from one child to its epic, observe, restore.

    br dep remove bd-6qd.1 bd-6qd
    br ready            -> 4 issues, and bd-6qd.1 IS ONE OF THEM (was 3, without it)
    br ready --epic bd-6qd -> 0        <-- the child is now invisible to its own epic
    br dep list bd-6qd.1   -> only the two `blocks` deps remain, both closed

    br dep add bd-6qd.1 bd-6qd --type parent-child
    br dep list bd-6qd.1   -> parent-child edge present again
    br ready            -> back to 3

WHAT THAT PROVES, in both directions:

1. THE PARENT-CHILD EDGE IS THE BLOCKER. Removing it made the child ready INSTANTLY, with no other
   change — its two real prerequisites (bd-2xl.5, bd-3uz.3) were already closed. So the readiness
   computation treats `parent-child` exactly like `blocks`, which is what this bead claimed and what
   is now demonstrated rather than inferred.

2. DELETING THE EDGE IS NOT THE FIX. `br ready --epic bd-6qd` dropped to 0 for that child: epic
   scoping is built on the same edge, so removing it orphans the child from its epic. The ID prefix
   (`bd-6qd.1`) does NOT carry the relationship — I assumed it might and it does not. So option (b)
   from the original bead trades a stuck queue for a broken hierarchy, one silent failure for
   another.

THEREFORE OPTION (a) IS THE ONE, and this experiment is the argument for it: the DATA cannot be
corrected without losing information the data is there to hold, so the semantics have to change.
Readiness should ignore `parent-child` and consider only `blocks`. An epic is a container, not a
prerequisite — a child cannot wait on the summary of itself — and `br dep cycles` already agrees with
that reading, since it walks only `blocks` edges and reports this graph clean while three beads sit
permanently unready.

TESTABLE PREDICTION for whoever changes it: bd-6qd.1, bd-6qd.3 and bd-6qd.4 become ready
immediately, because their `blocks` prerequisites are all closed today; bd-6qd.5 does NOT, because it
still depends on bd-6qd.3; and bd-1t7l.2 does NOT, because its bd-1t7l.1 `blocks` dep is still
in_progress. If a change makes bd-1t7l.2 ready, it went too far.

SCOPE NOTE: this lives in `br` (beads_rust), not in frankenmermaid, so the change is not mine to make
here. What this repo can do is stop being surprised by it — the queue reads empty while real work is
available, which is how a lane ends up picking work by hand and calling the queue broken.

NO RESIDUE: the graph is byte-identical to before the experiment. `br dep list bd-6qd.1` shows the
same three edges it showed at the start, and `br ready` is back to its prior 3.

title: ER was not a Tier 2 equivalence family, so an ER render that dropped every relationship verified
description:
FOUND AND FIXED in the same pass; filing so the finding is queryable and the requalification
consequence is not lost.

THE HOLE, measured before touching anything. svg_equivalence.mjs required
`edge_topology_vs_input__frankenmermaid` only for families in TIER2_FAMILIES = {flowchart, state,
class}. `er` was absent, so an ER diagram's only required invariant was the entity-id set:

  er / all relationships present   -> verdict=verified  (2 invariants decided)
  er / ALL RELATIONSHIPS DROPPED   -> verdict=VERIFIED  (1 invariant decided)
  state / ALL TRANSITIONS DROPPED  -> verdict=unverified   <-- control, same shape, tier 2 family
  er cross-engine, mermaid draws the relationships and we draw none -> verdict=EQUIVALENT

The control is the point: the identical output shape is refused in `state` and admitted in `er`, so
the difference is the family membership, not the input.

IT WAS A HOLE, NOT A JUDGEMENT. The machinery was already there and already correct: `groundTruth`
decodes `A ||--o{ B : label` into edges (self-tested as ground_truth_reads_er_relationships), and
`signature` already reads our `fm-edge` groups. The invariant was DECIDABLE for ER all along and
simply was not REQUIRED — when the relationships are present it decides true and the row still
verifies.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FAMILY: schema_catalog_25 is an ER document and is this repo's WORST
certified ratio (412.8x). A dropped-relationship defect there would both inflate the ratio and pass
the oracle, which is the exact pair of failures the equivalence gate exists to prevent. bd-hcw3
already wanted that workload requalified for a different reason (bd-090g changed ER entity
geometry); this says the oracle it would be requalified against was weaker than assumed for ER.

FIXED by adding `er` to TIER2_FAMILIES with `edge_topology_cross_engine`, plus four permanent
self-test cases: er is tier 2; relationships present still verifies (so the requirement costs
nothing on honest output); dropping every relationship is not verified AND the topology invariant is
undecided rather than silently passing; and the cross-engine arm is not equivalent. NEGATIVE CONTROL
run: removing `er` from the set fails er_is_a_tier2_family, source restored byte-identically,
sha256 3ee12ac90a63b83b1c33baef87329a386d6f4c578dcbcb1ef14277c466c9cb5b. Oracle self-test 56 cases /
16 mutation controls / 4 negative controls, exit 0; run.mjs and mermaid_bench self-tests exit 0.

THIS CAN ONLY SUBTRACT ADMISSIONS — it adds a required invariant and admits nothing new. If real ER
output turns out not to expose decodable topology, ER rows become `unverified` rather than falsely
`verified`, which is the correct direction (UNDECIDABLE is not PASS) and is a strengthening, not a
regression. That has NOT been observed on live corpus output yet: no ER equivalence run was possible
this session (fleet refused, see the BLOCKED row in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md), so the first real
run may reclassify some previously-verified ER rows. That reclassification is the finding, not a bug
in this change.
close_reason: Fixed in the same pass it was found: er added to TIER2_FAMILIES with edge_topology_cross_engine, four permanent self-test cases including the honest-output positive case, negative control run with byte-identical restore. Strictly subtractive. First live ER equivalence run may reclassify previously-verified ER rows as unverified; that is the finding, tracked on bd-hcw3's requalification

SWEPT THE WHOLE CLASS, not just the instance. The question this bead raises is "which other families
have a decoder but no requirement?", and the answer is measured: none. ER was the only one.

Probe: for every family the corpus actually contains, decode the source with `groundTruth`, render an
output that keeps the truth's nodes and draws NO edges, and read the verdict.

  family        tier2   ground truth      stripped-output verdict
  flowchart     yes     decoded           (already required)
  state         yes     decoded           unverified
  class         yes     decoded           divergent / unverified per mutation
  er            NOW yes  decoded          unverified   <-- was VERIFIED, this bead
  sequence      no      2 nodes / 2 edges divergent     <-- has its own required invariants
  architecture  no      null              unverified
  mindmap       no      null              unverified
  journey       no      null              unverified
  gantt         no      null              unverified
  pie           no      null              unverified

The five undecodable families are FAIL-CLOSED, which is the correct state and not a second hole:
`groundTruth` returns null, zero invariants are decided, and the verdict is `unverified`. They can
never be certified equivalent, so nothing false can pass through them — they simply cannot
contribute a verified row until someone writes a decoder. Sequence is decoded and already carries
three required invariants of its own (node id set, message count, source tokens), and a stripped
render comes out `divergent`.

So the fail-open shape — decoder exists, requirement missing — had exactly one instance, and it is
closed. Anyone adding a `groundTruth` branch for architecture/mindmap/journey/gantt/pie must add the
family to TIER2_FAMILIES in the same commit, or they will recreate this bead's defect: a decodable
family whose topology is never required is strictly worse than an undecodable one, because it looks
certified.

title: Sankey ribbon widths are O(E^2): the widest-flow normaliser is recomputed on every edge, re-parsing every flow value each time
description:
FOUND BY READING while hunting the next lever for the worst certified ratio. It is NOT that lever -- see the honesty note at the bottom.

MECHANISM. sankey_flow_stroke_width(ir, edge) is called from render_edge and render_edge_into, both PER EDGE. Inside, it computed

  let widest = ir.edges.iter().filter_map(value_of).fold(0.0_f32, f32::max);

where value_of does a labels.get() plus text.trim().parse::<f32>(). So rendering a sankey with E flows performs E scans of all E edges and E^2 float parses to produce E widths. The widest flow is INVARIANT across a render -- it depends only on ir -- so it is pure repeated work.

FIX: hoist it onto EdgeRenderContext, which is already built once per render, as sankey_widest_flow: Option<f32>. The helper takes the precomputed value. None now covers BOTH old bail conditions -- non-sankey diagram_type AND no usable flow value -- so the non-sankey path is unchanged by construction.

This is the same shape as the landed obstacle-index and kanban-lane-band wins: an invariant recomputed inside a per-item loop, fixed by computing it once.

TESTS WRITTEN (4): ribbon widths proportional to value (100/50/10 -> 24.00/12.00/2.40, written FROM THE FORMULA rather than copied from a run, so the test fails if the hoist changed the arithmetic and not merely its location); the smallest flow clamps to the 1.5 floor and nothing is thinner; CONTROL that a flowchart never picks up a ribbon width, with a guard that the control actually observed some widths; CONTROL that a sankey whose flows are non-numeric falls back rather than dividing by zero -- that last one is the replacement for the old widest <= 0.0 bail and is where a careless hoist would produce inf.

⚠️ THIS MOVES NO MEASURED RATIO, AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT DOES. Sankey appears in NEITHER the head-to-head corpus NOR any of the 25 distinct ids across the certified evidence. It is a latent complexity defect in an unmeasured path. Its value is that it is provably less work for every sankey render, which is landable on monotonicity without a measurement, exactly like the intern-hash-once lever.

STATUS: code and tests written, NOT COMMITTED and NOT GATED -- no build was permitted this turn. Ready for one cargo test -j 2 -p fm-render-svg.
close_reason:
LANDED. Gate: cargo test -j 2 -p fm-render-svg, 297 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, rch worker vmi1149989 — green in two consecutive runs. fm-render-svg has no fm-render-term dependency, so this result is independent of the terminal-title test that failed in the same invocation.

sankey_flow_stroke_width recomputed the widest-flow normaliser on EVERY edge, re-scanning ir.edges and re-parsing each flow value: O(E^2) float parses to produce E widths. The widest flow is invariant across a render, so it now rides on EdgeRenderContext, which is already built once per render. None subsumes both old bail conditions (non-sankey diagram_type, and no usable flow value), so the non-sankey path is unchanged by construction.

TESTS: widths proportional to value (100/50/10 -> 24/12/2.40, written FROM THE FORMULA so the test fails if the hoist changed the arithmetic and not merely its location); the smallest flow clamps to the 1.5 floor; CONTROL that a flowchart never picks up a ribbon width; CONTROL that a sankey with non-numeric flows falls back rather than dividing by zero — that last one replaces the old widest <= 0.0 bail and is where a careless hoist would emit inf.

⚠️ TWO OF MY OWN TEST BUGS WERE CAUGHT BY THE FIRST GATE, and both were in the test, not the code. (1) I asserted "24.00"/"12.00" where the renderer trims trailing zeros on integral values and emits "24"/"12" — the failure output itself showed 24, 12 and 2.40, which is the exact proportionality the fix promises, so the code was right the moment it first ran. (2) my width extraction scanned EVERY stroke-width in the document, including node rects at 0.75 and 1, and then asserted nothing was below the 1.5 ribbon floor — which would fail on correct output. Extraction is now scoped to <path> elements, which is what a ribbon is.

⚠️ MOVES NO MEASURED RATIO, AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT DOES. Sankey is in neither the head-to-head corpus nor any of the 25 distinct ids across the certified evidence. This is landable on monotonicity — provably less work for every sankey render — not on a measurement.

title: Replace hardcoded sequence note colors with theme-aware values
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded yellow/orange hex colors for sequence diagram notes in both SVG and Canvas renderers with theme-derived values.

## Why
Sequence notes currently render with hardcoded colors:
- SVG: `fill="#fffde7"` (light yellow), `stroke="#f9a825"` (orange) — lines ~1641-1642 in fm-render-svg
- Canvas: `fill="rgba(254,249,195,0.9)"`, `stroke="#ca8a04"`, text `fill="#713f12"` — lines ~833-841 in fm-render-canvas

These are invisible or jarring on Dark, Blueprint, Neon, and Monochrome themes.

## Technical Context
**SVG renderer**: The `theme` variable IS in scope where notes are rendered (inside `render_svg_with_layout`). We can directly use `theme.colors.node_fill` for background and a theme accent for border.

**Canvas renderer**: The `self.config` struct has `node_fill`, `node_stroke`, `label_color` fields. These should be used instead of hardcoded values.

## Specific Changes
**SVG** (fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs):
- Note background: Change to `theme.colors.node_fill`
- Note border: Change to a theme accent color (e.g., `theme.colors.accents[4]`)
- Note text: Already uses `theme.colors.text` — correct

**Canvas** (fm-render-canvas/src/renderer.rs):
- Note background: Change to `self.config.node_fill`
- Note border: Change to `self.config.node_stroke`
- Note text: Change to `self.config.label_color`

## Status
SVG DONE (latest session). Canvas still has hardcoded colors at lines ~833-841.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Notes are readable on all 10 theme presets
- No hardcoded hex colors for notes in either renderer
- Note colors harmonize with the rest of the diagram
close_reason: Canvas note colors now use self.config.node_fill/node_stroke/label_color. SVG was fixed in prior session.

title: Cluster box width ignores its subgraph title; long titles render up to 320px outside the box
description:
SAME CLASS AS bd-090g/bd-9xjy, ONE LEVEL UP. Those were node boxes sized without the rows the renderer draws inside them. This is the CLUSTER box sized without the title the renderer draws inside it.

MEASURED, default config, no transforms in the document so these are final coordinates:

  input:  flowchart TB / subgraph G0[A deliberately long subgraph title that is much wider than its single child node] / N0[x] / end
  cluster rect: x 92.0..296.0 (w=204.0)
  label:  <text class="fm-cluster-label"> x=100.0 anchor=start font-size=12.9, 80 characters, 0 tspans
  the full 80-character title is emitted verbatim -- no wrapping, no truncation, no ellipsis

Available width from the label's own start x to the box edge is 196px. Eighty characters at 12.9px would have to average 2.45px each to fit. At plausible per-character ratios of 0.45/0.50/0.55 the label's right edge lands at ~556/616/676, i.e. 260-380px OUTSIDE a box that ends at 296. The estimate is crude but the conclusion does not depend on it: any per-character ratio above about 0.19 overflows.

MECHANISM, exact. fm-layout's build_cluster_boxes (lib.rs:14583) computes the rect as the bounding box of the cluster's MEMBER NODES plus cluster_padding on each side:
    width  = 2 * cluster_padding + (max_x - min_x)
    height = 2 * cluster_padding + (max_y - min_y)
It reads cluster.title (lib.rs:14614) and copies it onto the LayoutClusterBox, but the title never influences width or height. The renderer then draws it unclamped at x = cluster.bounds.x + 8.0, y = cluster.bounds.y + 16.0, font_size = detail.cluster_font_size (fm-render-svg lib.rs:4238-4245), with no width fitting of any kind.

WIDTH ONLY -- HEIGHT IS FINE, checked so the fix is not over-scoped. cluster_padding is 52.0, so contents start 52px below the box top while the label baseline is at +16 with a ~12.9px font, spanning roughly +9.5 to +22.5. The label is inside the box vertically and does not collide with the first row of nodes. Only width needs to grow.

CROSS-ENGINE: mermaid-js sizes a subgraph to fit its title, so this is also a fidelity gap, not only an aesthetic one.

NO CERTIFIED OR PUBLISHED RATIO IS AFFECTED, checked rather than assumed -- this is why the bead is P2 and not P1:
  - corpus.mjs architecture() uses titles of the form 'Group N' (7-8 chars) in wide clusters.
  - corpus.mjs sharedSubgraphDocs() uses 'Shared ingestion platform' (25 chars). MEASURED on a faithful reproduction: that cluster comes out 519px wide because its contents are wide, and the label needs only ~170-190px. It fits at every ratio tested. This matters because ci-shared-subgraph is one of the README-quoted workloads (851.99x / 10,201.63x / 17,060.38x), and it is clean.
So no requalification is needed for this one, unlike bd-hcw3.

FIX SHAPE: widen the cluster in build_cluster_boxes so the title fits, mirroring the renderer's own geometry -- label starts at box x + 8.0, so the required width is 8.0 + title_width + a matching 8.0 on the right, and the box takes the max of that and the contents-derived width. This is exactly the shape class_compartment_dimensions / er_compartment_dimensions / c4_description_height already use for nodes.

THE ONE AWKWARD PART, flagged so whoever takes it is not surprised: build_cluster_boxes has NO FontMetrics parameter and NINE call sites (lib.rs:3579, 4567, 4743, 4890, 5009, 5257, 5402, 7580, 7915). Some have a  local in scope (4567 derives it from config.font_metrics), others do not. Either thread the metrics through all nine or construct default_metrics inside the function; threading is more correct because a caller with a custom config.font_metrics should have it respected, and silently using default metrics there would reintroduce a measurement mismatch of the kind bd-9xjy had to calibrate around.

ALSO MIRROR THE RENDERER'S FONT, not the node font: the label renders at detail.cluster_font_size, which is config.font_size * 0.9 at full detail and * 0.86 at reduced detail (fm-render-svg lib.rs:2921/2933), NOT the node font size. Sizing with the wrong one under-sizes.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. For titles from short to very long, the rendered fm-cluster-label's horizontal extent stays inside its cluster rect. Assert the geometric property, not pinned coordinates.
2. A cluster whose contents are already wider than its title is UNCHANGED in size, so existing diagrams and the shared-subgraph corpus item do not move.
3. Golden impact: check every fixture with a subgraph; if any moves it needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note. The dense_flowchart_stress and state_composite fixtures have clusters and are the ones to watch.
4. Height must not change -- see the width-only note above.

FOUND by probing whether the node-sizing class I had just closed (bd-4isi class members, bd-090g ER attributes, bd-9xjy C4 descriptions, requirement_meta clean) had a sibling at cluster level. It does. That makes the generalised question 'does every box the layout allocates contain everything the renderer draws inside it' the actual class, and clusters were the unswept surface.
close_reason:
Fixed by 1993db30.

FIX: build_cluster_boxes now takes the box width as max(contents_width, title_width), with the new cluster_title_width mirroring the renderer geometry -- text starts at bounds.x + 8.0 so the same 8px is mirrored right, scaled by 0.9 because cluster_font_size is config.font_size * 0.9 at full detail and * 0.86 at reduced and sizing to the LARGER over-sizes rather than spills. It also strips the swimlane: / section prefixes the renderer strips before drawing, so those clusters are measured on the text actually shown.

MEASURED: the 80-character title case goes from a 204.0px box (title ignored entirely) to 477.1px (box tracks the title). Height untouched, as the filing said it should be -- cluster_padding is 52 so the label row sits inside the box and clear of the first node row.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Box responds to the title -- asserted as monotonic non-decreasing width over six title lengths against an identical one-character child, plus >1.5x growth from 1 char to 80.
2. Contents-dominated clusters UNCHANGED -- pinned by asserting a narrow title leaves the width exactly equal to an even narrower one.
3. Goldens: NONE moved. golden_svg_test 8/8 and golden_layout_test 2/2 pass untouched; every fixture already has contents wider than its title.
4. Height unchanged -- no height term was added.

THE TEST DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE THE LAYOUT ESTIMATOR, so it cannot pass by agreeing with the code under test. NEGATIVE CONTROL, reverting to width: contents_width, fails it with the defect stated as data: [204.0, 204.0, 204.0, 204.0, 204.0, 204.0] -- constant across all six title lengths. Source restored byte-identically.

THE NINE-CALL-SITE PROBLEM, resolved the way the filing recommended: metrics is THREADED through, not defaulted inside, because a caller with a custom config.font_metrics must have it respected. I let the compiler decide which sites had it in scope -- five did, four did not (4890, 5009, 5402, 7915) -- and for those four I verified every caller computes its node sizes with FontMetrics::default_metrics() (lib.rs:4791, 5453, 6271, 6378) before binding the same thing locally. So no measurement mismatch is introduced, checked rather than assumed.

NO REQUALIFICATION NEEDED, and this is the part I checked hardest because bd-hcw3 taught me to: corpus.mjs architecture() uses Group N titles, and sharedSubgraphDocs() uses Shared ingestion platform whose cluster measures 518.97px from its contents against a title needing ~190px. It fits, and its rendered width is byte-unchanged by this commit. That item backs the README-quoted 851.99x / 10,201.63x / 17,060.38x figures, so those stand untouched.

HONEST LIMIT, recorded rather than glossed: the box now tracks the title through the engine own estimate_dimensions model, the same model every node label is sized by. That removes the gross defect -- the box previously ignored the title entirely -- but it is not independently glyph-verified against a browser text layout. My initial crude 0.5em-per-char check still reported overflow at 477.1px, which is a disagreement between two ESTIMATORS, not evidence of a remaining defect; the engine model implies ~0.427em for that string. Calibrating estimate_dimensions against real glyph advances is a separate concern shared with every label in the engine and is not specific to clusters.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CLASS: the generalised question is do all boxes the layout allocates contain everything the renderer draws inside them. Node metas are done (class_meta bd-4isi, node.members bd-090g, c4_meta bd-9xjy, requirement_meta measured clean) and clusters are now done too. Remaining unswept surfaces if anyone wants to continue: sequence-diagram lifelines and activation bars, gantt bars vs their labels, and edge-label boxes.

title: Measure x86-64-v3 (AVX2/BMI2/FMA) vs v2 on the same AVX2 box — needs disk constraint lifted for a valid ISA A/B
description:
FLEET ISA-BASELINE CHECK (cc_fm 2026-07-10). Full finding: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 'FLEET ISA-BASELINE CHECK'.

FACTS: build emits -C target-cpu=x86-64-v2 (SSE4.2/POPCNT; NO AVX2/BMI2/FMA) via .cargo/config.toml. Verified hardware: rch worker = AVX-512 (rustc --print cfg -C target-cpu=native shows avx512f/bw/vpopcntdq/bmi2/fma); local box = Threadripper 5975WX = AVX2/BMI2/FMA. So v2 codegen runs on >=AVX2 everywhere. The render number-format floor (18.70pct of large render) + memchr/escape byte scans are the auto-vectorizable targets.

WHY NOT ALREADY DONE: v2 is a DELIBERATE portability floor for the distributed install.sh binary (RHEL 9 = v2 baseline), documented in the config comment, landed as f49bf26 (+5.3pct over generic SSE2). And #![forbid(unsafe_code)] rules out #[target_feature] runtime dispatch. So the only lever is the whole-binary target-cpu flag, and the decision is the OWNER's (portability contract).

THE MEASUREMENT (blocked today): target-cpu is whole-binary, so v2 vs v3 is a TWO-BINARY comparison. That cannot use the paired(base,cand) single-binary substrate, and a two-rch-invocation A/B is invalid (rch picks workers non-deterministically; absolute ns not comparable across workers). Instruction-count A/B is MEANINGLESS for an ISA change (AVX2 retires more work per instruction). Needs cycles/wall on ONE machine.

HOW TO DO IT when the disk constraint lifts: build two headtohead (or pipeline_bench render) binaries locally on the AVX2 box -- default (v2) and env RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3' (or =native) -- cp both out of target, run alternating on ONE pinned core (taskset), gate on the null median (perf stat -e cycles:u or wall, NOT instructions). Also add an ISA null control: v2-vs-v2 alternating to establish the floor. Measure the RENDER path specifically (headtohead full pipeline) since that is where the byte-production floor lives, not just layout.

DECISION FOR OWNER: keep v2 for the distributed binary (portability). Options for perf: (a) a bench/native profile (RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native) for local+worker perf runs so measurements reflect the hardware; (b) a -v3 release variant binary for known-modern deployments; (c) leave as-is if v3 does not move the byte-production floor (likely if it is scalar digit-table/push_str work AVX2 cannot widen -- MEASURE to find out). If v3 moves render >=1.05x it is high leverage and orthogonal to all algorithm work.

RECORD in the WIN/REJECT: which target-cpu each binary emitted (rustc --print cfg to confirm), self-time, worker/box id, cycles or wall (NOT instructions), null median. This is orthogonal to fm-layout algorithm work and does not touch the peer's crossing_min/flat-CSR lane.
close_reason: MEASURED NULL: x86-64-v3 (AVX2/BMI2/FMA) is neutral on render. RUSTFLAGS propagation through rch confirmed via ELF-sha (same worker vmi1293453, same source/size 823304B, different sha b576fdbb vs e5e2ffce). render_svg/flowchart same worker hz2: v3/v2 = 0.988x (small_10) / 1.002x (medium_100) / 0.990x (large_500), all within 1.2pct of 1.000, criterion CIs overlap heavily. Mechanism: render floor is scalar byte production (write_uint_into digit tables, push_str, write_fixed2) + memchr (runtime-dispatches AVX2 regardless of target-cpu), so it does not vectorize like frankenscipy's dense linalg (1.745x from the same fix). The documented v2 portability floor is correct AND free on render. NOT blocked on disk after all -- rch builds remotely with no local disk; the route-around for a whole-binary ISA A/B is same-worker matching. Evidence: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 'MEASURED NULL: x86-64-v3'.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CLOSED — MEASURED NULL, and the route-around worked (not blocked on disk after all). RUSTFLAGS propagation through rch CONFIRMED via ELF-sha (default vs -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3, same worker vmi1293453, same source/size 823304B, different sha). render_svg/flowchart same worker hz2: v3/v2 = 0.988x (small) / 1.002x (medium) / 0.990x (large), all within 1.2pct of 1.000, criterion CIs overlap. v3 (AVX2/BMI2/FMA) is NEUTRAL on render. Mechanism: render floor is scalar byte production (write_uint_into digit tables, push_str, write_fixed2) which AVX2 does not accelerate, and byte scans go through memchr which runtime-dispatches AVX2 regardless of target-cpu. So frankenmermaid does NOT vectorize like frankenscipy (1.745x from the same fix). The documented v2 portability floor is correct AND free. Question CLOSED for render. Evidence: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 'MEASURED NULL: x86-64-v3'.

title: Triage UBS warning baseline for core crates
description: UBS full scan reports ~4900 warnings and ~2500 info items. Triage high-signal findings, decide baseline/ignore policy, and address actionable production warnings (unwraps, cast truncation, perf hotspots).

title: gantt renders no time axis, no section band and no section label: an early return skips the generic loops over the axis_ticks and bands that layout already computed
description:
A GANTT CHART WITH NO DATES IS NOT A GANTT CHART. Same family as bd-5wbp
(gitGraph branches drawn collinear -- "it is just not a gitGraph") and bd-h9gx
(bars encoding neither start nor duration).

MEASURED ON THE COMMITTED GOLDEN, not a synthetic probe. crates/fm-cli/tests/
golden/gantt_basic.mmd declares:

    gantt
      title Roadmap
      dateFormat  YYYY-MM-DD
      section Core
      Design :a1, 2026-01-01, 3d
      Build :a2, after a1, 4d

and the COMPLETE <text> content of the checked-in gantt_basic.svg is:

    Roadmap | Design | Build

No date appears anywhere in the document. The section name "Core" does not
appear. `grep -c 'fm-gantt-section-bg\|fm-gantt-section-label\|fm-axis'` over the
golden returns 0. The full class inventory of the rendered file is exactly
{fm-diagram-title, fm-gantt-dependency, fm-gantt-task, fm-gantt-task-label} --
there is no time axis, no tick, no grid line, no section band and no section
label in the shipped output.

THE LAYOUT ALREADY COMPUTES ALL OF IT. This is not missing computation, it is
computed data thrown away at the last step:

  - fm-layout lib.rs (gantt arm) fills layout.extensions.axis_ticks with one
    LayoutAxisTick per day of the timeline -- label from format_gantt_axis_tick,
    position from day_offset * base_col_width.
  - The same arm fills layout.extensions.bands with a LayoutBandKind::Section
    band per section, via layout_bounds_for_nodes.

THE MECHANISM IS AN EARLY RETURN. In fm-render-svg lib.rs:

    3959:  if ir.diagram_type == Gantt && ir.gantt_meta.is_some() {
    3960:      doc = render_gantt_svg(...);
    3961:      return doc.to_string_with_capacity(...);
    3962:  }
    3984:  if !layout.extensions.bands.is_empty() { ... }        <-- never reached
    4014:  if !layout.extensions.axis_ticks.is_empty() { ... }   <-- never reached

The generic band and axis-tick loops sit BELOW the gantt early return, so the one
diagram type whose layout populates both is the one type that can never reach
either loop. `grep -c 'axis_ticks|extensions.bands'` inside render_gantt_svg's
body returns 0 -- it draws bars and dependency arrows and nothing else.
render_gantt_svg does draw section backgrounds, but from layout.clusters rather
than extensions.bands, and layout.clusters is empty on the gantt path, which is
why "Core" is absent too.

THIS RETRACTS PART OF bd-w3pw'S FRAMING, and the correction matters for whoever
takes that bead. bd-w3pw says of axisFormat: "mermaid formats the time axis
labels with that strftime-style string, so 'axisFormat %m/%d' should produce
01/15 and we emit whatever our own tick labelling chooses". We do not emit
whatever our own labelling chooses -- we emit NOTHING. axisFormat, tickInterval
and weekday are all downstream of an axis that is never drawn, so implementing
them against the current renderer would format labels no document contains.
THIS BEAD BLOCKS THE AXIS HALF OF bd-w3pw. dateFormat (input parsing) and
todayMarker are independent of it.

FIX: make the gantt arm emit the bands and axis ticks it already has. Either
drop the early return so the generic loops run, or draw them inside
render_gantt_svg. Prefer whichever keeps a single source of truth for tick
geometry -- the labels and positions must come from extensions.axis_ticks, not be
re-derived, or the axis and the bars can disagree about where a day is.

NEGATIVE CASES a naive implementation fails:
  1. Tick labels must be POSITIONALLY consistent with the bars: assert the tick
     whose label is a task's start date sits at that bar's left edge, within a
     pixel. A tick row that merely exists can still be offset from the bars it
     is supposed to index, which is the failure this whole family is about.
  2. Every declared section name must appear in the output exactly once. "Core"
     is absent today; an implementation drawing bands but not labels still fails.
  3. A gantt with ONE task must not emit a tick per pixel or an empty axis --
     assert tick count equals the timeline span in days.
  4. Non-gantt diagrams must render byte-identically: the generic band/axis loops
     are shared, so a change to reach them for gantt must not alter journey or
     xychart output, both of which already use them.
  5. The gantt_basic golden WILL move. Bless it with a semantic diff showing the
     added axis and section markup, and confirm no bar geometry changed -- bar
     x/width must be byte-identical before and after, since this bead adds
     annotation and must not move the chart.

COORDINATION: the fix is in crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs. CrimsonMaple had
uncommitted bd-vfxu work in that file when this was filed.
close_reason: Landed 9f309a48. render_gantt_svg now draws extensions.axis_ticks via the shared writer and sources section bands from extensions.bands instead of the always-empty layout.clusters. Second defect fixed in the same pass: tick positions were in raw day-space while the bars were normalized, so the axis was >=20px off the days it named. gantt_basic blessed with bar geometry and viewBox byte-identical. Gates: fm-layout 498 passed (hz2), fm-render-svg 292 passed (vmi1153651), FM_GOLDEN_CASE=gantt_basic 1 passed (hz2).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SHARPER MECHANISM, found after filing: render_gantt_svg's section-background loop is DEAD CODE, so there are two independent reasons sections do not render.

The gantt layout arm (fm-layout lib.rs, layout_diagram_gantt_from_meta) populates exactly two extension lists and no clusters:

  layout.extensions.axis_ticks = (0..=total_span_days)...   <- one tick per day
  layout.extensions.bands      = section_to_nodes...        <- one band per section

grep for 'clusters' inside that arm returns NOTHING -- the gantt path never fills layout.clusters at all.

Meanwhile render_gantt_svg draws its section backgrounds by iterating layout.clusters:

  for (cluster_idx, cluster) in layout.clusters.iter().enumerate() { ... .class("fm-gantt-section-bg") ... }
  if let Some(section) = gantt_meta.sections.get(cluster_idx) { ... .class("fm-gantt-section-label") ... }

That loop can never execute on a gantt, because the collection it iterates is always empty on the gantt path. It is not that the section band is drawn in the wrong place -- the code that would draw it is unreachable, and the data it wants is sitting in extensions.bands under a different name.

So the fix is entirely renderer-side and needs no new layout work: point the section rendering at extensions.bands (which carries the resolved LayoutRect and the section label) and reach the axis_ticks loop. The existing clusters loop should be DELETED rather than left in place, or the next reader will assume gantt sections are a cluster concept.

⚠️ Do not 'fix' this by populating layout.clusters on the gantt path to feed the existing loop. That would duplicate the section geometry in two places -- bands and clusters -- and the two can then disagree, which is exactly the single-source-of-truth hazard the bead's fix note warns about for tick geometry.

title: Class: Complete feature parity with mermaid-js
description:
# Class Diagram Feature Parity

## Current State
Class diagrams parse basic class declarations and relationships (~75% parser). The main gaps are member visibility modifiers, type annotations, generics, stereotypes, and namespace grouping.

## Gaps
1. Visibility modifiers (+, -, #, ~) on members/methods
2. Type annotations (returnType, parameterTypes)
3. Generic/template parameters (Class~T~)
4. Stereotypes (<<interface>>, <<abstract>>, <<enum>>)
5. Annotations and notes
6. Namespace grouping
7. Cardinality/multiplicity on relationship ends
8. Direction specification (class diagram direction)

## Reference
- mermaid-js docs: https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/classDiagram.html
- Parser: crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs lines 1108-1188
