title: WIN: serialize SVG attrs without fmt::Formatter (render +5-12%)
description: Landed 194cb15. Attributes::write_into used write!(out, ' {}="{}"', name, value) per attribute (thousands per diagram), routing every piece + both Display args through fmt::Formatter. Replaced with direct out.write_char/write_str for the constant pieces + name, and AttributeValue::write_value<W: fmt::Write> for the value (extracted from Display body; Display now delegates). Byte-identical (216 tests pass). Reverse-order A/B: large_500 +12.4%, medium_100 +10.0%, small_10 +4.6% (all p<0.05, scales with element count). First render win after the swarm's micro-rejects (retain guard, capacity hint) — those were genuinely sub-floor/contaminated, but the Formatter overhead was a DIFFERENT, real cost.

title: kanban column names never reach the picture in terminal: the layout writes a placeholder band label and the terminal draws no band label at all
description:
TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS IN ONE CHAIN, both measured with a binary verified FRESH against every crate under test (binary mtime vs git log -1 --format=%ct per crate) -- the staleness gate that my retracted bd-oqfv taught me to apply first.

MEASURED, source 'kanban / Alpha / t1[Beta]':
  SVG       draws BOTH the column name 'Alpha' and the card 'Beta'
  -f term   draws 'Beta' only; 'Alpha' is absent
  node ids  [t1] only -- the column is NOT a node, so its name had no other route into the picture

DEFECT 1, fm-render-term. The band loop in render_subcell_mode draws each kind's GEOMETRY and no text for any kind: Lane a dashed lifeline, Section top/bottom rules, Column a right-edge separator. LayoutBand carries a  and fm-render-svg DOES draw it (lib.rs:5030). So every band label -- gantt sections, kanban columns -- is invisible in terminal output. Same family as bd-trsd, where gantt's section band and label were absent because a renderer skipped what layout had already computed.

DEFECT 2, fm-layout, and it is the reason a naive fix makes things WORSE. The Column bands are built with

  layout_band_for_rank(..., LayoutBandKind::Column, format!("column {}", rank + 1), 20.0)

so  is a GENERATED PLACEHOLDER -- 'column 1', 'column 2' -- never the user's declared lane name. The user's name is not merely undrawn; it never reaches the band at all.

⚠️ I WROTE THE TERMINAL FIX, GATED IT, AND REVERTED IT. The overlay worked, but with defect 2 in place it would have drawn 'column 1' where the user wrote 'Alpha'. A placeholder rendered confidently is worse than a blank, so shipping the renderer half alone would have converted a missing label into a wrong one. The test failing with 0 occurrences of 'Alpha' rather than a duplicate is what exposed the upstream cause -- had I asserted only 'some label appears', it would have passed while displaying the placeholder.

ORDER OF FIX: defect 2 first (carry the declared lane name into the band, via kanban_lane_columns which already groups by declared lane), then defect 1 (overlay band.label at the band's top-left, one-cell inset, skipping bands too narrow to hold it). The renderer half is ~25 lines and was already gated green apart from the placeholder issue; it is not the hard part.

CONTROLS a fix needs: a column label must appear ONCE per band, not once per card; a sequence diagram's lifeline bands carry no user-facing name and its participants must still appear exactly once each; gantt section names must appear.

fm-layout is under another agent's lease, which is why defect 2 is filed rather than fixed here.

title: Replace hardcoded SVG band/axis colors with CSS custom properties
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded hex color strings in `render_layout_band()` and `render_layout_axis_tick()` functions in fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs with CSS custom property references.

## Why
These functions render gantt section labels (#4a5568), axis tick marks (#94a3b8), and axis tick labels (#64748b). These colors are theme-unaware — they are legible on the Default light theme but invisible on Dark, Neon, and Blueprint themes where the background is dark.

## Technical Context
These two functions (`render_layout_band` at line ~2050 and `render_layout_axis_tick` at line ~2104) only receive `&SvgRenderConfig` — they do NOT have access to the `Theme` struct. The options are:
1. Thread `&ThemeColors` through the function signatures (invasive refactor)
2. Use CSS custom properties like `var(--fm-text-color, #fallback)` (minimally invasive)

Option 2 is preferred because the theme CSS already defines these properties via `ThemeColors::to_css_vars()` in theme.rs, and SVGs with embedded `<style>` blocks will correctly resolve them.

## Specific Changes
- `render_layout_band()` line ~2095: Change `.fill("#4a5568")` to `.fill("var(--fm-text-color, #4a5568)")`

title: Lean profile: stream the LABELED edge fragment too (sequence/er/sankey gain nothing today)
description:
Follow-up to bd-b2b6 (node half, 2288c78) and bd-6u9o (unlabeled-edge half, this commit).

render_edge's whole-LABELED-edge fast fragment (crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs, the '<g><path/><rect/><text/><title/></g>' streamer) is still gated on 'config.a11y.aria_labels && config.a11y.keyboard_nav && config.a11y.text_alternatives'. Under the lean profile every labeled edge falls back to the per-element Element builder (group + path + rect + text + title, ~5 allocs/edge).

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (bd-6u9o instruction A/B, perf stat -e instructions:u, two-point delta): sequence_20 lean 1.0003x and er_40 lean 1.0004x -- i.e. ZERO gain from the unlabeled-edge lever, because their edges are labeled. Every other corpus item moved 0.92-0.74x. Label-heavy diagrams (sankey especially) are the last un-streamed lean edge family.

LEVER: same const-generic move. Give the labeled fragment writer an A11Y: bool const parameter and relax the gate to uniform_a11y(&config.a11y).is_some().

BYTE-STREAM CAUTION -- the lean labeled edge is NOT simply 'drop the a11y bits':
  * the '<g id="fm-edge-N" class="fm-edge-labeled" data-fm-edge-id="N">' wrapper SURVIVES under lean (the group is structural -- it holds the rect+text children -- not an a11y wrapper). Only role/tabindex/<title> are dropped.
  * the child <path> carries NO id under lean (unlike the unlabeled case, where the id lands on the bare path because there is no group). Confirm against render_edge's labeled slow path (group.id(..) at the group, elem unwrapped) before writing the fragment.

VERIFY EXACTLY AS bd-6u9o DID (and reuse its oracle -- do NOT pin a literal): render_edge stays a11y-gated, so 'render_edge_into(..) == render_edge(..).write_to_string(..)' under A11yConfig::none() is a live parity assert. Extend lean_edge_streaming_matches_element_render with labeled edges. Then dump all 13 corpus items under both profiles with 'headtohead <corpus.json> <dump-dir>' from a pristine HEAD build and require all 26 SHA-256s unchanged.

MEASURE with 'FM_H2H_FORCE_PROFILE=lean|default' + perf stat -e instructions:u two-point delta (reps 36 - reps 6, warmup 2, batch pinned to 1). Watch sequence_20 and er_40 -- they are the two corpus items that should move.

DO NOT use a runtime a11y flag inside the writer: measured +0.1..0.33% default instructions on the node path.

FILE-OWNERSHIP: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs, render_edge labeled region only. The cod pane owns render_layout_to_svg / element.rs / attributes.rs / buffer plumbing.

title: Flaky: fxhash_faster_than_siphash asserts an absolute wall-clock deadline, so it reds under workspace load
description:
fm-core's tests::fxhash_faster_than_siphash intermittently reds `cargo test --workspace`. Observed FOUR times in one session on 2026-08-08, each time passing on isolated re-run (8/8), each time indistinguishable at a glance from a real regression in whatever change was being gated.

THE ASSERTIONS ARE PURE HOST-SPEED CHECKS, which is the whole defect. The test hashes 1,000,000 values with each of FxHash and SipHash and then asserts, in full:

    assert!(fx_time.as_millis() < 1000, "FxHash too slow: {:?}", fx_time);
    assert!(sip_time.as_millis() < 1000, "SipHash too slow: {:?}", sip_time);

That is an absolute wall-clock deadline on a machine that, during `cargo test --workspace`, is running dozens of other test binaries across every core. Two million hash operations exceeding one second under that contention is ordinary, not anomalous. Nothing here is a property of the CODE; it is a property of how busy the host happens to be.

WORSE, IT DOES NOT ASSERT WHAT ITS NAME CLAIMS. The test is called `fxhash_faster_than_siphash` and its own comment reads "We only assert it's not slower to avoid flaky tests" — but no such assertion exists. `fx_ns` and `sip_ns` are computed and then used only in a `println!`. So the one property worth checking, and the one that is ROBUST to load because contention slows both arms together, is the property the test does not check.

THE FIX IS NOT TO LOOSEN — it is to assert the ratio and drop the deadlines. A relative comparison between two arms measured back-to-back in the same process is exactly the shape that survives a loaded host; an absolute millisecond budget is exactly the shape that cannot. Raising the budget to 5s or adding a retry would keep a host-speed assertion and merely make it fire less often.

This repo already knows this failure mode. docs memory records "output depends on MEASURED WALL TIME" as a defect class, and the A/A-null discipline in AGENTS.md exists because absolute timings on a shared host are not decidable. A unit test asserting a wall-clock deadline is the same mistake at a smaller scale.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TEST: an intermittently red suite makes "main is green" unverifiable. During one session it cost four full-workspace re-runs and forced a manual isolation run each time to prove a landed change was not at fault.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. `fxhash_faster_than_siphash` contains no absolute wall-clock deadline.
2. It asserts the relative property its name states — FxHash is not slower than SipHash over the same workload in the same process.
3. The measured ratio is still reported (the println is the documentation value the test was written for).
4. `cargo test --workspace` run repeatedly under full concurrency does not red on this test.

RELATED: bd-ryxg tracks a different load flake (fm-layout's tracing_dispatch_event_contains_mandatory_fields) with a different mechanism — an event capture, not a timing assertion. Same symptom class, unrelated cause; do not merge them.
close_reason:
Landed 62560d1e. The test's only assertions were absolute wall-clock deadlines (fx_time < 1s, sip_time < 1s) — properties of how busy the host is, not of the code — and under cargo test --workspace, with dozens of test binaries on every core, two million hash operations exceeding a second is ordinary. It red the workspace FOUR times in one session while passing every isolated re-run.

NOT A LOOSENING. The test is named fxhash_faster_than_siphash and its comment promised 'we only assert it's not slower', but no such assertion existed — fx_ns and sip_ns were computed and used only in a println!. The deadlines are gone and the relative property is asserted for the FIRST time: FxHash must not be slower than SipHash over the same workload, measured back-to-back in the same process. A ratio between two adjacent arms survives contention because scheduling pressure slows both together; an absolute budget cannot. Raising the budget or adding a retry would have kept a host-speed assertion and merely made it fire less often.

All four acceptance criteria met: (1) no absolute wall-clock deadline remains; (2) the relative property its name states is asserted; (3) the measured ratio is still printed, which was the test's documentation value; (4) cargo test --workspace run THREE consecutive times, 0 failing binaries each — the first clean triple of the session, against roughly one-in-three before.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the FxHash arm made artificially slower it fails with 'FxHash must not be slower than SipHash over the same workload: FxHash 5.04770725s vs SipHash 132.717861ms'. The old assertion would have caught that mutation too, but with 'FxHash too slow' — a message that cannot distinguish a code regression from a busy host, which is exactly why it was useless as a signal.

bd-ryxg tracks a different load flake (fm-layout's tracing capture) with an unrelated mechanism; deliberately not merged.

title: class realization and dotted-link operators drew no edge
description:
UML REALIZATION (`Impl ..|> Interface`, `Interface <|.. Impl`) and the plain dotted link (`A .. B`)
matched NO operator in CLASS_OPERATORS, so find_operator returned None and the statement was not a
relation at all. Interface implementation - one of the most common lines in a class diagram - drew
no edge whatsoever. Neither spelling is a superstring of an entry that did match (`..|>` does not
contain `..>`; `<|..` does not contain `<..`), which is why nothing caught it by accident.

FIXED: three table entries. `..` -> DottedLine is EXACT.

APPROXIMATION, stated because it is a real loss: realization is a DASHED line with a hollow
triangle, and Inheritance/InheritanceReverse give the correct HEAD and DIRECTION but a SOLID line -
so a realization now renders indistinguishably from an inheritance. Smaller error than drawing
nothing (which says the classes are unrelated), but still an error.

TWO ROUTES TO THE EXACT RENDERING, neither safe to land unbuilt:
  * a Realization/RealizationReverse pair - exhaustive matches in fm-core's as_str, fm-layout and
    all three renderers;
  * the dash alone on the edge's inline_style - `stroke-dasharray` IS on fm-core's allowed-property
    list (there is already a test parsing it), and resolve_edge_inline_style reads
    edge.inline_style with every lean edge fast path gated on it being none. Needs the operator
    threaded to the push site.

⚠️ ORDERING HAZARD FOUND AND AVOIDED, worth keeping because no existing test covers it. find_operator
scans the table IN ORDER and returns the first operator found ANYWHERE in the statement, not the
leftmost one. UML multiplicity is written "0..*", so `Customer "1" -- "0..*" Order` contains `..`
inside a QUOTED cardinality that this parser already supports (set_last_edge_cardinality). My first
draft placed `..` above `--` and would have split that statement at the multiplicity instead of the
relation. `..` is now LAST in the table. The existing invariant test
(operator_tables_are_longest_prefix_first) only covers the PREFIX half of this constraint.

Found by probing SYMBOLIC syntax, which the 137-token lexer diff is structurally blind to.
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build

BLESS=1 for gantt_basic and commit the updated golden. Do NOT bless blind -- the whole point of the
snapshot is to catch unintended byte changes, and an FNV mismatch could equally mean a real gantt

title: gitignore matches repro_*.rs inside crates/*/tests/, where cargo auto-compiles it: a live test target that exists for nobody else
description:
REPORTED BY GoldenBison as a repo-guard scan; CONFIRMED and characterised here.

  git check-ignore -v crates/fm-cli/tests/repro_scaling_bug.rs
  .gitignore:68:repro_*.rs   crates/fm-cli/tests/repro_scaling_bug.rs

MECHANISM, and it is the exact INVERSE of the trap already banked for src/. A file in
crates/<pkg>/src/ that no 'mod' declares NEVER compiles, so code can sit there dead and
no tool warns. A file in crates/<pkg>/tests/ needs NO declaration at all -- cargo makes
every top-level .rs there its own integration-test target automatically. So the same
carelessness has opposite signs on the two sides, and .gitignore turns the tests/ side
into a gate that runs on ONE machine and exists for nobody else.

The .gitignore patterns 'repro_*.rs' and 'reproduce_*.rs' are UNANCHORED, so they match
at any depth, including inside a crate's tests/ directory. They were plainly meant for
scratch files at the repo root -- the neighbouring entries are SESSION_*.md, verify_*.sh
and newfile.txt, and the very next stanza IS anchored ('/test_*').

SCAN of the whole repo: exactly ONE such file exists today.
  crates/fm-cli/tests/repro_scaling_bug.rs   2.3 KB, one #[test]

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STRAY FILE: a local 'cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli' runs it
and reports it in the pass count, while CI, every peer and every rch remote build have
never compiled it. A green local gate and a green CI gate can disagree about which tests
exist, and nothing in either output says so.

⚠️ AND IT WAS HIDING A REAL DEFECT WHILE ASSERTING THE WRONG THING -- see the sibling
bead. Its single assertion is contains("Node49"), which PASSES today. The 50-node chain
it builds actually loses 28 of its 50 nodes in an 80x24 terminal, INCLUDING the root, and
Node49 is one of the survivors. So the file was invisible AND vacuous-in-the-direction-
that-matters: had it ever run for anyone, it would have reported success.

FIX: anchor the two patterns to the repo root ('/repro_*.rs', '/reproduce_*.rs') so they
keep their intended scratch-file meaning and can no longer capture a compiled target, and
re-home the reproducing test as a tracked one.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. A scratch repro_foo.rs at the REPO ROOT must still be ignored -- that is the entry's
     whole purpose and unanchoring it is not the fix.
  2. The re-homed test must actually be tracked; moving it under another ignored pattern
     just relocates the hole.
  3. No other ignored path may be un-ignored as a side effect.
close_reason:
LANDED at 23f34235. Reported by GoldenBison, confirmed and characterised here.

FIX: both patterns anchored to the repo root, /repro_*.rs and /reproduce_*.rs, matching the intent of the neighbouring entries (SESSION_*.md, verify_*.sh) and the already-anchored /test_* stanza directly below them.

BOTH DIRECTIONS VERIFIED, because half a fix here is invisible:
  root scratch file    git check-ignore -v repro_scratch_probe.rs -> .gitignore:72:/repro_*.rs   STILL IGNORED
  crates/fm-cli/tests  git check-ignore -v ...repro_scaling_bug.rs -> no match, now '?? ' in git status   VISIBLE

The stale file is NOT deleted. It is another agent's working file in a shared tree, and it is now visible in git status for its owner to remove or track deliberately. Its content is superseded by the tracked crates/fm-render-term/tests/terminal_fit.rs, which is where it belonged: it only ever needed fm-core and fm-render-term, so it was forcing a whole fm-cli build for a two-crate test.

WHAT IT WAS HIDING is the real cost, see bd-beqx: a live defect losing 28 of 50 nodes, under a test whose sole assertion passes.

Gate: cargo check --workspace --all-targets, rch worker hz2, 4m06s, exit 0 -- --workspace deliberately, since omitting it skips fm-wasm and has left main red under a green claim before.

title: block-beta: an invisible space node still emits an empty <text> element and an empty aria-label
description:
BLOCKS bd-7ute's stated acceptance gate. Found by running that gate after the layout defects it
names were fixed.

WHAT IS EMITTED, measured on `block-beta / columns 3 / A["a"] / space / C["c"] / D["d"] / E["e"] / F["f"]`:

  <g id="fm-node-space-4-1" class="fm-node ... fm-node-block-beta-space"
     data-id="__space_4" role="graphics-symbol" aria-label="" tabindex="0">
    <rect .../>
    <text x="391.38" y="130.25" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#1a1a2e"></text>
    <title>Node: __space_4, rectangle</title>
  </g>

A `space` is a grid spacer with no content. `render_node_into` already knows this —
`placeholder_space_node` (crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:8034) forces `raw_label_text` to "" and
gates six other fast paths on `!placeholder_space_node` — but the fragment writers still emit the
`<text>` element unconditionally, so the output carries an empty text node, an empty `aria-label`,
and a `<title>` naming an internal id (`__space_4`) that no reader should be told about. Same family
as the dead-`<defs>` finding: declared output with nothing behind it.

WHY IT BLOCKS bd-7ute. `node_centres` in crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs hard-errors when a
node has a `<text>` element whose content it cannot extract — deliberately, so that an absence it
reports can never be an unreadability in disguise. So
`block_beta_span_width_is_proportional_to_declared_columns` cannot run at all, whatever the layout
does. Its own doc comment states the premise this violates: "`space` is invisible and carries no
text, so `node_centres` already excludes it".

bd-7ute's geometry is therefore asserted at the LAYOUT level instead, in
crates/fm-cli/tests/integration_test.rs (`block_beta_container_span_reaches_the_geometry`,
`block_beta_space_holds_its_declared_cell`), and its golden guard stays #[ignore]d with its reason
repointed here.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN bd-7ute. The `<text>` is written by several `write_*_node_fragment_into`
writers, each paired with a byte-identical fast-vs-slow parity test
(`node_fast_fragment_matches_render`). Suppressing it correctly means editing every writer and its
slow-path counterpart together; that is a renderer change, not a layout one.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. A `space` node's group contains no `<text>` element.
2. It carries no empty `aria-label`, and no `<title>` exposing the generated `__space_N` id.
3. Every other node type is byte-identical before and after (the existing golden corpus is the
   check; only block_basic may move).
4. Remove the #[ignore] from `block_beta_span_width_is_proportional_to_declared_columns` and let it
   run — its two assertions are already correct and already pass at the layout level.
close_reason: Landed c64efaf0. A block-beta space now emits its rect and nothing else: no <text>, no empty aria-label, no tabindex, no <title> exposing __space_N, plus aria-hidden=true — the correct markup for a decorative element is to leave the accessibility tree, not sit in it silently. The document <desc> leaked the same generated id ('Key nodes: …, __space_9'); summarize_key_nodes now skips space nodes using the renderer's own is_block_beta_space_node rather than a private copy. GATE: block_beta_space_carries_no_accessible_content asserts all five properties with the NEGATIVE half that ordinary cells in the same document keep their text and accessible names, so it cannot be satisfied by suppressing labels generally. Criterion 3 met exactly: block_basic is the ONLY case that moves out of 37, -162 bytes in one region, node geometry untouched, the other four nodes keep their aria-labels. Criterion 4 met: block_beta_span_width_is_proportional_to_declared_columns un-ignored and passing. cargo test --workspace 0 failures; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: Implement diagram-level title in IR and render across all diagram types
description:
# Diagram-Level Title Support

## What mermaid-js Supports
Many diagram types support a title directive:
\`\`\`
---
title: My Diagram Title
---
flowchart LR
  A --> B
\`\`\`
Or inline: \`title My Diagram\` in gantt, journey, timeline, pie, xychart, quadrant.

The title renders as centered text above the entire diagram.

## Current State
- YAML front-matter title: NOT extracted from init config
- Inline 'title' directive: Parsed and SKIPPED in gantt, journey, pie, etc.
- MermaidDiagramMeta has NO title field
- SVG renderer does NOT render any diagram title

## Implementation Plan
1. **IR** (fm-core): Add title: Option<String> to MermaidDiagramMeta.
2. **Parser**: In front-matter parsing, extract title field. In diagram-specific parsers (gantt, journey, timeline, pie, xychart, quadrant), capture the title directive text and store in meta.title.
3. **SVG Renderer**: When meta.title is Some, render as centered <text> element above the diagram content. Adjust viewBox to accommodate title height.
4. **Tests**: YAML front-matter title, inline title in gantt, inline title in pie, no title (verify no empty text element), long title (verify wrapping or truncation).

## Impact
This is a high-visibility feature — users expect their diagram title to show up. Currently it silently vanishes.
close_reason: Completed

- cargo fmt --check
- cargo test --workspace (zero new failures)

title: Add classDef styling diagnostic: emit warning when classDef is parsed but ignored
description:
## Problem (interim fix before full classDef wiring)
Until bd-65l0 (full classDef→SVG wiring) is complete, users who write classDef directives get ZERO feedback that their styles are being silently dropped. This interim bead adds a diagnostic warning so users at least KNOW their styles aren't working.

## Scope
1. In fm-parser (or fm-core validation), after parsing classDef directives, emit a Warning-level diagnostic:
   "classDef directive parsed but not yet applied to rendered output. Styling will use theme defaults."
2. Same for `style` directives on individual nodes.

title: gantt dateFormat mismatches fall back to ISO silently, so a date that contradicts the declared format is accepted with no diagnostic
description:
SPLIT OUT of bd-w3pw, whose dateFormat half I refuted by experiment: the directive
IS honoured (see that bead's comment for the discriminating measurement). What
survives is a narrower and different concern, and it is the one bd-w3pw actually
articulated: "a user writing an unusual dateFormat would otherwise get silently
misparsed dates rather than an error".

THE MECHANISM, fm-parser mermaid_parser.rs:5971-5972:

    normalize_gantt_date_with_format(token, date_format.unwrap_or("YYYY-MM-DD"))
        .or_else(|| normalize_gantt_date_with_format(token, "YYYY-MM-DD"))

A task date that does not match the DECLARED format is silently retried as ISO. So

    gantt
        dateFormat DD-MM-YYYY
        T1 :a1, 2024-01-15, 3d

is accepted, parsed as 15 Jan 2024 by the ISO fallback, and the user is told
nothing -- even though they declared day-first and wrote something else. The chart
renders and looks fine.

WHY THIS IS ARGUABLE RATHER THAN OBVIOUS, and why it is filed rather than fixed:
leniency here may well be deliberate. Real documents mix formats, and mermaid-js
itself is permissive. Removing the fallback outright would reject diagrams that
render correctly today, which is a worse outcome than the ambiguity. So the fix is
probably a DIAGNOSTIC, not a rejection: emit a parse warning naming the token and
the declared format, and let the fallback still produce a date.

⚠️ THE AMBIGUOUS CASE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Where the two readings disagree but
BOTH are valid dates, the fallback silently picks the wrong one. With
`dateFormat DD-MM-YYYY` and the token `02-01-2024`, day-first gives 2 Jan; if that
succeeds no fallback occurs, so this is safe. The hazard is a token like
`2024-01-02` under a declared `DD-MM-YYYY`: day-first fails (2024 is not a day),
ISO succeeds, and the date silently becomes 2 Jan with no signal. A user who meant
something else never finds out.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. A date matching the declared format must produce NO warning -- the common
     path stays silent, or the warning is noise and will be ignored.
  2. The diagram must still RENDER after the warning; this is a diagnostic, not a
     rejection, unless a deliberate strict mode is added.
  3. A gantt with no dateFormat directive at all must be unaffected: the default
     is ISO and there is nothing to disagree with.
  4. The warning must name the offending TOKEN and the declared FORMAT. "bad date"
     is not actionable in a chart with fifty tasks.
close_reason:
LANDED at d475cda7, pushed to main and master.

THE DEFECT. parse_gantt_absolute_date retries a token that does not match the declared dateFormat as ISO. The leniency is deliberate and stays -- rejecting outright would break diagrams that render correctly today -- but 'dateFormat DD-MM-YYYY' with an ISO date in the body was accepted with NO signal at all, and where both readings are valid dates the user never learns which was taken.

FIX: parse_gantt_absolute_date_checked reports whether the DECLARED format was bypassed; ParsedGanttTaskMeta carries the offending tokens out (that function has no builder); the caller, which has builder and line_number, emits the warning. The date is still parsed and the task still renders -- a diagnostic, not a rejection. The flag is true only when the declared format FAILED, the ISO fallback succeeded, AND the declared format is not itself ISO.

TESTS assert the warning is ACTIONABLE rather than merely present: it must name BOTH the offending token and the declared format, because 'bad date' is not usable in a chart with fifty tasks. They also assert the task still parses, so the diagnostic cannot quietly become a rejection.

SILENCE CASES, all asserted: a conforming date warns not at all; no dateFormat directive warns not at all (the default IS ISO, so there is nothing to contradict); an explicitly declared YYYY-MM-DD warns not at all.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the flag forced false, gantt_date_contradicting_the_declared_format_warns FAILS (left 0, right 1) while the silence test AND the two pre-existing gantt date tests (normalizes_non_iso_dates, rejects_impossible_calendar_dates) pass either way -- which is what shows this touched only the reporting, not date parsing itself.

CONTEXT: this is the half that survived my refutation of bd-w3pw's dateFormat claim. dateFormat IS honoured -- measured with a discriminating fixture where day-first and month-first disagree, giving a 1440px gap = exactly 30 days -- so the directive is not ignored. What was missing was any signal when a date contradicts it.

The layout engine is the single biggest factor in diagram quality -- this is where we win against mermaid-js. All algorithms must maintain the determinism guarantee: identical input always produces identical output.

title: Implement superior cycle handling in Sugiyama layout
description:
This is THE core differentiator mentioned in the X thread. Mermaid-js handles cycles poorly. Our approach:

1. DETECTION: Tarjan's SCC algorithm to find all strongly connected components. Report cycle count, participants, and nesting depth.

2. MULTI-STRATEGY CYCLE BREAKING (user-configurable):
   a. GREEDY (current): Source/sink peeling. Fast, good for mostly-DAG graphs.
   b. DFS-BACK: Depth-first search, reverse back edges. Minimizes reversed edges.
   c. MINIMUM-FEEDBACK-ARC-SET: Approximation algorithm (NP-hard exact). Finds near-minimal set of edges to reverse. Better aesthetics for heavily cyclic graphs.
   d. CYCLE-AWARE: Don't break cycles at all -- render them as visible cycles with curved back-edges. This is the 'honest' approach that shows the user their cycles rather than hiding them.

3. BACK-EDGE RENDERING: For reversed edges in GREEDY/DFS/MFAS modes, provide metadata so renderers can draw them distinctly (dashed line, different color, reversed arrowhead) to communicate that these represent cycles.

4. CYCLE CLUSTER COLLAPSE: Option to collapse an entire SCC into a single 'cycle cluster' node that can be expanded. Reduces visual complexity for highly cyclic subgraphs.

5. QUALITY METRICS: Track number of reversed edges, total edge length increase from reversal, visual symmetry of cycle representation. Expose in LayoutStats.

Determinism: All strategies must be deterministic given identical input. Use stable sorting, break ties by node ID.

title: Implement force-directed layout algorithm
description:
Implement a deterministic force-directed (spring-electric) layout for diagrams that don't have a natural hierarchy. Used for: ER diagrams (entities with many-to-many relationships), architecture diagrams, generic graphs with no clear flow direction.

Algorithm: Fruchterman-Reingold variant with:
1. Repulsive forces: All node pairs push apart (inverse-square law). Use Barnes-Hut approximation O(n log n) for graphs > 100 nodes.
2. Attractive forces: Connected nodes pull together (Hooke's law / log-spring).
3. Cooling schedule: Start with high temperature, reduce per iteration. Use deterministic schedule (no RNG -- use hash-based initial positions).
4. Convergence: Stop when max displacement < threshold or iteration budget exhausted.
5. Overlap removal: Post-processing pass to ensure no node overlap.
6. Cluster awareness: Nodes in same IrCluster get extra attractive force.

Key: Deterministic initial placement using hash of node IDs (not random). Same input always produces same output. Iteration count configurable via LayoutConfig.

Output: Same DiagramLayout type as Sugiyama. Callers don't need to know which algorithm was used.

title: Implement specialized layouts for timeline, gantt, sankey, kanban, grid
description:
Implement purpose-built layout algorithms for diagram types that don't fit general graph layout:

1. TIMELINE LAYOUT: Linear horizontal arrangement. Time periods evenly spaced. Events stacked vertically under each period. Sections as labeled bands. Simple arithmetic positioning.

2. GANTT LAYOUT: Horizontal bar chart on time axis. Tasks as bars with start/end. Dependencies as arrows between bars. Critical path highlighting. Sections as swim lanes. Calendar grid background.

3. SANKEY LAYOUT: Flow-conserving layout. Nodes in columns, edges as variable-width bands. Uses iterative relaxation to minimize edge crossings while maintaining flow conservation (inspired by d3-sankey algorithm). Node heights proportional to flow.

4. KANBAN LAYOUT: Fixed columns (swim lanes). Cards stacked vertically in columns. WIP limit indicators. Simple grid-based positioning.

5. GRID/BLOCK LAYOUT: CSS-grid-like positioning with column/row spans. Used for block diagrams. Cells sized by content, spans merged.

6. PIE/RADAR LAYOUT: Polar coordinate systems. Pie: sectors by proportion. Radar: axes from center, data points on axes connected by polygons.

Each layout produces DiagramLayout with same interface as Sugiyama/force-directed. Specialized metadata (e.g. time axis ticks for gantt) stored in layout extensions.

title: Improve crossing minimization with advanced heuristics
description:
Upgrade the barycenter crossing minimization in the Sugiyama pipeline with more sophisticated heuristics for better edge routing aesthetics:

1. SIFTING: After barycenter, apply sifting heuristic -- try moving each node to every position in its layer, keep the position with fewest crossings. O(n^2) per layer but significant quality improvement.

2. TRANSPOSE: Pairwise swapping of adjacent nodes if it reduces crossings. Iterate until no improvement.

3. GLOBAL SIFTING: Move nodes across layers (re-rank) if it reduces total crossings. Bounded to prevent infinite loops.

4. EDGE BUNDLING: Group edges with similar source/target layers and route them through shared waypoints. Reduces visual clutter for dense graphs.

5. LONG EDGE OPTIMIZATION: For edges spanning multiple ranks, ensure dummy nodes are well-positioned to minimize bends. Current implementation uses median; try also left-right centering.

6. PORT ORDERING: When a node has multiple ports, order them to minimize crossings of attached edges. Currently ports are arbitrary; this matters for class/ER diagrams.

Quality metric: track crossing count before/after each heuristic. Expose in LayoutStats so users can see improvement.

title: Implement orthogonal edge routing with channel assignment
description:
Implement proper orthogonal (Manhattan-style) edge routing that produces clean, non-overlapping edge paths:

1. CHANNEL ASSIGNMENT: Between each pair of adjacent ranks, assign horizontal routing channels. Edges that need to turn are assigned to channels to avoid overlap.

2. NUDGE ALGORITHM: After initial routing, nudge edge segments to reduce total edge length and improve spacing.

3. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: When edges must cross, minimize crossing angle and ensure crossing point is visually clear (not on a bend).

4. POLYLINE SIMPLIFICATION: Remove unnecessary waypoints from edge paths. If three consecutive waypoints are collinear, remove the middle one.

5. SPLINE OPTION: As alternative to orthogonal, offer cubic Bezier spline routing. Control points computed from waypoint geometry for smooth curves. Configurable per-edge or globally.

6. SELF-LOOP ROUTING: Special handling for edges where source == target. Route as a loop going out the right/bottom and returning to left/top.

7. PARALLEL EDGE ROUTING: When multiple edges connect the same pair of nodes, offset them to be visually distinguishable.

This significantly improves visual quality over the current waypoint-based routing.

title: fm-wasm tests share a global RUNTIME_CONFIG with no serialisation, so any new config-reading test is order-dependent
description:
MECHANISM, measured rather than inferred. render_svg_js and render both read RUNTIME_CONFIG, a
process-wide RwLock. Exactly ONE test mutates it -- render_svg_js_uses_same_font_metrics_layout_path
_as_render -- and it restores the original through an RAII Drop guard, which is careful and still
not enough: cargo runs tests in PARALLEL, so while that test holds a non-default config every other
test that READS the config sees it.

OBSERVED BOTH WAYS on 2026-08-19:

  * A new cross-target digest test passed filtered and FAILED in the suite (0xf9c38140c62e9ffa vs
    0x8835c1df81b8f371) because it rendered while the font-metrics test had font_size 28 installed.
  * Resetting the config from the new test to defend against that broke the font-metrics test
    instead: it renders twice and compares, and saw detail-tier "normal" against "rich" because the
    reset landed between its two calls.

So the fragility is symmetric and latent: it is not that one test is wrong, it is that a shared
global has no lock and the suite happens to pass only while exactly one mutator exists. The next
config-reading test anyone adds meets this, and the failure looks like a defect in whatever the test
was actually about -- in this case it wore the costume of a cross-target floating-point divergence,
which is the one false positive bd-1s1g.6 must not produce.

FIX: a module-level Mutex taken by every test that reads OR writes RUNTIME_CONFIG. Contained -- the
mutator already has its restore guard, so this adds a lock acquisition to it and to the readers.
Poison-tolerant (lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())) so one failing test does not cascade
into every other test reporting a poisoned mutex instead of its own result.

UNBLOCKS: x86_64_and_wasm32_render_the_same_bytes is #[ignore]d solely for this reason and can be
un-ignored with the fix, which puts the only cross-target determinism evidence in the project into
the default CI run instead of behind a manual --test-threads=1 recipe.

⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE: commit 60199681 says five tests write the config. That is
wrong -- it came from a grep -c that counted the import line and the Drop impl. Exactly one test
writes it. The race is real, the count was not.

THE CODE SAYS SO ITSELF, crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:9168-9187:

    NodeShape::Circle | NodeShape::FilledCircle | NodeShape::DoubleCircle => {
        let r = w.min(h) / 2.0;
        let mut elem = Element::circle()…;
        if shape == NodeShape::DoubleCircle {
            // For double circle, we'll use a slightly smaller stroke
            elem = elem.stroke_width(2.0);
        }
        elem
    }

One circle, and a stroke-width tweak standing in for a second ring. The theme
already resolves the base stroke width to 2.0, so even that tweak is a no-op --
which is why the two elements above are byte-identical apart from position.

IT IS NOT A FLOWCHART-ONLY DEFECT. The parser maps a stateDiagram terminal `[*]`
to NodeShape::DoubleCircle (asserted at fm-parser mermaid_parser.rs:14324), and
deep history `[H*]` too (:14439). So every stateDiagram end state is drawn as a
plain circle. Measured on

    stateDiagram-v2
        [*] --> Idle
        Idle --> Done
        Done --> [*]

the START pseudo-state is <circle r=10 fill=#e2e8f0> and the END is
<circle r=12 stroke-width=2 fill=url(#fm-node-gradient)> -- two flat discs that
differ only in radius and tint. mermaid-js 11.15.0 draws the start as a solid
filled disc and the end as a BULLSEYE: an outer ring plus a filled inner disc
(.start-state / .end-state-outer + .end-state-inner). Initial and terminal states
are the two things a state diagram most needs to distinguish, and we render them
as near-twins.

FIX: emit the second ring. One circle at r, one at r * k (k < 1) with the fill,
matching the incumbent's outer-ring/inner-disc construction. Confine it to the
DoubleCircle arm so NodeShape::Circle and NodeShape::FilledCircle are untouched.

NEGATIVE CASES a naive implementation fails:
  1. `(((x)))` and `((x))` must NOT produce the same element set -- assert the
     double circle emits strictly more circles than the plain one at the same
     centre. A test that only asserts "a circle exists" passes today.
  2. NodeShape::Circle and NodeShape::FilledCircle output must be byte-identical
     to today; only the DoubleCircle arm may move.
  3. The inner ring must be INSIDE the outer: r_inner < r_outer, and the outer
     radius must not grow, or every double-circle node overflows the box layout
     sized for it.
  4. A stateDiagram `[*]` terminal must end up visually distinct from its `[*]`
     initial -- the two must not both be single discs.

Goldens verified element-by-element: all_node_shapes 156->156 with fm-node-shape-double-circle now 0 and the circle node keeping its group/class/aria-label; state_composite 206->212, exactly +3 per legitimate [*] end state. GATE: double_circle_draws_two_rings_and_a_plain_circle_still_draws_one on rch WORKER vmi1227854 (741.4s), HARNESS 'cargo test -j 1 -p fm-render-svg --lib'; golden_svg_test on rch WORKER hz2, 42 passed with the only failure being cycle_braid, untouched here and already red from peer parallel-edge work. comments.text: CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S DIAGNOSIS: the renderer is only half of it, and fixing the half named here REGRESSES every plain circle. I implemented the two-ring renderer change and wrote a test whose CONTROL failed immediately: 'a plain circle node must emit exactly one <circle>: left: 2, right: 1'. ROOT CAUSE IS IN THE PARSER, crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs:602 — 'let double_circle_content = just("((") … .then_ignore(just("))"))' maps '((label))', which is mermaid's CIRCLE syntax, to NodeShape::DoubleCircle, and it is FIRST in the node_shape choice. There is no '(((label)))' rule anywhere. So both syntaxes collapse to DoubleCircle before rendering, which is why the two nodes in this bead's repro are byte-identical: they are the same shape by the time the renderer sees them, and the renderer drew one circle for it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: adding the second ring in the renderer alone turns EVERY '((x))' circle into a double ring — the exact regression my control caught. The complete fix is (1) parser: '((x))' -> NodeShape::Circle, plus a new '(((x)))' -> DoubleCircle rule ordered BEFORE it, since a longest-match-first choice is required or '(((' will match the '((' rule and leave a stray ')'; and (2) renderer: draw two concentric rings, inset by a fixed 4px rather than a ratio so the gap does not collapse on small nodes. comments.text:
GATE RESULT ON THE UNCOMMITTED WORKING-TREE CHANGE: FAILS. Do not commit as-is.

I gated the bd-vfxu change sitting uncommitted in the shared tree, because it was
blocking crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs for bd-trsd. It is NOT mine and I have
not modified it: it is exactly as its author left it.

  harness: cargo test -j 2 -p fm-render-svg --lib double_circle
  worker:  vmi1153651 (rch, 25m05s compile)
  result:  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed (exit 101)

  test tests::double_circle_draws_two_rings_and_a_plain_circle_still_draws_one FAILED
  panicked at crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:17007
  assertion left == right failed: a plain circle node must emit exactly one circle
    left: 2   right: 1

THE TEST IS RIGHT AND THE FIX IS WRONG. I checked the baseline independently
rather than assume it. Rendering a one-node flowchart with a round node using the
SHIPPING binary built from c03be579 emits exactly ONE circle element document-wide.
So 2 is a regression introduced by the change, not a miscount by the test. The
control this test was built around is exactly what caught it. It is a good test
and it did its job.

THE MECHANISM, and it is a Rust footgun rather than a geometry mistake. The arm
reads, in substance:

    NodeShape::Circle | NodeShape::FilledCircle | NodeShape::DoubleCircle => {
        let elem = Element::circle()...;
        if shape != NodeShape::DoubleCircle {
            return elem;          // returns from render_node, NOT from the arm
        }
        ...
    }

render_node's signature is -> Element (lib.rs:8800-8812) and the match is bound
with `let shape_elem = match shape { ... }`. A bare return inside an arm therefore
exits the WHOLE FUNCTION. The CrossedCircle arm below uses that same idiom
deliberately, returning group.child(g).child(render_node_label_text(...)), i.e. a
fully assembled node group.

So `return elem` hands back a naked circle element as the entire node and skips
everything render_node does after the match: the fm-node group wrapper, the node
LABEL, maybe_add_class("fm-node-shape"), the gradient fill, the drop-shadow
filter, and the a11y role / aria-label / tabindex attributes.

BLAST RADIUS is wider than flowcharts. The same arm carries NodeShape::FilledCircle,
which is gitGraph REVERSE commits and the stateDiagram START pseudo-state. Every
one of those loses its group, class, label and a11y too.

THE FIX IS SMALL. Make the DoubleCircle case PRODUCE A VALUE for shape_elem
instead of returning: an if/else that evaluates to either the single circle or the
two-ring group. Or follow the CrossedCircle precedent properly and return the
COMPLETE group (wrapper + label), not a bare element.

Leaving the change in the tree untouched for its author. Not claiming this bead.

title: click link target _blank was rendered as tooltip text
description:
`click A "https://example.com" _blank` rendered `_blank` to the reader as a TOOLTIP. The third
position in a click directive is either a tooltip or a browser link target; we assumed tooltip
unconditionally. This is not a silent drop - it is visible hover text the author never wrote, the
same severity class as the phantom node in bd-xfmm.

EVIDENCE: mermaid lexes the four targets as dedicated grammar tokens (/^(?:_self\b)/, _blank,
_parent, _top) and setLink(t, r, i) stores `i` as `linkTarget`, separate from the tooltip. The
probe confirms `click A "https://x.com" _blank` PARSES.

PATH VERIFIED BEFORE FIXING - there are TWO click parsers. The chumsky one requires a QUOTED
tooltip and ends with then_ignore(end()), so an unquoted `_blank` leaves input unconsumed and every
alternative in the choice() fails; the statement falls through to the hand-written
parse_click_directive_ast, which is where the fix lives. The fully-quoted forms are still handled
by chumsky and are untouched.

FIXED: the four keywords are recognised in the tooltip position and skipped, with a warning saying
the target is not applied. Matched on the RAW token BEFORE quote stripping, so a deliberately
quoted "_blank" is still tooltip text.

NOT STORED: no IrNode field carries a link target, and adding one no renderer reads would be dead
IR. Dropping it loses only the browser tab choice; keeping it corrupted the diagram's visible text.
A follow-up that adds `link_target` to IrNodeInteraction plus SVG `target=` output would close it
properly.

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Three tests added, none compiled. The href
assertion is the non-vacuity control - without it, a click line that failed to parse at all would
also leave the tooltip empty and pass.
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build

title: Topological Persistence for Stable Layout Features
description:
## Topological Persistence for Stable Layout Features

Apply persistent homology (topological data analysis) to identify and preserve stable topological features of diagram layouts across edits, preventing "layout earthquakes" where small edits cause large visual changes.

## Mathematical Foundation
Persistent homology tracks the birth and death of topological features (connected components, loops, voids) as a filtration parameter varies. For diagram layouts:

**Construction:**
1. Build a filtration on the node positions: start with all nodes as isolated points (ε=0), increase ε, connect nodes when distance < ε.
2. At each ε, compute the Betti numbers: β_0 = connected components, β_1 = loops.
3. Track when features appear (birth) and disappear (death) as ε increases.
4. Features with long persistence (death - birth >> 0) are STABLE topological features of the layout.

**Application to layout stability:**
- Stable features (high persistence) should be preserved across edits. If a single-node edit causes a high-persistence feature to vanish, the layout change was disproportionate — trigger stabilization.
- Stabilization: constrain the new layout to preserve all features with persistence > threshold. This prevents "layout earthquakes" while allowing local adjustments.

**Persistence diagram:** Plot (birth, death) for each feature. Points far from the diagonal are stable features; points near the diagonal are noise. The bottleneck distance between two persistence diagrams measures how much the layout's topological structure changed.

**Wasserstein distance (stability metric):**
W_p(D_1, D_2) = inf_γ (Σ ||x - γ(x)||^p)^{1/p}
where γ ranges over bijections between persistence diagrams D_1, D_2.
If W_∞(D_before, D_after) > threshold → layout change is too disruptive → stabilize.

## Key Papers
- Edelsbrunner, Letscher & Zomorodian, "Topological Persistence and Simplification" (DCG 2002)
- Carlsson, "Topology and Data" (AMS 2009) — survey
- Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner & Harer, "Stability of Persistence Diagrams" (DCG 2007) — stability theorem
- Ghrist, "Barcodes: The Persistent Topology of Data" (AMS 2008) — accessible introduction

## Implementation in FrankenMermaid
1. Implement Vietoris-Rips filtration on node positions (or alpha complex for efficiency).
2. Compute persistent homology using a matrix reduction algorithm (standard persistence algorithm).
3. Or use the `gudhi` or `ripser` crate binding (if available for Rust), or implement from scratch for educational value.
4. After each edit: compute persistence diagram of new layout, compare with pre-edit diagram.
5. If Wasserstein distance > threshold: add constraints to preserve high-persistence features, re-run layout.
6. Expose persistence visualization in demo: show barcode diagram alongside layout.
7. Decision contract: adopt if layout stability measurably improved (fewer "earthquake" events) AND computation overhead < 50ms per edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Persistent homology computed for 2D node positions (β_0 and β_1)
- [ ] Persistence diagram correctly identifies stable clusters and loops in layout
- [ ] Wasserstein distance computed between pre/post edit persistence diagrams
- [ ] Layout stabilization constraint prevents high-persistence feature destruction
- [ ] Computation time < 50ms for 1000-node diagrams
- [ ] Demo visualization: persistence barcode displayed alongside diagram
- [ ] Decision contract: specific adoption threshold for stability improvement
close_reason: Implemented topological persistence module (crates/fm-layout/src/persistence.rs) with: Vietoris-Rips filtration on 2D node positions, persistent homology computation (H0 connected components + H1 loops), persistence diagrams with birth/death tracking, Betti numbers, stable feature filtering, bottleneck distance (greedy approximation), p-Wasserstein distance, layout stability comparison API (compare_layout_stability), disruption detection. 15 unit tests all passing covering: empty/single/two points, collinear points, square loop detection, persistence ordering, identical/different bottleneck distance, Wasserstein distance, small/large edit stability, Betti numbers, stable feature filtering, max filtration limits, determinism. All quality gates pass (check, clippy, fmt, 236/236 tests).

title: Implement gantt SVG rendering with time axis, dependencies, and today marker
description:
# Gantt SVG Rendering

## What mermaid-js Renders
- Horizontal time axis with date labels (auto-scaled: days/weeks/months)
- Section swimlanes with labels
- Task bars: colored by type (blue=normal, green=done, red=critical, gray=active)
- Milestone: diamond markers on timeline
- Dependency arrows between task bars
- Progress fill (partial bar for % complete)
- Today marker: vertical red/orange dashed line
- Weekend/holiday shading on background
- Grid lines for time divisions

## Current State
- Layout positions tasks as generic nodes
- SVG renders basic rectangles and labels
- No time axis, no date labels, no dependency arrows, no type-based coloring

## Implementation Plan
1. **SVG Renderer**: Draw time axis at top with date labels. Draw section backgrounds. Draw task bars with type-based fill colors. Draw milestone diamonds. Draw dependency arrows (right edge of predecessor → left edge of successor). Draw today marker if date is within range.
2. **Tests**: Verify SVG output contains time axis, colored bars, dependency arrows.

## Depends On
- Gantt date parsing task (for IR data)
close_reason: Implemented specialized gantt SVG renderer with: type-based task bar colors (blue=normal, green=done, red=critical, slate=active, violet=milestone), diamond markers for milestones, section background bands, section labels, progress bar overlays, task labels, dependency arrows, and diagram title. CSS classes for all elements. Golden snapshots updated. All quality gates pass.

title: effects_css is gated on cosmetic knobs, so semantic markers (C4 external border, block-beta space invisibility, highlighted) vanish in the config all 37 byte goldens are pinned with
description:
Found by bd-iicc round 6 (C4 semantic guards). This is a defect in what the BYTE GOLDEN CORPUS can see, and a narrower one in the shipping render for anyone who turns visual effects off.

THE GATE. crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:3661 (and the same predicate at :1818):
    effects_enabled = config.node_gradients
                   || config.glow_enabled
                   || inactive_opacity  < 0.999
                   || cluster_fill_opacity < 0.999
Four COSMETIC knobs. `effects_css` is emitted only when that is true.

WHAT IS INSIDE effects_css (lib.rs:3019+) that is NOT cosmetic:
  .fm-node-border-dashed {stroke-dasharray: 6 4}   <- the ONLY thing that shows a C4 System_Ext
                                                      is external rather than internal
  .fm-node-block-beta-space {opacity: 0}           <- the ONLY thing that makes a block-beta
                                                      `space` cell invisible
  .fm-node-block-beta rect/... {fill,stroke}       <- block-beta node fills
  .fm-node-highlighted {stroke-width, font-weight} <- node emphasis
So disabling gradients and setting both opacities to 1.0 removes SEMANTIC ENCODING, not polish. The element still carries `class="… fm-node-user-c4-external fm-node-border-dashed"`; there is simply no rule behind it, and a marker class with no rule is invisible — indistinguishable from having no marker at all.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A CONFIG EDGE CASE. `golden_render_config()` in crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs — the config ALL 37 byte goldens are rendered and pinned with — sets exactly those four knobs to the effects-off values (`node_gradients: false, glow_enabled: false, cluster_fill_opacity: 1.0, inactive_opacity: 1.0`). Therefore:
  * every committed C4 golden pins a picture in which an external system renders IDENTICALLY to an internal one;
  * every committed block-beta golden pins one in which `space` cells are not invisible.
The byte corpus is structurally incapable of catching a regression in these markers, because it never renders them. Measured directly: `.fm-node-border-dashed` occurs 6 times in the default-config render of c4_basic (5 selector positions + the class use) and exactly ONCE in the committed c4_basic.svg (the class use alone).

MEASURED EVIDENCE, from the guard:
  email is marked external by ["fm-node-user-c4-external", "fm-node-border-dashed"], none of which
  is defined in the stylesheet this config emits, so it renders identically to an internal system

ACCEPTANCE GATE, named and populated: remove the `#[ignore]` from
    c4_external_marker_survives_the_config_the_goldens_pin   (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs)
and it must pass. It currently FAILS with the message above — verified under `--ignored`, so it is a real specification and not a stub. The live sibling `c4_external_systems_are_visually_distinct_from_internal_ones` covers the shipping default config, passes today, and must stay green regardless of how this is fixed.

LIKELY FIX SHAPE — and note there are two defensible ones, so this needs a decision rather than a reflex:
  (a) Split `effects_css` into a cosmetic half (still gated on the four knobs) and a SEMANTIC half
      (border-dashed / block-beta / block-beta-space / highlighted) emitted unconditionally, or
      gated on whether the diagram actually uses those classes. This is the fix that makes the
      goldens meaningful, because the golden config would then render the markers.
  (b) Change `golden_render_config` to leave effects on. This makes the corpus cover the markers but
      moves every one of the 37 golden hashes — a large, legitimate GOLDEN-CHANGE that would need a
      semantic diff review, and it leaves the underlying coupling in place for real users.
(a) is preferred: it fixes the product rather than the test, and (b) can then be considered separately.

NOTE ON SCOPE: `.fm-node-inactive { opacity: … }` genuinely IS gated correctly — it exists to express `inactive_opacity` — so this is not "un-gate the whole block". The bug is that unrelated semantic rules were parked in the same conditional string.

RELATED: bd-7ute (block-beta) is in the family whose `space` invisibility is affected here; anyone working that bead should know the golden it is measured against does not render the `opacity: 0` rule at all.
close_reason: Landed 1abca2b6, fix (a) from the bead. effects_css split: inactive_opacity_css / cluster_fill_opacity_css stay gated on their knobs, SEMANTIC_MARKER_CSS (border-dashed, block-beta, block-beta-space, highlighted, border-double) no longer is. Emission order unchanged, so an effects-enabled render is byte-identical. Dead weight still nil, on a stronger test than the knobs: strip_unused_state_css drops the region when the rendered BODY uses none of the five classes, and its bounds now fall back independently so the effects-off case is bounded rather than skipped. Direct minified flowchart path returns before that scan, so it answers from the IR via ir_may_emit_state_classes, which SHARES scan_node_class_keywords with the renderer rather than restating it. GATE: c4_external_marker_survives_the_config_the_goldens_pin un-ignored; the shipping-config sibling stays green; added flowchart_state_marker_has_a_rule_under_the_golden_config for the direct path with both halves (marked flowchart gets the rule, unmarked one carries no dead region). CAUGHT UNPROMPTED: golden/flowchart_classdef pinned fm-node-highlighted on node A with no stroke-width: 2.4 anywhere — the same defect in a second diagram type. GOLDEN-CHANGE: exactly 3 cases (c4_basic, block_basic, flowchart_classdef), one 802-byte CSS region inserted each, nothing removed, no geometry; the other 34 goldens byte-identical. cargo test --workspace 0 failures; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: Five gantt directives are parsed into the IR and read by nothing: dateFormat, axisFormat, tickInterval, todayMarker, weekday
description: SAME DEFECT CLASS AS bd-f3tc - parsed, held in the IR, read by no consumer, so the user's directive silently does nothing. Found by sweeping every pub field of every Ir*Meta struct in fm-core against fm-render-svg, fm-render-canvas, fm-render-term AND fm-layout; exactly five fields are referenced by none of them, and all five are IrGanttMeta: date_format, axis_format, tick_interval, today_marker_style, weekday_start. WHAT EACH ONE COSTS THE USER, in mermaid terms: axisFormat is the sharpest - mermaid formats the time axis labels with that strftime-style string, so 'axisFormat %m/%d' should produce 01/15 and we emit whatever our own tick labelling chooses; tickInterval controls axis tick spacing (1week, 1month) and is ignored, so a year-long chart gets the same tick density as a week-long one; todayMarker styles or disables the 'today' line; weekday sets which day a week starts on, which moves every week boundary; dateFormat is the input parse format and is the one most likely already handled implicitly by our date parsing - it should be CONFIRMED rather than assumed, since a user writing an unusual dateFormat would otherwise get silently misparsed dates rather than an error. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is structural rather than effort: the axis tick LABEL text is built in fm-layout (LayoutAxisTick.label, lib.rs:2201), not in the renderer - fm-render-svg only draws tick.label at lib.rs:4017 - so implementing axisFormat/tickInterval/weekday means editing crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs, which is under an exclusive Agent Mail lease held by StormyFalcon. GOLDEN EXPOSURE: gantt_basic.mmd declares 'dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD' and nothing else, so four of the five directives have no golden coverage at all and the fifth is only exercised in its default form. Whoever implements these should add a fixture per directive rather than extending gantt_basic, since the point is that each one changes the output independently.
close_reason: Landed 45457d5e. Three of the four remaining directives implemented in the gantt layout arm: axisFormat (d3-style strftime writer, unknown specifiers verbatim), tickInterval (ticks only on period boundaries, with a first-day fallback when a span crosses none) and weekday (moves the weekly boundary). dateFormat was already refuted as honoured; todayMarker split out as bd-j0va because it is its own element and carries a wall-clock hazard. Every test carries a control separating 'accepted' from 'took effect'. No golden moves. Gates: fm-layout --lib 501 passed (hz2), FM_GOLDEN_CASE=gantt_basic 1 passed (vmi1149989).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE, and it changes what can be implemented. Filed as bd-trsd with the measurement.

This bead says of axisFormat: 'mermaid formats the time axis labels with that strftime-style string, so axisFormat %m/%d should produce 01/15 and we emit whatever our own tick labelling chooses.'

We do not emit whatever our own tick labelling chooses. WE EMIT NO AXIS AT ALL.

Measured on this repo's own committed golden. crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/gantt_basic.mmd declares 'section Core' and '2026-01-01'; the COMPLETE <text> content of the checked-in gantt_basic.svg is:

    Roadmap | Design | Build

No date anywhere in the document, no section name, and the full class inventory is {fm-diagram-title, fm-gantt-dependency, fm-gantt-task, fm-gantt-task-label}. There is no tick, no grid line, no section band and no section label in shipped gantt output.

WHY: fm-render-svg lib.rs:3959 dispatches gantt to render_gantt_svg and RETURNS at :3961, while the generic extensions.bands loop (:3984) and extensions.axis_ticks loop (:4014) sit below that return. The one diagram type whose layout fills both lists is the one type that can never reach either. This bead's own note -- 'fm-render-svg only draws tick.label at lib.rs:4017' -- is correct about where the code is, but that line is unreachable for gantt.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: axisFormat, tickInterval and weekday are ALL downstream of an axis that does not exist. Implementing them now would format labels that no document contains, and their tests could only assert on LayoutAxisTick.label in the layout struct -- never on rendered output. bd-trsd therefore BLOCKS the axis half of this bead and should land first.

STILL INDEPENDENTLY ACTIONABLE HERE: dateFormat (input parsing, and this bead is right that it should be CONFIRMED rather than assumed) and todayMarker (its own element, not an axis tick).

I am not claiming this bead -- recording the correction so whoever takes it does not start with the axis directives and discover this halfway through.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
REFUTED, one of the five: dateFormat IS honoured. This bead is four directives, not five.

This bead said dateFormat "is the one most likely already handled implicitly by our
date parsing -- it should be CONFIRMED rather than assumed, since a user writing an
unusual dateFormat would otherwise get silently misparsed dates rather than an
error". Confirmed by experiment, and the answer is that it works.

MEASURED with the shipping binary. My first attempt was NOT discriminating and I
discarded it: 'dateFormat DD-MM-YYYY' with '15-01-2024' produces the same geometry
as the ISO control, but it must, because 15 is not a valid month -- both readings
agree. A date pair where the two readings genuinely disagree is needed.

    gantt
        dateFormat DD-MM-YYYY
        section S
        Later   :a1, 01-02-2024, 1d
        Earlier :a2, 02-01-2024, 1d

Under the DECLARED day-first format, Later is 1 Feb and Earlier is 2 Jan, so
Earlier must sit to the LEFT. Under a wrong month-first reading the order inverts.
Rendered:

    Earlier  x = 92
    Later    x = 1532
    gap = 1440px = 30 days at 48px/day, and 2 Jan -> 1 Feb is exactly 30 days.

Day-first was applied, and the spacing is exactly right. Not a near miss.

THE MECHANISM, so the unread field is not mistaken for a dropped input.
mermaid_parser.rs:5971 normalizes each task date with the DECLARED format:

    normalize_gantt_date_with_format(token, date_format.unwrap_or("YYYY-MM-DD"))
        .or_else(|| normalize_gantt_date_with_format(token, "YYYY-MM-DD"))

so the directive is consumed at PARSE time and the IR carries dates already
normalized to ISO. IrGanttMeta::date_format is therefore a vestigial RECORD of
what the user wrote, not an input anybody failed to read. The sweep that produced
this bead looked for reads of the field and correctly found none -- the inference
that the directive does nothing is what does not follow.

⚠️ NOTE THE FALLBACK at :5972. A date that does not match the declared format is
retried as ISO rather than reported. So this bead's stated worry -- "silently
misparsed dates rather than an error" -- is still live as a DIAGNOSTICS question,
just not as a "directive ignored" one: 'dateFormat DD-MM-YYYY' with an ISO date in
the body is silently accepted. That is a much smaller and different bead than the
one filed here, and worth splitting out rather than folding in.

WHAT REMAINS IN THIS BEAD: axisFormat, tickInterval, weekday (all blocked behind
bd-trsd, since there is no axis to label) and todayMarker (independent, renderer).

title: Unreferenced fm-node-gradient def on all four dedicated chart renderers
description:
SECOND INSTANCE of the dead-<defs> class bd-a6uk closed, found by the generic invariant test that bead added rather than by inspection. That is the point of the invariant: it generalises.

MEASURED at default config, one fm-cli render per type, counting <defs> ids that never reappear as url(#id):

  flowchart LR       ids=2  dead: -
  sequenceDiagram    ids=2  dead: -
  classDiagram       ids=2  dead: -
  stateDiagram-v2    ids=2  dead: -
  erDiagram          ids=2  dead: -
  journey            ids=1  dead: -
  mindmap            ids=1  dead: -
  gitGraph           ids=1  dead: -
  timeline           ids=1  dead: -
  gantt              ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient
  pie                ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient
  quadrantChart      ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient
  xychart-beta       ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient

Four of thirteen types, and it is 283 bytes each — bigger than bd-a6uk's 166:

  gantt         5278 bytes total, 283 in the def = 5.4%, url refs 0
  pie           6438 bytes total, 283 = 4.4%, url refs 0
  quadrantChart 6761 bytes total, 283 = 4.2%, url refs 0
  xychart-beta  8070 bytes total, 283 = 4.2%, url refs 0

MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than incidental. node_gradient_svg returns Some purely on config.node_gradients (default ON) and the def is streamed into the gradients slot at lib.rs:3719. But these four types are each handled by a DEDICATED renderer that returns early, at lib.rs:3798 xychart, 3817 pie, 3825 quadrant, 3832 gantt, and none of them reaches the generic node path where every fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)" is written. So the def is emitted for a consumer that is unreachable by construction on these types, not merely absent from this fixture.

FIX SHAPE. Gate the gradient def on the same condition the dispatch uses: suppress it when the render will take one of the four dedicated chart paths. The predicate is computable at defs time because it reads only ir (xy_chart_meta / pie_meta with non-empty slices / quadrant_meta / Gantt+gantt_meta).

THE GATES MUST BE IN LOCKSTEP, and this is the whole risk. There are FIVE conditions to keep in agreement — four dispatch branches plus the new defs gate — which is exactly the shape that produced the fast-path-drops-a-feature family (bd-678053a) and this bead's own predecessor. Extract ONE predicate used by both sides rather than restating the conditions.

THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE ONE, and bd-a6uk's invariant does NOT yet catch it: if one of these renderers later starts referencing the gradient, suppressing the def yields url(#fm-node-gradient) pointing at nothing — invalid SVG, unpainted shapes. The existing test only asserts declared-but-unreferenced. It must be made BIDIRECTIONAL (also: no url(#id) may reference an id absent from <defs>) and run across diagram types, or this fix installs a silent failure mode.

Cross-checked so the next lane does not redo it: no undeclared url(#...) reference exists on any of the four types today, so the bidirectional assertion is satisfiable as written.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED FOR NOW: extend the existing strip_unused_markers output post-pass, which already collects every url(#id) in the finished document and would be exact by construction. Rejected because it early-returns Some(0) when the document has no <marker (true for exactly these chart types), and because its return value feeds the memoized CSS post-pass feature key — restructuring it risks cache correctness another lane built (212a285, e91eb82) for 283 bytes. Revisit if a third instance of this class appears, at which point the post-pass becomes the cheaper total fix.

EXPECTED GOLDEN IMPACT: gantt_basic, pie_basic and quadrant_basic are golden cases, but golden_svg_test pins node_gradients: false, so they never emit the def. Verify rather than assume.
close_reason:
Fixed by 569261ef.

FIX: two gates, one truth. takes_dedicated_chart_renderer is now the single source for the xychart/pie/quadrant/gantt dispatch condition, and gradient_def_emitted is the single answer to 'is the def actually in this document', read by BOTH the <defs> slot and print_css. The bead asked for one predicate rather than five restatements; that is what landed.

MEASURED, default config, one fm-cli render per type, before -> after:
  gantt         5278 -> 4910  (-368, 7.0%)
  pie           6438 -> 6076  (-362, 5.6%)
  quadrantChart 6761 -> 6399  (-362, 5.4%)
  xychart-beta  8070 -> 7708  (-362, 4.5%)
  flowchart (3 nodes)  8513 -> 8513, verified BYTE-IDENTICAL programmatically
Per type: 283 bytes of <linearGradient> def plus 79 bytes of print CSS.

SCOPE GREW BY ONE ITEM DURING THE FIX, and it was the right call rather than a separate bead: gating the def alone left bd-ccni's '#fm-node-gradient stop { ... }' print rule selecting an id no longer in the document -- 79 more dead bytes, and a cleaner-cut dead selector than before. print_css's parameter is renamed node_gradients -> gradient_def_emitted because that rename IS the fix: on these four types the two predicates differ, which is precisely what nobody had noticed.

THE BEAD'S CENTRAL WARNING WAS HONOURED. It said the dangerous direction is a url(#...) with no def, and that bd-a6uk's invariant did not yet catch it. It does now: defs_and_url_references_agree_across_diagram_types is BIDIRECTIONAL and swept across 13 parsed diagram types, and also asserts no CSS rule styles an absent def id. Cases are built by PARSING real Mermaid rather than hand-assembling metadata, because a hand-built IR can miss the condition a dispatch branch actually tests (pie slices / xy series non-empty) -- which is the gate under test.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all three directions measured:
  gate reverted to unconditional -> 'gantt: defs declared but never referenced: [fm-node-gradient]' plus 'gantt: gradient def and its referrer must appear together'
  gate INVERTED, suppressing the def where it IS used -> 'flowchart: url(#...) references with no matching def: [fm-node-gradient, fm-node-gradient]'
So the dangerous direction is genuinely detected, not merely asserted. File restored byte-identically (diff -q) after each control.

LOCKSTEP GUARD for the drift risk the bead flagged: the four dispatch branches keep their own meta bindings and cannot literally call the predicate, so dedicated_chart_predicate_matches_gradient_referrer_presence pins it to observed behaviour instead -- true exactly when no url(#fm-node-gradient) referrer is emitted, and the def present iff its referrer is. Changing a dispatch condition without the predicate fails the test.

DEFERRED, named rather than quietly dropped: render_scene_document_with_ir also emits the print block, and the only gradient-def emission anywhere is the site gated here, so that print rule may be dead on the scene path too. NOT fixed: I have not established what the scene path emits, and guessing there is exactly how the opposite (dangling-reference) defect gets introduced. Worth a follow-up bead if anyone touches that path.

ALTERNATIVE REJECTED as the bead anticipated: extending strip_unused_markers would be exact by construction but early-returns when the document has no <marker -- true for exactly these four types -- and its return value feeds the memoized CSS post-pass key, so restructuring risks cache correctness another lane built (212a285, e91eb82) for 362 bytes. Revisit at instance three, at which point the post-pass becomes the cheaper total fix.

BEAD PREDICTION CONFIRMED: no golden moved. golden_svg_test pins node_gradients: false, so gantt_basic/pie_basic/quadrant_basic never emitted the def. No bless, no GOLDEN-CHANGE note.

NO LEDGER ROW: output-correctness fix, no timing asserted anywhere.

GATES: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 40/40 suites green, 0 failures; fm-render-svg 279 pass / 0 fail; ubs exit 0 with no finding in the new code; cargo fmt --check clean on every hunk this commit authored. Pushed to main and master at 569261ef.

title: stateDiagram: a composite state's inner [*] is merged with the top-level [*], creating transitions the source never declared and swelling the composite's cluster to engulf unrelated states
description:
Found by bd-iicc round 7 (stateDiagram semantic guards). ONE root cause, two visible symptoms. They are filed together because a CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT proved the second is caused by the first rather than merely co-occurring with it.

SYMPTOM 1 — TRANSITIONS THE SOURCE NEVER DECLARED. golden/state_composite.mmd declares
    [*] --> Idle                         (top level)
    state Processing { [*] --> Validating ; ... }   (inside the composite)
Those are two different pseudo-states in two different scopes. The render collapses them into ONE node: exactly one group with data-id="__state_start", which then emits BOTH edges:
    fm-edge-0  __state_start points to Idle
    fm-edge-1  __state_start points to Validating
So the picture asserts the machine can begin directly in `Validating`, bypassing `Idle` and the whole entry into `Processing`. Reachability is the one thing a state diagram exists to communicate. The same collapse happens at the terminal: a single `__state_end` receives `Formatting` (declared inside the composite), plus `Error` and `Complete` (both outer).

SYMPTOM 2 — THE COMPOSITE'S CONTAINER ENGULFS THE MACHINE. The `Processing` cluster renders at
x 136.62..890.21, y 92.00..1242.00 and geometrically contains EIGHT states that `state Processing { … }` does not declare:
    __state_start, Idle, __state_end, Error, fork_state, join_state, TaskB, Complete
A reader sees a composite state that swallows almost the entire diagram.

THE EXPERIMENT THAT LINKED THEM, and it is cheap to repeat. Render a composite that declares NO inner `[*]`:
    stateDiagram-v2
      [*] --> Idle
      state Processing { Validating --> Computing }
      Idle --> Processing : start
      Processing --> Done
      Done --> [*]
Result: cluster at x 92..335.65, y 92..449, containing exactly `Validating` and `Computing`; `Idle` (y 657), `Done` (y 1030), `__state_start` (cy 527) and `__state_end` (cy 1228.5) all fall OUTSIDE it. The cluster is correct. So the swell in state_composite is caused by the pseudo-state merge pulling the shared start/end nodes — and the outer states positioned near them — into the composite's member set. Not a hypothesis: the only difference between the two inputs is the inner `[*]`.

Derivation of the swollen box, for whoever fixes it (cluster_padding = 52):
    x_min 188.62 - 52 = 136.62   (fork/join/Complete column)
    x_max 838.21 + 52 = 890.21   (Formatting right edge)
    y_min 144    - 52 = 92       (__state_start top: cy 154 - r 10)
    y_max 1190   + 52 = 1242     (__state_end bottom: cy 1178 + r 12)
i.e. the member set spans both pseudo-states and the outer fork/join/Complete chain.

ACCEPTANCE GATE, named and populated — BOTH must go green:
    state_pseudo_states_are_scoped_to_their_composite
    composite_state_cluster_contains_only_its_declared_members
(crates/fm-cli/tests/golden_svg_test.rs). Both currently FAIL, verified under `--ignored`, so they are real specifications and not stubs. The first asserts that no rendered node is the source of both a top-level `[*]` transition and a composite-scoped one; the second reads composite membership FROM THE FIXTURE's block structure, so neither can be satisfied by re-blessing. If fixing the scoping does NOT fix the cluster, the second guard is what says so.

Root cause: the parser interned every [*] source as the global __state_start and every [*] target as __state_end, so a composite's inner [*] and the diagram's own collapsed onto one node each. scoped_pseudo_state_id appends the composite's lookup key (from the same state_stack begin_state_cluster uses, so nested composites get the full path); top-level [*] keeps the bare id, so state_basic and 35 other cases are byte-identical.

title: strip_unused_state_css: ~20 full-document scans, single-pass them (byte-identical; helps DEFAULT profile too)
description:
PROFILE-DRIVEN. Symbolized perf record on wide_8x16 (bc56f72) showed frames present ONLY under the lean profile: <&str as Pattern>::is_contained_in 6.96%, StrSearcher 4.93%, String::replace_range 1.41%, __memmove_avx_unaligned_erms 7.00% (vs 2.85% default).
