  * 5x STATE_CLASSES .contains() over the body
  * 8x 'fm-node-accent-N' .contains() over the body (std::array::from_fn at lib.rs:406 -- note the comment above it claims a single scan, but the code is 8 separate contains())
  * 8x 'var(--fm-accent-N)' .contains() over the WHOLE svg (lib.rs:434)
str::contains on an ABSENT needle scans the entire document. Absent is the common case, so this is worst-case O(n*k) with k~20.

THE GATE IS PROFILE-DEPENDENT: it measures OUTPUT BYTES, and the lean profile shrinks output ~31%. So mid-size diagrams fall INTO the pass only under lean:
  wide_8x16:      default 134,629 B (skips) / lean 93,077 B (RUNS)  -> lean/default 1.330x
  cyclic_scc_100: default 107,649 B (skips) / lean 73,916 B (RUNS)  -> lean/default 1.092x
MECHANISM PROVEN with a diagnostic build (cap set to 0, pass disabled for both profiles, same instr A/B protocol):
  wide_8x16 1.330x -> 0.945x ; cyclic_scc_100 1.092x -> 0.978x ; wide_12x24 (control, both skip) 0.937x -> 0.937x unchanged.

All ~20 needles share two prefixes -- 'fm-node-' (covers fm-node-inactive / block-beta / highlighted / border-dashed / border-double / accent-1..8) and 'var(--fm-accent-'. Build one memchr::memmem::Finder for each and collect every hit in ONE traversal, reading the discriminating suffix at each match. Byte-identical: used[n] must be true iff the exact substring occurs, same as today.

Default-profile items that pay it today: flowchart_small_10 (13 KB), flowchart_medium_100 (72 KB), sequence_20 (43 KB), class_50 (46 KB), state_40 (35 KB), er_40 (52 KB), and every revision of edit_trace_60x20 (the live-preview workload). The single-scan fix is the byte-identical one. Keep the 100 KB cap; just make the pass cheap.

ALSO: the replace_range calls (lib.rs:381/414/440) each memmove the document tail. Once the scans are single-pass, consider collecting all strip ranges first and doing ONE rebuild (the pattern strip_unused_markers already uses: 'Single O(n) rebuild (no per-marker rescans)').

title: Mermaid init nodeSpacing/rankSpacing were unsupported; wire them to the layout hints
description:
The follow-up bd-d25j called cheap, and it was — the meta hint fields it added took the second dialect
with no new machinery, which is the payoff for naming them `node_spacing`/`rank_spacing` rather than
`dot_nodesep`.

WHAT WAS MISSING. Mermaid's own `%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 60, "rankSpacing": 90}}}%%`
was unsupported: `rg nodeSpacing` found nothing anywhere in fm-parser or fm-core. Both keys fell into
the flowchart-config `other =>` arm and were reported as "Unsupported flowchart config key". So this
is a MERMAID feature gap closed, not just DOT symmetry — a user writing standard Mermaid init spacing
got a warning and default gaps.

  flowchart.nodeSpacing -> meta.node_spacing (and init.config.node_spacing)
  flowchart.rankSpacing -> meta.rank_spacing (and init.config.rank_spacing)

WRITTEN TO BOTH PLACES DELIBERATELY: the init record so `parse --json` still reports the directive the
author gave, and the meta hint because that is the half fm-layout actually reads. Recording it only in
`init.config` would leave a value nothing consumes — the trap this session has hit repeatedly
(bd-hc5y's fontcolor, and `flowchart_curve`, which is still exactly that: parsed, stored, read by
nobody).

NO CONVERSION HERE, unlike DOT. Mermaid's numbers are already layout units; DOT's `nodesep`/`ranksep`
are inches and are converted at 72/inch in the DOT parser. Keeping the conversion in each dialect's
parser is why the shared meta field can stay unit-agnostic.

A NEGATIVE SPACING IS REFUSED, NOT CLAMPED. Reading `nodeSpacing: -10` as 0 would collapse the
diagram while looking like it worked, so it produces a typed config error. Fractional requests round
(60.6 -> 61) for the same reason the DOT path rounds: flooring would silently shrink every request.

FOUR STRUCTS had to agree, which is the only awkward part and worth recording for the next person
adding an init option: `MermaidConfig` (the intermediate parse target) and `MermaidInitConfig` (the IR
record) are separate types mapped field-by-field in `to_init_parse`, and both have explicit struct
literals plus a hand-written `Default`. The compiler caught each omission in turn, but a new option
touches four places, not one.

TESTS: 4 parser unit tests (both keys reaching BOTH the init record and the meta hints, an
absent-hint control, negative and non-numeric refusal, fractional rounding) plus an end-to-end test
asserting a Mermaid `rankSpacing` directive widens the drawn rank gap — the DOT-side equivalent
already existed from bd-d25j, so both dialects are now proven to move geometry.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p fm-core --lib -> 0 (408 passed); cargo test -p fm-parser --lib -> 0 (505
passed); cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli -> 0 (26 targets); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings -> 0.

NO GOLDEN MOVED, and this needed checking harder than any previous bead in this run, because the
change is on the MERMAID path and the golden corpus is Mermaid. It holds because no golden fixture
uses nodeSpacing or rankSpacing, so every fixture's hints stay None and `spacing_with_source_hints`
stays an identity function for them. Both golden suites pass unblessed. The one dirty golden file
(layout_checksums.json) remains another lane's pre-existing working-tree change from before this
session (last commit a656acc4, bd-f3tc) and has never been staged by me.

STILL NOT WIRED: `flowchart_curve` is parsed and stored and read by nothing — the same shape of gap
this bead just closed for spacing, and the natural next candidate if a renderer/layout consumer for
curve style exists or is added. DOT's `splines` would then have a real target too.
close_reason: Landed; flowchart_curve recorded as the remaining parsed-but-unread field

title: Requalify 20 rows refused by corrected null gate clause 3
description:
Adopting the corrected A/A null gate (bench: eaa77154) added clause 3: every null MEDIAN must be within 2% of 1.0. Re-certification over the artifact history: 88 rows re-scored, 68 unchanged, 20 previously-passing rows refused, 0 newly decidable (so 0 new wins, 0 new losses -- the change can only subtract decidability).

The 20 refused rows are INCONCLUSIVE, not regressions. Per harness doctrine they must be re-run in an assigned quiet window; never re-pin or retune to force a pass.

Highest priority: ci_batch_500@t8 (5875x, fm null median bias 3.154%) takes the t=8 row of the certified 64-thread CI sweep out of certification. Requalifying it needs a full thread sweep under the exclusive trj booking (--exclusive-host-claim trj-booking:<id>) plus host-wide quiescence; the other six widths survive at 0.464-1.424% bias.

Worst bias overall is flowchart_small_10 at 11.765%, from a loaded-host --reps-scale 0.3 smoke run -- clause 3 correctly identifying an unfit measurement environment rather than a bad effect.

CAVEAT worth acting on: clause 3's statistic is itself noisy. Across three runs of the same ELF on two cores at low load, sequence_20's null median bias moved 0.299% -> 1.289% -> 1.990%, landing 0.01pp from the threshold. Rows near 2% will flip run to run, so requalification should use full reps on a quiet host, and a row that lands within ~0.2pp of the bound should be re-run rather than recorded either way.

Full list in .benchmarks/headtohead/recertification/recertification-clause3-1785400000000.json

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ARCHIVE ANALYSIS OF THE CAVEAT THIS BEAD RAISES. No re-runs, no re-pinning, no retuning - the freeze forbids measurement and the bead forbids the other two. Clause 3's statistic is stored on every row as null_control.median, so it is recomputable from .benchmarks/headtohead/.

QUESTION: how much does the statistic move when nothing changes? The bead already suspected this from sequence_20 moving 0.299 -> 1.289 -> 1.990 across three runs.

METHOD: grouped by (case, engine, elf_sha256, thread_count_requested) - deliberately STRICT, since a looser key pools thread widths and binaries that are not the same run and would inflate the spread. Scored only groups with >=3 repeats. 60 such configurations exist.

RESULT:
  26 configurations pass every repeat (always <2%)
  30 configurations STRADDLE 2% - the verdict flips between repeats of the same config
   1 configuration fails every repeat: edit_trace_500x1000 / frankenmermaid, 4.171-6.279 (a real effect)

So clause 3 discriminates at the extremes and cannot decide the middle. For half the corpus the statistic's own run-to-run range crosses the threshold it is compared against:
  flowchart_small_10 mermaid-js thr=1  n=7   0.711 .. 11.765   spread 11.05 pp
  edit_trace_200x200 frankenmermaid    n=10  0.105 ..  5.171   spread  5.07 pp
  doc_build_40       frankenmermaid    n=6   0.177 ..  5.239   spread  5.06 pp
  ci_equiv_512       frankenmermaid t1 n=10  0.007 ..  4.090   spread  4.08 pp

THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY REFUSAL IS INSIDE ITS OWN NOISE BAND. ci_batch_500@t8 was refused at 3.154%. The archive holds 47 ci_batch_500/frankenmermaid rows spanning 0.000-4.008%. 3.154 sits inside that range, so the refusal is not evidence of an unfit environment - it is a draw. That does not certify the row; it makes the refusal UNINFORMATIVE, which is worth knowing before spending an exclusive trj booking on it.

CAVEAT, stated because it weakens exactly that claim: those 47 rows carry NO elf_sha256 and NO thread_count_requested in storage, so they could not be separated by binary or width. Their 0.000-4.008 range pools configurations the strict key separates elsewhere, and the true single-config spread may be narrower. The missing provenance is its own finding - a row that cannot say which binary produced it cannot be requalified from the archive at all.

WHAT FOLLOWS: evaluate clause 3 over REPEATS (k-of-n, or a median across repeats) rather than one observation. That keeps the discrimination the extremes show - 26 clean, 1 biased - without refusing thirty configurations on a coin flip. The rule is not wrong about the statistic; it is applied to a single draw of a statistic that needs several.

And several of the 20 refusals may be requalifiable from STORED DATA by pooling existing repeats, before any exclusive booking is spent.

THIS REQUALIFIES NOTHING BY ITSELF. It is evidence about the INSTRUMENT, not about any row's effect. Adopting a k-of-n rule is a gate change, which by this project's doctrine needs its own evidence and must not ride along on this note.

Full write-up: docs/parked-levers/bd_w91d_clause3_is_a_coin_flip_for_half_the_corpus.md

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SCORER LANDED, AND ITS k-OF-n VIEW DISCRIMINATES INSIDE THE STRADDLING SET (commit below). scripts/clause3_repeat_scorer.py, runnable now: it reads .benchmarks only, needs no host and no build, and its self-test runs in CI.

Run against the archive today (53 configurations with >=3 repeats under its strict key):
  26 always below 2%
   1 always at or above: edit_trace_500x1000 / frankenmermaid, 4/4 repeats, 4.171-6.279% -- a real effect
  26 straddle

THE NEW INFORMATION IS THE COUNT, not the range. My earlier pass could only say "straddles"; k-of-n separates cases the 2% rule treats identically:

  ci_batch_500  / frankenmermaid        6/47 exceed (13%)   range 0.000-4.008%
  ci_equiv_512  / frankenmermaid t=128  4/8  exceed (50%)   range 0.184-3.569%
  ci_equiv_512  / frankenmermaid t=1    1/10 exceed (10%)   range 0.007-4.090%
  doc_build_40  / frankenmermaid        1/6  exceed (17%)   range 0.177-5.239%
  flowchart_small_10 / mermaid-js t=1   2/7  exceed (29%)   range 0.711-11.765%

ci_batch_500 -- this bead's stated highest priority -- exceeds in 6 of 47 stored repeats. The refusal that took t=8 out of certification is roughly a 1-in-8 draw, not a property of the configuration. ci_equiv_512 at t=128 exceeds in half its repeats and is genuinely marginal. A single-observation rule cannot tell those apart, and requalification effort spent on them should not be equal.

COUNT DISCREPANCY, stated so nobody reconciles two numbers of mine by guessing: my ad-hoc pass reported 60 scored configurations, the scorer reports 53. The keys differ slightly (the earlier one also folded worker_threads). The SCORER is the reproducible one; prefer its output and ignore my earlier 60.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it reports, never gates and never certifies. Adopting a k-of-n rule is a gate change that needs its own evidence, and no row should be quoted because it appeared in this output. It also refuses --min-repeats below 3, since fewer cannot distinguish a draw from an effect.

PROVENANCE CAVEAT it prints itself: rows lacking elf_sha256 or thread_count_requested pool runs that are not the same run, so their ranges are UPPER BOUNDS. run.mjs now stamps both (583d1c3b); rows stored before that cannot be recovered.

title: Fix npm package: publish @frankenmermaid/core to npm or correct README
description:
## Problem
The README prominently tells users:
```bash
npm install @frankenmermaid/core
```
However, this package is NOT published on npm. Verified 2026-04-09: `https://registry.npmjs.org/@frankenmermaid/core` returns HTTP 404.

The WASM build IS working: `pkg/` contains `frankenmermaid_bg.wasm` (1.0MB), `frankenmermaid.js` (53KB), `frankenmermaid.d.ts` (3.1KB), and a valid `package.json` declaring `@frankenmermaid/core` v0.1.0. The build pipeline (build-wasm.sh) works. Only the npm publish step is missing.

## Options (choose one)
**Option A (preferred): Publish to npm**
1. Ensure `pkg/package.json` metadata is complete (author, keywords, repository all look good already).
2. Run `wasm-pack publish` or `cd pkg && npm publish --access public` (scoped package needs --access public).
3. Verify post-publish: `npm info @frankenmermaid/core`.
4. Set up CI to auto-publish on release tags (add to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

**Option B: Correct README until ready to publish**
1. Replace `npm install @frankenmermaid/core` with honest instructions: "Build from source: `./build-wasm.sh && cp -r pkg/ your-project/`"
2. Add a "Coming soon to npm" note.

## Why This Matters
This is the #1 credibility gap found in the reality check. A user who follows the README's install instructions on the FIRST LINE will get an error. First impressions matter enormously for open source adoption.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `npm info @frankenmermaid/core` returns valid metadata, OR README install instructions are corrected to match reality.
- If published: CI workflow includes npm publish step on tagged releases.
- If corrected: README clearly states the package is not yet on npm and provides working alternative.
close_reason: Corrected README to honestly state npm package is not yet published, with working build-from-source and GitHub Pages alternatives.

title: Flaky sibling of bd-u6z4: nodemap_performance_under_load asserts wall-clock deadlines too
description:
SIBLING of bd-u6z4, in the same file, found because closing that bead was premature.

bd-u6z4 fixed `fxhash_faster_than_siphash`, verified with three consecutive clean `cargo test --workspace` runs, and I closed it. The very next workspace run red on `fxhash_resilience` again — a different test in the same binary, carrying the identical defect:

    assert!(insert_time.as_millis() < 1000, ...);
    assert!(lookup_time.as_millis() < 1000, ...);

in `nodemap_performance_under_load`. Two more absolute wall-clock deadlines, on a host that during a workspace run has dozens of test binaries across every core. Same defect class, same failure mode, same file — and my three clean runs simply had not happened to hit it.

WHAT THE TEST ACTUALLY CONTAINS. It inserts 10,000 entries into a NodeMap and reads them all back, asserting `map.get(&IrNodeId(i)) == Some(&(i * 2))` for every one. THAT is the test: it proves the map is correct at a size where hashing behaviour matters. The two deadlines assert nothing about the code — only about how busy the machine is.

WHY NOT A RELATIVE ASSERTION HERE, unlike bd-u6z4. That fix worked because the test had two arms measured back-to-back, so contention slowed both together and the RATIO survived. This test has one arm. There is nothing to compare against, so there is no load-robust timing property to assert — inventing a second arm would be writing a different test. The deadlines should simply go, leaving the correctness assertions that were always the substance.

A genuine performance guard for NodeMap belongs in a bench under this repo's A/A-null discipline, where a loaded host is controlled for rather than assumed away. It does not belong in a unit test as a millisecond budget.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. `nodemap_performance_under_load` contains no absolute wall-clock deadline.
2. Its correctness assertions (all 10,000 lookups) are unchanged.
3. The measured timings are still reported for documentation value.
4. `cargo test --workspace` run repeatedly under full concurrency does not red on this binary.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING, and the reason this is filed rather than folded silently into bd-u6z4: "three clean runs" is evidence about a flake's FREQUENCY, not proof of its absence. When a defect is a CLASS rather than a single site, the right check is to grep the file for the pattern — which would have found this immediately — not to re-run until green.
close_reason:
Landed c6353f99. Both fxhash_resilience sites fixed; the third site in the class is deliberately retained and recorded below.

HOW THIS WAS FOUND, which is the part worth keeping: closing bd-u6z4 after three consecutive clean workspace runs was premature. The next run red on the same binary via a DIFFERENT test with the identical defect. Three clean runs is evidence about a flake's FREQUENCY, not proof of its absence — for a defect CLASS the right check is a grep, and rg 'as_millis() < ' found FIVE sites across three tests, not the one I had fixed.

FIXED: nodemap_performance_under_load (2 sites, 1000ms) and graceful_degradation_under_collisions (2 sites, 100ms — the most fragile of the family). Both asserted absolute millisecond budgets on a host running dozens of test binaries across every core. The substance of each is untouched because the deadlines were never the substance: all 10,000 lookups still asserted in the first, every colliding key still asserted to resolve to its own value in the second. Timings still printed.

NO RELATIVE PROPERTY SUBSTITUTED, unlike bd-u6z4, and deliberately: that test had two arms measured back-to-back so contention slowed both together and the ratio survived. These have one arm each; inventing a second would be writing a different test. A real NodeMap perf guard belongs in a bench under the A/A-null discipline.

DELIBERATELY LEFT: crates/fm-layout/src/egraph_crossing.rs:1291, fault_fallback_within_time_budget. It configures SaturationConfig { time_limit_ms: 100 } and asserts the call returns within 500ms — its SUBJECT is a time limit, so the assertion is a real detector for a real config knob rather than an incidental host-speed check. It remains unreliable on a contended host for the same reason as the others, but deciding what to do about a test whose subject is a deadline deserves its own judgement, not a mechanical sweep. Whoever takes it should probably assert on the RESULT (that the fallback path was taken) rather than on wall time.

VERIFIED: cargo test --workspace three consecutive times, 0 failing binaries — and this time backed by the grep as well as the runs, so it is a claim about the class rather than about three samples. rg 'as_millis() < ' over crates/ now returns exactly the one retained site. clippy -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean.

title: Shape-expectation audit: stateDiagram end state renders as two hollow rings, mermaid draws a ring around a filled dot
description: AUDIT RESULT, done as asked after 3cb6785d found one shape expectation that encoded its own bug. I extracted all 21 NodeShape assertions in the parser tests and paired each with the syntax that produced it. Nineteen are correct against mermaid semantics. Two are not, and one of them is a live user-visible defect. FINDING 1, live: 'stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle; Idle --> [*]' asserts FilledCircle for the start pseudo-state and DoubleCircle for the end. The start is right - mermaid draws a solid dot. The END is wrong in the RENDERER, and my own f2f508b6 perpetuated it: mermaid's end state is a ring around a FILLED inner dot, while our DoubleCircle now draws two HOLLOW rings (outer takes the node fill, inner is fill=none). So a reader sees a target symbol where mermaid shows a bullseye. THE COMPLICATION, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: NodeShape::DoubleCircle is shared with the flowchart '(((x)))' form, where two hollow rings ARE correct - mermaid does not fill the centre there. One NodeShape cannot express both, so the fix needs either a distinct shape for the state end pseudo-state or a diagram-type-aware fill at the draw site, and that is a design choice rather than a two-line change. title: CI clippy is red under default features: RenderOutcome.layout_cache_hit is only read behind feature serve
description:
MEASURED, not inferred. Exactly CI's quality-gate command for the crate fails on committed main:

  cargo clippy -p frankenmermaid-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings
  -> exit 101
  error: field `layout_cache_hit` is never read
      --> crates/fm-cli/src/main.rs:1064:5

The same command WITH the feature passes:

  cargo clippy -p frankenmermaid-cli --all-targets --features serve -- -D warnings
  -> exit 0

CAUSE. `RenderOutcome.layout_cache_hit` (main.rs:1064) is written at main.rs:4759 but every
READ is inside `#[cfg(feature = "serve")]` code (the preview handler at ~10278 and the serve
tests). A field that is only assigned and never read is dead code under default features, and
`-D warnings` promotes that to an error. Introduced by the bd-kgi4 serve work (reads added in
6028f4b7).

WHY IT MATTERS. .github/workflows/ci.yml:111 runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
-D warnings` with NO features, so that step is red for every commit since. Line 115 adds
`--features fnx-integration`, which does not enable `serve` either. Note the CI runs for the
last three commits were still `queued` when this was found, so nobody had seen the red yet —
this is a gate that is broken but not yet reported, which is the worst kind.

NOT A GATE-WEAKENING QUESTION. The field is genuinely used, just only by one feature. The fix
is to scope the dead-code expectation to the exact feature combination where the field really
is unused, next to the existing comment that already explains the conditionality.

Found while wiring bd-2xl.14 (the minimizer module had never compiled); this error is
unrelated to that change and reproduces on a clean HEAD.
close_reason: Fixed in db5e254c; ci.yml:111 command verified exit 0 workspace-wide

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED in db5e254c.

Scoped the dead-code expectation to the exact feature combination where the field is unused:

  #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "serve"), expect(dead_code, reason = "read only by `serve`"))]
  layout_cache_hit: bool,

`expect` rather than `allow` on purpose: if the serve handler ever stops reading the field, the
expectation goes unfulfilled and the gate fires again. Under `--features serve` the attribute is
not applied at all, so that build's dead-code checking is untouched.

EVIDENCE, exit codes captured directly (not through a pipe, which would report tail's status):
  cargo clippy -p frankenmermaid-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings              -> 0 (was 101)
  cargo clippy -p frankenmermaid-cli --all-targets --features serve -- -D w..  -> 0
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings                        -> 0
The last one is ci.yml:111 verbatim, so the CI step is restored workspace-wide, and its passing
also shows fm-cli was the only crate red under default features. Both crate-scoped runs printed
"Checking frankenmermaid-cli", so they recompiled rather than reporting a cached verdict.

title: C4 UpdateElementStyle was reported unsupported and its colours dropped
description:
`UpdateElementStyle(alias, $bgColor="red", $fontColor="white", $borderColor="black")` recolours a
declared C4 element. We reported it as an unsupported C4 directive and dropped every colour.

I had DEFERRED this one deliberately in bd-hebu, on the grounds that it "mutates styling and needs a
real consumer". That was right to check and wrong as a conclusion: the consumer already exists.

CONSUMER VERIFIED, not assumed - this is the whole reason it is landable:
  * IrStyleTarget::Node refs are read by collect_node_style_directives in fm-render-svg;
  * the hand-written C4 fast-path fragment writer is GATED on
    `shape_style.is_none() && text_style.is_none()`, so a styled C4 node falls back to the general
    render_node path that applies them.
Without that gate the style ref would have been dead IR, which is the trap docs/IR_FIELD_SWEEP.md
exists to catch.

MAPPING, read out of the bundle rather than guessed - its renderer reads
`t.bgColor ? t.bgColor : <default>` for the fill, borderColor for the stroke and fontColor for the
text, so: bgColor -> fill, borderColor -> stroke, fontColor -> color.

The alias is resolved with the NON-interning node_id_by_key. Interning would invent a phantom node
for a misspelled alias, which is exactly the defect bd-xfmm was filed for; a test asserts the node
count is unchanged for an unknown alias.

$shadowing, $legendText and the sprite options are recognised and NAMED in a warning rather than
quietly ignored - dropped styling should say so - while the colours on the same line still apply.

STILL UNSUPPORTED: UpdateRelStyle (needs an edge lookup by from/to) and RelIndex. UpdateLayoutConfig
is separately short-circuited already.

UNBUILT: written during the /data build freeze. Three tests added, none compiled.
close_reason: Compiled and tested green in the first post-throttle build

title: fm-layout bench harness: self-report executing ELF SHA-256 so layout perf results can be ledgered
description:
docs/PERF_LEDGER.md KEEP rows require:

  **Executing ELF SHA-256 (self-reported by process):** <64 hex>

and AGENTS.md is explicit that 'computing a hash beside the run is not sufficient. The executing process must identify its own ELF.' The fm-layout criterion benches do not self-report, so a measured fm-layout result currently CANNOT be ledgered as a KEEP row without violating that rule.

This blocked a real result on 2026-08-04: fusing dependency_topology_equal into derive_layout_edits measured -4.074% instructions cumulative (-3.63% marginal) on single_node_label_edit/incremental/1000 with an EXACT 1.000000 A/A null, two distinct ELF SHA-256s, and deterministic callgrind counts. It was landed as code with the numbers recorded in the commit and on bd-9rq7, but NOT ledgered, because inventing the marker would have been proof-class inflation.

WORK: have the bench binary read /proc/self/exe, hash it, and print the digest once at startup (behind an env flag or unconditionally to stderr). Then the harness output itself carries the provenance and the KEEP-row marker is satisfiable from inside the process.

Note this is provenance-STRENGTHENING infrastructure, not a gate change: it makes a currently-unmeetable requirement meetable, and must not be accompanied by any relaxation of the KEEP-row contract.

Applies to crates/fm-layout/benches/*.rs; the same gap likely exists for other per-crate criterion benches, so check them while here.
close_reason:
Done in 5b0ff735. incremental_layout now self-reports its executing ELF via a shared benches/bench_identity.rs module included by #[path] from both benches; harness_calibration switched from its own println! to the shared printer so there is ONE implementation and one output format (no forked helper). Reported from every benchmark group with a Once rather than from main, because criterion owns main and a filtered run executes only matching groups — reporting from one group would leave the targeted single-row runs, which is exactly what a ledger entry is written from, with no identity line.

Also removed the .expect() the original carried (unreachable, but a panic site inside provenance code) and kept the 'unavailable' fallback: a missing digest is a refusal to certify, a wrong one is a false certification.

INCIDENTAL FINDING worth keeping: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets does NOT build harness_calibration because it is gated behind the bench-internals feature. An unused-function error there passed the workspace gate and surfaced only under cargo clippy -p fm-layout --benches --features bench-internals. title: fm-layout never propagates subgraph style to LayoutClusterBox.color
description:
MEASURED while closing the canvas half of bd-lvj3.

A flowchart `subgraph one[One]` + `style one fill:#ff0000` produces NO cluster colour anywhere downstream, so neither renderer can honour it. The colour is dropped in fm-layout, not in a renderer:

  lib.rs:16484  flowchart cluster construction        color: None   (hardcoded)
  lib.rs:16848  "regular cluster box for rendering consistency"  color: None   (hardcoded)
  lib.rs:6249   group path                            color: group.color.clone()   (populated)

So LayoutClusterBox.color is only ever Some on the 6249 group path. fm-render-canvas now honours cluster_box.color when present (bd-lvj3), which makes it live for 6249 and INERT for flowchart subgraphs - the colour never arrives to be honoured.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY: a renderer test asserting the subgraph case would fail for a reason in another crate. That is a broken gate, not a reproducer, so the note lives in crates/fm-render-canvas/tests/node_styling.rs and the defect lives here.

NEXT STEP: confirm whether the parser records the subgraph style at all (style_refs targeting a cluster) before assuming layout is the only gap - if the IR has no cluster-style channel, the fix is wider than populating one field.

NOT VERIFIED: whether fm-render-svg colours a styled subgraph by a CSS class instead, which would mean the two outputs disagree here the same way they did for nodes and edges.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, AND IT IS NOT LAYOUT. My own filing said "confirm whether the parser records the subgraph style at all before assuming layout is the only gap". It does not, and the IR cannot.

  parser    mermaid_parser.rs:11521   `style <target>` resolves ONLY via node_id_by_key(target).
                                       A subgraph key is not in the node index (ir_builder.rs:1328
                                       looks up node_id_index over ir.nodes), so the branch is
                                       skipped and the directive is SILENTLY DISCARDED.
  IR        fm-core lib.rs:1843       IrStyleTarget = Class | Node | Link | LinkDefault. NO Cluster
                                       variant, so a parser that wanted to record it has nowhere.
  layout    fm-layout 16484, 16848    LayoutClusterBox.color hardcoded None on both flowchart paths.
  renderers svg 4365 / canvas         both read cluster.color and correctly fall back to theme.

THE "NOT VERIFIED" ITEM ON THIS BEAD IS NOW RESOLVED: fm-render-svg does NOT colour a styled subgraph either. It emits only the generic fm-cluster / fm-cluster-c4 / fm-cluster-swimlane classes (lib.rs:4400-4415) with no per-cluster declared paint. So there is NO cross-renderer disagreement here.

THAT DISTINCTION DECIDES THE FIX. bd-lvj3 was a RENDERER gap - svg honoured the channels, canvas did not, same document rendering two ways. This is a MISSING CHANNEL: both renderers are equally blind and correctly so, because the colour never reaches either. No renderer-side change can fix it, and my canvas work on bd-lvj3 could not have.

Full diagnosis with the two candidate fixes parked at docs/parked-levers/bd_xfmm_cluster_style_channel.md. Smallest first:

  1. PARSER ONLY, ~10 lines: warn when a `style` target resolves to no node. Today a typo and an
     unsupported subgraph target are equally silent, which is the worst property this has - the user
     cannot tell "not supported" from "you spelled it wrong". Precedent: the duplicate-gitgraph-branch
     warning in the same file uses builder.add_warning. Needs a control that an ordinary valid
     `style a fill:` emits NO warning.
  2. ADD THE CHANNEL: IrStyleTarget::Cluster(IrClusterId) through fm-core + fm-parser + fm-layout;
     both renderers already honour cluster.color once it arrives. Wants ONE agent holding all three
     crates. IrStyleTarget is PartialEq-matched in several places (fm-render-svg 2868, dot_parser
     2685+) - a new variant must be checked at each, not just added.

DO NOT populate LayoutClusterBox.color from something layout can already see: there is nothing to see, the colour was destroyed two layers earlier, and any value invented there is a guess dressed as the author's intent.

NOT IMPLEMENTED: crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs is leased by BeigeHill to 21:50Z. Written up rather than half-landed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SMALLER FIX LANDED: a dropped style target now WARNS.

`style <target> fill:...` resolved only via node_id_by_key and a miss was discarded in total silence, so a misspelled node id and a SUBGRAPH id produced the identical nothing. The author could not tell "you spelled it wrong" from "that is not supported".

THIS COLOURS NOTHING - `style <subgraph>` still has no effect. That still needs candidate 2, the IrStyleTarget::Cluster channel across fm-core + fm-parser + fm-layout, and this bead stays OPEN for it. What changes is that the failure is no longer invisible.

Four tests, two controls:
  style_directive_on_a_subgraph_warns_instead_of_vanishing
  style_directive_on_an_unknown_id_warns
  a_valid_style_directive_neither_warns_nor_loses_its_style   <- the load-bearing control
  a_comma_list_warns_only_for_the_unresolved_member

title: Implement subgraph direction override
description:
# Subgraph Direction Override

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
flowchart LR
  subgraph sub1
    direction TB
    A --> B
  end
  sub1 --> C
\`\`\`
Each subgraph can have its own direction that overrides the parent graph direction. This affects layout within that subgraph only.

## Current State
- The \`direction\` keyword IS parsed within subgraphs
- The direction is stored on IrSubgraph
- The layout engine does NOT honor per-subgraph direction — it uses a single global direction

## Implementation Plan
1. **Layout** (fm-layout/src/lib.rs): In the Sugiyama layout, when processing nodes within a subgraph/cluster, check if the cluster has a direction override. If so, apply rank assignment and coordinate assignment with that direction for nodes within the cluster.
2. **Tests**: Create a flowchart with mixed directions (parent LR, child TB). Verify child nodes are laid out vertically within the horizontal parent flow.

## Complexity
This is a non-trivial layout change. The current Sugiyama implementation uses a single global direction. Supporting per-subgraph direction requires partitioning the layout into independent sub-layouts and stitching them together. Consider a phased approach: first support the feature in the IR, then implement the layout logic.
close_reason: Completed

title: REJECT: attr_static for span-metadata data-* attrs (zero-gain, reverted)
description: Reverted (working tree back to 10b1654). Hypothesis: apply_span_metadata sets 7 data-* attrs/element via .data(name, &v.to_string()), each doing format!('data-{name}') (name alloc+Formatter) + value to_string + AttributeValue::String copy (~3 allocs+format! per attr). Added Element::attr_static(&'static name, owned String) to cut to 1 alloc, no format!. Reverse-order A/B: medium +8.9% SLOWER (p<0.05, contaminated), large -3.7% then -1.4% (n.s., CI spans 0) = NEUTRAL. LESSON: unlike the write!/Formatter wins on the SERIALIZATION path (tag/path/attr +12-18%), format!+alloc on the CONSTRUCTION path (building the element tree) is sub-floor — small-string allocs are cheap (source_line lesson) and LLVM optimizes format! of a const string+short literal well. Distinguish: serialization-path write! over the final buffer = real cost; construction-path format! building attr values = neutral. Output-identical (216 tests).

title: Implement class member visibility modifiers and type annotations
description:
# Class Member Visibility and Type Annotations

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
classDiagram
  class Animal {
    +String name
    -int age
    #List~Food~ diet
    ~void breathe()
    +eat(Food food) bool
    +sleep()* : void
  }
\`\`\`
- \`+\` public, \`-\` private, \`#\` protected, \`~\` package
- Type before name for attributes, after parentheses for return types
- \`*\` suffix for abstract methods
- \`$\` suffix for static methods

## Current State
- Class blocks ARE parsed, member lines are captured
- Visibility modifiers are NOT extracted — stored as raw text in member string
- Type annotations are NOT parsed separately from names
- No rendering of visibility symbols

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: When parsing class block members, extract leading +/-/#/~ as visibility. Parse \`type name\` for attributes, \`name(params) returnType\` for methods. Detect */$ suffixes.
2. **IR**: Add IrClassMember { visibility: Visibility, name: String, return_type: Option<String>, parameters: Vec<String>, is_abstract: bool, is_static: bool }.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Render three-compartment class boxes: header (class name + stereotype), attributes section, methods section. Prepend visibility symbol. Show types.
4. **Tests**: All visibility markers, attribute types, method signatures, abstract/static.
close_reason: Implemented class member visibility + three-compartment rendering. Parser already extracts +/-/#/~ visibility, types, static/abstract. Terminal renderer shows UML class boxes with compartment separators. SVG renderer shows three-compartment boxes with stereotypes, visibility symbols, type annotations, and separator lines.

title: Implement style and linkStyle directive parsing and rendering
description:
# style / linkStyle Directive Support

## What mermaid-js Supports
Inline styling for specific nodes and edges:
\`\`\`
style nodeId fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px
linkStyle 0 stroke:#ff3,stroke-width:4px,color:red
linkStyle default stroke:#333
\`\`\`

style applies to a node by ID. linkStyle applies to an edge by index (0-based declaration order) or 'default' for all edges.

## Current State
- Parser recognizes style/linkStyle lines but does not capture the property map
- No rendering path for inline styles

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Parse \`style nodeId prop:value,...\` and store as IrNodeStyle on the IrNode. Parse \`linkStyle index prop:value,...\` and store as IrEdgeStyle on the IrEdge.
2. **IR**: Add \`inline_style: Option<IrInlineStyle>\` to IrNode and IrEdge. IrInlineStyle is a BTreeMap<String, String>.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Apply inline_style as SVG attributes (fill → rect fill, stroke → rect stroke, etc.). For edges, apply to <path> elements.
4. **Tests**: Verify style is applied in SVG output, verify linkStyle by index, verify default linkStyle.

## Considerations
- Property names must be mapped from CSS-like (stroke-width) to SVG attributes
- Sanitize values to prevent XSS in SVG output
close_reason: style and linkStyle directive parsing was already implemented in extract_style_directives. SVG renderer already applies styles via resolve_node_inline_style/resolve_edge_inline_style. Now also populates structured IrInlineStyle on nodes/edges via populate_structured_styles(). Enhanced style directive to support comma-separated node IDs per mermaid-js spec. Tests pass.

title: the flowchart class-assignment directive fires on classDiagram block declarations, interning phantom classes from generic parameters
description:
extract_style_directives treats any line starting with "class " as the flowchart
CSS-class-assignment directive `class nodeA,nodeB className`. A classDiagram BLOCK
DECLARATION starts with the same prefix, so `class Container~T~ {` is parsed as
"assign CSS class { to node Container~T~" -- interning a phantom class and
attaching a CSS class literally named `{`.

MEASURED with the shipping binary, and the mechanism predicts every row:

  classDiagram / class Plain { }           ids: Plain
      no phantom (the node already exists) but Plain silently gains a CSS class `{`

  classDiagram / class Container~T~{ }     ids: Container
      NO SPACE before the brace, so rsplit_once(' ') returns None and the branch
      never fires. This is the control that proves the mechanism.

  classDiagram / class Container~T~ { }    ids: Container, Container~T~
      one space, so nodes_raw = Container~T~ and class_name = `{`; phantom interned

  classDiagram / class Box~K,V~ { }        ids: Box, Box~K, V~
      the generic list is split on its COMMA, so a two-parameter generic becomes
      TWO phantom classes named after fragments of the parameter list

THE CODE, mermaid_parser.rs inside extract_style_directives, around line 10855:
a `strip_prefix("class ")` branch does `rest.rsplit_once(' ')` and, when the tail
is non-empty, treats it as a CSS class name and splits the head on commas, calling
add_class_to_node for each fragment. For `class Container~T~ {` that rsplit yields
(Container~T~, `{`), and `{` is non-empty so it is accepted as a class name.

USER-VISIBLE EFFECT: a generic class declared with a space before its brace renders
an extra empty box beside the real one, named after the raw generic text, and a
multi-parameter generic renders one extra box per fragment. The real class also
carries a junk CSS class, so any rule keyed on class names sees `{`.

SAME FAMILY as bd-sq8p and bd-9x8r: a prefix collision causing syntax to be
interned as node identity. This one is nastier because whether it fires depends on
a SPACE before the brace.

NEGATIVE CASES a fix must handle:
  1. flowchart `class A,B myClass` must STILL assign myClass to both nodes. That is
     the directive this branch exists for and it must not regress.
  2. classDiagram `class Container~T~ {` must intern no phantom node.
  3. `class Box~K,V~ {` must intern no fragments.
  4. classDiagram `class Plain {` must not gain a CSS class named `{` either --
     asserting only "no phantom node" would pass while the junk class survives, so
     the class list has to be asserted too.
  5. A genuine CSS assignment with no brace must keep working.
close_reason:
LANDED, but ⚠️ ATTRIBUTED TO ANOTHER BEAD'S COMMIT. The fix and both its tests are
on main inside 382be227, whose subject is "fix(parser): architecture '<-->' is
bidirectional, not a bare line (bd-gp82)" -- an unrelated peer change. My working
tree was swept into that commit before I could commit it myself, so `git commit`
found nothing to commit. Verified with
`git log -S "!rest.ends_with('{')" -- crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs`,
which returns exactly 382be227. Recording it here because the commit message says
nothing about bd-yf4r and nobody reading that history would find this.

Nothing was lost and main is green: cargo test -j 2 -p fm-parser --lib at HEAD
gives 523 passed / 0 failed (rch worker vmi1227854, 83.3s).

THE DEFECT. extract_style_directives matched ANY line starting with `class ` as the
flowchart directive `class nodeA,nodeB className`. A classDiagram block declaration
shares that prefix, so `class Container~T~ {` was read as "assign CSS class `{` to
node `Container~T~`" -- interning a phantom class and attaching a junk CSS class
named `{` to the real one.

MEASURED, and the mechanism predicts every row, which is what makes this a
diagnosis rather than a guess:

  class Plain { }          ids: Plain
      no phantom (node already exists) but Plain gains a CSS class `{`
  class Container~T~{ }    ids: Container
      NO SPACE, so rsplit_once(' ') returns None and the branch never fires
  class Container~T~ { }   ids: Container, Container~T~
      one space -> (Container~T~, `{`), `{` is non-empty, phantom interned
  class Box~K,V~ { }       ids: Box, Box~K, V~
      the head is then split on the GENERIC'S OWN COMMA: one class becomes three

Whether it fired depended on a SPACE before the brace, and that is exactly what
pinned it -- the no-space spelling is an untouched control that already behaved
correctly.

FIX: a block declaration always ends at the opening brace and the CSS directive
never does, so `!rest.ends_with('{')` is the discriminator. `rest` is already
trimmed, so trailing whitespace cannot defeat it.

⚠️ ASSERTING "NO PHANTOM NODE" ALONE WOULD MISS HALF THE BUG. `class Plain {`
interns no phantom because the node already exists, yet the real class still gained
a CSS class named `{`. The test asserts the class list as well as the id list.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, and it separates the two directions cleanly. With the guard
removed:
  class_block_declaration_is_not_a_css_class_assignment  FAILED
      left: ["Container", "Container~T~"]   right: ["Container"]
  flowchart_class_assignment_directive_still_applies     ok
The control PASSING without the guard is the point: it does not depend on this
change, so it independently verifies the real flowchart directive was not broken.

GATES, harness cargo test -j 2 -p fm-parser --lib:
  pre-sweep   523 passed, 0 failed   rch worker vmi1293453, 295.8s
  re-gate     523 passed, 0 failed   rch worker vmi1227854, 67.9s
  at HEAD     523 passed, 0 failed   rch worker vmi1227854, 83.3s

and bd-ka77. Same family as the first two: a prefix collision interning syntax as

title: Flowchart ground truth misses --o, --x and <-->, so a correct render of those edges is reported DIVERGENT
description:
Found by running the EXISTING source-grounded oracle over all 37 committed golden pairs — no new
harness feature, just `verifyFrankenmermaidAgainstSource` called on data already in git.

THE FINDING. `golden/all_edge_types` decoded **7 nodes / 6 edges** from a source declaring 10 nodes
and 9 edges, against a render that correctly carries all ten `data-id`s A..J. Both
`node_id_set_vs_input__frankenmermaid` and `edge_topology_vs_input__frankenmermaid` decided FALSE
and the row was reported DIVERGENT. The renderer was right; the oracle was wrong.

MECHANISM. The flowchart link regex's arrow alternation was

    (?:-{2,3}>|-{2,3}|={2,3}>|-\.->)

with no case for the circle terminator `--o`, the cross terminator `--x`, or the bidirectional
`<-->`; a bare `===` and `-.-` were unmatched too. An undecoded edge does not merely lose that edge:
it removes its ENDPOINTS from `node_ids`, which is why one unmatched form also fails the node-set
invariant.

WHY IT MATTERS. Any head-to-head run whose corpus contained those forms would have reported our
CORRECT output as divergent, and the natural reading of that failure is "our renderer dropped
nodes" — a false alarm pointed at the engine, produced by the gate. This is the mirror image of
bd-tj1d: that one was the oracle admitting something it should have refused, this one is the oracle
refusing something it should have admitted. Both come from the same place — a decoder that silently
covers less than the syntax it is asked about.

FIXED. Alternation extended longest-form-first, so `<-->` is not read as a bare `-->` starting one
character late — that misreading drops the SOURCE endpoint rather than the target, which is the
subtle failure a shorter pattern produces instead of an obvious one.

Six self-test cases, one per form (`--o`, `--x`, `<-->`, `===`, `-.-`) plus an explicit
`bidirectional_arrow_keeps_its_source_endpoint`.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: restoring the old alternation fails
`flowchart_truth_decodes_circle_terminator`, exit 1. Source restored byte-identically, sha256
022b1732c8f2f689c49744a7b0e3760d9dfa9a0dc7a9acde68db0c40dfe9db45.

GATE: `svg_equivalence --self-test` 62 cases / 16 mutation controls / 4 negative controls, exit 0;
`run.mjs --self-test` exit 0. Corpus effect: `all_edge_types` moves DIVERGENT -> verified, 14 -> 15
verified of 37.

THREE DIVERGENT GOLDENS REMAIN, and they are NOT claimed as defects here — each needs its own
triage, because the oracle is as likely to be the wrong side as the renderer:
  malformed_recovery [flowchart] 3n/2e  — a deliberately malformed fixture; the parser RECOVERS, so
    a naive source decode legitimately disagrees with the render. Probably correct behaviour on both
    sides and an oracle scope question.
  sequence_advanced [sequence] 3n/11e   — `sequence_source_tokens_vs_output` fails; likely alt/loop/
    par block syntax the token decoder does not model.
  state_composite [state] 11n/16e       — composite/nested state ids.

title: Implement gantt date parsing, task types, and duration computation
description:
# Gantt Date/Duration/Task Type Parsing

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
gantt
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  title Project Plan
  excludes weekends
  section Phase 1
  Design           :done, des1, 2024-01-01, 30d
  Implementation   :active, impl1, after des1, 60d
  Testing          :crit, test1, after impl1, 2024-05-01
  Milestone        :milestone, m1, after test1, 0d
\`\`\`
- dateFormat: YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, etc.
- Task types: done, active, crit (critical), milestone
- Duration: Nd (days), after taskId (dependency), absolute dates
- excludes: weekends, specific dates

## Current State
- Parser recognizes sections and task lines, but does NOT extract dates, types, durations, or dependencies
- Layout has a gantt algorithm but operates on generic nodes, not time-aware bars

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: After the colon in task lines, parse comma-separated metadata: type (done/active/crit/milestone), id, start (date or 'after id'), end (date or duration). Parse dateFormat directive. Parse excludes.
2. **IR**: Add IrGanttMeta { date_format, excludes, sections: Vec<IrGanttSection> } with IrGanttTask { id, name, task_type, start, end, depends_on }.
3. **Layout**: Compute actual x-positions from dates. Apply excludes to skip weekends. Position milestone as diamonds.
4. **Tests**: Date formats, durations, after-dependencies, excludes, milestones, crit tasks.
close_reason: Already implemented: gantt parser extracts dateFormat, excludes (weekends + dates), tick_interval, sections, task types (done/active/crit/milestone), task IDs, start dates (absolute + after-dependency), end dates (absolute + duration), and progress values. IrGanttMeta fully populated. 9 existing tests verify all features. Marking as complete since the gap described in the bead has been closed by prior work.

title: State transition labels corrupt edges and nodes in realistic docs corpus
description: Full ci_docs_2000/5000 equivalence at 905b01f9 proves 105/169 and 227/390 state diagrams divergent. The failures are exactly diagrams containing one of five label forms. In parse_state_statements, the generic edge endpoint parser sees the colon-suffix label before state-specific extraction: top-level ampersands in Retry & backoff, Diff & merge, or Sign & upload are rejected as parallel endpoint lists, recovery then creates a phantom asymmetric node and drops each affected transition; Parse <config> is misread as an asymmetric-node delimiter; Rate limit (429) is misread as a rounded-node delimiter. The last two preserve edge count but lose visible label tokens. Fix the state grammar so colon suffixes remain transition labels and never endpoint syntax. Add focused parse/render tests for all five labels, exact node/edge/label assertions, and require zero state divergences/unverified in fresh full ci_docs_2000 and ci_docs_5000 linked equivalence artifacts.
notes:
FIX IMPLEMENTED AND FUNCTIONALLY VERIFIED (cc lane, LilacPike) — not yet committed.

split_state_transition_label() peels the ': label' suffix off before the generic flowchart edge
parser sees it, and the label is attached to FlowAst::Edge's existing label field.

Three deliberate design points:
- Only splits AFTER an edge operator, so a bare 'S1: description' (mermaid's state-description
  syntax, which sets the state's own label) still flows to the node parser untouched.
- label.or_else(...) not Some(...), so an explicit '-->|text|' keeps its own label instead of being
  overwritten by the colon suffix.
- Structural scan mirroring find_operator_core (quotes + [] () {} depth), not split_once(':'), so
  '[*]' and parenthesised text do not confuse it and the FIRST top-level colon wins, matching mermaid
  on 'S0 --> S1: Rate: 429'.

TEST RESULT at base 77c3a091 with the overlay, --no-fail-fast so nothing was masked:
  integration_test: 121 passed; 0 failed
  (119 before + my 2 new tests, so state_transition_labels_attach_to_the_edge_not_the_node PASSES
   across all five named label forms plus a plain control)
  every fm-parser and fm-cli functional suite: 0 failed

THREE GOLDEN-DERIVED SUITES FAIL with the overlay:
  svg_golden_snapshots_are_stable
  layout_golden_checksums_are_stable
  differential_all_golden_cases_pass_gate
The first two are EXPECTED and require re-blessing: state_basic.svg and state_composite.svg encode
the bug (they render 'Idle : stop' / 'Running : start' as NODE labels with no edge labels at all), and
layout checksums move because node/edge labels move. The third is ambiguous — see bd-uay6, where my
'pre-existing' claim about it was retracted after a base-drift methodology bug.

A recheck at PINNED base 77c3a091 with --no-overlay is running to establish which of these three are
already red before my change.

title: flowchart edge-id syntax 'A e1@--> B' invents a node named A_e1 and leaves the real source unconnected
description:
SPLIT OUT of bd-9x8r, which fixed the node-metadata half. FORM 2 measured with the shipping binary:

    flowchart TD
      A e1@--> B
      e1@{ animate: true }

renders THREE nodes where the source declares two:

    data-id="A_e1"  label "A e1@"
    data-id="B"     label "B"
    data-id="e1"    label "animate: true"

So 'A e1@' is an invented class name, and the edge runs from A_e1 rather than from A -- the real source node is not even connected to anything.

bd-9x8r's fix removed the invented DISPLAY name on the third node (e1 no longer renders as a class called 'animate: true') but it still declares a node e1, and it does not touch the 'A e1@--> B' form at all.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT: distinguishing an edge id from a node id needs an edge-id concept the IR does not have. 'Stop inventing a node' and 'support edge ids' are different sizes of work, and folding them together would have made bd-9x8r unlandable.

NEGATIVE CASES:
  1. 'A e1@--> B' must connect A to B, not A_e1 to B. Assert the edge endpoints by node id.
  2. A flowchart with no edge ids must be byte-identical.
  3. 'e1@{ animate: true }' must not declare a node once edge ids exist.
  4. A node legitimately named with a trailing '@' (if reachable) must not be mangled.
close_reason:
LANDED at f6318104, pushed to main and master.

MEASURED before: 'flowchart TD / A e1@--> B / e1@{ animate: true }' rendered THREE nodes for a two-node source -- data-id A_e1 labelled 'A e1@', data-id B, and data-id e1 labelled 'animate: true'. The edge ran from the phantom A_e1, so the real A was not connected to anything.

FIX, two halves, both deliberately narrow:
1. strip_trailing_edge_id drops the id from an edge's LEFT side. It requires BOTH a preceding token and an identifier@ shape, which is what keeps it off every other endpoint: a lone 'A@' has no left neighbour so it is left alone, and a node whose id genuinely ends in @ is not mangled. The id itself is discarded -- the IR has no edge-id concept and inventing one is a bigger change than this defect warrants.
2. @{...} metadata that describes NO node now declares no node. parse_flowchart_node_metadata returns Some(None) -- recognised, nothing to declare -- so the generic fallback still cannot intern the directive text. Metadata that DOES describe a node (shape/label/title) declares it exactly as before.

TESTS assert the edge ENDPOINTS by node id, not just the id list: 'no phantom node' alone would not catch the edge being wired to the wrong source, which was the more damaging half.

title: Edge routing: clip edges at node boundaries via CGA intersection (bd-2q3f.3 criterion 2)
description:
bd-2q3f.3 criterion 2: 'Edge routing uses CGA intersection for node boundary clipping'. Split out of bd-2q3f.3 because, unlike criteria 1/3/4 which were satisfiable in fm-core alone, this one CHANGES EMITTED GEOMETRY and therefore cannot ride along on a test-only change.

SCOPE: fm-layout edge routing currently clips edge endpoints at node boundaries with its own arithmetic. Replacing that with CgaRect::intersect_segment / CgaLineSegment::intersect would route every edge endpoint through fm-core's CGA primitives.

WHY THIS IS NOT A FREE SWAP:
- Edge endpoint coordinates appear directly in rendered SVG path data, so ANY numeric difference moves goldens. This requires a GOLDEN-CHANGE note plus a semantic diff review per AGENTS.md, never a bulk refresh.
- The CGA primitives fail closed to CgaPoint::origin() on malformed input. An edge silently clipped to (0,0) would be a visible corruption, not a diagnostic. Any adoption must distinguish 'no intersection' from 'rejected input' at the call site -- note bd-34yo was exactly this ambiguity biting inside fm-core.
- CgaRect::intersect_segment dedupes corner hits with an absolute f64::EPSILON comparison, which is magnitude-blind; check it against real layout coordinate ranges before relying on it.

PRE-SPECIFIED ASSERTIONS (code and tests in the SAME bead):
- POSITIVE: an edge between two separated nodes is clipped exactly at the boundary of each -- endpoint lies on the node rect within tolerance, and outside the node interior.
- NEGATIVE CASE a naive implementation fails: overlapping / nested node rects, and an edge whose endpoints are both INSIDE the source node. A naive 'take the first intersection' returns nothing or the wrong side; assert the documented behaviour rather than whatever falls out.
- NEGATIVE CASE: zero-size and degenerate (zero-width or zero-height) node rects must not produce origin-clipped edges.
- Determinism: repeated layout of the same input yields byte-identical paths.

GOLDEN HANDLING: expect movement. Every changed golden needs its delta explained semantically (which edge, which endpoint, by how much, and why the new value is the more correct clip). If a golden's geometry changes by more than a rounding-level amount, that is a finding to explain, not to bless.

DEPENDS ON bd-9mqa: if that decides the analytic queries are the intended endpoint, this bead's framing changes from 'adopt CGA meet' to 'consolidate duplicated clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives' -- same code, different justification, and the perf criterion (bd-2q3f.3 criterion 5) then has to price a real abstraction boundary.
close_reason:
REFUTED on inspection — both readings of this bead fail, so no code was changed. I filed this bead; closing my own.

READING 1, 'adopt CGA intersection for boundary clipping': dead on arrival. There is no meet()/join(), and bd-9mqa (closed, with measurement) shows CGA machinery costs 10-40x the direct arithmetic it would replace.

READING 2, the reframing I gave it after bd-9mqa — 'consolidate duplicated clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives': THERE IS NO DUPLICATION. Verified by grep across crates/: clip_to_rect_border has exactly one definition (lib.rs:9013) and exactly two call sites (lib.rs:8995, 8996, the two endpoints of one edge). cga_routing.rs does use CgaRect::intersect_segment already, but for a DIFFERENT job — testing whether a segment hits an expanded obstacle rect during routing — not for clipping an endpoint to a node border. The premise that two implementations had drifted apart is simply false.

AND THE SWAP WOULD REGRESS. clip_to_rect_border is a ~10-flop f32 ray-vs-centered-rect clip: center, direction, t = min(half_w/|dx|, half_h/|dy|), return center + t*d. CgaRect::intersect_segment would replace that, per edge endpoint, with: constructing an f64 rect and segment, iterating all four edges with a full segment-segment intersection each, an O(k^2) corner dedup, and a heap-allocated Vec<CgaPoint> RETURN — an allocation per endpoint in the layout hot path, twice per edge. It would also change emitted geometry (f32 -> f64 and a different formula), moving goldens to pay for a slowdown.

Existing implementation audited while here and is correct:  is always the node centre at both call sites so the centre-projection is consistent; zero-size rect yields t=0 and returns the centre; a degenerate direction returns . No latent defect found to justify touching it.

UNVERIFIED OBSERVATION, deliberately NOT acted on and NOT filed as fact: clip_to_rect_border always clips to the bounding RECT, so for non-rectangular shapes (circle, diamond, stadium) an edge may meet the bounding box rather than the drawn outline. Whether that is visible depends on what the renderers do at their end, which I did not check. If someone is working cross-engine visual fidelity, that is worth confirming — but it is a shape-aware-clipping question, not a CGA-adoption one, and it should not be smuggled back into bd-2q3f.

Consequence for the parent: bd-2q3f.3 criterion 2 ('edge routing uses CGA intersection for node boundary clipping') should be struck rather than implemented, on the same evidence as criteria 1-3 being reworded per bd-9mqa. Implementing it as literally written would knowingly make the engine slower and its output different for no benefit.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED — bd-9mqa is decided (option b, closed). Its dependency is satisfied and its framing collapses to the second of the two alternatives this bead names.

This bead is NOT 'adopt CGA meet for boundary clipping'. There is no meet() to adopt, and the measurement on bd-9mqa shows CGA transforms cost 10-40x the matrices they would replace while the one load-bearing use of conformal machinery (distance) was numerically wrong and had to be replaced (681cdf4a). So the work is: CONSOLIDATE the duplicated edge/node clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives that already exist (CgaRect::intersect_segment, CgaLineSegment::intersect), for single-implementation and correctness reasons — not for an algebraic abstraction.

Everything else in the bead stands unchanged, and the warnings in it matter more under this framing, not less: it still changes emitted geometry, so it still needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note with a semantic diff, and it still must distinguish a fail-closed origin result from 'no intersection' or an edge silently clips to (0,0).

title: architecture-beta edge SIDES are dropped: a:R --> L:b renders identically to a:T --> B:b
description:
MEASURED: architecture-beta with "a:R --> L:b" renders BYTE-IDENTICAL to the same diagram written "a:T --> B:b". The per-edge side specification has no effect on output.

ROOT CAUSE is at PARSE time, not render time: both sources produce ir.ports.len() == 0. No IrPort is created for the side syntax at all, so IrPort.side_hint is dead by construction - nothing can read a port that does not exist.

FOUND BY the corrected dead-field sweep. My earlier sweep only matched "pub struct Ir\w*Meta", which is how bd-jerh hid inside IrEntityAttribute; widening it to every Ir\w+ struct left exactly 3 candidates out of 183 fields, and this was one. IrGanttMeta.date_format is legitimately parser-side, and IrEdge.extras is a false positive - ER notation and class cardinality both reach the output through labels.

THE SWEEP ITSELF WAS BROKEN FIRST, and that is worth recording. My initial widened run reported ALL 183 fields as dead, including IrNode.label and IrPieSlice.value. The bug was mine: inside a bracket expression, \w matches the literal characters backslash and w, not a word class, so the consumer-token set was garbage. A uniform verdict across every case is the signature of a broken instrument, not a discovery. The rerun carries a sanity control asserting that fields which MUST be used are seen as used, and it refuses to report anything if they are not.

INCUMBENT: mermaid 11.15.0 models this explicitly - ArchitectureDirection with per-edge sourceDir and targetDir. The side is the defining grammar of an architecture diagram: a:R --> L:b says the edge leaves a's RIGHT and enters b's LEFT. We ignore both ends.

NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is scope rather than doubt. A real fix is three parts: the parser must create ports carrying the declared side; layout must anchor the edge endpoint on that side instead of choosing by geometric direction (clip_to_shape_border currently picks purely from the centre-to-centre vector); and the anchoring must survive the obstacle router. That is a layout feature, not an edit.

PINNED so it cannot regress further or be silently fixed without noticing: arch_edge_sides is a KNOWN_GAP entry in crates/fm-render-svg/tests/feature_parity.rs. That list is checked in BOTH directions, so when the sides start mattering the gate fails and forces the entry's removal.
close_reason:
LANDED AND GATED. architecture-beta edge sides are now a placement grammar, not a dropped token.

PARSE: parse_architecture_endpoint returns the declared side instead of discarding it; sides carried on IrEdgeExtras as fm_core::ArchitectureSide (a 4-value copy enum, not Box<str> - the alphabet is closed, so an enum makes the layout match total and costs no allocation). set_last_edge_architecture_sides calls mark_reusable_prefix_edge_dirty like every other edge mutator, so an incremental reparse cannot serve a pre-edit direction.

LAYOUT: new LayoutAlgorithm::Architecture + layout_diagram_architecture_traced places services on an integer grid from the declared directions, to a fixed point, then converts to pixels via finalize_specialized_layout. Dispatch is gated on architecture_declares_a_side(ir), so a side-less architecture diagram still takes the general path and its output is unchanged - the golden architecture_basic.mmd (no sides) is untouched.

EVIDENCE, cited:
- crates/fm-render-svg/tests/architecture_placement.rs: both previously-#[ignore]d gates are UN-IGNORED and pass, plus 4 new cases. 7/7 green.
- The KNOWN_GAPS entry arch_edge_sides is DELETED from feature_parity.rs; that list is checked in BOTH directions, so feature_parity passing is positive proof that a:R --> L:b and a:T --> B:b now render DIFFERENTLY.
- cargo test --workspace: exit 0 (unmasked - the first run's 0 was tail's, caught and re-run without the pipe). 53 test-result groups ok, 0 FAILED.
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0.

DECISION RECORDED (the sketch left it open): colliding targets FAN OUT along the axis perpendicular to the step, tested by architecture_colliding_targets_do_not_overlap. Implementing it surfaced a bug the sketch did not have - the perpendicular must be derived from the STEP, not the absolute cell, or a rightward step on a non-zero column fans out parallel to itself.

NEGATIVE CASE: architecture_reverse_operator_swaps_the_sides_with_the_endpoints. An implementation that reverses <-- endpoints without swapping their sides places the node exactly backwards and passes every other test here.

NOT A PERF CLAIM. No ratio measured, none claimed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIX PLAN, measured before implementing it. The plan in this bead's description would NOT have fixed the user-visible problem, and I am recording that before anyone spends a turn on it.

The description said: create ports carrying the declared side, then anchor the edge endpoint on that side instead of the centre-to-centre vector. MEASURED, that is the wrong layer.

architecture-beta is dispatched to the GENERAL graph path and lands on SUGIYAMA. For "service a / service b / a:R --> L:b" the layout stacks the two nodes VERTICALLY and routes the edge straight down:
  algo=Sugiyama nodes=2 edges=1  edge pts=[(53.83, 98.75), (53.83, 218.75)]
Identical points with a group added, and the same vertical chain for a five-node R-chain.

So the declared side is not merely unrendered at the endpoint - the entire DIRECTION SEMANTIC is absent. In mermaid, "a:R --> L:b" means b is placed to the RIGHT of a; R/L/T/B are a PLACEMENT grammar, not an anchor hint. Anchoring endpoints on the correct sides of two vertically stacked boxes would still draw a top-to-bottom diagram, i.e. it would satisfy the port plumbing and leave the picture just as wrong.

WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY NEEDS: a dedicated architecture layout that places nodes from the edge directions (a grid/relative placement), rather than ranking them. That is a new LayoutAlgorithm, not an edit to clip_to_shape_border. Note also that clip_to_shape_border has only TWO call sites and both are in force_build_edge_paths - the Sugiyama path that architecture actually uses does not call it at all, so the endpoint-anchoring plan would not even have executed on this diagram type.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING before choosing the port route: IrEndpoint::Port is effectively unsupported by consumers. There are 372 direct matches on IrEndpoint::Node across layout and the three renderers, against 3 uses of resolved_node_id. Switching architecture edges to Port endpoints would make them unresolvable almost everywhere.

STATUS UNCHANGED: still open, still pinned as a KNOWN_GAP in feature_parity.rs. The gap entry's text remains accurate about the symptom; only the fix plan was wrong.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PARKED IMPLEMENTATION written during the host throttle (builds forbidden, load 652, 78% iowait): docs/parked-levers/bd_zce4_architecture_direction_placement.md

⚠️ IT HAS NEVER BEEN COMPILED, and it says so at the top. Parked rather than committed live so an uncompiled lever cannot turn main red. Several names in it are asserted from reading rather than from a build - layout_diagram_general_traced, endpoint_node_index's signature, finalize_specialized_layout's parameter list - and the note lists them as things to verify rather than presenting them as fact.

It covers three parts: IrEdgeExtras gains source_side/target_side mirroring the cardinality fields; parse_architecture_endpoint stops discarding the side token it already detects; and ArchitectureBeta gets its own placement pass that reads the side as a GRID DIRECTION.

Two details found by reading the code that a from-scratch attempt would likely miss:
  * the new builder setter MUST call mark_reusable_prefix_edge_dirty, as every other edge mutator does - without it incremental reuse serves a pre-edit edge;
  * parse_architecture_edge's `reverse` arm for `<--` must swap the SIDES along with the endpoints, or a reversed edge gets its sides crossed.

It also falls back to the general path when no edge declares a direction, so architecture diagrams written without sides keep their current appearance and this cannot regress them.

ONE THING DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN rather than guessed: two targets can be sent to the same cell (a:R --> L:b and a:R --> L:c). Fan out along the perpendicular axis, or treat the second as unplaced - either is defensible, both need a test, and neither should silently overlap two boxes. I did not want to bury a coin-flip inside an uncompiled patch.

The acceptance gate is already executable and independent of all this: crates/fm-render-svg/tests/architecture_placement.rs, two #[ignore]d tests verified to fail today with a.x=0 and b.x=0. Closing this bead means un-ignoring them AND deleting the arch_edge_sides KNOWN_GAP from feature_parity.rs, which is checked in both directions.

title: REJECT (inconclusive): BK rank_pos_maps -> flat node_position Vec
description: frankenmermaid-cc: replaced brandes_kopf_secondary_coords' rank_pos_maps (BTreeMap<rank,BTreeMap<node,pos>>, R per-rank heap allocs, O(log) lookups) with a flat node_position: Vec<usize> (1 alloc, O(1) lookups). Output-identical (428 fm-layout tests pass single-threaded; node's position is global since each node is in one rank). BUT measurement inconclusive: same-worker A/B gave contradictory results across runs (cyclic_50 +35% then -10.5%; medium_100 consistently OPT-slower -4.5% to -20%). Root cause: stash-swap A/B has a WARM-UP BIAS (OPT always runs first, ORIG second runs systematically faster), which swamps small effects. Mechanically the flat Vec helps only WIDE/multi-node-rank graphs (lookups on multi-entry maps); for CHAINS (1 node/rank) the BTreeMaps are 1-entry so lookups don't improve -> net ~0. Cannot confirm >=3% on the common case. REVERTED (stashed, not dropped). LESSON: stash-swap A/B order bias favors the second (ORIG) run; for small effects, run a REVERSE-ORDER A/B (orig first) to detect order-dependence before trusting.
close_reason: Reverted ~0/inconclusive; warm-up bias swamps the small effect; chains see no lookup gain

title: packet-beta '==' draws a filled arrowhead the syntax never asked for, while flowchart '==' correctly draws none
description:
FOUND BY THE ARROW-EXPECTATION AUDIT. Sibling of bd-m0a9, and the MIRROR IMAGE of bd-e29r / bd-gp82: where those two lost an arrowhead the syntax asked for, this one draws an arrowhead the syntax does not ask for.

PACKET_OPERATORS (crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs:88), all four entries:

    ("-->", Arrow)   ("->", Arrow)   ("--", Line)   ("==", ThickArrow)

The first three are self-consistent: the two forms that draw a head in their syntax get Arrow, the
one that does not gets Line. The fourth breaks the pattern. `==` has no head in its syntax, and the
engine's own flowchart table says so:

    FLOW_OPERATORS:  ("==>", ThickArrow)   ("==", ThickLine)

Same two tokens, and FLOW gets the distinction right -- `==>` thick with a head, `==` thick without.
PACKET collapses both onto ThickArrow, so a bare `==` in a packet diagram draws an arrowhead the
author did not write, and there is no way to express a plain thick connector at all.

IT REACHES THE OUTPUT. Verified by reading the marker mapping rather than assuming:
    fm-render-svg:3319   ArrowType::ThickArrow => MARKER_FILLED
    fm-render-svg:12231  ArrowType::ThickArrow => marker-end="url(#arrow-filled)"
    fm-render-svg:3300   ArrowType::ThickLine  => 0            (no marker)
    fm-render-svg:12208  ArrowType::Line | ThickLine => (None, None, None)
So the same `==` renders with a filled arrowhead in a packet diagram and with none in a flowchart.

REACHABILITY CHECKED BEFORE FILING, because a dead table would make this cosmetic. PACKET_OPERATORS
is live: parse_packet passes it to parse_edge_statement at mermaid_parser.rs:6138. It is a FALLBACK
-- reached only for a line that is not a `start-end: \"label\"` field row -- so the blast radius is
smaller than the ER case, and this is filed P3 rather than P1 for that reason. It is still a
statement the parser accepts and then draws wrongly, not a statement it rejects.

⚠️ FIRST ESTABLISH WHETHER MERMAID ACCEPTS EDGES IN packet-beta AT ALL. I did not verify this and
it changes the right fix. packet-beta's documented grammar is bit-range rows; if mermaid has no
packet edge syntax, then the correct fix may be to DELETE this table and the fallback rather than
to correct one entry, and correcting `==` would be polishing a construct that should not parse.
Check the incumbent before choosing. Whoever takes this should not assume the table is meant to
exist just because it does.

NEGATIVE CASES:
1. Flowchart `==` must still be ThickLine and flowchart `==>` still ThickArrow -- this is a change
   to which ArrowType the PACKET table selects, not to what ThickArrow means.
2. A packet FIELD row (`0-15: \"Source Port\"`) must be unaffected. The operator table is only
   consulted on the fallback path, so a fix that reorders or removes entries must not change how a
   field row parses; assert a normal packet diagram's field boxes are byte-identical.
3. If the table is deleted rather than corrected, a packet line containing `-->` must degrade the
   way other unsupported constructs do rather than panicking or interning the operator text as a
   node.

NO GOLDEN EXPOSURE: grep over crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/*.mmd finds no packet fixture using any of
these four operators, so nothing in the corpus distinguishes the branches and no golden moves.
close_reason: Landed 607c42c6. PACKET_OPERATORS '==' remapped from ArrowType::ThickArrow to ThickLine, matching FLOW_OPERATORS which already gets the same pair right ('==>' ThickArrow beside '==' ThickLine). Test asserts the mapping with two controls: '==>' must stay ThickArrow so a blanket line-ification fails, and the other three packet entries must keep their heads so the DISTINCTION is pinned rather than a direction. No golden moves (packet_basic.mmd is eight bit-range rows). Gate: fm-parser --lib 546 passed, rch worker vmi1227854. STILL OPEN and recorded in the source comment: whether mermaid's packet-beta accepts edges at all — if not, the table and its fallback should be deleted rather than corrected, which needs the pinned mermaid-js harness. This mapping is the better one under either answer.

title: Implement composite/nested states with containment and concurrency
description:
# Composite/Nested States and Concurrency

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
stateDiagram-v2
  state Active {
    [*] --> Processing
    Processing --> Done
    --
    [*] --> Monitoring
    Monitoring --> Alert
  }
  Idle --> Active
  Active --> Idle
\`\`\`
- States can contain child states (composite state)
- \`--\` separator creates concurrent regions within a composite state
- Each concurrent region has independent start/end states
- Nesting can be arbitrarily deep

## Current State
- Composite state syntax (\`state Name { ... }\`) IS parsed — creates subgraphs
- Concurrency separator \`--\` is NOT parsed
- Layout does not enforce visual containment of child states
- SVG renderer draws clusters but doesn't render concurrency dividers

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Parse \`--\` within composite state blocks as region separators. Each region becomes a separate sub-cluster within the parent cluster.
2. **Layout**: Ensure cluster bounds fully contain all child node bounds. For concurrent regions, split the cluster horizontally with a dashed divider.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Draw composite states with rounded rectangle borders. Draw dashed horizontal line for concurrency dividers. Add region labels if present.
4. **Tests**: Nested states, three levels deep, concurrent regions, transitions crossing region boundaries.
close_reason: Completed
