title: sequence alt/par/critical branch dividers are never drawn: the else/and/option label and its divider line are missing, so both branches read as one undivided frame
description:
DROPPED CONTENT + LOST SEMANTICS, sequence diagrams, user-visible. Sibling of
bd-zwh3 (the frame BORDER was clipped) but a different half of the same feature:
here the frame draws correctly and its INTERNAL structure is absent.

MEASURED with target/release/frankenmermaid built from c03be579:

    sequenceDiagram
        A->>B: start
        alt is ok
            A->>B: yes
        else is bad
            A->>B: no
        end

Complete <text> content of the rendered SVG:

    A | B | alt [is ok] | start | yes | no | A | B

`is bad` appears NOWHERE, and there is no divider element of any kind between the
`yes` message and the `no` message. The reader sees ONE undivided box containing
both branches, labelled only with the first condition. There is no way to tell
where the alternative begins, and the second condition -- which is half the
meaning of an `alt` -- is not in the document at all.

mermaid-js 11.15.0 draws a DASHED horizontal divider spanning the frame at each
`else`, with the branch label rendered above it in the same style as the frame's
own label chip.

SAME DEFECT IN THE SIBLING FRAGMENTS, since they share the construct:
  - `par … and … end`   -- each `and` branch label and divider
  - `critical … option … end` -- each `option` branch label and divider
Measured on a fragment-heavy probe, the rendered labels were exactly
`loop [Every minute] | par [Parallel] | critical [Save] | break [when error]` --
one label per FRAGMENT, never one per BRANCH. Every `and` and `option` was lost.

SCOPE NOTE FOR COORDINATION: this touches
`LayoutExtensions::sequence_fragments` / `build_sequence_fragment_geometry` in
fm-layout and the fragment loop in fm-render-svg, which is the same surface
bd-zwh3 just landed on. Take it only when that lease is clear, and keep the
bd-zwh3 clamp intact -- a divider spans the frame, so it inherits the same
out-of-canvas hazard and must be clamped the same way.

NEGATIVE CASES a naive implementation fails:
  1. An `alt` with NO `else` must emit no divider -- an implementation that draws
     one per fragment rather than per branch boundary adds a line that means
     nothing.
  2. The divider must sit BETWEEN the last message of one branch and the first of
     the next, not at a fixed fraction of the frame height; assert it against the
     actual message y positions, with branches of unequal message counts.
  3. Both branch labels must reach the document -- a test asserting only that a
     divider exists passes while the condition text is still dropped.
  4. A sequence diagram with no fragments at all must render byte-identically.

Divider offset derived from the frame's own lead above its first message, not a new constant. sequence_advanced blessed: 148 -> 151 elements, all inserted, viewBox unchanged. comments.text: ROOT CAUSE LOCATED, and the data is already in the IR — this is a consumer gap, not a parse gap. crates/fm-core/src/lib.rs:4421 defines FragmentAlternative { label, start_edge, end_edge } and IrSequenceFragment.alternatives: Vec<FragmentAlternative> (:4436). The parser populates it: mermaid_parser.rs:2321-2340 turns 'else', 'else <label>', 'and', 'and <label>' and 'option' into SequenceStatement::FragmentElse with the label preserved. So 'is bad' DOES survive parsing. It dies at the consumers: rg 'alternatives' across crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs and crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs returns NOTHING for this field — layout's build_sequence_fragment_geometry emits only the outer frame bounds, and the renderer draws only that frame. THE FIX CAN BE RENDERER-ONLY, which matters because fm-layout is under a long-running peer lease: the SVG renderer already has  and , so for each fragment it can map alternative.start_edge through ir.edges to the corresponding layout edge path, take that path's y, and draw a dashed divider across the frame plus the alternative's label — no new LayoutExtensions field and no fm-layout edit. title: Sequence alt/opt/loop/par frames are drawn 2px outside the canvas on both sides, so their border is clipped
description:
Every `alt` / `opt` / `loop` / `par` frame in a sequence diagram is clipped on BOTH sides, because
layout anchors it outside the canvas and nothing grows the canvas to hold it.

MEASURED on golden/sequence_advanced.svg, viewBox `0 0 757.89996 1646.5`:

    <rect x="-2" y="550.50" width="761.90" height="432" rx="2" ry="2"
          class="fm-sequence-fragment" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-dasharray="6,4"/>
    <rect x="-2" y="550.50" width="188.50" height="23"
          class="fm-sequence-fragment-label-bg"/>

Left edge at x = -2 (canvas starts at 0) and right edge at -2 + 761.90 = 759.90 against a canvas of
757.90. So the dashed border loses 2px on the left and 2px on the right, and the `alt` label chip
loses its left border with it. The user sees a fragment box that is open at both ends instead of a
closed rectangle.

THE CAUSE, at crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs `build_sequence_fragment_geometry`:

    let padding = message_gap * 0.35;
    bounds: LayoutRect {
        x: -padding,                        // anchored to 0 minus padding, i.e. off-canvas
        width: total_width + padding * 2.0, // and widened past the right edge as well
        ...
    }

`total_width` is computed as `last_cx + last_half_w` — the right edge of the last participant, which
is also what the canvas width is derived from. So the frame is deliberately made `2 * padding` wider
than the canvas it will be drawn on. The overhang can NEVER be visible: it is not slack, it is
guaranteed clipping.

THE INTENT IS RECOVERABLE AND CHEAP TO SATISFY. The leftmost non-fragment element in that golden
sits at x = 3.77, so a frame anchored at `content_left - padding` would land at 1.77 and fit inside
the canvas while still bracketing every participant. Two candidate fixes:
  (a) anchor to the content span and clamp: `x = (content_left - padding).max(0.0)`, with the width
      taken to the last participant's right edge plus padding, clamped to the canvas. Keeps the
      bracket look, nothing clipped.
  (b) grow the diagram bounds to include the frame, the way bd-h9gx did for gantt labels
      (`extend_bounds_for_gantt_labels` exists precisely because only layout can grow the canvas to
      hold something drawn outside the content box). Keeps the overhang, makes it visible.
(b) is the more faithful reading of the original intent and matches the established precedent in
this repo; (a) is smaller. Whoever takes it should pick one and say why, not average them.

SAME DEFECT FAMILY as bd-h9gx and bd-tm5p: something is drawn outside the box that was sized without
it. This is the sequence-fragment instance, which the earlier sweep did not reach — that sweep
declared sequence CLEAN on the strength of participant boxes, lifeline spacing, activation bars and
message labels, and never looked at interaction fragments.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the correction that matters more than the finding: a first pass flagged EIGHT
goldens by parsing attributes within a fixed character window after each `<rect `, which let a
`<path d="… L353.35 …">` supply an "x" to the following rect. Seven of the eight were artifacts of
that. Parsing each element's OWN tag text (up to its `>`) leaves exactly one file and two elements,
the ones above. Pair attributes inside the element that owns them, never by proximity — the same
extraction trap recorded in the node-sizing sweep.

NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS: the change moves geometry, so it needs `golden_svg_test` re-blessed with a
semantic diff, and the rch fleet has refused this project's jobs continuously
(`active_project_exclusion=1`) while a peer's `cargo test -p fm-layout --test alloc_profile` run
holds the per-project slot. No local fallback was taken.

Golden verified: exactly 3 elements moved (fragment rect, label bg, label text), x=-2 width=761.90 -> x=40 width=677.90 inside viewBox 757.89996, arithmetic confirmed (layout emits -42, offset_x 40). comments.author: CrimsonMaple
comments.text: FIX LOCATION IS UNDER A PEER LEASE, so I am not implementing it. The change belongs in crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs build_sequence_fragment_geometry, and StormyFalcon holds an exclusive Agent Mail lease on that file until 2026-08-16T03:43:01Z while running the bd-oarm allocation profiler in it. Editing it would collide with an in-flight arena refactor. THE FIX IS FULLY SPECIFIED AND HAS A LOCAL PRECEDENT IN THE SAME FUNCTION, so whoever holds the file can land it in minutes: the cluster branch of the very same bounds computation already does the right thing - 'let min_x = cluster_min_x.min(0.0); width: total_width.max(cluster_max_x) - min_x' grows the canvas to include clusters that extend past the origin. Fragments need identical treatment. Concretely: hoist the build_sequence_fragment_geometry(..) call above the 'let bounds = ..' at ~6160 (all its inputs - participant_x_centers, node_sizes, message_y_positions, first_message_y at :6070-6073, diagram_bottom at :5969, message_gap - are already in scope there), bind it once, fold min(fragment.bounds.x) and max(fragment.bounds.x + width) into min_x/width in BOTH bounds branches, then pass the same binding to the sequence_fragments field at :6225 instead of rebuilding it. That keeps the intended padding overhang AND makes it visible, which is the (b) option and matches bd-h9gx's precedent that only layout can grow the canvas. A test should assert every fragment rect lies inside the viewBox, with a control that the fixture actually contains an alt/opt/loop/par fragment - otherwise the assertion is vacuous on a diagram with none.

comments.author: StormyFalcon
comments.text:
MAIN WAS WORKSPACE-RED ON THIS BEAD'S TEST. Fixed in eaefbfe0.

  cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast
  -> state_xl_2000_completes_structurally_and_deterministically ... FAILED
     assertion `left == right` failed: state_xl_2000 parser omitted authored edges
       left: 2001
      right: 2000

THE TEST WAS WRONG, NOT THE ENGINE. state_xl_input() authors, in order: `[*] --> S0`, then
XL_NODE_COUNT - 1 chain transitions, then `S1999 --> [*]`. That is 1 + 1999 + 1 = 2001 edges. The
expectation said XL_NODE_COUNT = 2000. Counted independently by regenerating the document and
counting `-->` rather than by re-reading the loop.

The node expectation already carried `+ 2` for the two `[*]` pseudo-states. The matching `+ 1` for
the two pseudo-TRANSITIONS those states bring was missed. Nodes were counted; edges were not.

TWO THINGS THE FAILURE MESSAGE GOT BACKWARDS, worth fixing in any sibling assertion:
  - It said "parser omitted authored edges" while left > right, which is an EXTRA edge, not an
    omission. The message can only ever be right in one direction.
  - It accused the engine of a defect it did not have. The parser returned exactly what the document
    authored.

NOT A GATE RELAXATION, and I am aware this edit has the same shape as one. NEGATIVE CONTROL: setting
the expectation to XL_NODE_COUNT + 2 fails with `left: 2001, right: 2002`, so the assertion still
compares against the real parsed count and still catches a parser that drops or invents an edge.
Only the arithmetic moved. Source restored byte-identically, sha256
d5a4c22058a1d3574aaa626ddd443c8d35a042d62949f5e0bd8ede4bba6c6532.

The other six XL structural tests (class, er, cyclic_scc, wide, dense_dag, sequence) are consistent
with their own generators and are untouched. corpus_ingestion is now 12 passed / 0 failed.
